title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
Alright, the computer is actually really solid. It came well boxed with a lot of protection inside and comes with a document of when the last time the PC was stressed test which is cool. Mines was in April. That being said, they didn’t clear out the plastic coverings for some of the parts so make sure to inspect thoroughly. The PC glass panels have plastic on both sides of the panel.

I am running games mid-high at 1440p w/ 120+fps. I’m not entirely sure why the 4060 gets hate but of course there is better. I wanted something basic to upgrade over time and well it seems more than that. The CPU is amazing.

1. The PC comes with mostly Gigabyte components. The motherboard is a B650 UD AX Y1. You can find it on the website directly, but most of the information is found on the Aorus gigabyte site. BIOS was on version F33, its updates behind but I won’t update it unless I really have to. It’s not the best from what I’ve seen in research, but so far it’s solid.

2. The AIO it comes with is a rebranded Deep cooler, heard these were cheap but it’s really good so far. My temps have never touched over 75. The fans are really strong and in BIOS the fan speed is set to normal.

You should 1000% change the fan curve in bios (change the speed at which the fans go depending on the temps reached). I say this because the same week, the AIO front fan started howling, couldn’t figure out why until I changed the speed and now it’s extremely quiet and still remains cool. It was set to hit max speed once it hits 70 degrees which isn’t needed. I was going to swap out the AIO but now I can hold off until I want a nice LCD AIO.

2. The RAM is patriot 16gigs with an XMP profile for 6000, I swapped these out for Corsair Vengence 32gig. If you do the same, it kept booting to bios because the XMP file was still enabled. Just disable it > reboot > it will go to windows > give it 10mins > reboot again and enable XMP or w/e profile you choose and it will boot back into Windows without issue. it was running at base speed but now at 6000.

3. The case is a Montech XR. The instructions it came with is not how you take off the panels. You want to first pop off the front glass panel and then the side. Pull from the very top, it will pop off and slide up. The side panel has a prop on the left, pull with some force and slide up. It will require force so don’t feel scared just don’t apply too much pressure at the same time.

4. The Power supply is a P650B from gigabyte. I plan on replacing this eventually because I’ve heard bad things about gigabyte PSU’s and I’d rather have something more premium or secure like a 750 seasonic or EVGA.

Essentially, it’s a solid build. I was expecting serious issues because it’s a prebuilt which is why I got it off Amazon since the returns are easy but so far it’s been great. Of course, I’ll update if anything changes.

I did have 2 issues mostly due to a windows update which freaked out the RGB But it does come with SIGNALRGB software to control it. I think it just got conflicted with the MOBO controlled RGB setting and signal. When you turn off the PC it will keep the LED on the AIO - you have to disable the feature where it keeps your USB ports powered when in turned off state. I forgot the setting name. Once that is done, you’re good.

The cable management is decent, could’ve been better but that is a problem I’ll deal with when I change out the AIO, PSU and GPU.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
Very nice PC for the money! Fast processor and excellent Nvidia graphics card. Very quiet fan operation. Plenty of fast USB3 ports, front and back. Cool looks.

Mine came with Windows 10 pre-installed and fully functional, but no Windows 10 "activation code". So at first it seems that Windows 10 cannot be activated properly on this machine. I noticed that there is no Windows 10 documentation anywhere in the paperwork that came with my PC. When you go to the Microsoft web site to register it, it says the PC's serial number is not registered for Windows 10, and they send you to a site to pay $120 for a Windows 10 Home license. Also, a watermark is seen on the lower right corner of your screen telling you your Windows 10 is not activated. Lack of Windows activation has given me problems in getting Office 365 to work, since the machine is currently unlicensed according to Microsoft. The Amazon description claims it comes with Windows 10 Home - which is only partially true due to the above situation. In fact, it may be an un-licensed copy. Might have to buy that license at some point.

EDIT : Found the Windows 10 Product key !! by opening PowerShell and typing this command :
wmic path SoftwareLicensingService get OA3xOriginalProductKey
and then pasting the long product key (make sure you write it down for future reference) into the PC Settings > Update>Activation window. All is good now !!

EDIT 2 : I am looking for a memory upgrade, right now it comes with 8+8=16GB of DDR4 2666MHz 288pin ram. I plan to use two sticks of 32GB ram, for a total of 64GB. The memory I am looking at is : Crucial Ballistix 3200 MHz DDR4 DRAM Desktop Gaming Memory Kit (288pin) 64GB (32GBx2) CL16 BL2K32G32C16U4R (RED), or https://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B083TRRT1N/ref=ox_sc_act_title_1?smid=ATVPDKIKX0DER&psc=1

Hopefully that should work straight out of the box !

text:
Update at the end!
—————————

PC runs great, I’m not a big fan of their software control center called GCC but it is nice to have all drivers and bios updated in one interface. GCC allows you to have control of the Lightning if you’re into that and the 9700x and 5070 ti pair up incredibly nicely. The packing was okay, it has these cushioned supports but it wrapped in this super cheap plastic bag, wish they had a more premium cloth to cover it with instead. The installation was easy, it was basically plug and play. Upon first boot you’ll install windows and the GCC app will open and it gives you a nice tutorial on what the software is. You can update drivers through there but you’ll still need to update windows via system settings. I also recommend going to their website and downloading and installing their listed drivers just to be on the safe side

For gaming this was amazing, I play a lot of shooter games unfortunately mainly CoD since it recently released. I was playing at an average of 130fps in 1440p at high settings, no DLSS, native image scaling. It was butter smooth. I did not get the opportunity to play other games as you’ll read why

Apart from the easy of installation and the gameplay capabilities the biggest drawback of this PC are the slow SSD, the DDR5 5600mhz and their GCC/software.

The reason for my poor review was because of a hardware issues regarding the GbE LAN port. I have gigabit internet and my router is capable of supporting such speeds, however the GbE port itself was stuck on 100mbps which created a bottleneck when connected via Ethernet. I was constantly getting connection timeouts or connection lost because of this. I tried everything, port forwarding, changing the speed from auto negotiate on the driver to 1000mbps but still no prevail. I went out and bought a Cat6a cable to see if the Ethernet was the issue, no luck. I changed firewall settings, updated drivers and still nothing. I came to the conclusion that the motherboard was defective so I am currently shipping it back.

Overall this PC would have been amazing it not for the GbE port malfunction and the crappy GCC app. Would I buy again? Yes I did, I had to reorder it and hopefully this time it won’t be defective.

UPDATE:
I was originally supposed to send this computer back because of what I though go be a faulty motherboard. Well I was able to do some deeper analysis and after hours of thinking of what possibly could be messing with the connection I came across a program called cFosSpeed which is basically a program that controls and tweaks your internet to give you less latency. After uninstalling that program I did not run into any issues whatsoever even after a 16 hour gaming session. Now that the computer is functioning like intended I am so glad I decided to do more troubleshooting than sending it back because they went out of stock shortly after I bought mine.

Highly recommend this computer just do yourself a favor and remove that cFosSpeed program ASAP

Had this for 6 months now. Got it on prime day sales. It was my first gaming pc. Been researching for awhile planning to build but with the prices these days pre builts really aren’t a bad way to go if you know what to look for and what you’re getting.

I ended up buying this for less than I could have built it for. I don’t have a microcenter anywhere close so ordering online it is.

The pros:
Better parts than expected
Pny 5070ti
Montech fans unlike what the Amazon post shows
Lexar 2tb gen 4 ssd
Team group t force delta 6000 cl36 memory
Ran great out of the box and no issues so far.
Nicely packaged and delivered without damage
Comes with m&k
Was impressed with great cable management

The cons: (I’m gonna be picky on some of these)
The keyboard is awful…started not working first day.
Mouse is cheap like the keyboard but hey at least they included both right?
It’s a gigabyte b650m mobo(cheaper end) so not as many usb ports as I’d like and 1gbps Ethernet port. (Personal problems imo)
No issues with it but cheaper no name non modular power supply.
Found a couple loose screws on the fans when I first opened it. Probably from shipping.

Overall thoughts:
It was priced right, setup was simple, arrived with no damage, nicely packaged, and gaming is great on it.

IMO if you come into a prebuilt knowing where things might be lower end to save the company some money and know what you’re gonna be in for/getting it’s not a bad route. If you order this pc before plugging any power to it make sure everything is plugged in in fully and maybe double check the screws are not loose anywhere. Shippers don’t like to be gentle so who knows how much movement it goes through before arriving to you.

I’m giving it 4 stars since I had a couple small things that I found. If I could have I would have gave it 4.5 stars honestly.

The screen and gpu support bracket I added after those don’t come with the pc.

Great machine, but two cons that might leave some people stuck and disappointed.
First the potential biggy. The system came with NO power cord. Oops!
Also, as other another review stated, the Wi-Fi is NOT built in by DELL as the description states. It is a tiny $5 USB type
but it works just fine and this makes no difference to me, but it might to some.
FYI, if you get this machine and the Wi-Fi sees access points but will not connect, try a different USB port. I started with the 4th USB3 (blue) port on the right and no go. I moved it to the first on the left, and it has been solid now for a few days. I don't know why this would happen, but I got it working so no big deal.
Neither of those issues flustered me, your mileage may vary.
I got this refurb PC because of its 8 core i7-9700, 32GB RAM and 1TB SDD all for a great price.
If you have never owned one of these DELL commercial grade machines, you will not be disappointed. The build quality and the heavy sheet metal used in these units is far superior to a discount consumer grade PC. I have had four similar mini towers like this over the years - 2 HP and 2 DELL, but this is the most powerful one yet. The $400 price point makes it a no-brainer for most business and home office uses. It runs Win11, Libre Office, some trading and charting platforms, and FL Studio DAW all at the same time without hesitation. The 32GB RAM no doubt helps with that.
The unit arrived well packed for shipping and reasonably clean, though it had what I thought at first was a small scratch on top. This turned out to be a splash of white-out from its past corporate life.
As I mentioned above, what could be a showstopper for most users looking for a turnkey machine, this unit arrived with no power cord. Now, having been a PC hardware nerd for decades, I have dozens of the standard power cords laying around, and it did not slow me down a bit. Obviously, though, a power cord should come in the box, and most likely will in yours. I can't imagine they left it out on purpose.
I have not tested the included CHEAP wireless keyboard and mouse, but I am sure they are fine for what they are and are probably an upgrade for laptop keyboard users.
Great value, in a small, solid package.

text: I am using this for a basic email and web surfer machine. It is very fast..... looks and runs like a brand new machine. Runs super quiet.... really not bad at all. Here is the deal as to why its so cheap for the most part. The copy of windows is an OEM version issued and licensed exclusively to Dell. You do not get a copy of Windows on disc with this machine, you get a hard drive with an image file on it ( the main drive has a partition on it) which is where the copy is located. You can do full factory restore from that partition and set the machine up like it was the day you got it and it will activate and be a legitimate copy/machine.... title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
The Short Version: (Please skip this as it has spoilers if you prefer to read ‘The Long Version’.)
16 GB RAM, 1 TB M.2 SSD. I noticed a vibration from the CPU fan and contacted TekRefurbs and they are shipping me a new fan. Their response time was quick and they were eager to make sure I was a satisfied customer. I added 16 GB more RAM, a 2.5 inch SSD, a low-profile graphics card (supports up to 3 monitors), and a dual M.2 card along with 2 more M.2 SSDs. With the 2 DP ports and HDMI port on the motherboard, I ACTUALLY RAN 6 MONITORS (all at once) while streaming 6 different videos on YouTube. I picked this up to replace my DELL Optiplex 9020 which is too old for Windows 11. (As of now, Microsoft has stated that they will be ending their support for Win 10 by the end of 2024.) Running Crystal Disk Mark I got transfer rates of 1.7 GBps (read) and 1.1 GBps (write) on the SSD that came with the computer and 2 GBps (read) and 1.6 GBps (write) on the HP M.2 SSD I added. **UPDATE: I replaced one of my M.2 SSDs with a fanxiang S660 4TB PCIe 4.0 NVMe M.2 SSD and now get the following speeds (read) 3.5 GBps and (write) 3.1 GBps. They actually make faster M.2s but they far exceed the capability of the motherboard.

I’m thrilled with both the computer and customer service couldn’t be happier with this purchase.

The Long Version:
I have purchased over 1,000 items from Amazon over the past decade and I only give reviews on the best (or the worst) items I have ordered. The renewed DELL Optiplex 7060 SFF I got from TekRefurbs is amazing and so is their customer support. (I had a little vibration with the CPU fan and I sent them a message about it, they replied the next business day and offered to send a replacement.) Awesome service!

With Microsoft stating that they will be ending their support for Windows 10 towards the end of 2024, I decided to replace my Optiplex 9020 SFF (not Win 11 compatible) now, rather than wait for a possible shortage of affordable/renewed Win 11 computers in the future. (As of now, the vast majority of people are still running Win 10.)

The model that I got was the 16 GB/ 1 TB version (other variants may be sold by different vendors). When I opened the box (and even the case) it looked like it was brand new, I couldn’t find even the smallest amount of dust anywhere. Included with the desktop was a free wireless mouse & keyboard and a few BT & WiFi dongles in addition to the built-in features from the motherboard itself. (Even without the dongles, I still have BT & WiFi connectivity.) **Models sold by TekRefurbs come with the built-in M.2 WiFi card which supports both 5 & 2.4 Ghz but for the fun of it I replaced it with the AX210 WiFi 6E Card M.2 NGFF and connected it to the 2 internal antennas.

Display Support: While some desktops (from other sellers) only have 2 Display Ports (DP) and either a VGA port (or missing the 3rd port), mine came with 2 DPs and an HDMI port. (Nice touch!) While being able to connect to 3 monitors (off of the motherboard) is nice, I added an inexpensive VisionTek Products Radeon 6350 SFF 1GB DDR3 3M DMS59 with 2X DVI-I to VGA Adapter Graphics Card that adds support for an additional 3 monitors AND I RAN A TOTAL OF 6 MONITORS AT ONCE while streaming different videos on each monitor. Granted, I’m not a gamer so I’m not concerned with Frames Per Second (FPS) but it did actually work (I normally just run 3 monitors stacked vertically – one on top of each other).

Storage Capacity (hard drives): This model, like most of the DELL SFF cases have 3 SATA ports and the newer models have a space for an M.2 SSD. The model I purchased came with a 1 GB M.2 SSD and the DVD drive and the cables were provided to connect a second hard drive as well. There is room for a 3.5 inch hard drive or you can get an adapter to mount the smaller 2.5 inch drive if you wish (there are adapters that can hold up to three 2.5 inch drives in a single 3.5 inch slot). But why settle for just one additional hard drive when you can have a total of FOUR HARD DRIVES? Thanks to the Dual M.2 PCIE Adapter for SATA or PCIE NVMe SSD with Advanced Heat Sink Solution,M.2 SSD NVME (m Key) and SATA (b Key) 22110 2280 2260 2242 2230 to PCI-e x 4 Host Controller Expansion Card, you can have up to 3 M.2 SSDs plus one 2.5 inch SSD. ***You can also get the M.2 NVME to PCIe 3.0 x4 Adapter with Aluminum Heatsink Solution (single M.2 slot) and add up to two additional 2.5 inch SSDs. I actually recommend getting this card instead of the one I purchased because the second M.2 slot has to connect to one of the SATA ports from the motherboard so the transfer speed is the same as if you connected a 2.5 inch SSD (which are cheaper). Running Crystal Disk Mark I got transfer rates of 1.7 GBps (read) and 1.1 GBps (write) on the M.2 SSD that came with the computer and 2 GBps (read) and 1.6 GBps (write) on the HP M.2 SSD I added.

RAM: The model I purchased came with 16 GB RAM (two 8 GB chips) which was nice because I added an additional 16 GB RAM for a small price. (32 GB is more than enough RAM for most applications.)

Free Extras: The extra dongles, mouse and keyboard are nice touches and pretty good quality as well. I admit that I haven’t tested them because I used a lighted keyboard (wired) and Logitech Trackball.

Summary: Whether you are using the computer ‘as is’ or you want to upgrade it, this is an excellent choice for an affordable and (still) powerful system that will carry you through the Windows 11 lifespan (and probably beyond). Despite this being the Small Form Factor (SFF) model, there is room to add a (low profile) graphics card, USB-C 3.2 card, M.2 card or whatever you wish. (Just be mindful of the power requirements of the graphics cards - this comes with a 200 watt power supply.)

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
So this is the second SkyTech PC I have bought and once again it was generally due to the fact that pricing parts to build my own was a bit difficult (COVID-19 has made GPU's scarce and pricey). My first PC is over 2 years old at this point and I was looking to actually just upgrade it's GPU but everything I was looking for was out of stock or outrageously priced (at the time a 1660 Super was running near $400). So settled on this machine, it had many of the parts I was looking to get myself: AMD 5 3600, 16GB RAM, GTX 1660 Super, B450 Motherboard (though I had looked at B550).
I am not disappointed. The machine is wonderful and came delivered without single flaw. It booted on the first try and immediately went into Windows all the RGB elements performed perfectly. I ran a series of tests after it finished setting up windows and was pleased to see that the SSD was not a total disgrace as some had stated before, getting about 530 MB/s sequential read times at 1Gib and 514 MB/s Write. That's not blazing fast, but it was better than I expected after reading reviews. I received an ADATA SU720 500GB model drive in my build and these Read/Write times are right on par with the stated performance for that drive, so I have no complaints. I dropped a NVMe drive in right away as well as a smaller 256GB solid state drive for games and other files. Storage was my only real concern with the build, but adding storage is not an issue (though it is a bit hard to get power cables up from the power supply, the cords are all quite well bundled and I had to cut a zip tie to get a free power cable for my SSD). Unlike the pictured model my build came with a B450M/AC so it had the Wi-Fi built in to the motherboard, rather than in a PCI slot. This was a pleasant surprise and also meant the motherboard had 4DIMM slots instead of 2 (like I saw some people received in their builds). The RAM I got was OLOY Brand, which is actually Chun Well Technologies and it was just standard RAM, no heat spreaders or anything fancy, but it was strong memory, running 16-18-18-36 at 1.3v with a clock speed of 100Mhz at a 15x multiplier, giving you 1500Mhz DDR, so in total it matches the 3000Mhz advertised. I am unsure what brand GPU I got, but I suspect by the I/O panel (DVI, HDMI, DisplayPort) it is an MSI Brand. Its a single fan, compact unit and I am quite happy with it, though I would have preferred a model without DVI and instead a second DisplayPort or HDMI port. In all I am very pleased with this machine, the quality, the build, the parts, and performance are all above what I anticipated and as a Cyber Monday deal for $200 off list it was pretty much a bargain.
Edit: so Cyberpunk 2077 has dropped and despite the poor reception I had it running at a smooth 60fps @1080p on this machine. I am not a crazy hardcore gamer looking for 4k and Ray Tracing, I was quite happy that my new PC ran the game with no hardware related problems and a strong graphical performance.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
If you’re researching and scouring the internet for advice on what starter PC you should invest in, you’ve found the review you need. I spent months looking for a decent starter PC which would allow me to play all my games and store my content effectively while maintaining speed and quality. I wanted something that was visually appealing and functional. Personally, I’m a broke college kid who needed an outlet to balance school and fun. I wasn’t sure where to begin my search, and had no idea what requirements and features were required to have an effective and quality PC.
In this review, I’m putting you in the same position as me when I started looking through the PC marketplace. When beginning the search for your first PC, the search can be incredibly overwhelming and daunting. However, you are doing an amazing job searching if the internet miraculously placed you with this item.
Let’s break down the features of the PC. This computer is a pre-built, which means there is no assembly required on your part. There’s a plethora of components that make a PC worth buying, and I’m going to break down the specifics of each component and how they correlate to the performance and quality of your gaming.
The primary function of any PC is the central processing unit (CPU). The CPU, also known as the processor, is responsible for executing and refining the power of the computer and directly affects how fast your computer, or computer games, run. The CPU also processes the inputs from the user. The CPU included in this pre-built is an AMD Ryzen 5 3600 3rd Generation.
Another important factor in the PC is the RAM. RAM stands for random access memory. The purpose of RAM is to store short term data and allow the computer to process applications properly. RAM’s data is temporarily stored while applications are currently operating, like having a game playing. This PC includes an 8 GB card, which means if your game requires around 8 GB of RAM, your game will function and run properly. If you’re not sure about a game’s required RAM, the developers include those requirements in the breakdown and analytics of each game. The RAM only holds the contents of the game for the duration you are playing. Once the application is shut off, the RAM is no longer active.
While RAM is temporary storage, the hard drive processor is not. The hard drive is responsible for keeping your saved digital storage. For example, the space required for saving your game or Microsoft Office software. The hard drive also stores pictures, videos, and the applications you have downloaded on your PC. Hard drives can be external or internal, which means saving data to an external memory device or to the PC itself, and the contents can be deleted or cleared once you no longer need them. The hard drive included in this pre-built is a 500 GB SSD card.You can store up to 500 gigabytes of content as soon as you start up the PC.
While those features are required for every PC, even for basic processes and storage, this review will highlight the rest of the features through a gaming perspective since this is a gaming PC. The graphics card is responsible for rendering the images and content in a game and running them effectively. It renders the movements, animations, inputs, and images that are in a game through a series of fast acting calculations completed internally in the PC. The graphics card included in this PC is a GeForce GTX 1660 Ti 6G GDDR5, which holds 6 GB of RAM.
If you are a little confused about whether or not your graphics card is going to make or break your gaming experience, multiple YouTube creators offer a compilation of benchmark videos with clips and segments from video games with demanding animation and experiences. The benchmark videos include multiple different video games from varying genres that allow gamers to evaluate how well the game is running and performing according to the graphics card.
In regard to usability and functionality of the PC, the developers include a detailed pamphlet that illustrates how to properly connect your PC to a monitor, how to enable your microphone and speakers, and the purpose of each feature throughout the PC. The PC does require a three-prong plug, and I recommend plugging the cord into a direct power source, like a wall outlet, instead of a surge protector or extension cord.
When plugging in a monitor, there are two different HDMI ports on the back of the PC for up to 2 different monitors to be used simultaneously. Computer speakers should have a USB port to plug into the back of the PC, and headsets unfortunately require a splitter to listen to music and use a microphone concurrently. Splitters are cords that connect to the aux section of your headphone cord, and it divides this cord into two auxiliaries that can be plugged into two corresponding holes. The PC permits one USB powered keyboard and one USB mouse. These assets are included in the Amazon listing.
This PC in particular is incredibly visually appealing. It features a white tower, which is the casing around all the important parts of the PC, with a tempered glass window on the side to look into the tower. It also has multiple RGB lights and various functions. There are seven varying lighting functions to encourage individuality and styles. Located around the lighting fixtures are three fans to cool the system down. The fans blend in with the circular lighting fixtures. The PC is very cohesive in design, and incorporates each feature into the overall aesthetic of the computer.
Overall, I believe this PC is a quality starter PC within its budget of $1200. It strives in multi-tasking, allowing the user to edit documents while having a YouTube video or music running in the background. I have been using this system for school and gaming for around eight months, and have had no issues with it. I give it an A for price point, functionality, and visual appeal. I believe this is an ideal PC for a casual gamer who wants something to balance work and entertainment with.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
The OptiPlex 7050 Micro turns out to be a surprisingly capable little lab box, especially when you throw Linux on it and let it breathe. The i7-6700T may be older, but paired with 32GB of RAM, it handles Docker stacks, lightweight VMs, home-lab services, and general experimentation without breaking a sweat. For a machine roughly the size of a sandwich, it’s shockingly stable under continuous workloads—something you notice when it’s been running for days without a hiccup or thermal complaint.

In practice, it makes an excellent “utility node” for the kind of mixed tasks labs tend to accumulate: small containers, automation tools, monitoring agents, or a handful of personal services. And yes—it even runs a Minecraft server just fine. The kids don’t care that the CPU launched during the Obama administration; they care that it doesn’t lag when someone decides to dump 12 stacks of TNT. The SSD and RAM make the whole setup feel modern, and Linux has no trouble with the hardware, meaning you spend your time deploying things—not troubleshooting drivers.

Limitations are predictable and manageable: no GPU means anything graphics-heavy is off the table, and CPU-bound workloads will eventually remind you this isn’t a workstation-class chip. But for a quiet, low-power lab machine that sits on a shelf and just handles whatever odd job you give it, the 7050 Micro punches well above its weight. It’s one of those “why didn’t we repurpose these sooner?” machines—cheap to source, easy to maintain, and perfect for homelab and testing environments.

Pros
• Handles Linux, Docker, and small services extremely well
• 32GB RAM = plenty of headroom for containers and light VMs
• Quiet, low power, and stable under long uptimes
• Great for kid-friendly game servers (Minecraft, Valheim Lite, etc.)
• Inexpensive and plentiful on the refurb market

Cons
• Skylake CPU will bottleneck heavy multi-container or CI workloads
• No dedicated GPU limits certain lab scenarios
• Limited storage expansion (one M.2 slot)
• Not suitable for large databases or high-throughput services

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
First some background:
I am not a Dell lover, more of a Dell Hater. I don't like how they used specialized components in their computers. This one is no different, use this as is, it can't really be upgraded. Power supply is a dell custom one, and it's tiny. Having said that, this one has turned out to be a really nice computer.
Cosmetic:
This computer visually has no issues, no scratches and the inside had zero dust in it.
Components:
The components are about 3 to 5 years old according to the counters on the hard drives. One of the drives is an M.2 Samsung drive made specifically for Dell, it contains the OS (I call these gumsticks because of their shape). The second drive is a 2.5 inch 1TB drive. It's empty. This computer allows for toolless installation of hard drives, which is great. I replaced the 2.5 1TB drive with a 3.5 8TB drive with zero issue. There is only one SATA power and data cable spot on the motherboard, so it can't fit more than 1 hard drive along with the gumstick. It comes with a keyboard and mouse. I didn't use them, so I can't comment. It also has bluetooth I guess. I use a hardwired ethernet connection so i can't speak to any wireless connections.
Initialization:
During initialization I logged into my Microsoft account and everything worked flawlessly. I didn't have to enter an activation code like the STG Skytech Global paperwork said I would have to. I later went on my Microsoft account and verified this computer was registered with Windows 11 pro. I don't know anything about STG, but this computer was well cleaned and setup, so good for them. I left the computer on and occasionally cycled power over a full day to get all the windows 11 updates before I tried to do anything to the computer. I would recommend this to everyone. Let windows get fully updated before continuing. I'm not at Windows version 25H2. No issues. No display glitches that some people have indicated. Again, I would recommend not altering the computer for a day, until windows has updated to 25H2. I keep doing the 'check for updates' in windows to make this go faster.
Performance:
This computer takes about 15 seconds to boot. Very fast. Draws about 30 watts even when performing a disk transfer of 3TBs. I have no idea how they get the power so low. I haven't played games on it, nor would I suggest it. I'm using this as a backup system for my main computer. There is no external video card.
Conclusion:
I really am impressed with this computer. It's very small, uses almost no power, and allows me to connect via my local network to my main computer for backing up files. And it has windows 11 pro installed.

text:
WOW!

My new GMK Core i9-13900HK (NucBox_K10) has put a smile on my face. It's replacing an outdated Win 7 machine for our everyday use: research, email, entertainment, surfing, and some gaming. It came preloaded with Windows 11 Pro, which includes New Outlook. For sure, I was immediately very impressed with the K10's performance.

Specifics:
Device name NucBox_K10
Processor 13th Gen Intel(R) Core(TM) i9-13900HK 2.60 GHz
Installed RAM 32.0 GB (31.8 GB usable)
System type 64-bit operating system, x64-based processor
Pen and touch No pen or touch input is available for this display
Edition Windows 11 Pro Version 24H2
Installed on ‎5/‎1/‎2025
OS build 26100.4202
Experience Windows Feature Experience Pack 1000.26100.107.0

First, I updated the OS using Windows Update. The update took perhaps 2 hrs (typical given other users' comments re: Win11 updates). Next order of business was to install my security software and run a full scan: pleasantly, no issues.
Bios access was simple using the esc key, though I had no reason to change anything.
The machine runs extremely quiet and was very fast at all the tasks I performed. I'm currently using WiFi and the GMK K10 is equally distant from my router and an Access Point in the lower level. I tested performance on 4 local networks I had defined: Router(2.4 and 5.0) and AP(2.4 and 5.0). No matter the network, the GMK K10 was impressively snappy.
The wi-fi antennas are clearly a plus. Web pages appear in a flash, and every task I perform delivers at turbo-speed.
I ran multiple applications simultaneously with numerous tabs open and everything ran flawlessly.
I plan to add a second SSD and the easy access panel on the underside should make things easier.
Additionally, the Kensington Lock capability provides for a layer of physical security if that's an issue.

On the flip side, the power button could use better illumination. Depending on ambient lighting, it can be difficult to tell if the machine is on or off (a tribute to how quiet it is). When I ran the OS update the screen went blank multiple times and, judging from the power button, I didn't know if the K10 was asleep, in the middle of a reboot, shutdown, or even if the update was complete.

In sum, the GMK K10 is a great machine. Big shout out to GMKTec, I'm impressed.
If you're looking for a low cost, up-to-date upgrade to replace your present pc, you should consider the new GMK NucBox_K10.

text:
GMKTec EVO-T1: A Mini-PC Worthy of Your Family’s AI-Learning Journey?

Is the GMKTec EVO-T1 an excellent choice for your school age children (grandchildren) to learn and build a solid foundation in AI tools while being capable of supporting more advanced AI development and experimentation as their interest and skills grow?
As a Grandparent who attended High School during the early days of the development of Personal Computing, I know firsthand how valuable it can be to have easy access to technology tools to experience, learn and experiment with developing technologies. Having access to these tools can provide a lifelong knowledge base that could lead to meaningful opportunities. Developing a solid technology skill base today is even more important than when I was a student. AI technology development is progressing so much more rapidly than in the past that I fear that if my grandchildren do not get on the learning train early, they might find themselves left shut out of future opportunities and find that catching up to their peers is an impossible task. One of the most satisfying and impactful gifts I can give them is the tools and opportunity today to learn skills that they can call upon to succeed in the future.
This was the basis for my purchase of the GMKtec EVO-T1. No doubt with its technology leading Intel Core Ultra 9 285H CPU and ARC 140T iGPU, it can easily handle any computing task that my family could ask it to do. The capability to upgrade the RAM from the included 64 MB to 128 MB and outfit it with up to three M2 NVME storage drives allows for future expansion. I was also impressed with the array of IO options available such as Audio ports front and back, dual 2.5 GB Lan ports and an Oculink port to support adding a separate GPU card to either support the needs of demanding game play or more demanding AI computation models and tools.
This level of hardware should allow the GMKTec EVO-T1 to function in almost any other technology roll such as a Home Server, Router or NAS long after my Grandchildren have outgrown and moved past its role as an AI learning and development platform. The attractive and compact design ensures it fits easily into a home office or workspace and with its cooling capabilities it does not create a noisy environment that might distract or take away from an effective learning environment.
I want to provide a capable technology device for my family to learn and develop AI skills beyond those provided by built in Internet connected LLM models offered to most computer user. I selected the GMKtec EVO-T1 believing it is up to this task and more. I want it to fill the gap between those that are highly advanced with AI development and require high end multi-GPU hardware in a dedicated AI Lab and what is currently available to novice AI users as part of most consumer computing hardware and software. At the same I wanted it to provide the added security and privacy of local AI usage thus removing the need to be tied to the public internet or to subscription fee models.

Here is my assessment of how well the GMKtec EVO-T1 meets my needs and hopefully it will be of use in your purchasing decision.

Most basic AI tasks start with using LLM’s through text-based prompts to have the AI models provide some answer to the prompt. To allow for easier access to these models several AI GUI wrapper applications are available. I tested the following AI GUI applications with several of the same prompts on the GMKtec EVO-T1 to ensure operations and determine if there were any issues. All these AI Wrappers perform their function and which one you choose as your daily driver will be an individual choice. I have included some brief notes beside each one based upon my impressions.

AIPC
This is the default application provided on the desktop. It has several advanced capabilities beyond simple prompt-based queries and provides them in a logical structure such as document analysis, translation, meeting minutes and image retrieval all accessed under the Skills menu. It also provides a LLM Model/App Store tab which allows access to eight popular LLM’s models locally along with the ability to also access many more paid Internet connected models and tools. You can use the AIPC application completely locally by simply clicking the “Offline Mode” selection on the screen following application launch. Or if you wish to utilize the Internet AI capabilities then on the launch screen you enter your email address and click on the “Send Code” button. Following receiving the code you enter it in the “Verification Code” field, check the User Agreement box and click “Login.”
I found this application to be feature rich and convenient for most normal AI interactions along with providing several more advanced capabilities that might be of use. From my inquiries the GMKtec team authorizes and approves the addition of any LLM’s that are provided on the local selection to ensure security and useability. Given that this application is new it is still evolving, and documentation and screens are not yet polished for an English audience. Given the ease of use of the application for a wide audience I am sure any improvements will arrive in short order.
LM Studio, JAN & AI Playground for Intel ARC
All these GUI wrappers provide basic functionality and additional features that might be useful. I have listed these together because when tested they all fully utilized the GMKtec EVO_T1 Intel Arc 140T iGPU. One caveat is that many other tools natively support the Nvidia GPU. Therefore, they require some more advanced configurations to allow us to utilize the iGPU instead of only the CPU. While my testing shows the Core Ultra 9 285H CPU does a respectable job while executing AI LLM functions it does not perform this task as fast and as effectively as the Intel ARC 140T iGPU. If speed of execution is desired, then you would want to investigate advanced configurations by searching PyTorch and ipex.llm and learning how to configure those within the other AI GUI wrapper applications.
LM Studio allows for almost any Open Source LLM model to be downloaded for local use and provides a well-integrated API back end as well as RAG integration. JAN provides one of the easiest GUI to navigate and use and also provides an API. While AI Playground for Intel ARC provides full and deep utilization of the Intel libraries and iGPU hardware. This allows for the use of CPU, NPU or iGPU selection while providing some preconfigured tools to accomplish image enhancement, text to image and text to video AI Generation within this GUI. A nice capability for the user.

GPT4All, Ollama, OpenWebUI, Msty, Cherry Studio, Anything LLM
I found that these tools utilize the Intel CPU and do not support the Intel ARC iGPU natively out of the box. My earlier comment that additional configurations work is needed to allow for iGPU use applies. I have confidence that some if not all these models will provide native use of the Intel iGPU in future releases and thus expand options for local model use.

So, what might be expected for Tokens/second results for local models run on the GMKtec EVO-T1 and what are its real-world functional capabilities? To answer this question, I ran samples in each of the following Generative AI functional areas. AI LLM Chat, Text to Image, Text to Video and AI Agents. AI LLM Chat was tested with a variety of prompts including plain text, document analysis, and coding. In each case my results only represent the average Tokens/sec not the quality of the output. From this data a few conclusions on the performance of the GMKTec EVO-T1 can be made. Each model was tested with the CPU and the iGPU as the main AI computational device as shown in the results.

Mistralv03:7b - CPU 9.95 T/s GPU 17.4 T/s
MINICPM-V - CPU 5.9 T/s GPU 9.8 T/s
QWQ:32b Q4 KM - CPU 2.7 T/s GPU 3.6 T/s
LLAMA3.1 :8b - CPU 11.8 T/s GPU 13.6 T/s
QWEN2.5:14b - CPU 6.2 T/s GPU 7.2 T/s
QWEN2.5:7b - CPU 10.6 T/s GPU 14.3 T/s
QWEN3-coder:30b - CPU 9.2 T/s GPU 19.1 T/s
DEEPSEEK_R1 :32b - CPU 2.8 T/s GPU 3.5 T/s
DEEPSEEK_R1 :14b - CPU 5.3 T/s GPU 7.9
DEEPSEEK_R1:8b - CPU 10.2 T/s GPU 15.6 T/s
GPT-OSS:20b - CPU 11.8 T/s GPU 15.5
In evaluating these results, I personally use the benchmark of my reading speed ability. Meaning that if I am waiting for text to display while reading then performance seems slow, and this would not be an effective use of my time. This benchmark will vary by person, but I find for me anything around 4-6 T/s is a comfortable reading speed to ensure understanding. Hence some of the 32b models when utilizing the iGPU are close to meeting this benchmark and I would find them useful when being executed on the EVO-T1.

For text to image and text to video several tools were used but primarily Comfy.UI. In all testing cases results with image generation finished in a reasonable time of less than a minute but with video generation this time expanded considerably depending upon settings. I find this functionality to be useable for learning and basic tasks on the EVO-T1. If video generation needs are higher for speed and resolution, then it is comforting to know that the EVO-T1 provides for this and other more demanding VRAM capabilities by including an Oculink port so that a separate and much more powerful GPU can be installed and utilized. Unfortunately, I do not have a more powerful GPU available, so this capability was not tested.

To examine the GMKtec EVO-T1 performance with the execution of AI Agents I utilized n8n installed in a Docker Container on the Windows 11 operating system. Instructions are easily available to accomplish this and were easy to follow with the installation and operation going seamlessly. Several simple to complicated AI Agents were tested with workflows utilizing many node types calling both local and Internet LLM’s, Websites, API, and Data Bases. The GMKtec EVO-T1 with its powerful Core Ultra 9 285H CPU and 64 MB of RAM ensured that all steps and function worked quickly and flawlessly. Clearly this hardware with the selection of an appropriate high T/s local LLM makes the EVO-T1 a powerful AI Agent development and operational tool.

Summary

From my testing I can say with confidence that the EVO-T1 is well equipped and highly capable of providing the family with the tools to explore and learn AI tools today while easily scaling up for more demanding family members to expand their capabilities deeper into developing, learning and experimenting with the tools of AI.

EVO-T1 Ultra 9 285H 64 GB RAM, 1 TB NVME SSD

This is one very nice mini PC. I originally bought this to use as my main server in my homelab. The first couple of weeks I kept Windows 11 on the system to use and test out the components. The is one great mini PC. I could easily be used a a small workstation for most people. The weakest link is the iGPU, but even this is not a deal breaker; it is very capable, and you can always use the oculink for and eGPU. It easily handled everything I tested on it and was very quite in comparison to my workstation with an NVidia GPU.

Since then I've removed Windows and installed Proxmox. It has been working great running many VMs and LXCs. It has been on 24/7 running everything from Frigate (with detector inference speeds of 6-8 ms with YOLOv9), to Windows 11, and everything in-between that a homelab runs.

The mini PC comes is a very nice box with and HDMI cable and external power brick. There is very little documentation, and it would be nice if there was info on the fan button and how to open the mini PC to add additional drives or upgrade the RAM. If you want this info you have to Google it, as their own GMKtec's website has no info on it.

I gave the product 4/5 stars, only because I could not do 4.5/5. It loses 0.5 because of the lack of proper documentation or the lack of being able to find it on GMKtec's website.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
For those considering this machine, please read carefully. I selected a reseller with a price higher than the lowest offered. Why? Because at the time of my selection, the lowest price seller had 71% satisfaction rating, but for $6 more I selected another seller with a 90% satisfaction rating (TekRefurbs.com). This is especially important with a renewed computer! Many reviews reflect problems due to the differences in resellers, so it pays to select carefully.

The first thing I did on receiving the computer was open the case and remove the new 256 GB ssd, and install a 1 TB nvme ssd into the m.2 socket, and a 2 TB ssd into the hard drive caddy and reinstalled the caddy and closed the case. The computer was spotless inside and out. The next step is very important. I went to the Dell website and downloaded the BIOS update. I run linux on a multi boot system, but linux cannot install the new bios so I booted into windows for the bios update. Just follow the on screen instructions and the update takes just a few minutes. It is crucial to update the bios as the machine is vulnerable until it is done. The machcine is capable of running Windows 11, but apparently the Windows 10 Pro that comes with the computer will not allow updating. Since I did not install Windows 10, but moved my existing drives into the computer, I was all set with Windows 11. Many users prefer Windows 10.

I recommend before buying or receiving the computer that the user/owner manual in pdf format be downloaded from the dell site as it is really mandatory if you are going to get your newly renewed machine set up properly. Curiously this computer will run with either the 65 watt or the 130 watt power supply cord; mine came with the 65 watt power supply and it works flawlessy. There are also two other m.2 sockets on the motherboard for WLAN and WWAN cards as shown in the manual for those who want or need them. The cards and cables and antenna are available on Amazon.

I hope this information is useful to any who take time to read it. The machines are not for gamers as they do not have the graphics horsepower for that use, but are great for other applications if you choose the reseller carefully. It is a shame the machines suffer less than stellar ratings due to the disparities between reseller preparations. Choose wisely and you will be rewarded.

For day-to-day routine computer tasks outside hardcore AAA gaming, such as YouTube, Facebook, internet browsing, household finance, schoolwork, etc. it's hard to beat these little boxes! They're cheap and powerful for most computing tasks and are surprisingly versatile, let alone easy to use and install.
I bought this one to replace my wife's 10 yo laptop. We used to travel more and needed the laptop when we visited my daughter during her undergrad and postgrad years and on family vacations. But these days you can do most of your usual life management tasks on your cellphone or tablet so why lug around a laptop. So with fewer trips away from home and the upcoming obsolescence of Windows 10 on the laptop, we chose to replace her laptop with one of these mini machines running Windows 11. I'd already bought a few of these small guys, an arduino to run my CNC Router and a Raspberry Pi to run my 3D printer, and a couple of $100+ Windows 11 boxes for interfacing to my NAS boxes as backup systems. But for my wife I wanted something more powerful to improve on the slow performance of her old laptop. And based on the performance specs of this BOSGAME PC along with its relatively low price I bought it.
It has been nearly perfect for her - easy to install and setup and then to customize it with all the apps she uses to manage our finances and household maintenance tasks. And compared to her old laptop, it's snappy with her not spending as much time waiting for internet access or for for data access to hard drives thanks to its fast processor and use of an M.2 SSD for data storage. Everything she does goes faster now.
We had already been using an accessory full keyboard, mouse, and Monitor with her old laptop so the transition was easy - unplug the laptop from the external monitor and USB keyboard and mouse and plug those items, along with the internet cable, into the ports on the BOSGAME E2 Mini and away we went. The new computer fit nicely under the left side of her monitor taking up no room on her desk
It took a couple of days to get all her online accounts and associated applications transferred to the new box but after that it's been flawless and efficient since!

text:
I recently purchased the Dell OptiPlex 3070 SFF Small Form Factor Desktop with an Intel Core i7-9700 processor, and I’m beyond pleased with the performance and quality. Here’s a breakdown of my experience:

Performance:
The Intel Core i7-9700 8-core processor, with speeds up to 4.70GHz, delivers impressive power. I use the desktop for a variety of tasks including office work, web browsing, and light photo/video editing. It handles multitasking effortlessly, and I haven’t experienced any lag even when running several programs simultaneously. The 32GB DDR4 RAM ensures smooth operation, and I can easily switch between tabs and apps without a hitch.

Storage & Speed:
The 1TB SSD is a significant upgrade compared to traditional hard drives. It boots up quickly, and file transfers are fast and responsive. The large storage capacity is perfect for storing all my files, media, and documents without worrying about running out of space. The SSD has made a huge difference in both the overall speed of the desktop and in the responsiveness of apps and games.

Design & Build:
Being a Small Form Factor (SFF) design, this desktop is compact and fits easily on my desk. The build quality feels solid and premium. It doesn’t take up much space, but still manages to offer great performance. The front panel is neat, and the overall aesthetic of the desktop is clean and professional, making it suitable for both home and office use.

Graphics & Display:
While this model comes with Intel UHD Graphics 630, I mostly use it for work and light gaming, so it’s more than enough for my needs. It’s not a gaming powerhouse, but it handles everyday tasks like web browsing, streaming, and office work with ease. If you’re a heavy gamer or do graphic-intensive work, you might need a dedicated GPU, but for most general users, the integrated graphics are perfectly fine.

Connectivity & Features:
The Dell OptiPlex 3070 comes with Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, and all the essential ports you need, including USB 3.0 and HDMI for easy connectivity. The presence of DVD burner is a nice touch, as it allows me to easily read and burn discs when needed, something that’s becoming rare in newer models but still useful for certain tasks. The Windows 10 Pro version comes pre-installed, and it has been stable and easy to use.

Condition (Renewed):
This unit is renewed, but it arrived in excellent condition. There are no visible signs of wear, and the desktop works just as expected for a brand-new machine. The refurbishment process seems to have been done well, and I didn’t encounter any issues upon boot-up or while using the machine.

Overall Verdict:
The Dell OptiPlex 3070 SFF Desktop is a fantastic option for anyone looking for a powerful, compact desktop. It provides excellent performance with the Intel i7 processor, 32GB RAM, and 1TB SSD at a reasonable price, especially considering that it's a renewed unit. I highly recommend this desktop for home or office use—it’s a solid choice for anyone who needs a reliable, fast machine.

A thing or two to be aware of:
RAM: It’s single-channel no-name RAM. The listing claims "dual channel," which is technically true if you go buy a second stick yourself. 2666MHz DDR4.
SSD: This is M.2 SATA, not NVMe. I realize this is stated now but note that sata is much slower than nvme.
Lazy BIOS: Zero effort on the software side. DMI strings are all just "Default String", as generic as it gets.

The Good (The Hardware):
Legit internals: The CPU/GPU combo is exactly what’s on the box. Performance holds up.
Cool & Quiet: It’s got a beefy heatsink and the fan is basically silent. No thermal throttling here.
Stacked IO: Plenty of USB ports and display outputs for such a tiny box.
Linux friendly: Everything works out of the box. No driver nightmares.
Solid Power: The included brick actually handles a full load without breaking a sweat.

TL;DR: The bones are solid and the cooling is great, but the RAM and SSD could use some work. If you’re okay swapping those out (or don't mind the speed hit), it’s a decent little machine.

Je voulais un mini pc pour remplacer deux tours des années 90 et que je puisses facilement le transporter lorsque je change de résidence entre l’été et l’hiver. Juste a rebrancher les périphériques monitor, clavier, souris, TV etc... Je ne connaissais pas les mini PC mais les performances annoncées semblaient intéressantes.

J'ai essaye un premier modèle décevant au niveau vidéo puis deux autres modèles plus performants mais j'ai rapidement compris les limites de cette technologie, Il faut quand même loger dans un mini espace les composants essentiels qui chauffent quand on les sollicites et le bruit des ventilateurs se fait rapidement sentir et devient insupportable. J.ai aussi eu des problèmes de bug (manque de puissance) pour redémarrer en sortie de veille, Il doit peut être exister des modèles très performants dans la catégorie des mini pc mais je voulais rester dans un prix raisonnable.

Avec ce mini pc ACMAGIC j'ai trouve un bon compromis, les dimensions sont comparables a un livre de bibliothèque ce qui me convient, l'installation a été rapide et efficace avec Windows 11 PRO. Il est très rapide,silencieux et me permet de travailler avec le monitor, pour la messagerie, internet et des vidéos pendant qu.il diffuse la TV sur le téléviseur via un switcher HDMI. La qualité d'image est très bonne et avec toutes les connections je peux simultanément transférer des documents du smartphone ou de stockages externes via les ports USB.

J'ai quand même eu un blocage de démarrage pour n'avoir pas bien stoppe auparavant toutes les connections et applications en cours. Si on est rigoureux cela ne devrait pas se reproduire. Il y a sur le boîtier un QR code d'un contact support par Whatsapp que j'ai utilise, un technicien répond dans la nuit (décalage horaire avec la Chine) mais les conseils n'ont pas été pertinent pour l'instant. J'essaye d'obtenir la clé Windows 11 pro par cet intermédiaire qui n’apparaît pas dans l'emballage ni sur le boîtier, Affaire a suivre. J'utilise ce Mini PC depuis une semaine et prévoit quelques commentaires complémentaires après le reconnexion dans un autre pays.

Je recommande ce modèle pour son rapport qualité prix,

J'effectue une mise à jour de ces commentaires après presque une année d'expérience. Les problèmes de démarrage n'ont pas été vraiment résolus mais après contact auprès du vendeur il a procédé rapidement
au remplacement du mini PC par un neuf. Le nouveau modèle malgré le processeur qui passe de Intel7 à Intel 5 reste aussi performant. Aucune difficulté. title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
I bought this mini PC for $209 and actually had very little expectations out of it at this price point. Also, in the past, products sold from this vendor contained Malware, so I was extra cautious and wary when I bought this item. But $209, who can argue with that. Especially with memory prices nowadays it’s ridiculous.

Anyway, first thing I did was go through the windows setup (without connecting to the internet…Important!) and installed Malwarebytes via USB key containing the full offline installer. Ran the scan…and it came up clean! No virus/malware found! This is good news as Acemagic had a stigma from issues with malware installed in past products, possibly compromising end user ho,e network security. This is good; great experience so far!

Since Windows 11 has a clean build of health, I deleted and wiped the entire drive so I can install Ubuntu Linux. I ran some extremely strenuous tests on this unit, and the cooling system is super impressive. I am running glmark2 (graphics chip benchmarking software) along with a stress utility that makes all 4 cores run at 100%. Even though with the heavy workload, this thing stayed relatively cool. The fan hardly runs. You can’t even hear it run. The glmark2 score was only 1269, so it is far from a hot rod, and having only a 4 core Ryzen 4300U CPU, you won’t be running large LLMs (for AI) on this, nor play any of the latest cutting edge games. Which is OK, because this unit isn’t for that. It’s for general purpose computing. And it’s oh so quiet! And doesn’t use up a whole lot of electricity, so you can have this running 24/7 with no issues. I’m planning to use this to run PiHole and Unbound (local DNS server), of which this K1 is overkill, since those apps were designed to run on a Raspberry Pi.

Just to set expectations, this is a very entry level machine meant to do general purpose work. However, you can still improve performance by doing upgrades on this (unlike any Mac hardware). If this is what you are planning to do, my suggestions is to get rid of that 256GB SSD drive. It is SATA and it is slow. Put a NVMe M.2 SSD 1TB or so. These newer NVMe drives are so much faster…bottlenecks are usually had in the storage drives, especially if you’re running an app that is using a lot of swap space in lieu of memory. You can actually leave the crappy SATA drive in there and install the NVMe alongside it (it has an extra NVMe slot in the unit).

Second thing to upgrade is the memory. This particular unit comes with 1 8GB SoDIMM module. There’s 2 slots available, so you can have up to 64GB memory in this.

All in all, I’m super impressed with this unit, especially at the price point. I highly recommend this for anyone doing general purpose computing and to play lightweight games (it’ll probably even run an Arcade emulator, like MAME with no issues!)

text:
This is a fairly decent mini PC system for browsing, watching videos (4K@60Hz), or general work/business tasks. It's NOT meant as a gaming system although light gaming (ones that don't require [significant] high resolution and high bitrates) are perfectly fine and it's not as if you absolutely can't play any games at all with this.

≡ Physical build
The physical build is just fine; it's got an all plastic case which is a bit disappointing to see but this won't affect the performance at all unless overheating is an issue (because it's all plastic vs. metal which dissipates heats better). The overall build quality is similar to most other such mini PCs out there and there. The internal bracket for SSD is however made of metal (pic 12) which is indeed nice to see to say the least.

≡ Connectivity/ports
It's got the typical ports as most mini PCs do; 2x HDMI (4K@60Hz) 1x VGA (3x displays in total), Wi-Fi 2.4/5GHz, GigE (wired), 2x USB 2.0, 2x USB 3.0, and a 3.5mm port. What it lacks really is a USB-C port that some others do have but this one doesn't and that's a real shame. An USB-C (10Gbps preferred of course, but 5Gbps would still be better than none) port would make this particular mini PC that MUCH more useful especially if you have an external dock or enclosure for NVMe (or even SATA) SSDs, or anything that can make use of the high throughput that USB-C delivers. As aforementioned, it does have a space for SATA SSD (max 2TB) which should be sufficient for most people (well, for a mini PC anyway).

≡ Processor
It comes with Intel Gen 11 N5105 (2GHz, turbo 2.6Ghz, 4x cores, NO HT) processor (~ 2 yrs old) which is pretty much the same as N5095 that you might've seen with some mini PCs as well but this is one is rated at 10W and a lot more power efficient whereas it's 15W for N5095. This particular mini PC is also noticeably (but not leaps and bounds) faster and a better performer than J4125 (~ 4 yrs old) processor that comes with some other mini PCs. N5105 is an obvious better choice over those if given the choice while other things being equal (or at least similar).

≡ Video performance
The built-in GPU (Jasper Lake, 24 EUs) does have native support for H265/HEC (8/10bit) for both decode/encode and support for PV8/9 which is great; however, it doesn't support AV1 which is a bit of a bummer (but then again, it's not a critical requirement at this point in time). Video playing at 4K resolution up until 60Hz is smooth without any issues at all. I also did a test video encoding which turned out to be just fine as well although Intel's QuickSync is still not as good as nVidia's but it's noticeably better in terms of video quality (at the hardware level) than previous version (v6).

≡ Operating system/general use
It comes with Windows 11 Pro that requires no introduction and it's running absolutely fine without issues. Your typical office suits of apps and/or common video playing, browsing (Firefox, Opera, Chrome), and ordinary video/audio editing tasks all run just fine as well. Again, this is MORE than sufficient for any office work and/or non-hardcore gaming activities.

≡ Upgradability
Keep in mind that the memory isn't upgradeable for this mini PC (whereas it is upgraded for some others) so you might wanna get the most you can afford because that's always a better and more cost effective route in the long run.

≡ Value
All things considered, this is a fairly decent mini PC that's quite versatile and it offers great performance as well as a small footprint that's suitable for many people who are looking for their next non-gaming systems. It's reasonably priced at $230 for what it provides (16GB/512GB) and its overall connectivity options; though, an USB-C port would've been that much better (even if it's 5Gbps only).

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
The largest AI model I am able to load onto my GMKtec EVO-X2 into the LM Studio software outputs about 8 tokens/second:

Qwen3-235B-A22B-Instruct-2507-gguf-q2ks-mixed-AutoRound-inc

This mixture-of-experts AI model is also known as:

Qwen3-235B-A22B-Instruct-2507-128x10B-Q2_K_S-00001-of-00002.gguf

This is a 235 Billion parameter model with Q2_K_S automatic Intel quantization. I am able to load this model with 96GB of memory dedicated to VRAM and the following model config in LM Studio 0.3.20:

GPU Offload: 80 / 94
Offload KV Cache to GPU Memory: NO (slider to the left)
Keep Model in Memory: NO (slider to the left)

All other model config settings are at their default values, including the attempt to use mmap option, which seems to be necessary to load this particular model.

In the magnifying lens / Runtime window, I had to select:

GGUF: ROCm llama.cpp (Windows) v1.42

ROCm allows more layers to be offloaded to the GPU and allows this large model to be faster than the Llama 3.3 70B parameter model, which outputs about 5 tokens/second with Vulkan and with the test prompt, "Why is the sky blue?" The smaller models seem to run faster with Vulkan.

When you reboot the computer, you can repeatedly press the Esc key to enter the BIOS configuration and set 96GB for the graphics memory and activate Performance mode.

I learned that it is possible to activate the High Performance mode in Windows 11 by right clicking in the Windows menu and selecting:

Terminal (Admin)

A command prompt will then open. You can then enter:

powercfg -setactive SCHEME_MIN

I then went into the Control Panel / Power Options to change the advanced power settings for the "High performance" plan which was now unhidden. I set the "Turn off hard disk after" option to Never. I set the "Sleep after" option to Never. I set the "Minimum processor state" to 100%.

The output speed of Qwen3 235B increased to 8.7 to 8.8 tokens/second for the test question, "Why is the sky blue?" This output rate is faster than the rate at which I can read when I think about what the AI model is writing. Smaller AI models might output answers faster, but the answers tend to be wrong with greater frequency than larger AI models. Wrong answers delivered fast are useless to me.

Qwen3 235B sometimes outputs gibberish, such as, "GGGGG..." I don't know if this is due to a memory shortage, a context window that is too small, a result of the quantization, or something else. I don't seem to have enough memory left to increase the context windows size from the default 4,096. Keeping prompts short on one line seems to help prevent this issue.

08/04/2025 Update: I was able to increase the context window size by setting the options:

Context Length: 262144
Evaluation Batch Size: 256
Flash attention: YES (slider to the right)

The default Evaluation Batch Size of 512 seems to cause an eventual crash, but 256 seems stable. The speed of Qwen3 235B gradually slows down as the context window fills up. After about 27,000 tokens are in the context window, the output speed drops to about 1 token/second, so 27,000 is about the practical limit for the context length unless you are patient.

I deleted OneDrive and the Recall feature. In the Edge browser, I disabled the Settings / System and performance / System / "Startup boost" option to prevent Edge from staying resident in memory all the time. I also disabled the option for "Continue running background extensions and apps when Edge is closed". I ran the msconfig program to disable the Print Spooler and some other print-related process which I will never use on this computer.

8/5/2025 Update: I was able to load the new AI model:

openai/gpt-oss-120b

The GGUF files come in 2 parts:

gpt-oss-120b-MXFP4-00001-of-00002.gguf
gpt-oss-120b-MXFP4-00002-of-00002.gguf

This is a 120 Billion parameter GPT Open Source Software version from OpenAI with MXFP4 quantization. The size listed in LM Studio is 63.39GB.

In the BIOS, I had to select 64GB dedicated to graphics memory. I am still able to load Qwen3 235B, but the output speed drops to about 7 tokens/second for the test question, "Why is the sky blue?" For Qwen3 235B, it seems better to have 96GB dedicated to graphics memory. The output speed of openai/gpt-oss-120b is about 10 tokens/second for the same question.

The following is the openai/gpt-oss-120b model config in LM Studio 0.3.21:

Context Length: 30000
GPU Offload: 36 / 36
Evaluation Batch Size: 4
Offload KV Cache to GPU Memory: NO (slider to the left)
Keep Model in Memory: NO (slider to the left)
Try mmap: NO (slider to the left)

All other model config settings are at their default values. Attempting to offload the KV cache to GPU memory results in a failure to load. Attempting to activate Flash memory results in a failure to load.

Setting the mmap option to NO seems to result in much more RAM being available once the model is loaded, dropping from about 57GB used to less than 5GB used according to the number in the lower right corner of LM Studio.

In the Magnifying lens (Discover) / Runtime window, I had to select:

GGUF: Vulkan llama.cpp (Windows) v1.44.0

Attempting to use the ROCm llama.cpp v1.43.1 causes the openai/gpt-oss-120b model not to load. So, if I switch between loading Qwen3 235B and openai/gpt-oss-120b, I must choose the version of llama.cpp that works with each model.

8/7/2025 Update: I was occasionally getting an error in GPT after it had finished outputting a response. The error message was something like: "Unexpected end of grammar stack after receiving input: G". Repeated outputs of the letter G, such as, "GGGGG...", seems to be related to the Evaluation Batch Size, which seems to be stable at a value of 4 for the GPT model. I used a variation of the following prompt and kept dividing the Evaluation Batch Size by 2 until I no longer got the error message:

Please write a story about people who wake up from suspended animation in another star system. The study of Arctic and Antarctic fish allowed scientists to develop an artificial protein that inhibits ice formation. The people left Earth due to warfare and did not have time to prepare. The ship's AI still thinks it is near Earth in the past, because that is when the AI was last updated while its atomic clock still functioned. The atomic clock was hit with shrapnel in orbit, caused by anti-satellite weapons, that was recorded as a micro-meteorite strike. Automated systems sealed the hole in the hull, but the clock remained non-functional. Any watches worn by the people in cryochambers caused frost injuries to the skin where bare metal contacted skin. The watches were broken by the cold in the cryochambers. Any watches that were stored outside the cryochambers either have depleted batteries or have not been regularly wound by movement in the case of automatic watches. Analog watch hands are halted at various time indications. An automated routine in the cryochambers wakes the crew up independently of the main AI system. Any views of the outside are through cameras and sensors which are controlled by the AI. A crew member tells the AI system to start up the main systems, but the AI system refuses to do so, because the AI refuses to accept that time has passed and thinks the crew is discussing a hypothetical scenario. The crew must either convince the AI that time has passed or somehow bypass the AI's control over the ship to survive. Bypassing the AI will result in loss of navigation and dynamic fusion containment. The AI shows the crew a picture of the Earth before they reached escape velocity as if the Earth were outside in the present. The image causes one crew member to believe that they are still on Earth. The crew member's mental illness had been well treated on Earth before the war made prescription refills impossible. The crew attempt to improvise a new clock for the AI, but the AI recognizes the inaccuracy of the clock and ignores the clock. The crew attempt to manually restart the fusion reactor but abandon the attempt when they almost lose containment. All hope seems to be lost. However, the improvised clock allows the AI's predictions, which are analogous to dreams or hallucinations in humans, to move forward in time. Previously, the AI's predictions had all been overlaid on top of each other at the same instant in time. The AI decides on its own to search for a pulsar as a time reference.

8/10/2025. I feel the need to respond to Bill Bohn's review of a computer which he apparently does not own. There is nothing misleading in my review. The numbers are what they are. If you actually had a GMKtec EVO-X2, then you could reproduce my numbers. Moonshot Kimi-K2 is simply wrong when it writes, "The reviewer is running a GMKtec EVO-X2 mini-PC that houses a Ryzen 9 8945HS (8 Zen 4 cores + Radeon 780M iGPU) plus 96 GB of system DDR5 and BIOS UMA set to 96 GB." Why are you reviewing a computer that you apparently do not own and apparently know nothing about? Do not blindly accept whatever information an AI system gives to you.

8/11/2025. I have changed the previous Evaluation Batch Size from 16 to 4 for the gpt-oss-120b model. This seems to be most stable setting so far.

8/17/2025. The gpt-oss-120b model from OpenAI now outputs 36 to 40 tokens/second for the prompt, "Why is the sky blue?" This speed increase was made possible by selecting the new ROCm llama.cpp v1.46.0 and choosing 96GB of memory to be allocated to video memory in the BIOS. Thanks to whomever made this dramatic speed increase possible. What's funny is gpt-oss-120b tells me it is impossible for consumer-level computer hardware to achieve this speed.

In the gpt-oss-120b settings, I set:

Context Length: 63000
GPU Offload: 36/36
Evaluation Batch Size: 256
Offload KV Cache to GPU Memory: YES (slider to the right)

In the magnifying lens / Runtime setting, I set:

GGUF: ROCm llama.cpp (Windows) v1.46.0

All other parameters are at their default settings for gpt-oss-120b.

Qwen3 235B now outputs about 9 to 10 tokens/second. The new version of ROCm llama.cpp v1.46.0 seems to allow 81 layers to be offloaded to the GPU instead of 80 layers. My model settings for Qwen3 235B are now:

In the magnifying lens / Runtime setting, I set:

GGUF: ROCm llama.cpp (Windows) v1.46.0

Currently, there seems to be no substitute for experimenting with the various parameters to get a stable configuration in LM Studio. The parameters that AI models recommend do not work. I recommend dividing the Evaluation Batch Size by 2 if you get gibberish from one of these large AI models or if the AI model crashes.

8/26/2025. After upgrading to AMD Adrenalin 25.8.1, the gpt-oss-120b AI model stopped working with ROCm llama.cpp v1.46.0 in LM Studio 0.3.23. I am still able to use Vulkan llama.cpp v1.46.0 but at a reduced output speed of about 33 tokens/second for the test prompt, "Why is the sky blue?" cked this up on a whim after seeing the specs—Ryzen AI Max+ 395, 128GB LPDDR5X RAM, 2TB SSD, and that Radeon 8060S iGPU that supposedly trades blows with a desktop 4060. At $2k, I was sweating bullets. Thought, “Is this mini PC hype or actual magic?” Spoiler: it’s magic.

I’m running 4K edits in Premiere without breaking a sweat, local LLMs (70B params at 20+ tokens/sec), and games like Cyberpunk at 1440p ultra hitting 80-100 FPS with FSR. Multitasking? 50 tabs, Discord, OBS streaming—zero lag. Fans whisper until you hammer it, then it’s a gentle hum at 85-90°C max.
