text:
I ordered 3 of these. On paper, they are great. The first one I received had a 256GB SSD instead of the advertised 512. It also only had 8GB memory instead of the 16GB advertised. I contacted amazon support and they wanted me to contact the seller. I contacted the seller and they said "We are sorry for the inconvenience. Please reach out to Amazon customer support for a return/replacement as this was fulfilled by Amazon." According to Amazon "Sorry, this order is not eligible for a refund under the A-to-z Guarantee because you have not yet submitted a return request with the seller. Please request a return via the Online Returns Center and allow the seller two days to get back to you."

I had already remotely deployed the unit in a customer's environment, installed AV, Office, & joined to their domain and setup user profiles, so I just gave up.

The other two, came as advertised, but the 2nd unit I setup is so slow it took about 2 hours to get through the out of box experience. Once in windows, it was not possible to open an explorer window or browser. the cursor just spun for hours. I tried about 10 times after rebooting, etc. I gave up on that one as well ready to return it. (haven't tried starting that process again)

I was able to setup the 3rd unit in place of the 2nd one okay, but later I noticed it wasn't as quick as it should be for a computer with a 6 core i5, 16GB of ram and SSD. Task manager showed it running at .79GHz. So I changed the performance profile to High Performance and rebooted. That changed nothing. I created my own custom high performance profile, selected that and rebooted. Again only .79GHz. I checked the advanced power settings and min and max CPU were set to 100%. I then reset the bios to factory defaults and low and behold on boot I got a message that the type of power supply could not be determined. When this happens to a DELL, it throttles the CPU at the slowest possible speed. The seller is providing a PSU that on paper would have more than enough power for this micro pc, but the barrel jack is too long so the center pin doesn't make contact. That is required for the system to determine the wattage of the PSU.

THE SELLER INTENTIONALLY TURNED OFF THE POST ADAPTER WARNING about the PSU not being identified. I verified this to be the case on ALL 3 UNITS! Unfortunately, I don't have time to wait for returns and refunds, so I ordered myself 2 new PSU's that are advertised as being for this specific model. I will be returning the 2nd unit because despite the PSU .79GHz issue, there has got to be something else going on with the hardware as the other two units were still somewhat usable at .79GHz. If you don't believe me look at the images.

Update 1/2/2022:
After ordering 7 of these, I can say that I've received only 1 unit with the advertised Wireless KB & Mouse. Sadly only the mouse worked...

This is a VERY solid laptop for the price. I tested it for a day to make sure there were no issues. It performs well, the screen is in pristine condition, the battery lasted several hours of light, on/off use. The keyboard is clean and has no worn or sticky keys (it is the non-backlit version). There are a couple cons - a vinyl skin was added to the laptop, presumably to refresh the finish, which is fine, it's a nice finish and probably looks a lot nicer than whatever scratches might be on it, but they covered all the screws on the bottom. Not great if you want to upgrade or service it in the future, you'll have to cut or poke through the vinyl. I also smell the slightest hint of "the previous owner was a smoker" when the fan comes on. It's not a huge deal and can be expected from a used machine, I think I'm just a little extra sensitive to that smell, I used to repair computers and you could always tell.
The laptop is advertised and pictured as coming with a CD drive. Mine didn't. Which is fine with me, I'll never need it and would honestly rather not have it.
Finally, the included charger seems to work just fine, but it's a generic unbranded one so I don't fully trust it. Luckily it charges via USB-C so there's plenty of other options if you're picky about that.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
Not what I wanted. I made the mistake. I ordered this computer under the new Dell's renaming plan. I wanted the renamed Latitude, not the renamed Inspiron which this computer is, and the seller CLEARLY titled it as such. The Latitude has more ports than the Inspiron. Again, MY BAD. Why... Why me. After looking and looking and then making this mistake...GRRRR. Anyways, what a fantastic computer!! I purchased my previous computer around ~2008, so yes, I am impressed with the newest and latest. I chose the upgraded components such as the Ultra 9, 32GB the high-end LPDDR5X (I'm talking about a max of 8,533Mbps, OMG), 2TB SSD... Logi M650L mouse. This combo is so fast, I mean so fast, I can't even keep up. Just a blink of an eye and my photography program(s) run, and the task is finished.
The backlit keyboard keeps turning off and turns back on with a touch of any key. I'll have to find the way to disable this in that I want to see the keyboard when I initially place my fingers. After that, it can turn off as I know where the symbols are.
Very easy and actually very quick setup. I chose to use a thumb drive to bring my programs and data over. Recognized my printer very quickly. My home webpage already saved my 'favorites', so no problems there.
Speaker is sufficient in that I do not have to turn it up to 100, just to barely hear it. Usually, 50-55 suffices with this computer. I can actually hear the stereo separation. Even with the audio/video players equalizer, it still plays music flat. Absolutely no bass. Yes, I know this isn't a home 5,000w speaker system, but this is 2025. I would expect a laptop to sound like a mini stereo system with, I don't know, BASS... or at least better than the cheapest cellphone. Come-on.
USB ports... As stated before, I wanted the Latitude with more ports. This one has only one USB. My mouse takes that one. That's it. No more ports. Hmm, 2025 says at least 2 ports standard?? It has 2 USB-C ports. One is occupied for power, although I believe it can be used if running off of battery.
This computer gets slightly; I mean very, very, VERY slightly warm on the bottom of the left side. Hardly even noticeable unless you are actually looking for it. The fan is also very quiet. I do not notice it unless I'm looking for the noise, slightly turning my head or it speeds up Still very quiet. Other than that, I can't hear it with the awesome, no bass music playing.
Screen is crystal clear and is advertised as "Low Blue Light (Hardware Solution)". Yeah, don't ask me. It seems to work.
I love this computer...BUT, as stated previously, I wanted the Latitude. Meh, I'll have to use my USB adapter.
Only one con I see. When turning on the computer, everything loads up fast to include connecting to the internet. However, the computer is slow to allow the home webpage to connect to the internet. I don't know why. I click the internet icon and shows it, in of itself, will not connect for a good minute, although the computer itself indicates it is connected to the Wi-Fi network. Could be my non-McAfee internet security checking things out first or could be this newest and latest Wi-Fi7 but who knows. Just a minor inconvenience.
Lesson learned. Take your time and know which model you are purchasing.

Having upgraded from a cheaper 1080p webcam, these are my comparisons:

Pros:
- Auto-focus works amazing. No more fighting with manual adjustments. You really couldn't do better in the settings yourself. Trust me, I tried.
- Low light image quality is a definite improvement.
- HDR mode works great to balance highlights and shadows.
- AI tracking is a neat feature though I don't intend to use it.
- Zoom feature in DELL software is nice (though its not really an optical zoom, it's just a blown up image).
- 65 degree vs 78 degree viewing angle options are also nice. (though again, it just looks like 65 degrees seems to be a more zoomed in version of 78 with no improvement in sharpness or image quality).
- Build quality is solid.
- Camera feed has never randomly dropped out. I always had to unplug and re-plug my old webcam.

Cons (kinda):
- Coming from a 1080p camera I expected the image detail on a 2K camera to be twice as sharp?
Well, not really.
The output resolution is definitely 2560x1440p and there are bit more details in the image, but I guess I had forgotten to do the actual math. The difference in horizontal and vertical resolution is about 33% (from 1920x1080), so remember, 2K doesn't necessarily mean twice as much. There is also a definite improvement in image quality as well. I was going to give this 4 stars because I expected something near a 2x improvement, but after doing a side by side comparison I've changed my mind. It was a poor assumption to begin with and probably a ridiculous expectation as well.

Conclusion:
While I haven't had other 1080p cameras to compare to, I'm pretty sure there are others out there that might probably do what this does, for cheaper, with comparable image quality, albeit at a slightly lower resolution. So if you really don't *need* that extra resolution (to show the real texture of your skin during those Zoom meetings), I wouldn't bother with getting a 2K webcam. That being said, everything that this webcam does, it does do pretty well, so, if you specifically want to get a 2K camera, this is the one I'd get.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
Dell USB DVD Read Write DW216. Upon plugging provided cable and drive into computer, the drive functioned as a plug and play device on Microsoft Surface laptop running Windows 11 64 bit. Device manager, file explorer, and media software functioned normally. Surprisingly, the drive functioned normally on computer battery alone.

Provided CyberLink Media Suite 12 disc did not auto run as Windows blocked installation requiring Administrator access even though I am the administrator for the computer. I used/mixed two suggestions found in these Amazon reviews to install the Suite. 1. In the search bar, I typed "command prompt" and then clicked "Run as Administrator" on the right side of window. 2. In the command prompt window, I typed "net user administrator /active:yes" (exactly - keeping the spaces in between words & symbols) and tapped enter. 3. The computer replied "The command completed successfully". 4. I determined the drive letter of the DW316 in file explorer. I right clicked on the drive and selected properties to see the drive letter. 5. In the command window, I typed the drive letter and a colon sign and tapped enter. 6. I typed "cd cms" and tapped enter. 7. I typed setup.exe and tapped enter. 8. From this point the software installation process started. 9. After installation, at the command prompt, I typed "net user administrator /active:no" and tapped enter which was followed by the message "The command completed successfully" to take the computer out of administrator access. Good luck.

I am building a pc, so I anticipate to go back to my old docking station for my work laptop and giving this one to my fiancé her desk. She puts far less stress on the docking station, so it works perfectly for her. I, however, am doing music and video production, development and gaming, along with other basic tasks along the way. title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
Gosh, where to even begin? I've been using Dell Monitors for over a decade now - regardless of what brand PC system I was using. I've always found Dell monitors to be a cut above, given what you spend.

Over the past week, one of the audio components that I had on a shelf directly above my previous Dell monitor, fell from the shelf, hit the table and bounced back into my Dell screen, smashing it - talk about a negative surprise. So I had to find a PC monitor quickly to replace it. Problem is that I needed a monitor whose height adjustment capabilities were a step above. So I called Dell, talked to a sales agent, who asked me what exactly I was looking for. I told him that my PC monitor needed to have substantial height (lowering and raising the monitor) capabilities.

After researching a variety of PC monitors, he recommended that I try the Dell S2425HS monitor, which had a height adjustment capability of 5"-6", which is phenomenal. You see, my monitor is sitting within a small nook space (height-wise), and I needed to have a monitor that would allow me to lower the screen substantially to fit into this space.

So I thanked him and immediately ordered it on Amazon - and it arrived the very next day. When it arrived, I was gratified to see the same care and packing of the monitor that Dell had always provided. Assembly was quick, and I was then surprised to discover that there were two 5-watt speakers (I don't know the actual size of the speakers) integrated inside the monitor.

After connecting everything and subsequently doing a color calibration of this new S2425HS (I do lots of photography, and I need an accurate monitor to process digital photos), I was gratified to then witness a wonderful-looking screen. As an aside, I also am an audiophile that maintains a desktop, near-field audio system around my PC. The gear used includes names such as KEF, Adcom, NAD, SMSL, and more - all providing me with a glorious audio experience while working.

And believe it or not, the biggest surprise for me - besides the excellent screen qualities of this new S2425HS - was the sound of these two 5 watt built-in speakers. In the settings menu on the monitor, you have the options to tune the sound of the integrated speakers for Movie, Music, Standard, Sports, and a few other modes. So I set mine to music, fully expecting these two little speakers to sound tinny and compressed due to their small size.

But boy was I surprised. The speakers had a fuller-bodied sound with excellent separation and an almost holographic sound quality while listening to a variety of materials. It is a good 5 steps above the typical built-in tiny speakers you get with some other monitors. This came as a welcomed treat because I periodically like to give my audiophile amps and associated electronics a rest. In fact, I was watching a band perform on YouTube just a few minutes ago, and for a second, I thought I was listening through my KEF speakers. Of course, when the bass section was performing, I realized then that I was listening to the PC monitor speakers because let's face it, those tiny speakers were limited with what they could do.

So all in all, I am absolutely delighted with this quality-made Dell S2425HS monitor. It provides superb screen and picture qualities, and also gives you the bonus of including two small, yet highly competent speakers that provide excellent sound qualities, despite their small size.

Highly recommended!

Excellent Balance of Style, Comfort, and Performance

I’ve been using the Dell S2425HS for a few weeks now, and it’s easily one of the best monitors in its class for everyday use—whether for work, casual gaming, or streaming.

🔍 Display Quality:
The 23.8-inch FHD (1920x1080) screen delivers crisp visuals and sharp text. Colors are vivid and accurate, with good contrast thanks to the 1500:1 ratio, which offers deeper blacks than most monitors at this price point. The 100Hz refresh rate is a nice bonus—noticeably smoother than 60Hz for everyday browsing, light gaming, and video playback.

👁️ Eye Comfort:
One standout feature is the TÜV Rheinland Eye Comfort 4 Star rating. I work long hours, and this monitor genuinely reduces eye fatigue. The low blue light tech and flicker-free screen make a noticeable difference during extended use.

🔊 Integrated Speakers:
The built-in 2x5W speakers are surprisingly good for a monitor. They're not meant to replace desktop speakers, but for video calls, YouTube, or light music listening, they’re more than adequate—clear, loud, and convenient.

🧭 Ergonomics & Design:
The height, tilt, swivel, and pivot adjustments are all smooth and solid. I love how easy it is to get the right angle. The Ash White finish gives it a sleek, modern look that fits beautifully in clean desk setups or minimalist environments. Cable management is also well-designed.

⚙️ Ports & Connectivity:
It has the essentials—HDMI and DisplayPort, plus a few USB options depending on your configuration. Easy plug-and-play with no driver issues.

Comfortable viewing experience

Sleek, modern white design

Versatile stand with full ergonomic adjustments

Good built-in speakers

🔴 Cons:
No USB-C input (would be great for modern laptops)

Final Verdict:
The Dell S2425HS hits a sweet spot for users who want a stylish, ergonomic, and eye-friendly monitor with solid performance. It’s not a high-end gaming or content creation monitor, but for general productivity, media consumption, and casual gaming, it's excellent. A strong value pick—especially with the enhanced comfort features and quality-of-life design.

text:
The Bluetooth mouse I use at work started to disconnect randomly. Cleaning, batteries, remove and reinstall... nothing fixed it. I looked around on Amazon and bought the Tecknet based on reviews. What a mistake! I wrote a review on that one. Terrible mouse. Avoid it. I didn't even waste my time to return it. It felt good to throw it in the trash.
I like Dell equipment. My work laptop is Dell. My gaming PC is Dell Alienware. Love them. So, I spent about 30% more on this Dell mouse and I love it. One AA battery so it is not heavy. Slightly beveled sides (wider on the top) so it's easy to pick up if needed. Very comfortable in the hand and is symmetrical so it's great for left handers too. I called it a wireless mouse because it works with an included USB dongle or with your native Bluetooth. The dongle stores inside if not used. Easy to set up - follow the instructions because there is an option to link to Bluetooth or the dongle. You can switch between the two, indicated on the bottom. The power switch is good. I only turn it off when it's in my backpack. On the desk, it sleeps and wakes seemlessly. The optical sensor on the bottom works onall surfaces and there is no red laser to blind you when you look for the switch. You can adjust the dots per inch sensitivity for your needs. This helps me for drawing sketches with the mouse. There are buttons. The usual left, middle, and right. The middle button is a wide scroll wheel, and it works as left and tight tilt, too. Two thumb buttons (for right hand use). All buttons are configurable through the provided application. I'm not using them for anything yet, but it's a nice option.
All-in-all I highly recommend this inexpensive wireless mouse for every day use. I have an expensive Alienware wired gaming mouse specificly for gaming use. But for work documentation, occasional CAD use, surfing the web, this is my new favorite. Dell MS5120W.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
Dell AC511 USB Wired SoundBar ... by Dell

IN THE BOX ... was the Dell AC511 USB wired SoundBAR, and a USB (male to Femaile) extender. The Dell AC511 is packaged in a heavy corregated box by the manufacturer and shipped inside a shipping box.

CONDITION AND OPERATION... is very good. The Dell AC511 is brand new and was designed to work with designated DELL monitors. Overlooking the design intent, I have used the DELL AC511 on my Dell 755 SFE and my Lenovo laptop. There is no power supply, the power is supplied through the USB cord. There is NO AUX JACK. Only the USB connection.
... The AC511 bypasses your sound card and you don't need any additonal software.
... If you dont have sound, look at your sound source in your computer. Should list the AC511 as a selection. True with Linux systems as well.
... If the sound is noisey, or scratchy, which may happen if plugged into the monitor, try a different USB port, try a port on the computer.
... The AC511 has head phone jacks on the side. If the jacks are noisy, try cleaning the jack and plug.
... The AC511 DOES NOT HAVE AN AUX JACK to plug in a MiniDisc player or MP3 player. Does not have that capability. Only USB input.
... The AC511 was designed to work on designated DELL monitors because DELL installed a USB port for the soundbar on the monitor. However, the AC511 does work on most computers with a USB port.

THE LAST WORD ... The Dell AC511 has a pretty good sound for a small-ish sound bar. It is a quality product and may be an answer for a computer with a bad sound card as the AC511 replaces that sound card. Sound control is from the volume control on the AC511 on the side and/or from the computer volume controls. The sound is rich and good quality. the only way you will get better sound is with separate speakers and then unless you add a sub woofer, you may not experience that big of a difference.
... For a laptop with those built in speakers or a computer that needs a set of speakers, this should work fine. All you need is a USB port.
I would recommend the DELL AC511 speaker sound bar.

EDIT 071518 There are on going reports of uncontrollable static after using these speakers for awhile and I did have this happen to mine. I actually shelved these speakers for awhile because I couldn't figure out how to stop the static noise that would randomly pop up.
BUT one day I was working on a computer and just plugged one of these in for the sound. It worked with no static, and it continued to work. The only difference was the USB cable was no where near a monitor or computer except for where it plugged in.
--- one suggested fix was to put tin foil over the speaker unit, I have tried this and had some good results. But I have now found that the USB cable is acting like an antenna and will recieve signals that can trigger the stattic noise.
--- I want to make one thing clear, these are rather good sounding speakers. They sound better than my replacements when the static noise made them useless. It would be a plus to be able to get these working again.
--- I have experiemented recently by shielding the speaker box with tin foil, or you can place them under a metal container, and keeping the cord away from the monitor and the computer, and especially away from any of the other cords from the monitor and computer. I have had good results, no static. There have been many complaints to DELL and they haven't found a fix other than discontinuing the speakers. But the sound is good enough that it is worth the extra trouble to shield them to keep any outside signals from triggering that static noise which obliterates any usable sound from the speakers. Of course, pulling and replacing the USB corrects this for the moment but it will come back.
--- If you still have yours, try some shielding, These were a good idea but some spurrious signals are mucking up the output.

I don't work for Dell or the seller and did not receive any monies or product for my random review

No vibrations are caused at all by the sound bar at all either. I have one thing to say off the bat as a negative - If you call it that. I have a couple Side-By-Side monitors as shown in the photo above where I was able to place a wired Logitech USB mouse on the plastic pedestal from the monitor. I have nothing bad to say at all about these speakers. They are great looking, connect easily to the monitor itself and the cable connection is straight forward with a simple USB connection. Dell has another couple models of soundbars that have more features and may sound a bit better - I say them while shopping amazon. One of their newer ones (the Dell Pro Stereo Soundbar AE515M) had video conferencing buttons and a good mic as well but I just picked up 4 of these bad boys because I already chose a webcam with a mic on it. But, one of these days if I upgrade to a 4K monitor of larger than 24", I'm going to throw down a few bills and get the Dell Pro Stereo Soundbar AE515M for sure! For now, I'm happy with the sound quality, the looks, and the simplicity of them.

Dell has some nice monitors and their newer soundbars are supposed to be able to mount on the underside of the monitor or the pedestal arm so that's nice. Pick some of these up if your looking for good quality sound.

text:
Recently my 15 year old PC monitor with inbuilt speakers died on me. Had to get a replacement, but found that the ones with speakers were either way too big, or too expensive. I decided to get a reasonably priced one minus speakers and use a soundbar instead. Found this Dell AC511 , read the reviews and did the usual bit of research before purchasing. I have to say, its performance for the price is very, very good. However, I have to admit that I have had it unboxed, just sitting there for about a week because although I am fairly computer savvy, the instructions for setting it up were not the best, and reading through all the Amazon Q & A's, I found so many varying suggestions on connecting it - I honestly was not sure whether it connected to my monitor, or the PC, or both!! Today I decided to connect it how I thought best, because after all, this is a plug & play device. For anyone contemplating buying this soundbar, and like me, are not sure how it will connect and work, here is how I did it - absolutely simple.
It comes with a reasonably long USB lead. Put the USB into a vacant port on the back of your computer whilst it (and the monitor) is on - I have an HP desktop running Windows 7 Pro, but I am sure it will work the same with any usual operating system
Windows recognised it immediately and installed the driver.
Next, go into Start/Control panel/Hardware & Sound. At the bottom of the list you will see the Soundbar called "SRS Audio Control"
To adjust sound to where you want it to be (bass/mixer etc), click on the "SRS Audio Control" and all the settings are there relating to the device. Just adjust with the slider buttons.
You can adjust the sound via the knob on the right hand side of the bar, or via your speakers icon on your PC taskbar.
How simple is that? No configurations required, no A to B cable, no additional USB cables - just the attached USB cable the soundbar comes with.
I tested the sound with a Youtube video recording of music to get the sound I wanted, and it was excellent. Good bass - no tinniness, or distortion even when I had the speakers up louder than I would use. I found even at about 38% it was quite comfortably loud enough.
Looks unobtrusive and sleek - and most of all - absolutely does the job. You could, if you wish, pay a few hundred pounds for one, but in all honesty I am more than happy with this to say the least. Excellent piece of kit.
Arrived very quickly, and well packaged - all credit due to the Seller.
If you cannot attach it to your monitor, it will look just as smart placed in front of it at desk level (put a bit of bluetack underneath to keep it secure)
So glad I did not bother with another inbuilt speaker monitor after all - never could get such a great sound as this . produces!!

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
I was hesitant to buy this speaker for my Dell U2415 monitor based on so many reviews that said it didn't work as advertised (i.e. that it needed both a USB connection for power as well as an aux cable for the sound signal "THAT ISN'T EVEN INCLUDED!!!). Some folks even said that it didn't work with both a USB and aux cable connected.
But I wanted a speaker that wouldn't take up any space on my desk and I don't need disco club volume nor thumping base, so I went for it. I figured worst case I'd need to use an aux cable (or worst worst-case it wouldn't work for me at all and I have to return it, but hey, returning stuff is one of Amazon's strengths, right?)
So anyway it delivered next day after ordering (the joys of living in a metropolitan area!), I pulled it out of the box and connected the speaker's USB cable into one of the monitor's USB hub outlets and voila, sound was coming out of the speaker even before Skype and all of the other annoying Microsoft bloat-ware had finished starting up after I powered my computer on. Absolutely no setup of any sort required from me on the computer side of things. See the attached picture to this review for how the computer shows the speaker in the audio output section after all is said and done. So easy and I'm running Windows 8 on this machine, for Pete's Sake!

Which leads me to wonder; do people not realize that if you plug this speaker's USB plug into one of the monitor's USB ports that the monitor itself has to ALSO be connected to the computer independently via its own USB cord?
Even if you don't have your monitor hub connected (or don't have a monitor hub at all), the attached USB plug on the speaker has quite a long cord so hypothetically it would easily plug directly into the computer itself. I haven't tried that, but am absolutely confident it would work just fine. Even better, theoretically, since plugging the speaker into the monitor USB port instead of the computer's means the audio has the extra complexity of going through the USB hub in the monitor. Not that I've noticed any problems at all with that but I suppose if you were doing high data-rate transfers through the hub the sound could take a hit because of it.

Sound is perfectly fine, even great, for the size and price of this thing. Again, I don't need disco club volume nor thumping base nor battlefield realistic sound for my application so you may feel differently.
Actually I had to lower the speaker, computer, and music app volumes all down to the lower ends of their respective sliders while playing some test tracks since my kid's bedroom is right next to my "office" and the sound output was pretty significant when I first plugged it in.

My U2415 has two slots in the bottom of it that were covered up with some glorified tape pieces. Once I pulled the tape off with a mini-screwdriver the two tabs on top of the speaker slotted right into the monitor slots and it looks just like one of the photos Amazon has posted for this item.

If you go to Dell's page for this speaker, click on the "Tech Specs" tab, and scroll down to "Compatibility" you'll see a long list of Dell monitors this speaker is designed to work with. I'd guesstimate 2 out of 3 or maybe even 4 out of 5 in that list don't need the included monitor stand mount (the list differentiates which do or don't). Mine was one of those that don't so I can't speak to people's issues with the monitor stand mount, but I'm wondering if their monitor is even on that list at all.

text:
I got this for a desktop computer I was building and added it under my Dell monitor. I use it for conference calls, not for music. It plays music just fine and plenty loud but it is a soundbar. Simple USB cable was plug and play with Windows 10. Zoom, MS Teams, etc... all recognize it. It is small and discreet but the buttons are big enough for you to find and press with ease. Check the compatible Dell monitor stands but it attached with ease to mine.

Sounds: Voices are loud and clear for calls. The soundbar has volume adjust buttons which increase or decrease the Windows volume control. The sound is a bit deeper and richer than you get from typical "tinny" sounding PC speakers. I have not run into any issues with audio.

Mic: This unit has an integrated far-field microphone. I typically sit 2-4 feet from the microphone and it picks my voice up well. Feedback has been that I sound clear on calls. There is a mute button on the soundbar, in addition to buttons for answer and hang-up, which could be handy in certain circumstances. The microphone on this soundbar is far better than the integrated mic on my USB camera. However, I would say it's generally of average sound capture quality. I have had no issues with it and it is sufficient for hours of daily conference calls.

I have attached pictures of the front view under monitor and the rear view of the mounting adapter.

I purchased this because it had an integrated microphone. I believe that is the key feature to choose this soundbar over all other alternatives available. The second feature would be mounting compatibility with Dell monitors. The third feature would be the inclusion of front mounted buttons for volume, mute, and call handling if someone were looking for a setup without easy access to a keyboard or mouse (i.e. distributed setup or TV display as a conferencing interface).

This is the 2nd mount of this type I've purchased. The JUGGHOME Mini PC Wall Mount is very similar to my other mount with 3 main exceptions.

I like to attach that mount to the side of my bookshelf with the prongs facing up so I can use these as stoppers for leaning my keyboard against the shelf.

Sometimes the receptables are recessed on the back of TVs so the longer screws are needed.

Overall it's a decent mount for anyone looking to mount an Optiplex Micro, although if you decide to mount it someplace where it's not normally visible such as under a desk or table, I'd highly suggest a product from another vendor. title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
I have an HP EliteDesk 800 G5 SFF running on Windows 11 and noticed my 3 DELL 32" LCDs sometimes flicker and reset (black screen). I also noticed maxed GPU utilization on the task manager. There are 3 built-in Motherboard display ports for this SFF PC; 2x DP and 1x HDMI. I have to use passive/active HDMI adapters as my Dell LCD's only connection is via HDMI and VGA (no longer using VGA, all HD). So I determined that the best course of action to remedy this issue is to purchase a PCIeX GPU and I decided to try this Glorto Universal Graphics Card (Glorto GeForce GT 730 4Gb, 2x HDMI, 1x DP, and 1x VGA). The reason I picked this product is I needed a GPU card that would work on SFF and at the same time does not require a power supply wattage upgrade (current power supply cannot exceed 250 watts).

Install:

To properly install this graphics adapter on my PC, I had to remove the existing faceplate and the VGA port to fit in the SFF chassis. The product came with a faceplate bracket for the HDMI and DP ports. I installed the card in the PCIeXP X16 (black) slot to maximize efficiency since high-performance devices tend to rely on PCIe x26 almost exclusively. I had to use a combination of different HD cables as the DELL HDMI cables won't fit in the slots as they have wider heads.

Once all install tasks were completed, I powered on the PC and it only detected 1 display monitor so I logged in and proceeded to the next steps.

Setup/Config of new GPU card:

Having only 1 display active, I checked the display adapter under the device manager and it showed "Standard Windows Display". Right-click on it and update the driver using Windows Update. The WU automatically detected the chip and installed the appropriate driver (NVIDIA). Right after the update, the 2 remaining displays turned ON and all my desktop icon settings were back to NORMAL!

Device Manager shows "NVIDIA Display Adapter" and Task Manager shows GPU information and utilization.

Summary:

I don't play a lot of OL games purely work-related and multi-tasking kinds of stuff. I am hoping this GPU card will prove itself worthy of its reputation and last longer.

Overall, I am satisfied with my purchase of this Glorto GPU card. It has met my requirements and solved my built-in graphics card issue.

UPDATE: Does fit!
So after actually having mounted the bracket under my desk, the locking nut actually worked! Okay, it was a bit tight, but it's now connected. So the metal, after having been mounted, must have just gotten shape/moved back in its intended shape. The only down side is, I don't give minus points for this, the computer is only fixed in the bracket at one side. Meaning when I pull out a usb peripheral or a USB stick from the front, the computer moves a bit in the frame, as it is only hold in place on the far right side.

--- original review ---
Nice bracket, but doesn't quite fit at least on one point. Let me explain.
My Dell USFF OptiPlex 7040 fits nicely in the bracket, but the locking nut at the back, used to fix the computer to the bracket doesn't fit. Meaning there is a little metal flap that stick out with a slotted hole, however when I wanted to screw the locking nut (part of this set) it turned out the slotted hole should have been 90 degrees rotated. It was elongated in exactly the wrong direction. Result: the screw didn't fit and I haven't installed it yet. Simple solution is to use some power tool and expand the hole, but you'd have to be careful not making it too big so it would hold the nut any more. (Of course you can also file the hole bigger by hand.)
Another point is the bracket arrived and it was bent. Now the metal isn't super thick, thick enough for sure, but at the same time bendable to get it back in shape. Not sure if it was packaged like this, or happened during transport. (No visible damage on the packaging.) Note: I did double check for the locking nut issue, but I didn't have anything to do with the bracket being bent open a bit.
Simple solution: just gently squeeze it back in shape. Simple and has no adverse effects of any kind.
I'm going to mount this to the bottom of my desk, but I did check the VESA mount:
Took off the back cover of my Dell 27" screen and the VESA holes are perfectly aligned. I don't expect any problems should you choose that mounting option.

This could have been such a cool thing, but the design is just terrible.

For this to work with a Dell micro, you must mount the machine upside down (with the ventilation openings directly against the shelf). How stupid is that? And the mounting tray has only a few small vents, so you are essentially giving up maybe 90% of the units ventilation.

Also, in case you missed it in the pictures, the hinges on this thing are screwed down on each side. So if you're in front of the rack and you'd like access to the back of the computer, you will have to unscrew both screws on one side. Why not make one side snap in and out? Then rear access would be really easy. As it is, it's not convenient at all.

So yeah, I'll be returning this. You're way better off just velcro-ing your micro to a 1u shelf. That would give you much easier access, and it won't obstruct the vents.

title: 3.0 out of 5 stars
text:
Purchased as a used-like new DVD-RW device from Amazon, the drive arrived bent and not able to eject the disc tray. An hour's careful bending of the very flimsy sheet metal typical of these 9.5 mm thick drives, adjustment of the ejection latch, and repeated installation - removal from a desktop tower, yielded a unit both physically and electrically "up to snuff". The drive plays back and records as expected.

This drive arrived with the front bezel left retaining tang (plastic) broken off, and the right tang bent through failure. The front bezel flopped free during first installation of the drive. The bezel is now super-glued in place, AFTER the required sheet metal and ejection latch repair.

This CD / DVD-RW unit is identified by Windows 10 Device Manager (from the drive firmware) as HL-DT-ST DVD-RW GU70N, a Hitachi-LG Data Storage device. The name "OSGEAR appears nowhere except on the wholly inadequate zip-lock bag in which the drive was packed, and in Amazon's advertising.

All-in-all, a perfectly usable DVD-RW drive for a pittance in cost, but requiring judicious repair by the buyer to be made usable.

title: 3.0 out of 5 stars
text:
This mount fits very loosely; to the point that I’m not sure that I feel that my computer is secure in it. The computer is held in by a single screw, against a flexible bit of metal. I can easily see that bit of metal breaking under stress from repeated use (repositioning monitor, mounting/unmounting computer, etc.) and dropping a computer straight on the floor.

There’s a lot of space in the mount for the computer to rattle around in. So much so that it seems it was built for a slightly larger computer. However, I double checked that it is indeed intended for my computer (A Dell Optiplex 3080 MFF).

If you do use this mount, make absolutely sure that the computer is horizontal. Either upside-down and parallel to the floor in the under-desk configuration, or parallel to the wall with the front of the computer to the left, and the rear to the right. These are the orientations in which the computer is most well supported.

In any other configuration, *all* of the computer's weight is supported by a single, 1 cm² bit of metal.

This would be greatly improved with:
- Slightly tighter tolerances, and some padding, so that the mount actually grasps the sides of the computer.
- A bit more support; e.g. one or more of
- Another metal tab on the opposite side to support some of the weight and prevent sagging
- A bar or lip across the back
- Perhaps something that would interface with the Kensington slot in the rear of the computer

I was hoping that a metal mount would be an upgrade for me, but I think 3d-printing a plastic mount is a better option at this point.

text: This is a great product. I use them for USB-C cellphones and tablets. It is a higher amp transformer with a data line that communicates with devices that use USB-C and have fast charge capability. It has 3 wires. A hot, a ground for power to charge and a data cable which the device uses ti command the power supply transistors to decide whether your device is warm and only needs a volts for standard charge, or whether the device is cool enough to take 9 volts fast charge. It is much more dependable than any phone charger and with a higher amp/watt transformer, will take a load without slowing itself down to prevent damage. A standard cell phone charger will get hot fast in the car or home and slow down sometimes when tge phone is okay, but the charger is overworked. You of course can get these devices in a 12 volt car charger too that is for any laptop that is USB-C. I have tested many different watt units and for android devices, I prefer from 65 watt to 100 watt. The 130 watt or above is too much and while it likely won't hurt the device, it will often shit down to prevent damage. 130 watt is good for a laptop or starling. The 12 volt car charger is the same about watts. I never have a problem with the phones and don't use anything, but these. It also has an advantage in the fact that it doesn't have the open connection from the block to the cable I the middle, leaving the very common drain in the middle. Don't just get them for your laptop. Try one on your android. They're cheap compared to a block charger and much much better. Sometimes the block charger will show a faster charge at first and after a little, gets overwhelmed and slows down. These transforms are more powerful and doesn't fail you.

text:
I have been involved in the homelab scene for about a year and a half now and took the plunge to get my own small 19in network rack to mount some of my nodes. One of the items I intend to mount in my system is a 13th gen Dell OptiPlex mini pc. I could have put it on a basic rack or even placed it on top, but neatness counts for me, so a dedicated mount was in order so I ordered this little beauty.

First, the quality of the sheet metal used in construction is great, not thin, not unnecessarily heavy. Next, the instructions are clear and concise. The mounting hardware including cage nuts and bolts are included. Moreover, a thumbscrew to affix to the Optiplex itself is also included. Straps for the power supply are also included with the kit.

The bonus I mentioned with this mount is the unique hinged setup that adds a heap of functionality to the setup. Simply remove either the left or right set of bolts, and a hinge on either side allows the shelf to swing out so that you can access the pc to work on it, add peripherals, clean, etc. This is a really convenient design since rack space is precious and access can be difficult. Not having to remove cage nuts and place your fingers and hands in places with raw metal edges is wonderful.

The Optiplex fits in this mount well. While designed for the Dell Optiplex, other mini pc's might fit in this if they share the 1L form factor, but do consult the dimensions of your particular model. Also note that the thumb screw is designed to hold the Optiplex precisely and it may not line up with other pc manufacturers. That said the shelf has more space than it needs for the Optiplex. I plan to try to place a single board computer on the same shelf that is running other services. As such, given the flexibility this mount adds, it's a great value for money and well worth consideration if you're getting serious with your home lab or running services on one of Dell's mini pc's.

title: 4.0 out of 5 stars
text:
the center flap/divider and compartment oppo the PC cavity are okay in function, but design is lacking, IMO.

The zippered mesh bag area is okay, but would be better served as a couple of molded cavities, or even an open area with a hook-n-loop tabbed divider so one could better keep/carry/access any additional cables and cords, or perhaps a mouse/trackball. A wide open bag ends up being too generic, and is easy to overstuff, or stuff lumpy.

The divider to that same mesh bag side is bunch of tiny pockets, whereas when I looked (not closely enough I suppose) at the item online before purchase, thought instead of pockets they were elastic-y bands that were specifically for cable/cord management.
6 pouches, that don't have any closures other than the thin bands at the top of each pouch, don't really have a good use in the form here.

Stuff that goes in too easily comes out, and again, I believe having stretchy bands without the pouches would go much farther in affording some storage versatility.

Case isn't internally hardshelled, either, and I feel like, for the purpose of carrying a micro client PC and (presumably) associated hardware and cabling, more structural rigidity would be beneficial.

Did I expect this to be like a Pelican case – no, and it remains to be seen if/how well any impact will get absorbed or deflected by this case's construction.

It's a bit pricey, too, but then my mate nudges me from time to time to remind me that EVERYTHING is pricey in our current world. Welcome to Earth, eh?

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
This is one of many reconditioned products I have purchased from Amazon. And this desktop computer is outstanding.

I did run into a couple of issues setting it up. So let me fill you in. First thing, there are 3 wireless USB adapters that must be plugged into the back of the tower. One for the wireless ability for the tower, one for the mouse and one for the keyboard. I found the wireless adapter for the mouse inside the battery compartment.

The next issue I ran into is the keyboard was defective. It took some time for me to figure that problem out. My monitor screen, on whatever website I was on, kept flickering with a yellow cursor box everywhere. It acted like a virus was in the computer. Yet, thanks to Gemini, he helped me diagnose the issue. A defective keyboard really didn't matter to me, I had all the parts I needed to hook up two towers to one keyboard, one mouse and one monitor.

The photo on Amazon's description of the rear of the tower is not accurate. I have attached a photo so you can see the rear. Just know that the output for a monitor is a display port. So, I had to order an adapter that converted display port to HDMI. This is a very inexpensive part that works great.

My current desktop is Windows 7. I have had this tower since Windows 7 was released. So changing to a Windows 11 tower was frighting to me. Well, let me tell you this. Windows 11 is awesome. Very intuitive and takes some time to get to where want to go. Mainly because it looks nothing like Windows 7. I found the best thing for me was to PIN the most used features along the bottom of the toolbar. The setup was super easy. Although when it wants you to choose a PIN number for Microsoft, that number is the lock code number you enter every time to open your desktop . DON'T FORGET THIS NUMBER!

Last thing, this is a full size tower. Not a compact. Full size!

It works great, and it is super fast. I hope this information helps. Enjoy, this computer is worth every penny, I absolutely recommend it 👌.

Everything listed online was included and like all the other reviews, the mouse and keyboard are so cheap they probably shouldn't be included...lol. I used VGA but had a HDMI adapter cord/unit that I could have used also. If you've been using Windows 10, Windows 11 is a snap to figure out. Actually you shouldn't have any problems coming from any of the older Windows systems either...11 is very intuitive. The only negatives were the frustration with not being able to connect my HP laser mf277 printer and the sluggish performance in the morning from waking up from sleep mode. title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
What I needed:
I needed a computer for my electronics lab. It didn't need to be immensely powerful, but I wanted something that would be easy to expand as needed. This PC met my needs almost perfectly, and at a very economical price. I purchased this 6 months ago (almost to the day), so this is not an "out of the box" impression, but one based on months of experience. It has been powered on (or sleeping) continuously, so I can remote access it when needed.

My uses are primarily centered around my lab work: Electronic Design, PCB Layout, and 3D Rendering of PCBs, along with Design of small enclosures and modest software development. I also have several PC connected pieces of bench equipment: Digital Scope, Power Supplies, Function Generator, and whatever thing I'm creating. Most of these connect via USB, and one via RS-232.

This PC:
You can see in the pictures that the front panel has 4 USB ports - 2 are SuperSpeed. These have already proven valuable for quick attachments.

The rear panel is loaded up with 6 more USB ports (2 of which are SuperSpeed), and I've used most of them. If I had to, I could easily dig out an old PS2 Keyboard to free up another USB port - but with 4 empty ports on the front I'm ok for now.

As noted above, I needed RS-232, and this PC had one - which is a bonus. Of course, I could have plugged in a USB to RS-232 adapter. Beneath the back-panel RS-232 port (the gray plug in the picture) is a VGA connector, which I don't expect to use. To the left of those are a couple of Display Ports - one connected to my big screen (3440 x 1440). The specs say that each can support a 4K monitor, but my bench doesn't have space (and the screen resolution works for my eyeballs and needs).

The host processor in the unit I purchased is an i5-4590 quad core running at 3.3 GHz. The motherboard memory slots are full, loaded with 16 GB of RAM. The motherboard has 3 SATA ports, but they are fully occupied, connected to a 240 GB SSD hosting Win10 Pro, a 1GB spinning HDD, and a DVD drive. The graphics is served with an integrated Intel HD 4600. For further expansion, there are 4 PCIe slots: 2 x X1, 1 x X4 and 1 x X16.

Other Discoveries:
* The BIOS still had the name of the prior "owner" (a company), which is probably where many of these came from. It was simple to change, so now is hosts a name appropriate for my lab.
* This PC is not for gaming, so I didn't rate that since I've never run a game on it. With my single high-resolution monitor connected, spinning a 3D model of a modestly complex circuit board is fast - it more than meets my needs.
* And I had no need for Tech Support, so I didn't rate that either.

My Expansion:
* In the pictures you'll see one of the PCI slots is occupied - with the 4-channel SATA adapter that I added. The 3 on the motherboard were occupied but I needed one more for an external HD dock.
* I expect to add a Webcam soon.
* I also expect to add one more PCI card to it, to add USB-C connectors. My newest gear (Laptop, Phone, etc.) all have USB-C, so this will be necessary.

My Summary:
This was the right PC for my needs. It was also relatively inexpensive. It has been running close to non-stop since my unboxing. It "seems" quiet enough for most any location, but my lab isn't the best place to judge that.

It didn't have support for every interface I needed but was more than expandable enough to add to it. I do wish the overall unit was a bit smaller (for my lab space), and in years prior I had a large tower PC, but tired of crawling under the desk to swap cables around.

Inside, not a speck of dust, literally, like a new computer, you can't tell that it's renewed/upgraded.

Even though it's smaller everything is easy to see and get to so if you need or want to do anything inside it's awesome. You can see everything and get to it with ease. You don't have to be a contortionist or have tiny hands and fingers. The drives and optical reader (DVD) are contained within a rack that you just pivot upward to release and you have full easy access to them. Additional expansion slots to add what you like. If you should want to increase RAM from 16 to 32 GB there is nothing around them so removing and replacing them in the slots would be effortless. I was surprised how cool this computer runs even when using multiple high resource software at the same time with no lag.

As for the USB Keyboard and Mouse, USB WiFi Adapter. These are low cost and just so you have something. As low cost as keyboard and mouse are I really like them. If you use something else don't throw them out as others have said. Save them as an emergency back up or give them to someone. I have a Logitech wireless keyboard and mouse but still using the ones that came with this computer. USB WiFi Adapter isn't the best it's not real fast and not great for long-distance so I did buy a better one at the same time. There are a lot of cheap USB WiFi Adapters that stop working after 2-3 months but here is a low-cost $17 good one I use so can avoid the hassle.
Just search amazon for -
TP-Link AC600 USB WiFi Adapter for PC (Archer T2U Plus)- Wireless Network Adapter for Desktop with 2.4GHz, 5GHz High Gain Dual Band 5dBi Antenna, Supports Windows 10/8.1/8/7/XP, Mac OS 10.9-10.14
It increased my transfer speed from 300 Mbps or less and 3 bars signal strength to a transfer speed of 433 to 490 Mbps and 5 bars signal strength.

All you have to do is connect a monitor, the keyboard, mouse, and USB wifi adapter and power up. You do need to set up you user account like any new computer. This is Microsoft so it wants you to use a Microsoft account to have a better "online experience". But all you need to do is enter your login for a Microsoft email account or create one during set up. That step requires connecting to the internet and entering the password. Or you can create an offline user account like the old days. The rest of the setup questions are about your preferences and you're ready to go.

Windows 10 Pro works perfectly. My daughter got one of these a while ago and wouldn't stop praising it so I got one. She gave me a heads up about the USB WiFi Adapter solution too. I couldn't be happier with this purchase.

This was my first time ordering a renewed PC and I took a leap of faith-- given my outstanding, years-long experiences buying from Amazon as well as the 90-day $$ back guarantee -- and ordered this HP ProDesk. Took it over to his house yesterday and set it up for him--WAHWAHWEEEWAH, I was blown away by how nice it was, especially for the price. It looked brand new. I had ordered a separate 27" monitor (will review that as well). Unboxing everything and setting it up took probably 15-20 minutes and consisted of mostly plugging in cables and cords. Although I still gave it 5 stars, it wasn't all peachy, however, so please be aware of the following: 1. The power cord is really short-- I think it was 24"? (I wish I had measured it), and we had to move his desk a significant distance to be closer to the wall outlet -- okay, an extension cord would have helped but stepdad just didn't have one on hand. 2. There was no HDMI port to connect the monitor to the computer -- we tried every port on the PC, to no avail. We figured out that the only way to connect monitor to PC was through a VGA cord-- not included with either the monitor or the PC. This necessitated a run to Best Buy where thankfully they had such a cord (you guys are the best!), $14.99 and yes, it worked perfectly. When that monitor screen lit up and displayed the Windows logo we both let out a whoop of joy, that's how good it looked. I went ahead and set up the starting questions for him and we connected the PC with the ethernet cable to his router (or was it the modem? not sure, but it worked) and he was in business. Absolutely fabulous, despite the 2 snafus we encountered with the short power cord and the lack of HDMI port on PC. Totally worth it, and I'm even considering chucking my old PC here at home -- which I purchased new, cost over $1000-- and "upgrading" to a computer exactly like this one. On an amusing side note-- the box that the computer came in is the perfect size for an adult cat to sleep in. As soon as I took the PC out and into the home office, within 5 minutes, Fluffy was in that box sound asleep, on top of the packing materials. Highly recommend this product! Even if you don't have a cat! :)

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
If this PC matches your needs, it is an excellent buy.
Comments:
It has two expansion slots, one short, one full. Both PCIe. (The current picture shows four expansion slots. This is an error, it has two.)
It has room for two SATA SSDs (it comes with one, 1TB SSD.). I read somewhere that the max size is 2 TB, so the max internal storage would be 4 TB. If you add a second drive, you'll need a SATA data cable and a SATA power splitter (1 to 2) and a mounting bracket (The bay is for a 3.5" drive, most SATA drives are 2.5".)

The literature says it comes with five USB-3 and four USB-2 ports. All 9 ports are colored black. Normally USB-3 is colored blue. Based on the exposed pins inside of the ports, the four in front are USB-2, and the 5 in back are USB-3.1 (AFAICT.) USB 3.1 gen 1 supports transfer speeds of up to 5 Gbps. USB 3.1 gen 2 supports transfer speeds of up to 10 Gbps. As I read the spec I think it has gen 1 (5 Gbps.)

It comes with two display ports. If your monitor only has HDMI inputs, you will need an adapter. It also has VGA output.

I got the 32 GB memory version -- it is very fast. I would recommend also getting the insurance for any renewed item.

If you need more storage, use a USB drive. If you want it fast, use USB 3.2 gen 2x2 (20 Gbps.) You can also get a larger capacity drive (~20TB). For Gen 3.2 2x2 you'll need to use the short expansion slot for a USB 3.2 gen 2x2 card. Use the Small Form Factor (SFF) size. Usually a SFF USB card supports 2 drives.

Windows S Mode dose not allow you to install and run any app that is not Microsoft verified and found on the Microsoft Store. In S Mode, you cannot install and run any browser other than MS Edge or Bing. I finally got MS Support on the phone and they told me this is a very common problem with this product and the only way to resolve it was to reset the PC. A total reset, wiping the OS and all files you may have added. No big deal as this is a new PC and I did not transfer anything from my old PC. After the PC was reset, I was able to switch out of S mode so that I now have Win 11 Home instead of Win 11S Home. title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
I live in a more remote location where most bargain places (recyclers, etc) won't ship at all, or want crazy $$ to ship. So this review is partially based on my limited choices... but I like this machine enough that I'd probably buy it anyway. This is perfect for the general office use I need it for.

First of all, the one I have up on my workbench now is exactly as the ad says. CPU, RAM, SSD are all correct, and test OK. Also, the machine is a lot newer than I expected. This one has a "born on" date of May 16, 2021. Based on the CPU, I was thinking it'd be a bit older.

The inside looks very very clean. Almost immaculate. The ad does not specify an optical media drive but the chassis can accommodate a slim (laptop size) drive, if you want to add one.

The shipping box was a simple affair with very strong inflated padding inside. I suggest they use a bit more tape, but the box arrived ok. Inside, there was the PC, plus power cable, USB adapters for WiFi and BT, Keyboard and Mouse, and an adapter for DP to HDMI. Really a thoughtful combination. Just make sure to look through the entire box, as these items are loose. [A small baggy for these, taped to the machine would be good idea]

Before trying to power on, I opened the case to make sure RAM wasn't jostled loose during transit or the CPU cooler hadn't come off somehow. All was fine. On powering up, my machine sputtered a bit (on/off itself a couple times) and complained about a loss of date/time. This is normal for when the CMOS battery is too low/dead. I switched it out for a good battery and all works well. (This may be frustrating for some buyers, but if you leave the machine plugged in, it won't need the battery anyway until there's a power outage)

I'm ordering 2 more and will probably order more later on too. It's a 5-star product. Maybe a wee tiny bit expensive for big metro areas, but a great deal for me where I am.

EDIT: I've now ordered quite a few of these, and the price is better than ever. Some had SSD (SATA) and some NVMe. One had an optical drive. There's a relatively recent BIOS update too. I believe this vendor is merely following the correct MS **requirements** for selling refurbished machines which generally requires putting the original OS version back in it's initial state for a new user, and must include a kyb/mouse.

title: 4.0 out of 5 stars
text:
Long read, so to summarize: Everything as described was included. Booted up just fine with Windows 10 Pro. Included mouse and keyboard, a USB WiFi dongle, a DC adapter, and a separate power cable. Was a little dusty inside. Had one 16 GB stick of RAM Samsung brand. Looks like there was a WiFi card at one point, which was removed. Appears that the rear antenna external part was removed and the wire was cut, leaving a cut piece of wire laying around under the motherboard. The front side antenna was left there. Value for money was good. Detailed post below.

Everything as described in the description was provided and nothing was missing. The model I purchased did not include WiFi and Bluetooth (which I knew), but I did purchase a WiFi card and a set of antennas separate to install myself. They did include a USB WiFi dongle, which was not the best performing one, but it worked. Also included was a mouse and keyboard set, a DC adapter, and a separate power cable.

Before I did anything to this machine, I did make sure it booted and it booted up just fine and Windows 10 Pro was installed and activated. So no issues with booting up. No bloatware or anything as well which was great. After powering off, and inspecting the back, I noticed in one of the holes there was a cut wire nearly sticking out the hole and I had no idea what it was. I tried to pull it out thinking it was just a small piece of wire but couldn't. More on this later on.

When I took this apart, there was a noticeable bit of dust inside which I just cleaned with some compressed air. The CPU cooler fan was clean though as well as the heat sink. There was single 16 GB stick of RAM that I later changed to two identical 8 GB sticks. The thermal paste was still new and good, but I replaced it anyways before putting this back together.

Now the interesting part, there were antennas already installed so it looks like there may have been a WiFi card at some point. The wire going to the front was still intact, but the wire going to the back appears to have been cut. On this machine, the rear antenna has a little piece that protrudes the rear side about 1/4 an inch out and snaps on to the back. It looks like that someone removed that external piece and instead of removing the whole antenna, they simply cut the wire connecting to that piece. This resulted in a piece of cut wire just laying around under the motherboard which in my opinion is very sloppy and some additional care could have gone to proper removal of this. I also don't like having lose wires hanging around inside machines since they may cause damage if they come into contact with any conductive parts. I attached an image showing the cut wire. May not be on the seller, but I think as a refurbished machine seller some time should go into inspecting the machines for things like this (especially since that cut wire was one of the first things I noticed before even taking it apart). Anyways, the antennas were replaced and a new card installed and connected.

After putting it all back together, restarted the machine and the WiFi is significantly better. Other than that, everything else worked great as they did before I took the machine apart.

text:
I bought this months ago, but amazon showed it in my history and I had not written a review for a product(s) I like and use daily. But as a 30 year IT person, I often have needs to find cheap PCs either for clients or myself at home.

Earlier this year I was in the market for a miniPC, as I wanted to use it as a server for my home network (running linux). Its me, so I didn't want to spend a ton of money, but wanted something decent, that I could upgrade. I'm familiar with this product line, as these are business grade computers, so I've used this specific model at companies (when these were new). In short, HP G-series PCs are pretty reliable, and last longer than their home ones. So no surprise they are for sale as refurbished on here.

I was comparing a Dell of similar spec to this one, but this one just won out for price point for what I was getting. I liked them so much, I bought two of them. One for the server, and one to use as spare testing Windows machine that didn't take up a ton of space (and wasn't a laptop).

Full Disclosure, I added a 500GB SSD NVMe M.2 drive as the boot drive, so your results may vary in terms of speed. But I will say, it was speedy with the stock drive that came with it (see below)

Here's what I liked..

- First off, who it came from. I was pleasantly surprised that the Amazon Certified Reseller that this came from (as the box said) is a company I know from my IT experience for decades. While they are a business2business company, many HP (and Dell) PCs I bought over the years, came from this company. So I know they know what they are doing. However, I can't say yours will come from this place, but have hopes that others are as high calibre as this one since they would be Amazon-certified also.

- This thing is small, its no bigger than a standard mouse pad.
- It's very clean, it almost looked new. No dents, scratches, or dings. The inside was spotless and the CPU had been remounted with fresh paste!
- Its powerful. I've done some hard video encoding and testing, and it just purrs along, and this was still with the included 500GB drive!
- It's quiet, unless I'm chewing the processor up with something the fans spin up. But even then it is not as loud as my desktop workstation (an HP also!).
- It's an energy sipper. I connected a power meter to it for a month, it used so little power (vs my desktop)
- Processor speed is pretty speedy and windows preinstall is pretty zippy on it
- This model has 16GB of ram which is plenty of ram these days for most applications
- Two drive support. This can take 2 drives, a 2.5" SATA drive & a NVMe M.2 2280 drive (just add a screw!)
- Plenty of USB 3.0 , 2 USB Type A (flat plug) and 1 USB-C in the front and 4 USB Type A ports in the back
- 2 Displayport ports for dual monitor support and a VGA port
- Onboard 10/100 ethernet & audio
- This specific renewed model comes with a Windows 10 Pro license! (some do not!)
- If you're security minded, this does come with TMP 1.0 and other UEFI related security tools.
- Since this is an HP Business PC, spare parts and support are easy to find and locate. Everything is HP standard, well tested, and made for years of reliability.

Here's what I thought was "meh"

- Because its tiny, the power supply is a brick on a cord. Not a big deal and the cord from the brick to the PC is long, but the brick itself has to be put somewhere vs a straight cord.
- This model does not come with WiFi or the antenna kit. The MiniPCIe slot exists though so Wifi can be added later and it's not a show stopper for me as these will be hard wired.

Here's what I didn't like..

None. I do not have any huge things I do not like about this product, other than my meh. I'm extremely pleased with this product!

Overall, as stated above, I'm extremely pleased with this product. Add a NVMe M.2 drive as your boot drive and you will be screaming for a low low price.

text:
I ordered two of these. They were advertised as being refurbished by a certified refurbisher. These were going to be put in use as a continuous operation thin client, so i decided to double check the condition of the internals. I opened the case and on both units, the hard drive was installed incorrectly, and both were missing hard drive mount grommets. I pulled the heat sinks off the processors to check thermal paste. on the first, only 75% of the processor had contact with the heat sink from thermal paste, and the silicon thermal pads were falling apart and missing in some places. On the second unit, it appeared that thermal paste was applied by a stencil, however only about 50% of the processor was making contact because the heat sink was installed incorrectly, and the mounting screws were cross threaded into the chassis. This unit also had degraded silicon pads. I corrected the issues myself and put these in service. They are functioning well. Had this been left as provided, hot spots on the processors would have significantly impacted performance and shortened the life of the processors.

I did reach out to the seller and was offered a return authorization. I let them know that I corrected the issue, and it was pretty much left at that. I guess I expected something to cover my efforts to correct their failed attempt at refurbishing. I did ask if thermal management was something they addressed in their refurbishment process and did not get an answer on that. Being that I ordered 2, and both were in poor condition, I suspect this is the level of quality that can be expected.

I realize these are older units, and I would fully expect this quality from a private seller or surplus purchase, but I specifically ordered refurbished units to ensure they would serve the purpose I needed. I still think I got a good deal with this purchase, but understand, you will need some level of technical capabilities to ensure these meet the needs you have. Always check, because the issues above would quickly render these paperweights. Had these failed due to me not checking, the rating would have been 1 star, but because i was able to catch this ahead of failure, I saved the seller 2 stars on this review.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
This little computer is a bargain for a desktop system or an HTPC. It has plenty of compute power for an small office or home PC. It can even run some low end 3D games, although you might have to turn down the graphics settings in the games. All you need is a monitor along with a Display Port to HDMI cable for a complete setup. You can download OpenOffice or LibreOffice for an effective office software suite. It is one of the most inexpensive ways that you can get a Windows 11 compatible computer.

Any time you buy one of these refurbished systems, and i have bought a few, you can expect some minor variations in configuration from what is stated. They usually give you more rather than less (which would annoy buyers). Mine came as advertised with the one exception that it has a 3400G processor that is a bit faster than the 3400GE, but that draws 65W of power instead of 35W. I would have preferred the lower wattage GE for my application, but it is fine. Internally, it came with a Toshiba 256GB M.2 NVMe SSD, an Intel AX210 M.2 WiFI/BT card, and a single Micron Technology 8GB DDR4 2666 SODIMM memory card.

It has a empty removable tray for a 2.5" SATA HD or SSD. You have to remove that tray to get to the M.2 slots underneath. It is a bit harder to remove that tray than it is on the 800 G2 or 805 G5 that I also own. it is only more difficult because there are cables both front and back on it. The back is the SATA ribbon cable and the front is the fan cable. I think the safest way to remove it is to first remove the SATA connector from the tray carefully so that you don't pull the ribbon cable out of its connector on the board - which wouldn't be the end of the world, but they are obnoxious to reinsert. Then you pull off the front screw. slide the tray forward, lift it up and out, then rotate it towards the front to not pull out the fan connector. BTW, mine came with the SATA ribbon cable already pulled out of the board - perhaps the only minor complaint I had.

Because there is no HDD in the tray, you do not get the special bushings it takes to mount a drive there. But, I found that drone M3 anti-vibration standoffs, such as the ones from FPVDrone, work well enough. You can find them here on Amazon.

If you hold down ESC when you boot it, it goes into the BIOS. In that BIOS are diagnostics to run that you can use to check out your computer. I recommend that you do so before installing the OS. Mine passed just fine. You also might want to go through the settings. I couldn't get mine to boot from a USB stick until I checked the box in the BIOS to allow that. Businesses often lock down USB ports for security reasons, and these PCs come out of businesses that have moved on to more current computers.

If you are looking for a low cost way to get a computer for non-gaming usage, this is a great value.

You can download OpenOffice or LibreOffice for an effective office software suite. It is one of the most inexpensive ways that you can get a Windows 11 compatible computer.

Any time you buy one of these refurbished systems, and i have bought a few, you can expect some minor variations in configuration from what is stated. They usually give you more rather than less (which would annoy buyers). Mine came as advertised with the one exception that it has a 3400G processor that is a bit faster than the 3400GE, but that draws 65W of power instead of 35W. I would have preferred the lower wattage GE for my application, but it is fine. Internally, it came with a Toshiba 256GB M.2 NVMe SSD, an Intel AX210 M.2 WiFI/BT card, and a single Micron Technology 8GB DDR4 2666 SODIMM memory card.

It has a empty removable tray for a 2.5" SATA HD or SSD. You have to remove that tray to get to the M.2 slots underneath. It is a bit harder to remove that tray than it is on the 800 G2 or 805 G5 that I also own. it is only more difficult because there are cables both front and back on it. The back is the SATA ribbon cable and the front is the fan cable. I think the safest way to remove it is to first remove the SATA connector from the tray carefully so that you don't pull the ribbon cable out of its connector on the board - which wouldn't be the end of the world, but they are obnoxious to reinsert. Then you pull off the front screw. slide the tray forward, lift it up and out, then rotate it towards the front to not pull out the fan connector. BTW, mine came with the SATA ribbon cable already pulled out of the board - perhaps the only minor complaint I had.

Because there is no HDD in the tray, you do not get the special bushings it takes to mount a drive there. But, I found that drone M3 anti-vibration standoffs, such as the ones from FPVDrone, work well enough. You can find them here on Amazon.

If you hold down ESC when you boot it, it goes into the BIOS. In that BIOS are diagnostics to run that you can use to check out your computer. I recommend that you do so before installing the OS. Mine passed just fine. You also might want to go through the settings. I couldn't get mine to boot from a USB stick until I checked the box in the BIOS to allow that. Businesses often lock down USB ports for security reasons, and these PCs come out of businesses that have moved on to more current computers.

If you are looking for a low cost way to get a computer for non-gaming usage, this is a great value.

After using this HP 15.6" touchscreen laptop for several weeks, I’ve been consistently impressed by how well it handles everyday tasks. The i3-1115G4’s strong single-core performance allows quick boot times, fast app launches, and responsive system navigation. The 32GB RAM is a major advantage, enabling seamless multitasking with numerous browser tabs, office applications, and streaming content open simultaneously.

The 1TB SSD offers excellent speed for file transfers and significantly improves overall responsiveness. With this much storage, it's easy to keep large photo libraries, documents, and multiple applications installed without worrying about space.

The touchscreen is responsive and intuitive, making browsing and media viewing more natural. While the display is HD rather than Full HD, the colors are pleasant, and brightness is adequate for indoor use.

The keyboard provides a soft, comfortable typing experience suitable for long sessions. The touchpad is accurate and reliable, with smooth gesture support.

Key strengths:

-Quick boot and file operations due to the 1TB SSD

The built-in speakers are serviceable for video calls and casual media consumption but lack depth for music playback. Additionally, the HD display may feel less sharp for users accustomed to Full HD or higher.

copilot, calculator & a dedicated omen hub button. you can remap the copilot button to search so its not all that annoying.
