text:
Resolution wise, these are amazing for the price! I’m not so sure I’d compare them to something like a Pimax or in the 4K league, but they do wonders. I hear a lot of people complain about periphery but I don’t see that issue as much, partially because I tend to be tunnel visioned when I play games. Primarily I use them on iRacing and Digital Combat Simulator, which have both been amazing titles to play in VR. I also played Assetto Corsa, except that I can’t get the FOV to work for me in that game.

I also ended up making a custom bracket to hold everything on the rig I use which made the whole thing much more organized to work with.

That was a good, here’s the bad.

Nearly every time I start my computer and open up windows mixed reality, I always have to power cycle or USB cycle the headset before I can use it. It will not come straight onto the computer without some kind of issue. It’s a very simple thing to address in drivers or what not, I’m not sure why HP doesn’t deal with that. I heard on the newer revisions there’s a reset button on the power/usb block you push to jog power on/off. Really???

Then there’s just a general issue of getting it to work on the computer. Not very straightforward, not that its HP‘s fault necessarily. There’s a lot of gears in the process of making it work. Steam VR is an option, but very unrecommended if you want good frame rate without a lot of overhead from the system. That means doing a bit of detective work for now until vendors and software developers get their act together.

Within 6 months the right ear cup has become chronically intermittent. Meaning, you’ll be playing a game and the audio will cut out, but shaking your head or tapping it brings it back. Some sort of disconnect. I’m eventually going to move to a set of Bluetooth earbuds to address this problem. I don’t put that many hours in the seat at a time, so they should be able to last long enough. My other option would be to get some wired earbuds but that means running another cable to the computer which is difficult from a simrig, plus the added cabling that follows your head.

Headtracking overall has been very good provided there’s enough light in the room. That seems to be the only thing I’ve noticed in terms of headtracking issues. I imagine if you had something else with satellites (a la Steam Index or similar) this would be a non-issue in the dark, but I didn’t want to have the extra equipment in the room just to use it. I rent an apartment, so I don’t wanna constantly have to keep moving those things around form place to place, plus it’s more things to break.

For the image quality and cost, hard to beat this! Just know it may take a bit more proficiency and troubleshooting to iron out the kinks from day to day.

title: 3.0 out of 5 stars
text:
I use this monitor as I work from home 4 days out of the week & I absolutely loved it at first but the more I used it I learned that it simply doesn’t live up to the price point. Before I dive into the cons some of the pros are that for its size it’s honestly not that heavy, it’s pretty clunky but I had no issues carrying it around by myself. The monitor slides up and down which is awesome so you can be sure whether or not your webcam is on & it’s like an added layer of privacy (the webcam is super high up so if you’re short like me your head might get cut off).

And last PRO - The monitor also comes with built in speakers, they get pretty loud & although my MacBook Air sound much better the fact this monitor even comes with speakers & a built in microphone is pretty dope! some of the expensive gaming monitors don’t even come with speakers!

Ok, now for the cons…
1. If you are saving up for a high quality, expensive monitor to last you a long while please keep your options open. If you have expendable income & this isn’t a big purchase for you then buy it but if this is possibly a big purchase I honestly wouldn’t take the chance. I was able to buy this with a work from home stipend & while I make a decent salary I would be extremely upset if I paid for this with my hard earned money.

2. I had high expectations for the picture and color quality but those expectations weren’t met, I was actually a little shocked at how bland and fuzzy the screen appears. The colors seem washed out, the best way I can think to describe it is being kind of matte and not “glossy”, the picture isn’t crispy. Even just browning the web if you look close to the screen you can see the text looks slightly fuzzy. This isn’t a big deal but again, it should be clear and crispy for $500.

3. The size is awesome for gaming, if you have a Gaming PC with a graphics card this would honestly do the job but my Truly honest opinion is if you are interested in buying this for strictly gaming I’m not sure if this will be enjoyable to truly enjoy the gaming experience. I would look for monitors specifically built for gamers.

4. IT BREAKS VERY EASILY!!!! I initially thought it was a tough monitor as I’ve taken it out of town with me, hauling it in and out of the car without issue, while it held up great in the car it didn’t stand a chance against a small light piece of plastic. A figurine I keep near my desk somehow fell against the monitor & it completely demolished the screen. Immediatley broke the screen with a 2-3inch wide black line down the screen with the right side glitching out. It gradually got worse over the next few days, at first the left hand side still worked great so I honestly didn’t mind since the screen is so incredibly large but eventually horizontal purple & green lines started popping up making it hard to read my work files.

I understand that if something it’s a monitor screen it will break but I truly was shocked at how sensitive this monitor was to barely being hit by the plastic figurine. Growing up my mom was in IT and worked on computers for a school district and my uncle built gaming PC’s so I’ve used a lot of different computer monitors both high quality and crappy - unfortunately this monitor is up there with the crappy quality ones due to the fact the entire screen went out so easily.

I truly expected higher quality and for the monitor itself to be quite durable since it’s over $500.. I’ve had run of the mill monitors that have fallen off the back of a truck & still worked perfect. Since it’s a curved monitor I’m sure that plays a part into the screen being so sensitive.

The monitor lasted roughly 6 months with no issues but I really enjoyed using it as a work monitor & I felt spoiled due to how big the monitor is. I honestly think it’s BIGGER than 32 inches, it feels more like 35-38 inches because my 27inch monitor at the office is half its size.

text:
This dock is definitely a statement piece. It really looks and feels premium, with the embossed HP logo on top and the high-quality (if needlessly heavy) construction. All the major ports show up, including 1 HDMI, an Ethernet, 2 Display Port (I guess DP won the war against HDMI?) and 4 USB-As, 2 on the back and 2 more on the side, alongside a audio jack. The front houses both the USB-C (over thunderbolt) connection to your PC/Laptop, along with the singular other USB-C port (though I really could have used 1 or 2 more, as more and more devices start using that port instead of traditional USB Type-A ports).

In any case, setup is very easy, though it comes with a massive power brick that, ingeniously, plugs in through the bottom. Setup is as simple as plugging all devices you'd like to use into the back/side of the dock and it just works. No extra drivers or anything were needed and you can even charge your laptop through that same singular cable to provides all the data as well.

I do want to mention that the dock to PC cable coming out of the front is a bit strange. I mean, you don't usually have your laptop directly in front of you and, if you do, it covers the singular USB-C port altogether. title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
When I opened the package just now, I was skeptical. I'd expected something that went over the edges of the keyboard to keep it in place and to have deep "wells" for the keys. The key wells are very slight. Maybe 1/16 inch. However, not a problem. The silicone has enough "grab" to keep it in place. It hasn't budged an iota as I have been typing up this review

Plus, I did add a few pieces of scotch double stick tape on the keyboard itself for good measure in a few strategic spots. I don't think it was needed now that I have used it some but it couldn't hurt

I got the black instead of the clear. The black is only on the keys. The rest of the cover is clear. This helps cut down the glare as the black is a matt black. I had a glare problem with my previous cover which is why I thought I would give black a try. I am glad I did. The lettering is a silvery color that does reflect a small amount but not enough to be an issue.

The feel of the keyboard is cushiony but not enough to feel bulky. Just a nice soft feeling.

I am very happy with this and will buy again if needed. It was very reasonably priced and should make my keyboard last a long time. TBH, I have a pretty cheap keyboard. $30 or less. But I like the feel of it and it fits my hands which are small so I don't want to have to find another if I spaz out and pour coffee on it. Not to mention the work disruption.

That makes buying the keyboard protector worth it.

Note to review: It is still a 5. I bought it in 2021 and it has held up great. My only issue is that the most used letters are wearing off because I bought the black with lettering. Since I am not a "natural" keyboardist (very small hands), I have to have the letters. I have had to put "stickies" on those keys which tend to peel off after a time. I am going to order the clear version so that the actual keyboard letters will show through.

Addendum to Note Above: I ordered the "clear"' It is not. It is just transparent. Clear would be better. However, I can see the letters and it is better than having the black version where the letters wear off. Still fits perfect.

title: 4.0 out of 5 stars
text:
I was needing a mount for one of my elitedesk mini pc’s and this caught my eye. It arrived well packaged with hardware and a cheap screwdriver so everything you should need unless you have to drill holes for a wall or under desk mounting situation. The instructions are not very clear and after a little fiddling around I figured the way the mini pc needs to slide into it so it can be secured.

You have to slide the mini pc in back first with the pc’s feet toward the small bar to line up the two screw holes with the vesa mount on the PC after you have attached the bracket to whatever location you have chosen. I’d do a test fit and check the orientation where you plan to put it first.

Of note, if you have one of the 65w models with the additional ventilation grate on the top of the case, the proper orientation go in bracket sorta blocks air flow. Granted the airflow for cooling the CPU comes through the front panel, your SSD or M2 drive doesn’t benefit from the air flow.

If mounting on the back of your monitor, if the monitor stand is already using the VESA mount this will likely not work as it needs to have the VESA mounting holes unused and enough clearance. I my case I am mounting to the side of a work bench so the VESA holes will be used to secure it there.

There is a tab in the back of the bracket that sorta lines up with the Kensington lock….its close but not quite. I my case it’s not an issue. I’m probably going to trim part of that tab off so I can face the on top of case ventilation grate outward and add a shim to make it a more snug fit in that orientation. It lines up properly with the Elitedesk 800 G3 mini’s. The Prodesk 600 G2/G3 it’s slightly off. The G6 Elitedesk 800 is a bit different, it’ll work but fit isn’t as good.

Overall I think it is a good value as long as you understand whether or not it will fit your needs. I’ll probably get a couple more as I have several of these mini’s.

It is painted steel and appears to be well made.

The Elitedesk 800 Gen3 mini’s are the best fit for this bracket keeping in mind the info mentioned earlier.

So I bought an hp desktop from my mom and put it in my room. Excited, I was, to play Minecraft, work on school, and even watch Netflix. Every time I looked at the desktop, taking up my whole desk, I remembered what was on the way. Except days upon days were going by… One day it dawned on me that it had been three weeks. Fine. Whatever. It was probably poor judgment on my part and there’s nothing I could do to get my money back. I will go on good ol’ Amazon. Reliable, affordable I should have done gone here straight after my bunny chewed the cord. So I bought this product and within the week was able to reunite with my long unused computer.

One little bite was all it took with those sharp teeth. The new cord was beyond function, beyond use. I am currently deciding to give up. My hopes and dreams, visions of minecraft and YouTube, died in a graveyard of mangled phone chargers, computer cables, lamp cords, and even a heated blanket. title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
I bought this Lenovo ThinkCentre M920s, i7, 512 GB storage SFF computer as a replacement for an earlier Lenovo model, the ThinkCentre M93p, which I bought refurbished and then used for a remarkable 10 years, with no complaints except that it could not be upgraded to Windows 11. I did at one point install a low-powered video card in the old one because I needed an HDMI port. The reliability of the older machine was a big factor in choosing Lenovo for the new one. The small form factor works well for me, too.

Another reason that I chose this computer is that it has a DVD drive. Many of these refurbished SFF computers don't have those. I didn't want to pay extra for one or fuss with installing one myself.

The vendor that mine came from is different from the vendor that is now shown on the listing.

The unit arrived well-packed and as described. It shipped with a power cord and a USB wifi 5 dongle which says, "BT + AC600, Driver free." I used the dongle while I set up the computer and transferred over my stuff. I am using an ethernet connection now, though.

The first surprise is that there was a fair amount of noise during the initial Windows update. It sounded like a vacuum cleaner. I don't recall my old computer making any noise at all, except a slight fan noise after I installed the aforementioned video card. After the Windows update, I don't detect any noise from this one.

The first thing I did after the initial setup was to disconnect the unit from OneDrive. I want my files to all be stored locally.

The second surprise: this new-to-me computer has a faster processor and more memory than my old one, and I had assumed that it would be faster in every way that I could perceive. However, I have found that start-up on this machine is slower than on the old one. I see a black screen with white characters for several seconds. So that is a disappointment. The difference is so noticeable that I checked to make sure that I actually have an SSD drive, and I do.

Overall, I'm glad that I bought this, but I do have some reservations due to the two things mentioned.

Edit to add that I downloaded the Lenovo Vantage software and it scanned my computer for updates, which led to an update of the BIOS. Start-up is faster now. Thank you to the reviewer who recommended downloading the Vantage software.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
Like all the refurbished stuff, what I get from "supplier A" may not be what you get from "supplier B". That's just how this works. If you go over to the little pull down, you can see a number of folks who all are happy to sell you one of these.

What I happened to get this time was: No SSD bracket, and no DVD. I did get a keyboard, mouse, power cord, built in WiFi, the specified RAM and NVME drive. It also has a pair of serial ports and a VGA. Unlike a few others mine came with the CPU that shows up in the listing. The photo's on the listing are stock photos from who knows where. The certainly did not show what mine look like. Other than the missing SSD bracket, the rest of the "what did I get" really does not matter for my use case. There is "another place" you can go and get them pretty darn cheap ....

Everything functions as it should. It booted fine to Windows 10. That went away as soon as I had a chance to fiddle the BIOS and load Linux.

Mine happened to come with two 8 GB RAM sticks to make up the 16 GB needed. Might another one come with four 4GB? I have no idea. The "two stick" option makes adding more RAM a bit easier. Oddly enough the BIOS showed the installed ram running as 2666MHz rather than 2400MHz. I guess I got lucky. The NVME in mine is a stock Lenovo part. Is it new or has it lived there forever? There's no way to tell. BIOS was last updated in 2024.

Mechanically everything looks fine. No major scratches or dents. Nothing busted or caved in. It would look fine if you wanted to put it on a desktop. This is not a super duper modern CPU and 16 GB is not a lot of RAM. That will impact how it will do running Windows vs something a bit newer.

For the price, I'm quite happy with what I got. Right now this one is the "low cost leader" of the M920s refurbs. That's true here on Amazon and on "that other place".

text:
One strange issue I ran into is when I went to add a 2nd SSD drive - it wasn't recognized by the BIOS nor Windows. After doing some searching online, the fix was to swap the slots, switching the original SSD to the 2nd M.2 slot and the new to the 1st. You can then change the boot load order in BIOS.

Build quality seems solid. The lid opens/closes without bouncing around due to stable hinges and the weight of the base which helps hold the laptop in place.

A bit daunting at first to disassemble when upgrading/replacing battery, but it's not difficult. Be sure to have a quality set of assorted precision screwdrivers.

The black chassis gets smudgy easily even with clean hands.

Keyboard has nice tactile feel. Nice layout - not cramped or oddly arranged. The backlight is especially helpful.

I'm not a huge fan of RGB, but the colors on this really pop. It looks very nice! Custom-configurable in software, too.

The Lenovo pre-installed software is very helpful in checking for and installing driver updates, BIOS firmware, etc. It's not overly intrusive or gimmicky. McAfee software was not desired but it was simple to uninstall.

Weight is not as bad as expected. I've owned prior gaming laptops, which were much clunkier. This fits nicely in a standard 16" laptop carry case and doesn't feel like a workout to transport.

Performance is solid. I leave mine on 'balanced' and opt not to push the wattages/temps. It handles like a champ.

Have only used it for about a month now and will update this if issues arise.

Recommended.

title: 4.0 out of 5 stars
text:
I’ve been using the Lenovo ThinkPad T14 Gen 5 for a few weeks now, and it’s clear this machine was built for professionals who need performance, durability, and reliability.

Pros:
• Excellent Build Quality – Classic ThinkPad design with a sturdy chassis, spill-resistant keyboard, and that iconic red TrackPoint. Feels like it can survive the daily grind of travel and meetings.
• Great Keyboard – Typing is a dream. The keys have great travel and feedback. Ideal for long typing sessions.
• Powerful Performance – With the latest Intel (or AMD) processor, it handles multitasking, data-heavy spreadsheets, and remote work apps without breaking a sweat.
• Plenty of Ports – No need to live the dongle life. USB-A, USB-C, HDMI, Ethernet – they’re all here.
• Strong Security Features – Fingerprint reader, optional IR camera for facial recognition, and a physical webcam shutter give peace of mind.
• Battery Life – Easily gets me through a full workday with moderate to heavy use.

Cons:
• Display Is Good, Not Great – It’s sharp and bright enough, but if you’re doing color-sensitive work like photo editing, you might want an external monitor.
• Not the Lightest – At around 3.2 lbs, it’s not heavy, but there are lighter ultrabooks if portability is your top priority.

Final Verdict:
If you’re looking for a dependable workhorse that balances power, durability, and business-ready features, the T14 Gen 5 should be at the top of your list. It’s not flashy, but it gets the job done – and does it well.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
I came from the world of Thinkpads to fall for this Legion. I had (still have) a Lenovo Thinkpad X1 Extreme 2nd with i7-9750H, 64GB of RAM, 3TB of storage, 4K OLED touch panel and the GTX 1650 max-Q. I purchased this laptop in 2019 when it was announced (very pricey, but it was one of the best). It was very good at the beginning, but his thinness was a major flaw because it was overheating like hell with time passing. Since my work requires a powerhouse laptop with both the CPU and GPU, my laptops couldn't handle the workload anymore. I use a lot of virtualization labs and video rendering and it takes too much time to render one video session. So I looked for a replacement and found this Legion and I was quite impressed but a bit disappointed. Here are the pros and cons:

Pros:
- Very light: almost the same weight as my older Thinkpad
- The OLED screen is amazing (The thinkpad was a bit better because of its 4K panel, but less bright than the Legion)
- The CPU is sooo powefull and everything is snappy. The GPU is also very good for my needs (I'm not a hardcore gamer, just a casual one)
- The laptop is quiet all the time, but the fans kick like a jet taking off when I run some heavy tasks (video rendering) lol. I don't mind the noise for performance.
- The lid can be opened with one hand, not like my old Thinkpad
- The webcam quality is way better than my Thinkpad's
- You can switch between performance modes using Fn+Q shortcut
- You can overclock the GPU and undervolt the CPU (haven't tried it yet)
- the HDMI and power port are located behind the laptop
- Webcam switch to enable/disable it

Cons:
- Only 16GB of RAM for this price, which make it pricier
- No fingerprint scanner or Windows Hello compatible Webcam
- Typing on the Legion's keyboard is quite good, but not as delicious as the ThinkPad (1.5mm key travel vs 1.8mm for the Thinkpad)
- in my opinion, the numpad keyboard wasn't necessary since by adding it, they had to shift the keyboard to the left which needs you to get used to it.
- The black color is a fingerprint magnet.
- The battery life is average. Coming from my Thinkpad that had less than 2h of battery life, I can squeeze more than the Thinkpad if I enable the Quiet mode and reduce the screen's brightness. But it's more than enough for me since I'm plugged in almost all the time
- No SD card reader and not enough ports

Regarding the delivery, Amazon used the " Lenovo Legion 5i Gaming laptop...." instead of "Lenovo Legion 5 15IRX10", which is the accurate name of the product, and that created an issue with the customs. Please Amazon, next time use the real name of the product because there are many models and generations of the Legion 5.

I received the laptop 2 weeks ago, so I'll wait to see if there are any other issues.

title: 4.0 out of 5 stars
text:
I gave these a good run through and have some thoughts. I'll start with the negatives. First, these do not sound great for music. It doesn't matter how I've EQ'ed them, I could never get the bass to a level I liked. These are mainly heavy on the highs with a lack of detail in the mids. Their sound signature, even after EQ'ing, works well for calls but didn't sound great with music or music-heavy movies. Second, Lenovo doesn't make an app for Android, iOS, macOS, or anything other than Windows. You must download Lenovo's Windows app to update their firmware, adjust settings, and EQ them. Third, their touch controls are limited. There’s a glossy strip on the earbuds that seem like they’d be great for volume controls, but they only have basic tap controls that are wonky. Fourth, Atmos sounds terrible. Like every other company that tries to upscale stereo audio to faux surround sound, the results are awful sounding, and I left Atmos off. Lastly, their ANC is on par with $40 earbuds from competing brands. It’s nice that Lenovo offers ANC, but it isn’t anything to write home about and it had issues with my space heater, something earbuds from other companies (even at $40) had no issues cancelling out.

Despite these negatives, there are a few positives that make these a solid purchase for PC use. They maintain a solid connection to my Lenovo and Dell PCs. I could stay within a 10ft radius without experiencing dropouts or skips, even when in Teams meetings. I didn’t have anyone complain about microphone quality or other issues. The microphone tech here was able to cancel out the space heater in my office along with other low office noises.

Latency was low enough I could watch training videos and other videos without having lip sync delays. My Lenovo has Bluetooth 5.3, but my work-issued Dell system has Bluetooth 5.1 and latency was still low with it. Lenovo’s app is easy to use once you get it installed, and it always connects to the earbuds without issues. The EQ was easy to adjust from a list of pre-sets or a simple band EQ you can adjust. Like I said, I could never get the bass levels I wanted or clarity in the highs, but having an EQ is better than not (I’m looking at you, Apple).

The case doesn’t have Qi charging, I wish it would, but USB C charging was quick. These earbuds were getting me about 5 hours of use with ANC on, Lenovo advertises up 7 hours without ANC enabled. Much to my surprise, these earbuds feature wear detection. It’s a simple light sensor, but it works. Take one earbud out while playing content and it will pause. You can use the earbuds independently as well.

Overall, these aren’t bad if you’re looking for a pair of inexpensive earbuds to use for Teams meetings. They aren’t great for music or movies, but they’re still serviceable. These excel with calls and meetings while providing a solid connection to Windows PCs during Teams meetings, something other earbuds have issues with. I don’t recommend these for media consumption, but they are great “business” earbuds to get work done.

text:
Coming from multiple MacBook Pros, I was looking for a laptop with similar build quality and this delivers. The chassis is solid with no flex when you pick it up. The screen is excellent (actually better than my MacBook), battery life has been great, and the keyboard feels good with nice backlit keys. The trackpad is highly customizable. The built-in Bluetooth works great with my earbuds and allows them to switch back and forth to my iPhone as needed.

I installed Linux Mint immediately (never even booted Windows 11), and it pairs really well with the hardware. The one thing that doesn't work yet is the NPU (the Ryzen AI chip for local AI processing); Linux support for that is still developing. If you require NPU functionality now, you'll need Windows. If you can wait, this is a great Linux machine.
Highly recommended for anyone wanting a well-built, portable laptop that runs Linux well.

One word of caution: some sellers on Amazon are buying stock laptops, replacing the hard drives, RAM, and other components with larger but much cheaper parts, then trying to sell them at an elevated cost implying they are from the factory that way. Read the listing details carefully and make sure it says new, unopened box, from the factory, etc. Otherwise you might get a base model with cheap upgrades that don't last.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
Bought this to temporarily replace the windows laptop I normally use when away from my desk until I could replace screen after a child sat on it. Turns out it has more permanently replaced that laptop.

The windows laptop I was using was overkill for what I needed to do when away from my main PC. Plus I have tablets and other laptops for various situations. I normally used that laptop for online shopping, light games, browsing, streaming to tv, etc.

It turns out this Chromebook was the perfect replacement. It is much more portable than my 17" pc laptop and does exactly what I need it to do. Its been about 6 months since purchase and I haven't felt I needed to rush to replace the screen in the old one.

This Chromebook is very light and portable and feels well made. If you do heavy duty gaming, have to work with graphics editors, or need to store lots of data, this isn't for you. But if you do online shopping, internet research, email, or light games this might be a good alternative.

Chromebooks use android apps via the Google Play Store to extend their capabilities. We are searching for houses right now, so Zillow works well and I can cast the computer screen to our TV to review houses we have identified. Plus, when visiting areas of interest we can take this little computer with us, attach to our vehicle hotspot and view listings online. Various browsers are compatible with the Lenovo. Obviously, Gmail also works well.

Wifi 6 makes it faster if your router is wifi 6 enabled. Battery life is good and it charges remarkably fast.

If you have AR/XR glasses the USB-C port apparently doesn't have video out, there is only one such port on the machine and it is used to recharge the machine. It comes with a charging brick. Bluetooth earbuds, mice, etc work fine. The touch screen is a really nice addition. The screen is bright and sound quality is good.

When the machine starts feeling "slow" a restart seems to cure it. You do have to manage storage, don't overload the machine with pics, data or apps. I have used the Lenovo daily now for about 6 months and am happy with its operation. I am a computer speed freak and am constantly upgrading and tweaking my PCs and routers, but haven't felt like this little machine needs any such attention. Again, it isn't for heavy computing.

i would recommend this for people with light computing needs who understand android devices, play store apps, can manage storage and don't mind the Google environment. It is a good value. I would purchase again. Manage your expectations, understand your needs and it will be a good experience.

text:
La Lenovo LOQ Essential cumple con lo que promete: es una laptop básica para gaming, pensada para quien busca lo mínimo funcional. Con ella es posible jugar títulos AAA, pero únicamente con gráficos reducidos y bajo ciertas condiciones.
El punto más importante es la memoria RAM. De fábrica no es suficiente para este tipo de juegos, por lo que es obligatorio actualizarla a 16 GB para obtener un rendimiento aceptable. Aquí hay una advertencia clave: la laptop solo cuenta con un slot de RAM, lo que limita futuras mejoras.
En cuanto a la refrigeración, el equipo solo tiene un ventilador compartido para CPU y GPU, lo que provoca que, bajo carga, el ruido sea considerablemente alto, especialmente al jugar. Esto puede resultar molesto para sesiones prolongadas.
Considerando que una memoria RAM de 16 GB ronda actualmente los $2,500 MXN, mi recomendación es evaluar seriamente si vale la pena invertir ese dinero en esta laptop. En muchos casos, es mejor destinar ese presupuesto adicional a una laptop de gama superior, con mejor sistema de enfriamiento y mayor margen de actualización.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
I am an IT professional and manage laptop / desktop deployments where I work.
After extensive research within the market of fold-able 2-in-1 laptops, I found this gem of a machine.
I purchased this for one of my power users.
Battery life is excellent.
weight is perfect considering it is a 16" chassis.
screen is really pleasant to work from and is easy on the eyes.
The Ryzen 8840hs is a fantastic CPU for this use case and has 0 issues handling heavy workloads.
The RAM is Soldered which is a disadvantage for future upgrades BUT, Lenovo put 16GB of LPDDR5X-6400MHz which is literally the fastest RAM on the market (at time of writing this review) for this chip set.
This machine also has support for USB-C 3.2 Gen 2 (DP 1.4a, PD 3.0) on 2 ports which allows you to charge the device, run ultra high def video, and USB pass-through all on the same cable.
I LOVE the on board 780M graphics, the end user needed to have a highly mobile device that could also pull up or manipulate 3D CAD type images and this machine handles them with ease.
Also, just about ALL the major CAD, CAM and 3D imaging software companies support Lenovo so you shouldn't have issues with getting support for your software if considering this laptop.

I set this user up with a Dell U3425WE screen which has a built in docking station that also supports charge through USB-C.
The end user only has to plug or unplug 1 cable to fully dock / undock his laptop yet still have multiple USB devices supported through his screen ports, Ultra high def curved Display Port screen AND keep his laptop fully charged.
I can't stress the coolness factor of the de-clutter effect of having 1 port to rule them all this laptop supports. His desk is quickly becoming the envy of all his co-workers.
Lenovo out did themselves with this laptop, I hope they keep it up and don't mess this up in future products.

I Lastly want to say, I was a Lenovo HATER before finding this device but since it was the only device that could fully meet this user's needs, I had to buy it and VERY glad we did.

title: 2.0 out of 5 stars
text:
I have had a positive view of Lenova laptops and was excited to finally purchase one for myself. My kids have had some in the past and they have really held up to normal day to day use quite well. But this purchase just didnt work out for me.

It is a bit unfair because I am comparing this to my LG Gram which really blows most other laptops out of the water. But my gram is 5 years old and there are signs of wear and tear so I wanted a new primary laptop. Ive had the Lenova for 3 months now and it just does not compare, even to a 5 year old LG. The reason I am writing this review today is because the Lenova hasnt been able to connect to the internet in a few days. So Im writing my review about my Lenova on my Gram.

Other issues: the laptop came out of the box unable to be used with Zoom. The camera has some crazy setting that makes it constantly adjust the contrast and brightness even if nothing is changing in the image. It took forever to figure out how to change the settings, but it seems that this is the result of Lenova adding custom software to try to improve the camera. It doesnt work. So you will have to disable that software. In the process of figuring out what was going on, I found multiple Reddit conversations on the same issue so it is not unique to me.

I also cannot modify graphs in Excel. If I select any interior portion of a graph in excel, the laptop acts as if I am constantly selecting and deselecting it. This makes it very challenging to edit graphs in Excel. I can copy them into PPT and modify them there but not in Excel. Ive never seen any issue like this before on any previous laptop. Certainly this is also Lenova trying to improve some feature of their laptop that has backfired.

Im not thrilled with the audio. The speakers are rich but not clear, if that makes any sense. When listening to music they sound good but when on a Zoom call I have to crank the volume up a bit more than I would have on my Gram because the voices are not clear.

I would also say I miss my keypad on my Gram. This is my fault - I didnt look carefully enough before I purchased.

Also, the Lenova is twice as heavy as the Gram, again something that is clear from the specs. But it does make me wonder why I didnt just buy an upgraded Gram. What I did get was a longer battery life (the Gram never lived up to its stated specs) and a better camera. But if I had the chance to go back, I would and I wouldnt buy this computer.

My former gaming laptop crashed and I needed another, so I went with this one, which is a bit smaller than the one I had previously (but was also far less expensive). I'm pretty happy with this one with a couple of caveats.

First, I'm really happy with the RTX 4070 in this: it's an upgrade from my older laptop which struggled a bit with a few games like Dragon Age Veilguard (which, frankly, I think is more about the game than the laptop), but this one had fewer problems, and it runs all the new games i have beautifully. That was my main concern, and this laptop meets that need beautifully.

I've had it since December and these are my caveats: first, I think the power adaptor could be better. It gets quite hot even if I"ve only been playing for an hour or so and I tend to play for hours at a time. I may just replace this eventually with a better adaptor. Also, the laptop itself still gets pretty hot, in spite of having better cooling than my previous laptop did. This may simply be a problem for all laptops running demanding games, but I had hoped for better with this one. It's also not very big--which is both good--easier to transport if need be--but the screen isn't that big either.

Still for just a bit over $1000, I was pretty happy with what I got and my caveats may be simply something everything laptop struggles with.

Overall, I think it's a pretty good deal, and am glad I got it.

title: 4.0 out of 5 stars
text:
I gave these a good run through and have some thoughts. I'll start with the negatives. First, these do not sound great for music. It doesn't matter how I've EQ'ed them, I could never get the bass to a level I liked. These are mainly heavy on the highs with a lack of detail in the mids. Their sound signature, even after EQ'ing, works well for calls but didn't sound great with music or music-heavy movies. Second, Lenovo doesn't make an app for Android, iOS, macOS, or anything other than Windows. You must download Lenovo's Windows app to update their firmware, adjust settings, and EQ them. Third, their touch controls are limited. There’s a glossy strip on the earbuds that seem like they’d be great for volume controls, but they only have basic tap controls that are wonky. Fourth, Atmos sounds terrible. Like every other company that tries to upscale stereo audio to faux surround sound, the results are awful sounding, and I left Atmos off. Lastly, their ANC is on par with $40 earbuds from competing brands. It’s nice that Lenovo offers ANC, but it isn’t anything to write home about and it had issues with my space heater, something earbuds from other companies (even at $40) had no issues cancelling out.

Despite these negatives, there are a few positives that make these a solid purchase for PC use. They maintain a solid connection to my Lenovo and Dell PCs. I could stay within a 10ft radius without experiencing dropouts or skips, even when in Teams meetings. I didn’t have anyone complain about microphone quality or other issues. The microphone tech here was able to cancel out the space heater in my office along with other low office noises.

Latency was low enough I could watch training videos and other videos without having lip sync delays. My Lenovo has Bluetooth 5.3, but my work-issued Dell system has Bluetooth 5.1 and latency was still low with it. Lenovo’s app is easy to use once you get it installed, and it always connects to the earbuds without issues. The EQ was easy to adjust from a list of pre-sets or a simple band EQ you can adjust. Like I said, I could never get the bass levels I wanted or clarity in the highs, but having an EQ is better than not (I’m looking at you, Apple).

The case doesn’t have Qi charging, I wish it would, but USB C charging was quick. These earbuds were getting me about 5 hours of use with ANC on, Lenovo advertises up 7 hours without ANC enabled. Much to my surprise, these earbuds feature wear detection. It’s a simple light sensor, but it works. Take one earbud out while playing content and it will pause. You can use the earbuds independently as well.

Overall, these aren’t bad if you’re looking for a pair of inexpensive earbuds to use for Teams meetings. They aren’t great for music or movies, but they’re still serviceable. These excel with calls and meetings while providing a solid connection to Windows PCs during Teams meetings, something other earbuds have issues with. I don’t recommend these for media consumption, but they are great “business” earbuds to get work done.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
This is an awesome machine! I was honestly a bit scared to make the jump because I’ve used x86 processors my entire life, but this Snapdragon X Elite handles everything I throw at it with zero hesitation. As a Cyber Security student, I was worried about software compatibility, but between the native ARM apps and the Prism emulation layer, it’s been a non-issue.

The "MacBook-Killer" Build
The first thing you notice is the build quality. It has that premium, cold-to-the-touch aluminum chassis that usually only comes with a MacBook, but it runs Windows exactly how I want it to. It's incredibly thin and light, yet it feels like a tank.

Performance & Dev Work
I’m running Visual Studio 2026, Python 3.14, and Node.js natively on ARM, and the speed is incredible. I even have a Kali Linux VM running in VirtualBox for my labs, and it’s snappy. Even though mine only has 8GB of RAM, the memory management is so efficient that I rarely feel a bottleneck.

The Screen is a Cheat Code
That 3K OLED screen is hands-down the best I’ve ever seen on a laptop. The blacks are perfect, and the 120Hz refresh rate makes everything feel fluid. If you do any coding or content consumption, this panel is a massive upgrade over standard IPS displays.

The Verdict
If you're a student or developer hesitant about the ARM transition—don't be. This thing stays cool, the battery lasts all day, and it has more personality than any laptop I've owned. It’s the perfect balance of premium hardware and open software.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
When I first opened the box, I found that the laptop had a relatively solid build quality. Even for plastic, the solid quality to it doesn't make it feel flimsy or loose to type into. Some minor flex is noticed, but doesn’t make it feel "hollow" or cheap either. Two days into continuous usage and some stress tests and I'm contented to how snappy it feels. The i7 model I went may be a little bit of an overkill, but it is more than enough for anything. (The i5 model runs out of stock pretty quick.) For someone who came from a Surface Pro 4 i5 and MBA, the build quality is rather impressive for the years I have owned aluminum-based devices. I have not really experienced any serious issues with gaming either. The Lenovo Vantage app is a great touch and I was able to optimize the usage I have for my computer. Speakers were decently capable, and I was able to tune it out using the Nahimic program. The 120hz display is silky smooth and clear with its anti-glare surface.

Bottlenecks, Recommendations + NOTES:

Upgrading the RAM helps...but is rather necessary. I experienced some lag in some areas when I had a lot of programs opened, including FPS drops when I played games requiring a lot of memory. Task Manager showed consistent 40% or more RAM being used. I strongly advise others to focus on upgrading the RAM to at least 16GB to prevent lagging and some potential crashes in other software. Keep in mind, the RAM it uses for intel (both i5 and i7) model laptops is DDR4, which isn't the best, but a great performer nonetheless..Just unusual that the Ryzen version has a MOBO that uses DDR5. I recommend getting 3200MHz to get most out of the performance you need for the RAM. The "16GB" limit stated from the manufacturer is uncertain, the possibility to use 32, or even 64GB of RAM should work.

The storage is decent, however the 512GB may not be enough especially for gaming. So I recommend upgrading the memory. NOTE: It is necessary to use the smaller M.2 (2242) SSD (gen 4 capable) if you don't intend to replace the stock 512GB M.2, as it occupies 2280 M.2 already (for what I know about intel)

The display of this laptop is good. It could definitely be better, but for everyday tasks and gaming it does more than enough for what I need. I don't highly recommend doing art/design related work on it, as the colors aren't going to be impressive for this laptop, they are okay at the best. I recommend getting a separate display for that. Some light bleed may be noticed on a very dark background as well.

Battery life may also be lacking if the user uses extensive graphics in this computer. It is decent for the most part, and could possibly range from the least 2-7 depending on how it is being used and the specification it has. I'm yet to run out of battery since I have kept it charged in most cases. I don't travel that much either.

Note: To mitigate with battery life, I recommend opening the Vantage app to switch the power mode to "Hybrid-Auto" mode, so it switches to the integrated graphics when unplugged for lower power usage. Unless you intend to game, you may put it back to Hybrid mode. I also recommend switching the thermal mode to "quiet" mode, so it reduces performance that may hinder battery life. The hotkey Fn-Q can switch power modes seamlessly. Which is indicated by the power button LED.

I highly recommend updating all drivers as well.

I bought this laptop in mind to use it long term and for moderate tasks and not solely for its gaming purposes. Overall, it is value for price, definitely needs upgrades though.

title: 4.0 out of 5 stars
text:
Bought this product on sale as a gift for about 650 total. Received it when expected but in packaging that was truly beat to hell. The box was covered in 2 different types of tapes so it’s also entirely possible that with all the craziness of Black Friday the outside-most box just got decimated. No star loss here as the inside box had the appropriate amount of shock resistant packaging material to make it seem protected despite circumstances. I opened the undamaged computer and moved onto the required ssd and ram upgrades and the optional battery upgrade.

I wanted to point out that through the Lenovo Vantage app I found out that the battery warranty had already started back in August. From my experience with the Lenovo Legion 5 that period starts once someone registers the product. After searching there is a place to note the date as incorrect and resubmit through the email created alongside the Microsoft one during setup- for people uncomfortable with products that appear to be returned/refurbished be forewarned that appears to be potentially possible. In my case it wasn’t very relevant as you will see. After a more careful inspection I moved on, but nothing in the product description, listing, or packaging made it seem like anything but new. Skip to the end but if you want my attempt at tldr.

The required ssd upgrade was a 500gb 2280 NVMe Samsung 970 Evo Plus, the ram was recycled from the above mentioned legion 5 but they are two 8gbs running at 3200m/t from Critical, and optionally I decided to try to port the newish 60wh battery from the legion 5 to replace the 45wh within. The ram and ssd were typical, the laptop came with a baggie of screws that sorta fit the 2280 screw hole but left just a bit of play that does long term worry me will potentially loosen. The battery upgrade did require relocating the bios battery 2/3 inches and the larger battery fit but required some firm but gentle coaxing to sink in its new home. Case closed normally and battery was recognized in Lenovo vantage with normal temps.

All upgrades were recognized in the system and after tweaks, updates, and stuff- the attached photo shows the score in user benchmark. If you time the deals correctly the ram and ssd upgrades should be sub 150- even sub 100 if you really got a tight budget. The 60 wh battery can be found 3rd party for a reasonable price as well and with necessary connections, but if you’ll only ever use it plugged in that might not matter. Overall, for the price this laptop can’t be beat as a sub 1k gaming laptop. L4D2 with maxed settings and graphically intense workshop content added barely touches 45% gpu load per Nvidia’s stats. Newer content such as Deep Rock Galactic ran closer to 80-85 fps on maxed settings so playing around with the options/DLSS/reflex boost can yield close to or in excess of the 120hz refresh rate if that matters as well. Overall, 1080p gaming is probably no worries but I didn’t test Crysis so who knows.

***The most important thing to say imo is that if you’re unwilling or unable to do the upgrades then I would avoid this computer at any price point.*** The Ryzen 5 gpu hardware reserves 2g of ram by default (disabling the integrated gpu does not yield worthwhile results- don’t bother) and lowering the UMA to 512mb costs more in the computers ability to multitask/multimedia surf effectively. User benchmark proved the performance was worse. That left the free memory on the computer at around 2-3gbs for gaming on the base version which would bottleneck very quickly. Furthermore you definitely want to move windows to whatever 2280 NVMe you upgrade with, the base 256 gb 2242 (or 2246 i forget the size) is adequate but uninspiring and you would benefit from the main system being on the higher bandwidth option- leaving the base storage as overflow.

For the DIY capable or willing, this laptop (when upgraded) perfectly captures decent build quality, incredibly cheap price, and capable budget 1080p gaming.

text:
Sacándola de la caja, esta laptop tiene dos puntos negativos que son obvios: la paupérrima, terrible y dolorosa cantidad de RAM (es prácticamente inutilizable) y la duración corta de su batería.

Sin embargo, el primer punto negativo es algo que fácilmente se supera comprando un kit de memoria DDR4 para portátiles. Cabe señalar que se le pueden instalar hasta 64 GB de RAM en dos módulos de 32 GB. Y no, Lenovo no recomienda ni dice que la máxima cantidad de RAM es 16 GB. En la especificación detallada lo que dice es que 16 GB de RAM es la cantidad máxima con la que Lenovo vende una variante de esta laptop, nada más. Yo llevó un año usándola con 32 GB de RAM. Solamente la encendí una vez con sus tristísimos 8 GB de RAM de fábrica. Si no le van a poner más RAM, entonces busquen otra laptop.

Por otro lado, un punto sumamente agradable es que el SSD que incluye está ocupando el slot pequeño, y no el más estándar de 80 mm (M.2 2280), así que es muy fácil que quede con dos SSDs y así no dejar de aprovechar el que ya incluye. El slot 2280 también es PCIe Gen 4 (por ahí andan datos falsos volando que dicen que es Gen 3), así que se va a calentar si le instalan uno rápido, y la laptop no trae un pad térmico extra para este slot, por lo que les recomiendo que compren un disipador de metal delgado para laptop (aquí en Amazon venden unos) o al menos un pad térmico ancho que alcance a hacer contacto con el metal de la tapa.

En cuestión del display, pues cumple y ya; nada sobresaliente. El sonido es mediocre. La batería es mala (ya lo había mencionado). Y la laptop se siente decente al tacto; es lo suficientemente sólida. En estos aspectos, cumple con lo que se puede esperar de un modelo de su gama, excepto por, tal vez, su batería.

En conclusión, esta laptop tiene una excelente relación calidad-precio, y para quienes saben qué esperar de ella, es una muy buena compra; pero no se la puedo recomendar a todos porque sus 8 GB de RAM iniciales la hacen inutilizable para quienes no están dispuestos a hacerle la mejora.

I generally don't like to give corporations free advertising, but this thing really impressed me. I bought it to play 3 games streets of rage 4, never winter nights, and retroarch. I was debating about getting a switch, or steam deck, but I am glad I got this.

I can't believe how powerful the CPU is in this. The 2 pictures are of the legion and my liquid cooled 5600x. The legion almost beats it in everything, but most important is the single core score of 3600 which is really high, and what games need. Can't believe they sell this for 600. Just the screen and cpu alone are worth that.

The screen is top notch, it's almost as good as my 120 OLED tv, the colors are great, the black uniform is decent, and in some ways it's better, it does white better than a oled can. Oleds have a tint on white screens this is doesn't, it is really a high quality screen.

It plays streets of rage 4 at max settings and it's native resolution fine. It can do never winter nights at around 60 fps on high settings, which is surprising good. It's that 3600 CPU doing it, nwn is old and can't use a lot of cores.

I was worried it would be hard to control mouse and keyboard games with this, but it has everything you need a touch pad, mouse wheel, and more importantly the control software they give you is excellent.

That is a big one, most companies get the hardware right, but fail miserable at the software side, making it a night mare to control, or worse it's just bloat spy ware, looking at you Alienware. The program they give you works super well, easy to use, and does everything you want, from fan control, updates, onscreen keyboard, shortcuts, and its linked to one of the buttons.

It stays very cool, for such a powerful machine the fan system they use is definitely good. The controllers are easy to use, they are backwards of the switch, they slide down not up to take them off, which had me for a second.

This machine is Superior to all hand helds out there, by leaps and bounds. The only down side is it is a bit heavy. title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
With appropriate performance expectations this is a great gaming handheld, you can emulate basically all consoles up to PS3 and play them well along with playing PC games at reasonable settings. Keep in mind the integrated graphics on this are not going to match a dedicated graphics card, but setting the resolution and quality low will enable you to play a lot of AAA PC games.

I own this and the original ROG Ally Z1 Extreme, I find myself preferring this handheld thanks to the larger screen though I wish the resolution was lower on this device and the screen was VRR. At 1600p this screen is very sharp, though it would still be sharp at 1200p considering a 24-inch monitor is plenty sharp at 1080p. Colors on this device are vibrant and it gets bright enough for me. I wish it was HDR for an improved picture but that's probably in works for the future.

Speakers are okay with this, top-firing was an odd choice. They get plenty loud and sound alright but the ROG Ally is superior here. The speakers are more than serviceable though.

Controls are great for the most part. The sticks work great and feel very comfortable to use. The device overall is comfortable to hold and use plus you can set this up using the included kickstand and detach the controllers or use a third-party controller. All the face buttons are great though the d-pad is much more inset than I expected and sort of odd. The triggers are great and I have no issues with them. I understand the choice for the buttons on the back of the device as they are not symmetrical, but it takes some adjustment to get used to. The FPS mode for having mouse control is pretty neat and just adds to the flexibility of this device. No issues with the touchscreen or touchpad, touchpad is on the small side though.

Performance wise, without a frame counter on screen this feels the same as my ROG Ally at basically the same resolutions and settings. I can't discern a performance difference in any games without looking at specs on screen.

Would I recommend this device? Possibly, if you want a gaming handheld now and are not interested in waiting for the new generation, then yes. New handhelds will be releasing with the newer generation of AMD processors, these will perform better than the current generation by a substantial amount thanks to the newer integrated graphics. I'd readily recommend this over the original ROG Ally Z1 Extreme for several reasons: integrated kickstand, larger screen, included case, the Legion Go has not ruined a 1TB micro-SD card for me, more features, etc. The Legion Go battery is also lasting longer than my ROG Ally which has been great. Realistically, a laptop may be a better choice depending on your needs, you can get a lot more performance and some user upgradability past storage.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
I have gone through dozens of mice trying to find one that's shaped enough for my hands, that will also allow me to reach the buttons. From mini Gaming mice to more high end models, I have had suggestions, comments, and samples, with most being either are too wide, or too long, poor quality, and so on. I have a modified Palm/Finger grip, or something...and occasionally pick up the mouse too. So, I have been expecting less and less, the more I look. I was ready to make my own mouse. A good mouse needs to fit like a good pair of shoes. If they aren't comfortable the first time you try them on, they probably aren't going to be later.
Enter the M500. I expected an OEM gaming mouse, a few frills, and it looks like it too. Lenovo has had good products, a little pricey, with poor support and/or software. It's smooth tracking and quality switches are typical of more pricey mice, and it's got a funky ego shape that really works. In fact your thumb ends up where it normally is as you hold your hands relaxed: slightl/almost under your index finger. Plus it gives a slight tilt of your wrist too, which means less fatigue later on. Most people who know nothing of ergonomics are not going to like it at first, just like tented splitkeyboards, but it works.

Pros:
Tracking and tuning are simple, and work
Ergonomic shape (it's not flat)
Great for smaller/medium hands.
Simple software supports macros, surface tuning, and some colour settings.
Real grip sides
Configurable LEDs that don't overglow
Light weight (but a single weight is included).
Quality switches and sensor
Flexible and light braided cable.
Great for everyday use too!

(Possible) Cons:
Light weight might turn some off, or feel "cheap" even with the include weight.
Larger hands might find this an odd shape
No track record on a first gaming mouse for Lenovo.
Lighting isn't so bright (brightness settings are limited).
Software only has basics, and might be too simple for some.
Ergo shape might turn off more "traditional" gamers.
Could have more buttons.

title: 4.0 out of 5 stars
text:
[This review is for a refurbished M720S 16GB / 512GB SSD]

Measured at about 3.5" x 10.5" x 13.5" the M720S is a nice little compact desktop. It is sturdy built and Includes 8 USB ports, microphone and headset port, and 2 DVI (display ports). Of course the downside of such size is the limited ability of upgrades, however the M720S can easily host an extra drive and 3 extra PCI cards (including a graphic card) as long as they are low profile (2.5" high). The one I got also has a laptop style DVD drive. I would give this computer 4/5 due to limited overall performance.

Now if you decided to buy this machine the 2nd question is, should I buy it here on Amazon? And here it is questionable. The machine is refurbished, you don't get to see the actual machine you will be getting, so they make you feel like you will get a like-new machine, but mine had some scratches on it and the packaging was very minimal and it sat in Styrofoam which broke and pieces of it were embedded in the computer grill and had to be manually cleaned. There was not even a "fragile" or a "this side up" sticker on the box. I can see how this can easily be a DOA due to shipping.

Moreover, the packaging was missing the DVI to HDMI plug which makes it impossible to connect to any modern screen. I had to contact Amazon to get a replacement and they sent me a new cable for free. I decided to buy from Amazon, which is more expensive than other outlets, because I thought it would be hassle-free and the box will be new, however it was not the case.

Remember that this machine can be found in many different configurations, as far as CPU architecture and speed, memory size, and drive size. It looks the same from the outside, but you are paying for what's inside. In any event never get a machine that cannot be upgraded to Win 11, that would substantially limit the lifetime on it.

A word about software- the machine comes with a brand new Win 11 install, it has no issue and does not come with any bloatware or adware that I could see. The WiFi / BT plugin works well. If you intend to use this machine for gaming, be prepared to add a $100 graphics card to make this machine viable for gaming, otherwise it is a nice home-office machine.

Summary:
Pros:
1. Nice form factor
2. Relatively cheap i7 CPU
3. Win 11 software / no bloatware
4. Reliable manufacturer / return policy
5. DVD drive, lots of SSD space
6. Easy to upgrade

Cons:
1. It is not 'like new' shape
2. Bad packaging - missing add-ons
3. On-board GPU is not good enough for gaming and has DVI out only
4. Needs plug for WiFi / BT (supplied as extra in box)

Overall 3.5 / 5, I rounded it up to 4 since at the end I am happy with the purchase, but really the packaging here should be better. Hope this was helpful for you to make a decision.

You will understand what I mean if you put it on. Since the top part that lays above the head is stretched with springs, there is no need to constantly adjust to find a decent spot. I work in a call center. When I started there, they gave me the option to either buy my own headset, or have them take the $40-50 for the gaming headset they usually get out of my first two paychecks. I chose the latter.

That other headset didn't even last 6 months, before the plastic near the earpiece pivot broke, and the earpiece was just hanging there. So I went looking for something better. I was looking for three things: one, it needed to be sturdier; since I can't go buying a new headset every few months. Two, it needed to be more comfortable; the other headset made me sore where it sat on the top of my head. And three, it needed to not be super-expensive, since despite being employed, I'm still living below the poverty line.

This headset gets a green check mark for all three of those points. The metal top makes it super durable (not to mention cool-looking), the spring and cushion system makes them way more comfortable than my old ones (plus they don't fall off so easily when I have to lean over or tip my head back), and the price, while a little on the high side for me, was worth it for the quality. title: 4.0 out of 5 stars
text:
Having recently built a home lab, I've been gathering up some mini PCs here and there, especially a Lenovo ThinkCentre M720Q Tiny. I happened to be in the market for a dedicated shelf for this ThinkCentre I picked up recently, and the Amazon Vine program pointed me to this 1U rack mount, so I couldn't help but order one!

This is the Freejia 1U Mini PC Rack Mount for the Lenovo ThinkCentre tiny PCs. It's a 1U rack that holds one ThinkCentre in the middle, along with its power adapter. It includes all the necessary screws and cage nuts to get it up and running on your server rack, so you only need a screwdriver. The ThinkCentre M720Q Tiny is a perfect fit through the cutout, and it only sticks out about half an inch (about the length of the front plastic faceplate).

Some of the quirks I've found with this shelf is that the hinging part feels a little flimsy. With the whole weight of the shelf, along with the mini PC and it's power adapter, there's significant sag to it when you unscrew one side and swing it out. It's not something I'd trust fully swung out without holding one side with your hand. The hinge is just a thin metal rod riveted into place, with the metal mounting bit swinging freely. Keep the cable length behind the PC in mind if you intend to access it frequently, otherwise you won't be able to swivel it out all the way without disconnecting cables.

Another quirk to this shelf is attaching the PC to it. My M720Q had an unused Wifi antenna connector in the back, which obstructed its ability to fit onto the shelf. However, there was another screw hole on the opposite corner of the PC's backside, which gave me a place to put in the thumb screw but the PC would end up being upside down. I didn't want to see the ThinkCentre logo upside down on my shelf, so I ended up mounting the whole shelf upside down, contrary to how it shows in the Amazon listing photo. It still holds up though, as the PC is supported by the thumb screw, and the power adapter is held in tightly with those straps. There's a couple other PCs under it, so it won't have a long way to fall if I rig up additional support underneath it.

Quirks aside, it still perfectly functions as a dedicated 1U shelf for my ThinkCentre PC, which was what I really wanted by the end of the day. For about $36, it's reasonably priced for a 19-inch shelf, though I would not base a major part of the purchasing decision on the hinging functionality. Overall, I'm still quite satisfied with it!

title: 3.0 out of 5 stars
text:
I purchased the Freejia Mini PC Rack Mount primarily to consolidate my home server setup and create a cleaner, more organized workspace. I was looking for a secure and reliable rack mount for my Lenovo ThinkCentre mini PC, and this option seemed like a good value, especially considering its compatibility with 19-inch cabinets. After installing it and testing it for a couple of weeks, I’m generally pleased with its performance, though there's one significant design issue I want to highlight.

The mount itself is constructed from high-strength steel and feels solid and well-built. It fits snugly into my 19-inch server rack, and the hinged design with hand-twist screws is easy to install and adjust. The mount’s design is compatible with Lenovo ThinkCentre 1U mini PCs, which was a key requirement. It provides a stable platform for my mini PC, and it’s noticeably cleaner than simply placing it on the rack.

The high-strength steel construction suggests a good level of durability, and the hand-twist screws allow for fine adjustments to ensure a secure fit. The mount’s compact size is also a plus – it doesn’t take up much space in my server rack.

However, and this is a crucial point, the single screw attachment for the mini PC is surprisingly insecure. The screw only partially engages with the mounting points on the PC, resulting in noticeable wobble, particularly if the rack is bumped or moved. This is a significant design flaw that compromises the stability of the mount. I've had to use additional padding to minimize the movement.

While the overall construction is good, this single screw attachment detracts significantly from the product's overall value. It suggests a lack of attention to detail in the design.

Despite this issue, the mount is still functional and provides a decent solution for mounting a mini PC in a rack. With a minor adjustment (perhaps a secondary screw or a more robust mounting bracket) this could be a near-perfect product.

My experience has been a constant source of frustration, and I sincerely hope that Lenovo will recognize the extent of my dissatisfaction and agree to replace the dock.

Pretty good overall. Most laptop bags wouldn't fit my Legion 7i Pro and I wanted something to protect it that I could also use for a few books etc. It keeps its formvery well and can stand upright on its own both when it is full and empty. That's also a tradeoff because it's form will naturally limit how much you can store in it, but it's big enough for a laptop, tablet, large textbook along with maybe a notebook and a bunch of smaller items. Laptop protection seems good but if you're want more drop protection you might want to stuff some additional padding in the bottom of the laptop pocket.

If you're using it exclusively for trasporting your laptop and gaming accessories like headphones, charger, even keyboard etc. it will well appointed with dedicated pockets for PC peripherals and devices.

The biggest downside IMO is that the zipper around the 'armor' outside pocket is a bit tight and you can to be careful to prevent it from snagging etc. This zipper issue is kind of annoying so I would give this a 4.5 stars if I could but it's not big enough of a deal to drop it to 4 stars.

Overall this is a good verstatle bag for play/office/school as long as you dont' mind being intentional about what you will bring with you and not try to overstuff it with a ton of books etc. If you have a smaller laptop, there are a lot more options available on the market as far as premium tech/travel bags like swissgear etc. But for larger gaming laptops you are really restricted in your options.

text:
Be careful if you have a cat. My kitten loves to play with things and especially dangling things such as zippers.

Today she got extremely stuck in the zipper tag and started panicking and it looked like she was about to tear her claw off. I had to wrestle her to get ahold of her paw and even then took me over a minute to get it out.

Very dangerous oversight in a design choice that adds nothing to the backpack. That being said I understand it's a niche error that I would have likely overlooked as well. I was able to remedy the issue (or at least I hope so), by wrapping electrical tape over the zipper hole.

If Lenovo were to update this item, I would personally opt for an engraved logo instead of fully cutting through it. I would imagine that depending on the manufacturing process this could be a cheaper method of production although it would technically use more material so depending on if it's a cast piece or cut that would vary.

Other than that, it's an excellent backpack with solid construction and layout for the price. The top connection for the straps seems a bit thin but it's a very wide flat rope(?) and I would trust one of them to support my body weight. No sign of wear/breakage a couple of weeks in.

To add some more thoughts: I would honestly much rather have no branding on it as I don't like possible thieves knowing I have a gaming laptop in there. Even if MacBooks are typically the same price if not much more expensive, I have no doubt that this backpack's pointless branding makes it a prime target. I have placed stickers over the legion branding, but this last point may be a pointless concern.

Thin laptops just don't have many ports. And when my portable secondary display died, I did some self-assessment and thought: you have a multi-monitor setup on your desk, how often do you use your portable display on the go or is it mostly at home? Given some changes in my life, I decided I am better off just getting this sort of splitter for now.

As far as I can tell, from a construction/design point, pretty much all of these are about the same: a rectangle covered in ports with a tail. Plug-and-play it is, and almost every port I tried worked on the first try. The notable exception was that it will not acknowledge the second HDMI port if the first is not in use. Frustrating but not terrible. Given the compatible device list is just a jumble of words, I don't of they would blame that on my brand of laptop, but it is a mainstream LG model. I will also note the refresh rate when even using one additional display is rough, but I just want more desktop real estate for additional browser windows and reference documents, so I didn't mind much. I also got pretty low power draw on the USB ports, even the C, but again, not using my laptop to charge other devices typically. In short, effective for basic use, but limited if you are demanding a lot from it, along with a multidisplay quirk makes for four stars from me.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
This dual-pack Lenovo PC VESA bracket is crafted from a dense metal, providing a stable mounting platform for Lenovo tiny computers onto a VESA mount. The paint finish is a uniform and excellent coating. However, the brackets have a substantial weight, which may pose challenges for monitors with limited weight capacity.

The mounts are compatible with most Lenovo series, as the dimensions remain consistent across generations. I’ve confirmed the fit with P330, m90q Gen 3, and P3. Based on my experience the list would be quite extensive as to which PCs it would fit.

While it’s a great mount, air flow might be a consideration for some Lenovo tiny models that have ventilation on the top of the lit. This ventilation could be partially obstructed by the bracket.

Overall, the product is well-made and of high quality. I would recommend it, but potential buyers should be aware of the added weight and airflow issues.

title: 4.0 out of 5 stars
text:
I got this TUDIOW Protective Case for Lenovo Legion Go Gaming Handheld 2023, Shock-Absorption Anti-Scratch Non-Slip PC Protective Cover with4 Thumb Grip Caps for Lenovo Legion Go 8.8'' Accessories (Black)

This protective case is decent for everyday protection, but it’s important to know its limits. I don’t think it would do much to prevent damage if the Lenovo Legion Go were dropped hard, as it’s not heavily padded. That said, it does a good job protecting the device from scratches, scuffs, and general wear during regular use or when setting it down.

The case fits well and adds some grip without making the handheld feel bulky. One of my favorite parts is the included thumb grip caps. I wasn’t a fan of the low concave shape of the Legion Go’s original thumb sticks, and these caps raise them up just enough to feel more comfortable and improve control. Overall, it’s a nice accessory for scratch protection and better thumb stick feel, just not something I’d rely on for serious drop protection.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text: I have a Lenovo E15 Gen 4 Intel laptop model 21E6007QUS and have been using this cover for almost a year. I realize that the vendor states that this is only for the AMD version, which is just slightly smaller than the Intel version, however after reading a couple of other reviews from people who had the Intel version, I figured it was worth a shot as I am very particular about protecting my tech products from scratches or other damage. The clear cover that I have is a tight fit, but I wouldn't want a loose fitting cover as I think that movement between the laptop and the cover might actually cause scratches. I have had the case on and off about three times since my purchase. Each time I have removed the cover, I have checked for any scratches under the areas where the small tabs hold the cover in place and have found absolutely no damage whatsoever. It is not easy to get on and off, however once it's on, it feels very secure. I searched everywhere and could find no other similar cover for my laptop that was designed for the Intel version and I'm sure that there are others who are in the same situation. I would highly recommend this cover for the E15 Gen 4 Intel version, even though it's not supposed to fit. It may not be designed to fit the Intel version, but in my opinion, it fits like a "tight glove", but if it can be installed, looks good, and doesn't cause any scratches, what else could you ask for? You may have to bend it slightly when installing it but if done carefully, it should not cause scratches. I do want to specify that my laptop is the Mineral Gray color, which would probably not show scratches as easily as a black laptop, but even after checking with a magnifying glass, I can see no scratches. I hope this helps someone else who is looking for a cover for the E15 Intel version.
