title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
I take FAR too many photos with my phone! It’s hard to stop myself until I use up ALL my memory on it! (Which happens quite regularly).
I’d purchased a Blanbok memory flash stick a few months ago and was using it to transfer/save my photos from my iPhone (8). It was working great until something happened last week, and now I’ve tried everything the seller recommends to fix the problem & it still won’t copy photos to the device anymore.

I just got this JD Drive photo stick a few days ago. It’s not as easy to create folders and they’re more of a learning curve with it, but the seller does have some YouTube tutorials which are helpful.
The BEST thing for me so far, in the few days I’ve been using it, is the BACKUP feature!!! It took several days to back up all 37,600 photos & videos on my iPhone, but now they’re all safe! I’m traveling away from home and have a small hard drive I’m putting the backup on as well- just to make sure my photos are safe in 2 places before I start deleting them off my phone.
To do the backup, at first I was scared & kept stopping because of the message on the page about how much could be deleted. The wording made me unsure if it was automatically deleting what it was backing up. After watching the tutorial video, I found out it’s just telling you how many photos have been backed up that you COULD delete them IF you want to.
The other thing that’s great about this memory stick is that it stays plugged in better. I was able to keep my phone in my pocket while the stick was busy backing up. I was able to back up around 5000-10,000 every full phone charge (depending on how large the photo or video file was and also how completely my phone was charged. It did take several hours each time, and multiple days, to back up all 37,000 photos. (At one time recently, I had 42,000!)
Another positive is that I was able to do other things on my phone or even turn the screen off and it would keep backing up in the background. And it knew which photos & how many were left to be backed up each time I restarted the process. It makes a backup of each album you have in your iPhone. You can also back up your contacts. And you can backup your iPad.
I haven’t tried this yet for watching movies on my iPad, which I’d like to do. That’s next to try.
I’ve only had this less than a week and the Blanbok drive was working great for 5 months. So time will tell if this continues to work. But at least I know I’ve got my precious memories backed up and safe.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
Using this off-brand keyboard for a few days fixed the official name-brand keyboard. I know this is a ridiculous claim, but here's what happened:

At work we have an iMac for secondary purposes (such as making sure stuff also works on iOS and watching Netflix). It doesn't get used much, but it is beyond its warranty. The $50+ official Macintosh keyboard that came with it one day suddenly stopped responding to presses of the spacebar. (Everything else still worked.) I removed, cleaned, and reattached the spacebar a few times, and also rebooted the machine several times, but the spacebar would not start working again. (Apparently spacebar failure is very common in official Macintosh keyboards.)

For the sake of typing the space character, I hooked up a for-Windows PC USB keyboard that I bought at the second-hand thrift store for a whole dollar. I also reattached the original Mac keyboard for the usefulness of its extra buttons such as the volume controls. This was an acceptable arrangement for a while, but then the Mac spacebar started to get and remain "stuck," even after I fully removed the physical key. (The experienced effect was that web pages would scroll all the way down, because that's what typically happens when you hammer the spacebar when no input field has focus. Netflix playback also experienced seizures because the spacebar pauses and resumes videos.)

I detached the fancy-pants aluminum keyboard because of its latest malfunction, leaving us with just the plain ol' PC keyboard. Again, this was a mostly acceptable solution, but we eventually decided we should get an operating-system-appropriate keyboard since the Windows key doesn't behave like the Quatrefoil key and the PC F[unction] keys don't do any of the extra stuff that the Mac F[unction] keys do, so we ordered this one for $20.

After a few days of use, I was about to put away the old Mac keyboard when I thought of trying one more test: I went to keyboardtester-dot-com, plugged in the old keyboard and started mashing keys. To my surprise, the spacebar was working properly again!

We put this new keyboard back in its box and we're holding on to it as an emergency backup, but unless the official Mac keyboard craps out again, we'll probably never ever use it again (for lack of need).

By the way, this "Macally 103 Key Full-Size USB Keyboard with Short-Cut Keys for Mac" isn't really full-size; it's about an inch narrower than an actual "full-size" keyboard, which is achieved by smooshing the arrow keys and the six above between the main keys and the num pad, so its actually a "compact keyboard (with num pad)."

The keys are comfortable to press, but one person said she kept getting confused by the compact arrangement of the arrows and the six above. I should knock a star off for this, but this product earns an extra 10 stars for A) having a functioning spacebar, B) fixing the other keyboard, and C) not being *incredibly* overpriced like everything else for Mac is.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
There are so few true bargains on Amazon - this, though, is one of them.

We've got an older Macbook that has been working well, but was recently replaced and this one handed down to the kids. Needless to say, there was an 'accident' with a can of soda on the keyboard, and half the keys were destroyed. There is no way the value of the computer would've been worth replacing the keyboard (which had always been problematic in this particular mac), so I figured adios.

Well, at least one last try before adios, which was the purchase of this keyboard. It's cheap, so how could we go wrong? The keyboard is full sized (as in very full sized) and hangs over the edge of the Macbook, which is a 15 incher. Plugged it into the USB port, had a pop-up menu that recognized the keyboard, and viola...instant new keyboard for old mac computer!

We don't need a mouse since the touch pad still works fine. I'm typing on it right now, in fact, and the keys are light. They don't feel cheap at all; in fact, it's a lot more pleasant to type on this vs. the laptop's original keyboard (that particular keyboard for the model of Macbook has been a huge pain and was replaced once before.)

There are very few things you can buy for $15 that solve a problem as well as this keyboard. The kayboard is nice, but sure, it's not lovely to look at, hanging over the edge of the laptop. But so what? It works great! And the kids like sitting back with the keyboard in their laps (it's got a nice length to it) and doing video games.

This was an inexpensive solution that will enable us to get at least another year out of an old laptop. I couldn't be more pleased!

title: 4.0 out of 5 stars
text:
After extensive researching, this is one of a handful of controllers I've found that supports direct input mode on PC. This protocol allows the gyro and extra buttons to be seen by the OS and bound to things like keyboard presses via Steam Input or other programs.

This functionality is highly sought after, but for some reason controller manufacturers dont yet realize this. Holding the star and B buttons while powering on the controller in 2.4ghz mode enables direct input. I'm including this information because for some reason it is not in any of the manuals or information provided by the manufacturer.

Pros:
- Direct Input mode!!! This cannot be overstated enough. On PC the additional buttons and gyro functionality are very helpful for flightsim games.
- Value: This controller provides excellent build quality, features, and a charging dock at a very reasonable price.
- Onboard profile storage. Storing up to 3 profiles is great and they can be swapped to with a single button press.
- Inputs feel great. Buttons have just the right amount of travel, they arent clicky, but arent excessively long either. Sticks are very smooth and accurate.

Cons:
- Powering on the controller via the power button seems to revert from direct input back to xinput. Most of the time if I just pick it up from the charger it auto-wakes into direct input mode, but sometimes still reverts to xinput here as well and needs a reboot. There needs to be a way to force the controller to stay in direct input mode. Perhaps this can be a setting in the Ultimate Software profile.
- Auto power off. It shuts off after about 15 minutes of inactivity. For my use case, this is a bit annoying as I will regularly leave it inactive, but need to pick it up and have it ready on a moments notice. There is no way to disable the auto-power off, this should be a setting in the Ultimate Software as well. You can get the controller to stay on by plugging it in, but that defeats the purpose of a wireless controller.

Feedback for 8BitDo if you read these reviews:
- Thumbsticks: The thumbstick caps are removable, it would be amazing if there were longer thumbstick caps available for purchase.
- Direct Input mode: This feature should be more evident in your marketing, and more supported by your software. Many PC users desperately want this functionality, and you have it. But the steps to take advantage of this functionality are nowhere in your manuals or documentation. I had to find it in a random reddit post. Also, it needs some work as the controller frequently reverts back to xinput mode. A firmware update addressing this would be very welcome.
- Also a firmware update allowing users to disable the auto-shutoff feature would be great!

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
This is a great keyboard. I am using it on Apple products (a Macbook Pro, a MacBook Air, an iPad, and an iPhone) and haven't had any problems connecting with each of the devices or switching between devices. I haven't had the keyboard long enough to rate the battery life, but I will check back in when I do have to change batteries to give an update. The keys are satisfying to type on and I feel right at home with the configuration being nearly identical to any of my devices built in keyboards or the Mac Magic Keyboard.

I think this keyboard has many advantages to the user who wants to own and use a Magic Keyboard but doesn't want to shell out the $99 for one. I use one at work, and I like it well enough, but for when I work at home, this keyboard actually has more features that I find useful than the Magic Keyboard.
1. I can switch between devices quickly after I set them up with (command+1, command+2, or command+3), which makes switching between my two Macbooks a breeze.
2. It takes maybe a second to unpair and repair to the newly selected device. This is a fantastic feature that is not included on the Magic Keyboard.
3. Being pensive about buying a non-mac keyboard, a lot of other keyboards reviews on Amazon talk about lag between the keyboard and the computer, but there isn't any more lag on this than the Magic Keyboard, which is to say there isn't any lag that I can perceive. When you press a key, it registers on the screen immediately, even in a flurry of keystrokes.
4. There is an on/off button on the side, but I haven't been using that, instead opting for the keyboard to shut itself off when it is no longer being used. It does so, and I will report back on the battery life at a later date, as I said above. When I come back to the keyboard when it is off, I just press a key and within about 3 seconds I am up and running on the last device it was paired with.

Overall, I am very impressed with this keyboard's price, features, and usability. I am glad I didn't shell out $99 for an official Magic Keyboard from Apple, at least at this point. On a side note, I bought the 4 year extended warranty for a $1 and change just to cover my investment, so I will also report back if anything breaks or dies on the keyboard, but I don't see that happening.

Bottom line, a great keyboard with easy device switching at a great prize with zero lag. I would definitely recommend this keyboard to anyone using a Mac and not wanting to pay full price for an official Apple keyboard.

text:
I bought this one after an unexpectedly disappointing experience with an Arteck multi-device Bluetooth keyboard. The Macally keyboard is very good indeed. Good design, good keys, got paired with all of my devices in less than 5 minutes. I don't think that you get what you pay for always: there are crappy expensive products, and there are excellent cheap ones. Personally, I learned to go on case by case basis. This keyboard is well made. In the UK at least, if you want a multi-device Bluetooth keyboard, what are the choices? Cheapie keyboards that rattle and flex as you're typing on them aren't going to be anyone's everyday keyboard. Something like Logitech M380 may well be a good keyboard, but not everyone wants round keys. I certainly didn't. There was also a gamers' keyboard that looked interesting - but then your keyboard would be lighting up orange or blue or whatever. I wasn't keen on those additional attractions, but I did want a well designed, high quality Bluetooth keyboard that allowed switching between 3 devices. That's how I bought this Macally, and I definitely recommend it.

Update Feb 2021. I am still happy with the keyboard, but note that if you use your keyboard a fair bit, you'll need to change batteries pretty much every 6-7 weeks. And that's with switching the keyboard off overnight every day without fail. Considering the price of this keyboard, it should have been better thought out in terms of battery consumption, or made rechargeable through USB. Initially rated as 5 star, now 4.

Update Feb 2022. All good. Still my main keyboard, doing noble service.

Update Sept 2022. The keyboard abruptly stopped working, and putting in new batteries didn't help. It was dead. I contacted Macally who asked me for my Amazon invoice, which I sent them immediately. Then the rep said that, as I purchased the item through Amazon but from a seller called Dureg, and Dureg are the ones handling UK warranty issues, I should email Dureg directly - and I did. A bit later response came from Dureg, instructing me to send the keyboard to GERMANY! So the UK buyer is to track down a suitable courier and to pay out of pocket to send this faulty item to Germany, after which who knows what will happen and how soon. And if this is your main keyboard, as it is for me, and you need it for work, well, too bad. And this keyboard cost £50 in November 2020, just so you know.
So there you have it, fellow UK buyers. I am changing the rating from 4 stars to 2 stars. One star would have been too harsh, as the keyboard is very good when it works. But when it stops working, that's how we, the buyers, find out that we'd been let down by the manufacturer.

It’s just okay, does the job but not without discomforts.

I’ve worn this cover for a month and wanted to give it some time before I wrote a review, and I just noticed the side is already breaking. Good thing there were 2 snap-on covers in the package.

The cover does a decent job of keeping the watch protected, but adds bulk even if it’s clear. This is expected. It snaps on easily enough, and I presume it’ll snap off easily too, especially given that one side is partially broken now.

I found that the screen lost some sensitivity, and I disagree with the reviews that claim otherwise. It’s not a huge loss, but the part that did annoy me was the knob-button is harder to use with the cover on. There’s no issue pressing the button or holding a finger over it for the ECG function, but so much of the sides are covered by the protector that it’s hard to turn. I have to use my nail on ridge to turn it in tiny increments. I wish there was a more functional way to keep the watch protected.

I tried showering with the cover on and it’s not waterproof. Water got stuck btwn the watch face and the protector.. Also, I noticed some suds got stuck along the sides. I didn’t remove the cover to dry the watch to see how long the water lasts and on the face, it was at least 2 days and the sides took a day to dry out, with me trying to wedge a paper towel on the edge to soak up water.

But my biggest gripe is that the edges of the sides hang lower than the profile of the watch and dig into my skin. It’s uncomfortable and leaves deep indents on my skin, so I find myself pushing the watch up and down my arm to give the skin under the edges some relief. So now that the first cover is breaking after a month of wear, I’m considering not using the second cover and looking for a different option. I used the watch for 3 weeks without screen protector and nothing got damaged, so I wonder if I need anything at all.

This keyboard is replacing my much more expensive mechanical switch keyboard at work. That’s because I have specific requirements that the mechanical keyboard can’t do. I have to type patient progress notes while I’m seeing patients in the office or via videoconference. So the mechanical keyboard was too noisy, even though it had linear switches. Also, desktop space is at a premium, so I need a small keyboard. I prefer a wired keyboard because my previous wireless keyboard missed keystrokes when passers-by tried to pair their cellphones with my desktop computer’s bluetooth receiver. (I have no idea why they wanted to do that.)

Therefore, this keyboard met all of my requirements. Set-up is simple: plug-and-play into a USB-A jack. Despite being very lightweight, it still has a good feel and is easy to type accurately. It also has cursor keys, which my previous 60-key mechanical keyboard didn’t have. The keys actuate quickly for my work purposes, though I’m not sure how well it would work for gaming. My only complaint is the keycaps are labeled for use with Macintosh computers. I wish it came with additional keycaps for the standard Windows and Alt keys (instead of Command and Option).

The only problem I experienced is not with the keyboard itself, but how Amazon shipped this to me. They only put the keyboard, with its corrugated cardboard box, into an air-cushioned envelope. The first one I received was broken during shipment because something had fallen on it and crushed one side of the keyboard.

The replacement they sent also had the envelope and box punctured. Initially, the keyboard did not appear damaged. But when I used it, I found the space bar only worked intermittently. It would pick up a key press if I mashed it down really hard. So I had to return this one also. But Amazon only offered me a refund this time, without an option to get a replacement keyboard.

I suggest Amazon should package future shipments of this product in a box instead of an air-cushioned envelope.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
At this price I don't know of any other controller that boasts hall effect sticks and high polling rate wireless connectivity. Using it with my steam game library has been effortless. The controller is also advertised as being compatible with android and Nintendo switch. I didn’t test android support, but switch support works very well. The C6 makes a very compelling replacement for the switch pro controller, considering how much those cost.

The first thing you will notice when you hold the C6 in your hand is how relatively light weight it is. At first this was a turn-off for me; I like heavier electronics because I think they feel more premium. Maybe the other manufacturers believe this too, because every other controller I own weighs noticeably more. However, after a while I began to appreciate its low weight. Sometimes after playing for a couple hours with heavier controllers, one may begin to notice the controller and rest it on his lap. That doesn’t really happen with this controller. That being said, the weight of a controller isn’t very important to me. My satisfaction wouldn’t change if the controller’s weight were comparable to other popular options.

The second thing you’ll notice when you pick up the controller is the feel of the buttons, sticks, and controllers. The face buttons are excellent; they’re membrane but they still give really tactile feedback when you push them. Lately game controllers that use mechanical switches for the face buttons have become popular. The feel of the C6’s membrane face buttons approximate the feel of switches as much as a membrane button can, while still retaining the silence of membrane buttons. Suffice it to say they’re not mushy at all. The shoulder buttons and analog triggers are on par with other common controllers. It should be mentioned that the analog triggers don’t have much travel. This really only impacts racing games: shallow analog trigger travel makes precise throttle and brake control difficult. For most other types of games short trigger travel is preferable. The analog sticks are good. The best part about them (the hall effect sensors) is hard to observe when the controller’s new, but I imagine that in a few years when my other hall effect-less controllers start to drift, the benefits of hall effect sensors will really speak for themselves.

The weakest part of the whole controller is the d-pad. It works fine in games, but the feedback as you rock the d-pad around with your thumb isn’t as clearly defined as other gamepads. It wasn’t a turn off for me but it should be noted. The controller’s rumble is really impressive, likely due to the controller's low weight. It’s more powerful than most other controllers I’ve used. Some might not like that level of rumble strength, but fortunately for them it can be lowered. I really like the satin textured finish of the controller. It provides good grip, and doesn’t feel slippery or sweaty after long sessions like the switch pro controller does.

To my knowledge, the abxylute C6 is the best gamepad at the $30 mark. I highly recommend it.

text:
評判の良さに惹かれてAbxylute C5Pを購入しました。初めて使うコントローラーということもあり、最初から丁寧に使い心地や機能を確認しながらレビューしています。

◾️外観と持ち心地
手に取った瞬間から、しっかりした作りと軽さのバランスが印象的です。グリップ部分には滑り止め加工が施されており、長時間プレイしても手が疲れにくいのが特徴でした。これまで使っていた他のコントローラーよりも軽くて持ちやすく、アクションゲームや長時間のRPGプレイにも最適だと思いました。

◾️操作感と応答速度
Hallエフェクトジョイスティックのおかげで、ドリフトしにくく、細かい操作もストレスなくできるのがいいです。特にシューティングや格闘ゲームでは、キャラクターの動きやコマンド入力が非常にスムーズで、これまで使っていたコントローラーよりも反応の良さを実感しました。ボタンの押し心地も軽く、連打や素早い入力にもしっかり対応。ワイヤレス接続も安定していて、PC・Switch・PS5のいずれでもラグを感じることはほとんどありませんでした。Bluetoothだけでなくドングル対応できるのも、レスポンスが大事なゲームでは重要。

◾️カスタマイズ性と機能
背面のバックボタン（マクロ機能）は、最初はあまり使う機会がないかなと思っていましたが、実際に使ってみるとFPSや格闘ゲームで非常に重宝します。よく使うコマンドや特殊な操作をワンタッチで実行できるので、ゲームの勝率も上がった気がします。
Turbo機能は設定が簡単で、連打が必要な場面で活躍します。実際にTurbo機能が真価を発揮するのは、FPSや一部のアクション、シューティング系ゲームです。たとえば『Apex Legends』や『Valorant』、『PUBG』、『Fortnite』などのFPS・バトルロワイヤルゲームでは、セミオート武器の連打や一部の武器の速射が求められる場面が多く、Turbo機能があると指の負担が大きく軽減されます。また『モンスターハンター』シリーズなど一部のアクションゲームでも、連打が必要な武器や技でTurbo機能が役立ちます。

◾️プロコンとの比較
プロコンと比較すると、Abxylute C5Pはグリップの滑り止めや軽さ、バックボタン・Turbo機能などカスタマイズ性が高い点が大きな違いです。FPSや格闘ゲームでワンタッチ操作や連射を重視する方には、C5Pの方がより実用的だと感じました。

◾️振動・ライト・バッテリー
振動機能は4段階調整可能で、ゲームの臨場感を高めてくれます。RGBライトはシンプルながらも部屋の雰囲気を盛り上げてくれ、夜間にプレイする際にも映えます。バッテリーの持ちも良く、最大で約10時間連続使用できるため、普段使いなら数日に1回の充電で十分。充電も3時間ほどで完了するので、急な充電切れの心配も少ないです。

◾️多デバイス対応と注意点
PC、Switch、PS5と多デバイス対応で、1台でさまざまなゲーム環境に対応できるのも便利です。コスパも非常に良いと感じました。ただし、デバイスのモード切り替えが若干覚えにくいです。初めて使うときはどのボタンでどのモードに切り替わるのか分からず、何度かマニュアルを確認しました。メーカーの公式ページにはマニュアルが見当たらず、付属のマニュアルをスマホで撮影して保管しておくと、便利だと気付きました。

◾️まとめ
Abxylute C5Pは操作感・カスタマイズ性・コスパのどれもが高く、多デバイス対応で汎用性も抜群でした。マクロ機能やTurbo機能も便利で、特にFPSや一部のアクション、シューティング系ゲームで活躍します。背面ボタンや連射機能などカスタマイズ性が高く、実用的ただ。モード切り替えは最初だけやや覚えにくいですが、マニュアルをスマホで保管しておけば安心。コスパ重視の方や、長く使いたい方におすすめできるワイヤレスコントローラーだと思います。

I’m impressed. I’ve been gaming since the NES days, gone through more controllers than I care to count, and this thing actually holds its own. It’s got that nice heft—not too heavy, not cheap-feeling either—and the buttons have a really satisfying click. The sticks feel smooth, kinda like a modern Xbox pad but with a tighter snap-back.

Wireless is solid too. I didn’t notice any lag, even messing around with some shooters where I’d normally feel it. Battery life’s decent; I got a couple long sessions in before even thinking about charging.

If I’m nitpicking, the d-pad isn’t perfect—I’ve used better for fighters—but it’s not a dealbreaker. For the price, it’s kinda shocking how good it feels. Definitely doesn’t feel like some knockoff brand you’d regret buying.

If you guys are looking for a solid backup controller or even a main one without dropping 70 bucks on a big name, I’d say this is worth checking out.

text:
このブランドのゲームに対する情熱や思想に感銘を受けて買ってみたけど、なんか普通って感じ。

【C5P】
所見ではパンダに見えたので勝手にハチロクパッドと命名した。
きっとレースゲームで使えば峠の下りだけ速く走れるに違いない・・・気がする😂
スティック左右対称形でABXYボタンはXBOX配置の製品ってあまり多くはないのでやや貴重（カスタマイズ配置変更可能な機種の話は除く）。
スティックはドリフト防止のためのデッドゾーンが微量に存在するタイプでオフにはできない様子。
キャリブレーションなどガチゲーマーが最低限度要求する機能は見当たらない。
公式サイトも調べたけどアプリも見つからない。
ボタン類はポクポクなメンブレンで、十字キーは押下が深めで格闘ゲームに不向きに感じた。
ついでに技適マークが見当たらない。
ホールセンサー採用とは言え、玩具っぽいカジュアルゲーマー向きですね。
質感は安っぽいです。
パッケージは茶箱ですがただの箱ではないので風合いはあるかな。

【C8】
購入前にそうだろうと思ったけど、色が違うだけでHitabt S30AのOEMですね、全く同じです（どっちがオリジナルなのかは知らないけど、Hitabt S30AはAmazonでこの製品の三分の一以下の価格で売ってたので３つ買ってある😅）。
先日発売されたGRAPHT Omni Plusの充電ドック付き初回限定版も基本的に同じOEM品で背面ボタンが追加され、メカニカルキーになった程度の違いしかありません。
この製品のスティックもデッドゾーンがオフにできないタイプ。
キャリブレーションは出来ます。
拡張ボタンは本体下部にあるのでゲーム中に押すのは困難でしょう。
やはり技適マークが見つかりません。
これもアプリの情報は見つからず。
憶測ですが、マニアックな調整をしたければアプリのKeyLinkerが使えるかも、スマホ用アプリなので無線必要ですが。
カジュアルゲーマーには勿体ないが、ガチゲーマーは不満あるかもという微妙な製品です。
パッケージは大きな茶箱ですが、風合いがある作りです。

ってな訳で、
C5Pの評価は星３つ。
C8の評価は辛うじて星５つ、
平均で星４つの評価としました。

パッケージのみがブランドの思想や情熱を感じられるガレージファクトリーっぽいムードがあって好感を感じるのですが、
重要な中身が伴ってないのが残念に感じましたね😩

text:
I bought this controller mainly to use with my PC and Steam Deck, and I have to say it has exceeded my expectations.
First of all, the weight: only 186 g, which makes it very light, yet it still feels sturdy and well built. The Hall effect joysticks and triggers are incredibly precise and guarantee zero drift issues.
Responsiveness is where it really shines: both wired and with the dongle it reaches up to 1000 Hz polling rate, and you can immediately feel the difference. On PC, inputs are lightning fast, while on the Steam Deck it works perfectly in wireless mode, smooth and with no noticeable lag.
There are also some excellent extra features:

-Adjustable vibration with 4 intensity levels, so you can tune it to your liking.
-Turbo and Auto-Turbo modes, very handy for fast-paced games.
-6-axis gyroscope, which works on Nintendo Switch for a more immersive experience.

The built-in 600 mAh battery is another plus, with up to 18 hours of playtime as claimed by the manufacturer. From my experience, it lasts through long sessions without the need to recharge often.
Compatibility is simply amazing: besides PC and Steam Deck, it also works with macOS, Switch, Android, iOS, and even Tesla! Truly a universal controller that adapts to almost anything.
In the box you get everything you need: the controller, USB dongle, USB-A to USB-C cable, and manual, ready to go right out of the package.

In summary:
✅ Lightweight (186 g) yet solid
✅ Hall effect joysticks and triggers, no drift
✅ Up to 1000 Hz polling rate (wired and dongle)
✅ 4-level adjustable vibration, Turbo & Auto-Turbo
✅ 6-axis gyroscope (Switch only)
✅ 600 mAh battery, up to 18 hours of use
✅ Wide compatibility: PC, Steam Deck, macOS, Switch, Android, iOS, Tesla
✅ Comes with dongle, cable, and manual

This controller combines precision, lightness, and versatility. I’ve been using it daily and it has never let me down. Highly recommended if you’re looking for a serious, universal controller, at a cheap price!

text:
First thing that you will notice if you buy this is the quality – the drive itself is made of metal, and seems very solid. I also liked the packaging, it feels really premium.

The drive works as expected – I use it as a portable storage that I can plug into anything (computer via USB-A, laptop via USB-C, iPhone via lightning) without any extra adapters.

Be aware though – on an iPhone, it requires an app. It does NOT work without the app, and all transfers need to happen through the app.
The app is pretty easy to use and the suggestion to launch it pops up automatically as soon as you connect the drive, but it does creates nuisance for some use-cases. For example, you can't copy a folder from the drive directly to iCloud Drive (or Dropbox) – the app can only work with the local storage, or export files one-by-one via the "Share" button.

If 3rdParty app is a deal breaker for you, consider getting a microSD iPhone adapter instead – they work directly with the built-in "Files" app, and you can easily plug the card anywhere, so they essentially provide the same functionality.

Another issue is the heat. The drive get pretty warm even when you're not working with it (but leave it plugged in). I'm not sure what will happen if I try to copy 100 GB of data on it...

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
I recently started a new job where I have to use a MacBook Air Laptop. I'm one of those folks who wants a full-size keyboard and external mouse (not a trackpad). I had a Logitech Keyboard/Mouse combo that connected via USB-A that was both Mac and PC compatible. I used it for a few weeks but soon learned that it's pretty helpful to have a Mac-specific keyboard in the long run. [for me, it came down to the copy/paste keyboard shortcuts]

I started looking around and was astonished to see the cost of the Apple Keyboard and Mouse products. When I found this product for the price, I thought I'd give it a shot. I was very pleased and would recommend these items for several reasons:

Design and Build quality: The aluminum body of the keyboard is way more than I expected. It has a premium feel that I wasn't seeking, but enjoy. It's a full-size keyboard with a 10-key numeric, which I love. I appreciate the keyboard's design, especially the key height and responsiveness. Unlike some other brand models I've used, the keys here are comfortably low-profile, making typing more ergonomic and enjoyable. Overall, I'm satisfied with the feel and functionality it offers.

Sound: The keyboard is not overly crunchy or loud; comparatively, it's on the quiet side, but it's not silent. I have used many keyboards that are much noisier than this one, but, if I were on a conference call and typing while not speaking, I would hit the mute button. The mouse, however, is pretty silent. No sharp clicks from the L/R buttons. For me, that's very desirable. If you're looking for a mouse with more audible feedback, this one may not be for you.

Ease of Use & Connectivity: The set was as simple to connect as any Bluetooth headphones. Once I connected the keyboard/mouse combo via Bluetooth for the first time, I never needed to adjust, search, or reconnect. I've been using the set for about 3 months and I haven't encountered any lag or connection issues.

Charging: ***Micro USB Charging*** I was surprised to see that these items are charged via micro-USB (see pic). USB-C is now the norm, so this is not super convenient in my cable management setup; I would much rather have the now-standard USB-C charging connection that I use for almost all of my other devices (except, of course, the iPhone). But honestly, I have so many extra old micro-USB cords in my cord collection box that it was not an issue for me.

Battery Life: The charge on each of these has been between 2-3 weeks. The mouse loses charge faster than the keyboard. An incredible usability function that I really appreciated was that the devices can be used while charging. For example, one day I shook my mouse to wake up my computer an nothing happened. Eventually, I realized it was because my mouse was dead. But instead of having to switch to using my laptop keyboard and mouse (for me, personally highly undesirable), I was happy to learn that I could use my mouse while plugged into the micro-USB power cord. I let it charge while I used it and then some extra time after work. I don't know what the charge times are, but I've not encountered any noticeable issues with them.

Overall Experience: I'm extremely happy with this product and would recommend it, especially for the price.

Comparison with other products: I am not a native Mac user. I'm not able to compare this to other premium Mac products. For me, as a long-time PC user, I'm extremely happy to add this to my desktop setup and would recommend.

title: 4.0 out of 5 stars
text:
This is a very functional keyboard and mouse set. The set looks very aesthetically pleasing - I got the set in pink. I'm writing this review using the keyboard right now. The keys are easy to press and all of the keys work. On the one hand, the keys are very easy to depress and react instantaneously, so I can type really fast on this keyboard; on the other hand, sometimes random letters show up when I didn't press down on them but just brushed them on my way to the letter I meant to press. So I would say it's both easy and a little difficult to type using this keyboard - I have to be more precise than normal. The space bar on my keyboard sometimes isn't as responsive as the rest of the keys, so I end up skipping spaces because I'm using the same amount of force on all of the keys, including the space. These are all minor adjustments that are not too difficult to make - overall, it's nearly easy to type on this keyboard once you get used to it as on a full sized regular keyboard. In fact, the spacing of the keys feel pretty good - if not standard sized, it's close. I don't feel like my hands are cramped together when I type on this keyboard. The keys feel loose even though the mechanical action is there. The clicking sound is fairly quiet relatively speaking, which is what I wanted.

Connectivity is great. Both the keyboard and the mouse paired with my Samsung tablet without a hitch and reconnect immediately when they are turned on. The mouse works as well as any other bluetooth mouse I've used, though it is definitely cheaply built and I had a really hard time inserting the two required AAA batteries so that the mouse would turn on. I have never seen battery inserts that cheaply made - one of the connectors isn't even connected to the body of the mouse but is loose and free floating, albeit there's a wire soldered to it (I had to use one finger to hold it against the mouse in order to get the battery contact point to connect to the right spot).

The build quality of the keyboard and mouse is, unfortunately, super cheap. Both are flimsy, blendable, with parts that look to be holding by a hair, so they may not last long - time will tell, and I will return and update this review if they break in less than a year. The keyboard literally bows from just the action of typing... I kid you not. But it is super lightweight, so it's good for travel, and the price for the set was pretty cheap.

Now the GOOD part and why I gave this set four stars: There is a dedicated back navigation button on the keyboard - this is so convenient when using this keyboard with a tablet! ALSO, the keyboard comes with a bunch of shortcuts. This isn't mentioned anywhere in the package, but if you hit Command + "/" a keyboard shortcuts menu will pop up (the menu will differ if you are in Gmail or Calendar).

The keyboard comes with little sticky foam dots - stick those on tin bottom of the keyboard; they keep the keyboard from sliding around and make it so much more stable to type on!

title: 4.0 out of 5 stars
text:
This is a great mouse, close to what I was looking for. The signal is flawless and love that it uses a USB-C adapter that frees up a regular USB 3.0 port to be free for my other adapters. Make sure to peel off the plastic film underneath the mouse to get a better grip on the mouse pad unless you prefer having more glide, up to you. Love the DPI button, not going to use this, I'm comfortable with the first setting, but there may be users out there that appreciate having faster DPI, can't really think of what applications you would want faster than 1200 DPI though. Might want to consider creating an application to control the functions of the DPI or what the buttons do, but I'm guessing there's probably some third-party application that can do that, just haven't taken the time to look into that.

Constructive feedback:
-The mouse is on the smaller side for those with larger hands such as myself, my index and middle fingers are hanging off the front of the mouse because if I slide them back then my wrist isn't resting on the mouse at all, which isn't a dealbreaker honestly, that's why I bought it, but might want to consider making the mouse larger or at least offering a larger option.
-I absolutely dread these two buttons where your thumb is for going back or forward on web pages in the browser. Just a couple days of use I have found myself accidently hitting them and for the work that I do that involves data entry into a database it is a nightmare. I've had to resort to ripping these two buttons out of the mouse to prevent this moving forward. I find these two buttons to be completely useless.
-I'm not left-handed but if you are, this is not the mouse for you, designed solely for right-handed users only.
-The AA battery is tough to insert and even more so to remove, I think the design flaw is having a spring on both ends instead of just having it on one side for the negative part of the battery. That needs a redesign for sure. I have to smack the mouse a few times and sometimes have to bang it against a surface just to get the battery out. Needs to be an easier way to insert and remove the battery.
-Would love to see a USB-C insert on the front of the mouse, like I mentioned above I deconstructed the mouse just to remove the two buttons where your thumb is and there is plenty of room to add a USB-C receiver for charging the mouse, and if you're using a rechargeable AA battery like I am, that receiver could charge that battery, just something to think about, but I don't mind switching out the battery.
-The scroll wheel does not have the ability to move left or right to slowly (or quickly) scroll up and down a page if you know what I'm referring to. (a small white circle pops up on the page with up and down arrows) which is unfortunate. Sometimes I like to slowly scroll through something as I'm reading or showing other users the work I'm doing.

I'm writing this review after using the keyboard 4 or 5 weeks now.

Having a full keyboard at a smaller than usual size was a must - this keyboard is optimal in this discipline.
The keys feel very precise and sturdy, the backlit is super useful as usually I do not use artificial light and it tends to get pretty dark in my office beginning at early afternoon.

This one is a wired keyboard with USB but that's fine as I don't tend walking around with a big keyboard in my hands anyway.

I am utilizing this keyboard 5 days a week at least 9 hours a day - it's my business workplace. My hands and fingers would not show any sign of getting tired during a full workday.

Typing is very quiet and effortless.

The position, height, and size of the keys are perfect for my hands/fingers.

The only thing I don't like is a POWER button which is placed immediately above the BACKSPACE key. When typing fast - and in my job I have to type very fast I frequently hit the POWER button by accident once or twice a day which drives me nuts because all gets dark and I have to login again. I wish there was a setting that would disable this (for me) useless POWER button. I seriously thought about reducing my rate to 4 stars due to this design flaw but then again - it's my fault if I cannot target the BACKSPACE key right.
If there is a way to disable the POWER key - someone would make my life better quite a bit if you could gimme a hint.

A little wish for the next version: give me an indicator light for when my CAPS LOCK is on - I have to enter passwords all through the day and often I need two attempts because of CAPS LOCK.

All in all this is one of the best keyboards I ever had - probably as good as my Logitech Craft at not even a third of it's price. I am using the craft for maybe 5 or 6 years now at my other computer and it's literally indestructible. Will my new POWZAN hold that long? Time will tell.

ADDITION: I managed to make the power key blocked - pulled the key cap out, turned it a bit and put a piece of tape over it - happy - no accidental power outs anymore.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
Couldn't have asked for anything more. I wanted a Sega Genesis style controller with a USB connector to use on my retrogaming laptop, and that's exactly what this is. Will work fine on your Raspberry Pi-based rig, too.

This mimics a classic 6-button Genesis controller, with a mode button on the shoulder, start in the middle, three mains, and three secondaries.

D pad is responsive and feels good, not too stiff, not too soft. Seems to sit just a bit higher off the control pad than I remember the classic Genesis pads doing, but that's not been an issue. Lots of gameplay with no worn down thumbs.

Buttons are responsive, don't seem to get sticky or stuck, and work well. Shoulder-based mode button does not get accidentally clicked, so that's good. And overall, the whole thing feels fairly substantive and relatively sturdy, too. Not as sturdy as the originals, but also not a cheap throwaway, either.

Windows 10 recognizes this right away. No installation needed. Maps easy on most emulators, too.

I've primarily used it with Kega Fusion (all Sega systems), Higan (Snes), and Mesen (NES). Works great on all of them. Also works with my chosen TurboGrafx 16 emu.

No luck getting it to play nice with Stella (Atari 2600), some games were fine, most weren't. Spotty on a few others as well.

But for the ones I wanted it for -- Genesis, Master System, Game Gear, and the main Nintendo systems -- it's been a champ. For the price, this thing is great.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
Several years ago, laptop makers quietly stopped including DVD drives, and I’ve missed them ever since. I know it probably makes laptops lighter and sleeker, but I’ve always liked having the option to pop in a CD or DVD. I’m right at that in-between age where I was late to the whole streaming and digital-download thing…really late! I held on to my CDs and DVDs for as long as possible.

I found a stack of old DVDs from when my older kids were in preschool—a learning program about sight words and early reading. It was an expensive program at the time, and I don’t think they make it anymore. My youngest son is now five and the perfect age for it, so I really wanted to use it again. I used to play DVDs in a regular player, then later on our Xbox 360, which could read some DVDs but not all. Eventually the console stopped working, and no one used it anymore, so I boxed it up. Now, years later, I realized I didn’t have anything left that could play a DVD at all.

That’s what led me to get this external drive. It’s slim, plug-and-play, and works great with my Nemo laptop. It read my old DVDs instantly without needing any setup or extra software. I honestly didn’t realize at first that it could also burn and rewrite discs, which is a nice bonus…especially since it supports the main formats like CD±R/RW and DVD±R/RW. It gives me the option to back up older discs or save files digitally if I ever want to.

I’ve also used the wireless charger on it for my iPhone and AirPods, and both charge perfectly once it’s plugged into a 15W power Hadapter. It’s not meant to be the fastest charger, but it’s convenient and works as expected.

The build feels sturdy, it’s quiet while running, and it’s compatible with pretty much everything I need.

Five stars! ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️

No cursor, no keyboard = no computer. I panicked. I spent an hour on the phone with Apple tech support. After trying out a few things with no success, they tried to help me reinstall Mac OS X Lion via "Command/R". But, again, I had no control of the cursor/pointer, so I couldn't click on "reinstall". After I hung up from the rep, I powered all the way down and back up several more times; and, magically, somehow I was able to "re-pair" my mouse to Mac. Now, I had keyboard and mouse back up and everything returned to normal. Checked "Documents" and "Downloads", and couldn't see that I lost anything--everything worked fine. Beside tech support, I spent 2 to 3 hours of my own time trying to dig out of this mess. Above, I rated it the 2nd star, because Amazon allowed me to return the item, and they have already returned my money to my credit card. When it comes to finding the perfect accessory for your laptop, this Bluetooth Wireless Mouse presents a tempting option, especially for those who want to save a few bucks. However, while it successfully fulfills its basic function, it comes with a few compromises that you should consider.

First and foremost, this mouse is markedly made from lightweight plastic, which feels cheaper compared to Apple's sleek and sophisticated offerings. The material choice certainly makes it less durable, raising concerns about its longevity over time. If you're someone who values aesthetics and build quality, you might find yourself missing the premium feel of an Apple mouse.

Ergonomics is another area where this mouse falls short. It's not designed with extended comfort in mind, which could be a dealbreaker for users who spend long hours working or gaming. Instead, it feels flat and lacks the contours you might expect or desire from a higher-quality mouse, leading to potential discomfort during extended use.

That said, it’s important to recognize the positives. The price point of this mouse is hard to beat, especially for budget-conscious consumers. It connects easily via Bluetooth and functions well enough for everyday tasks like browsing the web, checking emails, or casual document editing. The responsiveness is commendable, making it an adequate tool for light use.

In summary, this Bluetooth Wireless Mouse delivers basic performance at an attractive price. While it can't compete with the ergonomic and aesthetic standards of Apple's offerings, it serves its purpose for users who need a functional mouse without breaking the bank. However, for those who spend significant time using a mouse, investing in a more ergonomic and durable option might be worth considering. Overall, I’d give it a solid three stars—it's a decent budget choice, but it also leaves a little to be desired.

text:
Fit:
The bumper case fits perfectly.

Screen Access/Protection:
Since the bumper doesn't have a built-in screen, the watch's screen remains unprotected. Positive: touch screen works great. Negative: the screen can/will get damaged.

I'm using a stick-on screen protection film. The watch is bumped way too often during the course of a day to leave unprotected. Also, I have the aluminum watch (Ion X glass), which also has a less durable screen than stainless steel (sapphire crystal) Apple Watches. So definitely need the protection since the bumper case doesn't provide any screen protection.

Appearance:
The bumper case is a bit plastic-looking. It matches the case. But it is a bit bulky.

Button Access:
This is where the case has some issues. The digital crown can be accessed for push-button functionality. But barely any part of the crown is exposed to actually turn the crown. You have to get used to sliding your finger against the top of the knob, up or down.

The bumper has an opening to access the side button. But the thickness of the case makes it a bit awkward to press.

Summary:
The bumper case does a good job for what it is. But it does look a bit bulky and plasticky. There's too much bulk. If the case was less than half its thickness, the issues with crown access wouldn't be as much of an issue.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
Needing some speakers that were a bit more than just the ones that come with a monitor or TV, I ran across these guys and gave them a try.

I am extremely happy I did.

These 2.0 stealth shaped speakers sound sublime.

For being a pair of speakers with no dedicated subwoofer, the Bass quality coming from these actually sounds pretty great for a small or medium room. Throwing on various music and games and everything came through crisp and clear with decent highs and lows that didn't give me "cheap speaker" sound in any way which is always a worry but thankfully not something I felt they sounded like in my entire testing range.

Not only do these speakers sound really good, but they do look pretty neat as well.
Starting off on their shape, they sort of look like a large D&D dice cut in half and then the front has a mirror finish around the speaker which also is an infinity mirror with the RGB Lights turned on. The Lights themselves have many options for the effects and even sound responsive reaction and color choice so if you like RGB you are in luck, and if you Don't like RGB you can easily change to something you may like, or leave them off completely.

Then comes connectivity which also surprised me a bit.

The speakers offer 3 different input modes.

You have your standard Aux In using a normal headphone sized Aux cable.
Then you have Bluetooth which works great tested from my phone and laptop.
And lastly you can use USB-C to plug in to either USB-C or A on a PC and the speakers show up as a USB Sound Device and again, work perfectly within Windows 11 and Linux in my testing.

Sound quality was great on all inputs with no apparent lag or input noise in my testing.

The only Con's I can think of are that you do need to use a cable to connect the speakers to each other, and that there is no battery within the speakers to use as portable bluetooth speakers, and that you cannot power the speakers over USB-C alone while plugged in as USB-C devices. None of these are real Con's against these as they are not sold as battery powered BT speakers but PC/TV Speakers that you would probably setup on a desk and keep in place for a long while. The additional input methods are more icing on the cake as having all 3 feels like a big bonus over what I usually don't expect from a set of desk speakers.

Overall I highly recommend these speakers as they impress me in both audio quality as well as connectivity and have a unique but in my opinion a great appearance that can either blend in on a desk, or stand out all their own and liven up a space.

If the features and appearance intrigue you, give these speakers a shot, they should not disappoint.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
The first thing that I noticed about these speakers was the extremely good sound reproduction. I put them through their paces with some heavy, pounding, percussion‑heavy music, and they performed like a champ. Medium and high range reproduction was also quite good. Piano notes were crisp and clean, as were strings. They're advertised as gaming speakers, and I must admit I'm not a computer gamer, but these do an excellent job with tough music reproduction, so I'm sure they're going to do well with gaming soundtracks as well. The second thing that really impressed me was the high directionality of the sound, which is something that would be very desirable in a gaming speaker, so as not to disrupt the entire household. Sitting about 5 feet away from the front of the speakers with heavy percussion music, I recorded 85 decibels of sound pressure. With the same music playing at 90 degrees from the front of the speaker, also at about 5 feet, the sound dropped to 75 decibels. I suspected I was getting a fair amount of reflected sound as well, so I stepped into the room next door at a 90-degree angle from the axis of the speakers. Even though the two rooms were connected by a very large archway, which really didn't obstruct sound, the decibel meter dropped all the way down to 65 decibels. Since decibels are not linear but rather logarithmic, this is actually an extremely noticeable drop in sound intensity off to the side of the speakers. That's great for producing full sound intensity to the gamer, but it's very easy on the other members of the household. 
The two speakers connect to each other via a provided cable, and there are inputs for USB-C, as well as auxiliary input and Bluetooth. There is also an auxiliary out jack if you want to plug in headphones. This is a miniature 1/8 inch plug. What is a little bit difficult to capture in the pictures is the very attractive infinity design of the speakers. The speaker is mounted in a two-way mirror. It is framed with blue LED lighting which reflects back and forth, giving an infinitely deep pattern. This is really stunning and would definitely fit right in with today's tendencies to make gaming computers both visually appealing and functional. I really did not anticipate rating these speakers this high, but the sound was really great. Just remember, if you are going to use them for music reproduction as opposed to gaming, that they are highly directional, and this is not something that is going to provide you with a room full of sound, unless it is reflected.

If this mouse lasts 2-3 years, then I guess it's worth it. My Apple mouse is more than 5 years old and it works fine.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text: I have used a bunch of different bluetooth and wireless mice and this is probably my current favorite. I had been going through a ton of batteries in them and decided that it was high time to try a rechargeable one since I have probably 7 different cables at my desk at any given time. The real deal breaker was using my last bluetooth mouse while traveling and having the battery die early on and then killing the spare before even getting to the destination because I left it in and there wasn't an on/off switch. This mouse is perfect for travel as its very thin, about half the height of my other standard portable mice. I have big hands so I thought that might be a problem but its slightly longer than average length mean it fits perfectly at the tip of my palm (I usually wear 2xl gloves) where normal mice don't extend past my fingers. It is very comfortable to use for extended periods and it is now my daily use mouse as well as travel. It has an on/off switch on the bottom which I use most days just to keep it from waking my computer when I bump it (I have multiple computers on my desk with multiple mice) but it does power down after sitting for a while. It was very easy to pair and I have not had the connection problems I usually have had in the past with bluetooth mice (where they stop working mid day and I have to disconnect and reconnect them). The scroll wheel is silent and easy to use other than clicking it as a third button which is the only thing that makes much noise as the buttons are very silent. The scroll wheel is easy to click no matter where you are in the scrolling process which isn't always true of other mice and third button use is important to me in my normal workflow. The dpi button on top is unobtrusive and I don't hit it by accident often but I never change it in the mouse so its wasted on me. The pairing button on the bottom is obvious even if it isn't listed but I only used it the once and it worked fine. The real star of the show is the charging port, I honestly can't tell you have long the batteries last, I typically charge it once every couple of weeks and it has never died, however, the reason I remember to do so is because I can just plug it in while I am using it and it acts like a corded mouse. Super simple to use and no docking station or open up a door or flap, just plug it in while I am using it and when the lights change to indicate its charged unplug it. If it dies while I am traveling I can power it from the tablet or wall charger or even a portable battery charger but its so easy to have it charged up before you go that it would take weeks to kill it. Way better option in my mind and if you use good batteries in your normal bluetooth mouse eventually you will hit the cost of one of these so just buy it.

text:
* I purchased this keyboard February 2024.
* I'm a retired male in my late seventies -- and I use this keyboard in a home office several hours a day for volunteer activities.
* About January 2025 the space bar got weak (it felt like the spring mechanism underneath the space bar was going bad).
* I contacted Macally support, and they sent me a replacement keyboard in January 2025.
~~~~
* About May 2025 the "cmd" key on that 2nd keyboard started working unreliably.
. . (Often I highlight text and press 'cmd+x' for 'cut' {this is a Mac}, and later when I try to 'paste', there's nothing on the clipboard. I look back where I did the 'cut', and there's an 'x' -- because the keyboard sent just an 'x' instead of the 'cmd+x' that I typed. So I've lost what was highlighted. Very frustrating.)
* I recently sent them another note on their support site, and have heard NOTHING back from them -- presumably because it's now out of warranty -- and they're not willing to replace it a 2nd time.
~~~~
* These keyboards have hardly any "travel" to the keys -- and apparently they're using a somewhat DELICATE mechanism underneath the keys -- that just doesn't "hold up" for some of us.
* I have several older keyboards that still work, so I think the older ones may be made sturdier??
~~~~
* Note my experience CONTRADICTS others' experiences.
* Other Amazon reviewers on this same page, report "I've had this keyboard for several years now. It is long lasting and durable" -- so I'm guessing they maybe have a "lighter touch" than I do ??

The guy who helped me told me that he, coincidently, had the same exact drive before and it had the same issues I was having. He showed me how heavy the drive was compared to a regular USB and said the heaviness is due to extra metal used to make the USB and can interfere with the polarity of the USB, causing it the problems we both had. He recommended me to just use a regular USB next time with a USB/iPhone adaptor.

PLEASE do not get this product. It may seem convenient, but it is not quality made and you will have a high chance of losing your data/have formatting problems. $200+ later I am still hoping and waiting that they can recover the photos I lost.

Overall, the Apple Watch Ultra Clear Band is an excellent addition to any Apple Watch enthusiast's collection. title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
I was concerned when I saw the size of the package, but honestly the keyboard is about the size of a laptop keyboard once you get it out of the box. It's compact, but not difficult to use. I honestly kind of like the compactness because it travels well, and I use it for multiple devices. And it didn't have excessive packaging - which I appreciate. Typing on it is easy, it has raised keys with a nice "pop" to them. No fancy features, but that was what I wanted. It has all of the correct buttons for a Mac keyboard. It actually seems pretty well built, and I think it will last a while.

Pairing was really easy. I just turned it on and followed the instructions. No issues with it registering via Bluetooth with my Mac Mini and I was ready to go in 10 seconds.

It does require AAA batteries. Not AA. I was on the fence about knocking off a star, but I knew what I was buying when I bought it, and honestly the self-charging keyboards and mice run out so fast half the time I don't even know if it's worth getting them sometimes. I just have some rechargeable AAA batteries I use, and at least I can swap those out instead of waiting 10 hours for my keyboard to charge again because I forgot to charge it at night.

I do find it a teensy bit cramped, but I also have big hands (like objectively, they're pretty big). It also has a pretty low profile, with how compact it is. I think most people won't have an issue with it, and honestly, for me it's nothing that won't be solved by a decent wrist rest.

title: 4.0 out of 5 stars
text: Been doodling and doing digital art most of my life in one way or another but there’s always been a disconnect between my photo manipulation on the computer and drawings and sketches on paper. Decided to plunge in and try to assimilate the two and you do not want to do that with a mouse so inevitably a tablet was in order. Am I going to even like that? How difficult will it be to look at a screen and draw with my hand separately? Well I wasn’t going to spend a bunch of cash on a tablet to try it out so I caught this one on sale watched some YouTube videos and made the call. The build quality of this seems ok enough I wouldn’t drop it off a building or anything but if you’re doing that perhaps digital art may not be your thing. But everything seems well put together and the tablet is perfectly responsive and MOSTLY easy to use. My only complaint is that it took me about a week of trial and error and various YouTube how to’s to finally figure it all out. For me the issue was I kept losing pressure sensitivity and therefore couldn’t get the tapered lines. I could literally just walk away for an hour and come back and it wouldn’t work it was mildly infuriating but ended up just having to tick the box for “windows ink” in the driver and has been working flawlessly since so if you’re on windows 11 and having that issue check that box. All the extras were a nice bonus as well, just the glove would have been a nice addition but the inclusion of the stand was a very nice thing to have. It’s perfectly fine to just lay it down but having the slight elevation is nice and the stand is good quality metal construction so I’m not worried about breathing on it too hard and it exploding into bits. The pen feels slightly flimsy but I have no plans to mine ore with it in the immediate future and I’m an adult that attempts to take care of my things so it’s not really a concern. I do wish the usb cord was a removable cord but it’s not the end of the world just know that if you mess up the connecting cable you’re pretty borked unless you know how to solder. But again for the price it’s not a huge concern I’d just buy another one and go on about my day. Smaller tablets are just as good and comparatively priced but why wouldn’t you want the larger size? If you want to do your drawings on a post it note go for it it’ll work fine and not even be that awkward but personally I like having all the screen area for the same price. Overall this thing is pretty nice can’t give it a full five stars for the couple small complaints but shipping was fast, product works great after some setup and I would absolutely make this purchase again. Keep in mind your pc power has a bit to do with performance if your using this on an amiga then you might have lag and stuff but if your using an even remotely modern pc (I highly highly recommend the ACEMAGICIAN Mini Pc with the ryzen 7 and 32 gb of ram also available here on Amazon, it’s a beast and the size of a Bluetooth speaker) but none of that is a constraint of the tablet just a heads up if you’re new to this. Get this product and download Krita (a free open source alternative to photoshop) and you’re ready to draw badly like me. That’s it that’s all there really is, buy this.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
I wanted a wireless mouse with BT, min. 5 programmable buttons (6 preferable), light weight, long battery, PixArt PAW3395 sensor and LED lights (nice to have) and low cost. After couple weeks of investigation on the matter I have decided for this.
Manbasnake X3 crossed all my requirements on paper, except for RGB lights and only 5 buttons, granted from the pictures I thought there is a DPI cycle button in the middle, but that is only a shape and a small LED that will indicate battery/charging status.
Please NOTE: I paid for this item, I did not receive any personal discounts or future promises. I will update this review as time passes.
1. Presentation: a simple decent box containing mouse with dongle, USB type-C cable and instructions. Instructions are short, they do not say how to charge the mouse (sic), the obvious “do not immerse the mouse in liquid”, but most important in my view, and I quote here: "Violence against pressing the mouse is prohibited". You have been warned! Save the instructions in case you ever need to pair the mouse with dongle, or better download PDF instructions from MFG (manba-snake com) website. There is a small rattle noise when shaking the mouse, but usually I glide and not shake.
First thing I did was to connect the mouse to the cable, plug it in to charge, remove the plastic from the feet, go to MFG to download and install the software for X3. When plugged in the software does not show battery percentage.
2. Sensor: PAW3395 it is a new gaming sensor 26K dpi, 650 ips, 50g, 1k Hz/1ms and programmable lift cutoff that is suitable for wireless due to its low power requirements, about 2V with 1.7mA in High Performance mode and 1.3mA in Low Performance mode.
3. Connection: Once fully charged, I unplugged the cable and switch to BT and right away it connected with my Intel AX210 BT 5.3 card. The switch button can be set to OFF, BT or 2.4GHz dongle but if USB cable is connected, the position does not matter. Also, there is BT switch on the back for 5.2 or 5.4, that’s two channels so you can connect the mouse with two BT devices – nice! The 2.4GHz dongle that stored inside the mouse can be used as well but I used this mode very short time since I favor BT connection. I did not notice any input lag or issues with BT.
4. Battery: the battery is supposed to last 200h. Cannot confirm that yet, but after 5 days of use (about 50h) the battery shows 80% when connected to dongle and 80% when connected to BT (via windows BT devices). To conserve the battery, mouse will go into light/deep sleep and can be woken up move/click. I emailed MFG to inquire about battery and warranty, but I received no response. I emailed the seller (Magic-Refiner) and I received a prompt response in less than one working day: battery is LiPo and capacity is 500mAh. After 11 days and a rough estimate of 90-100 hours of use, mostly on BT, mouse battery shows at 50%.
5. Weight: I used a kitchen scale and found the mouse weight without dongle at 54g. This is the lightest mouse I ever had.
6. Shape: mouse is for a right-handed, I have an average hand and usually a fingertip grip and the size and shape feels nice for me.
7. Buttons: I wished there was an extra button after scroll wheel. There are 5 programmable buttons. Side buttons are well placed, if I lift my thumb and press, I hit button #4 (forward), but move just a bit back and I can hit #5 (back), in other words easy fast access. While working, from time to time I had the impression that left click was a miss, though I heard the click, but while gaming I never missed a beat, maybe I’m pressing harder? I will continue watching this possible issue and will update. There is also a DPI cycle on the back and an LED indicator for that purpose. In the next hardware version, please move that button behind scroll wheel.
8. Switches: mouse has Kailh GM 8 switches (available here on amazon) and they are like a mechanical keyboard switch, in other words loud. I do think that sometimes I put less pressure on my left click and I hear the sound, but the action is not going through, still investigating this possible issue…
9. Scroll wheel: does not have side tilt, no infinite scroll/free spin, scrolling is smooth, easy and I like the feedback of the wheel. Middle click is a bit on stiffer side compared with other buttons, but that’s ok for me. Wheel’s edges are smooth and nice to the touch.
10. Feet: mouse feet are PTFE and they come covered with a thin transparent plastic for protection so do not forget to remove the plastic when setting up. Feet are white and this is a sign that they are 100% pure virgin grade PTFE and will offer lowest friction.
11. Software: after installation mouse was plugged and software is showing “charging” but no percentage indicator so at this moment I assume I keep it plugged until top LED turns to GREEN. Ther are several sections: Button settings (each click what to do), Macro Manager (this part can be improved), Profile (useful to have work/gaming profile), Battery (Percentage visible only with dongle, status only with cable) DPI Settings (6 DPI settings between 50 and 26k in 50 increments, tip use the wheel to fine adjust your desired DPI), Polling Rate Settings (125Hz, 250Hz, 500Hz, 1000Hz options only available for dongle/wired connection), Mouse attribute (opens old OS mouse properties), Lift of Distance (1mm or 2mm). Ther is no Apply/Save button for when you make changes, they are applied instantly, and it takes a couple seconds to do so. Software is 32-bit only, and it does not tell you, but you will have to reboot after installation. I had a froze once when I switched from BT to dongle and changed profile almost at the same time, I had to kill the app and launch again.
12. Warranty: Seller specified that warranty is 1 year.
Overall: first keep in mind this is an on-going review, but so far, despite some minor things (software, no clear battery percentage, light rattle) I like the shape, the sensor, battery endurance, BT connection and response. In over 10 days of use, my BT connection was smooth and never dropped. For gaming, please keep in mind that if you are going to use BT, polling rate is limited to 133Hz, in other words, if you click the mouse more than twice in about 8 milliseconds, then BT is not for you and you will need dongle or wired connection, and this is not my case ☹. For the price, right now, I consider this hard to beat!

Apple Watch cases are cheap and provided by a ton of companies at different price points. I’ve used a number of brands over the years, with my recent favorite being Smiling brand, but they didn’t have a model ready for the Apple Watch 10, so I went with this one instead.

I have to say, so far I like this one better. It has all of the standard features like a tight fit that is still easy to get on and off the watch, the case is clear and doesn’t affect the touch sensitivity. The one thing that I like better about this model is that it offers a clickable button for the flat button under the Digital Crown. This is a lot better than the cut out that Smiling and other brands offer. It clicks in a pleasantly tactile way and doesn’t falsely trigger clicks. Time will tell how well this holds up, but so far, so good.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
purchased two of these to replace self-built gaming machines following a house fire. I've been building gaming machines for 25 years. Never bought a pre-made system myself. I consider this an act of humility :). Only because I don't have the tools or workspace to do it myself, not being able to live at home at the moment.

Pros:
1. I love the top vent cover. It goes across almost the entire top, and is magnetically attached. very flexible and easy to remove for cleaning.

2. Performance for the dollar is spectacular.
all settings at maximum:
-- I can play pubg on my 2K display at the monitor's max of 180FPS, consistently.
-- Elder Scrolls Oblivion Remastered, even with HDR and ray tracing, 60-70 FPS consistently.
3. Lighting is beautiful. The included MSI app is very easy to operate to choose different light patterns and colors.

The only issues I have, I found consistently across brands:
1. I couldn't find a gaming system with 5.25 bays. I previously had BDXL drives, and none of the newer pre-built systems have 5.25 bays, so I'll be using my external USB drive
2. Adding storage. The wire management at first glance is fantastic. only when you remove the non-window side panel do you see where they crammed all the extra wires for other devices, along with some tiny space for hard drives or SSD's. I have big man-hands and had a little trouble pulling out the cables I want, and then trying to fit them back in once I'd connected one of my salvaged SATA ssd's. I think moving forward, I will buy a PCI-E M.2 card, and add an M.2 drive instead, if not just for speed, but so I don't have to deal with the cabling.
3. Bloatware. I was surprised to find Norton still rearing its ugly head. it was the first to go, followed by the Office 365 trial. The latter could not be easily removed from the add/remove programs. it listed every available language as one to be removed. I ended up downloading a tool I use from work: Office Scrubber. A utility from Microsoft that runs a separate script to remove all things office.
4. non-back panel ports. I'm not a fan of ports on top of the case. Practically ensures they'll get caked with dust if something isn't always plugged in. Considering getting dummy USB port inserts.
5. Still has some USB 2.0 ports. WHY on earth!? I have two 8TB drives I use to back up movies, family photos and videos, and once one is updated, I use Free File Sync to update the other drive. I found myself with a countdown timer of days, only for me to realize one of them was connected to a 2.0 port. Switched to the USB 3.2 ports, and it was down to less than 30 minutes. (also has a PS/2 port...again WHY?)

Final note: Not the fault of the system, but still noting it since the componentry is part of the issue. For best refresh rate on your screen, use DisplayPort. the HDMI version on this board is slower than DisplayPort.

Overall, VERY satisfied. again Bought two of these, one for me and the wife.

text:
Purchased this PSU as a first step effort to repair a freezing new PC build that was leaning on an older, excellent EVGA PSU that was well past its own 10 year warranty. While the EVGA PSU was ultimately not to blame, I did keep this MSI one on hand to keep vendor variety to a minimum on my MSI 870 Tomahawk build that was still giving me issues, and it was nice to have a power supply that natively had the 12VHPWR cabling available.

I appreciate the modular design of this PSU, the only variety I tend to buy these days, and this one in particular has a much smaller footprint than the one it ended up replacing which affords more room during the cramped cabling stage. I do find it much more difficult to remove the cables from this PSU than I do others that I own, something that can be a bit of a pain when you're trying to remove just a single cable rather than the whole PSU to do so. While the warranty is amazing in length (10 years!), I can say from having to deal with MSI's warranty service for the motherboard, I'm not a huge fan of the process; primarily they're quite slow to turn things around, and will use the slowest shipping process available (not to mention shipping to them on your dime). There's also no Advanced RMA option (though that seems to be losing favor in general with companies). Contrast that with other vendors like AMD who sprung for overnight inbound shipping for me and used 2 day to send parts back and I'm hoping I don't need to lean on them for this PSU in the future.

Overall though, I'm happy to have this more condensed unit in my new build and it shows no signs of trouble with my limited use case thus far.

3 Months Later: Fan already seems to be failing a bit; PSU still works fine, but the thing is easily the loudest component in my PC while idling...in a case where there are at least 10 other fans to compete with. A bit disappointed with it, though probably not worth a warranty replacement yet, assuming MSI would humor one at all for mere fan noise. Worth shaving a star off; this one pales in comparison to the now ancient EVGA PSU it replaced.

title: 1.0 out of 5 stars
text:
Poorly designed. Awful assembly documentation. Front panel connection cable is a joke.
Memory channel B defective

About me: I am a Systems Engineer with more than 25 years of experience making my own PCs.

A few moths ago I built an 9950X on a Asus Strix X870E no issues at all with that system. Rock solid.

This time I decided to make a second workstation with an 9950X3D and this MSI Board

Te board came poorly packaged on Amazon box without any cushioning. The Board box itself came without any seal altough after inspecting it everything seemed fine.

I assembled the PC as I allways do (I do this job about 3-4 times per year as I keep upgrading my systems for better work performance).

The board has no clear identifiers on their internal connections for USB, Audio and front panel. The Dimm slots are not identified either (the Asus Board is as clear as it can be) so I downloaded the manual on my phone to check the connections (the box didn't include any basic reference printed documentation but MSI choose to put some cartoon stickers jajaj). The connections in general are mostly cryptic acronyms so If you are unexperienced don't get this board by any means.

I finished the build and tried to boot the system to configure the BIOS. It keept giving C5 error code on the diagnostic panel. After a lot of trial and error I found out that the memory channel B was not working. Removing the memory from that slot booted wihout issues (I have 4 memory kits available so I was able to make many tests). I suspected bent pins on the socket (I was very, very carful installing the CPU as I know how easy is to damage the socket), so. I removed the cooler and the CPU and using a magnifying glass inspected the socket. didn't found any issues with it as I was fearing even if I was extremely careful on the CPU install.

Second step I removed the board from the PC case and inspected it. No physical issues where found. The memory slots don't cross the back of the board so no shorts are possible either.

So, the board is just a lemon that wasn't properly tested on factoy and I lost a complete day of work.

I would also mention the stiffness of power connectors and the memory slots itselfs. It was very hard to disconnect the components. Specially the power connector. Comparing this roughness to the Strix is night and day.

So, I am now dealing with returning this POS to Amazon and getting a refund.

If you want a secure experience get the Asus. I am done with MSI and would not buy again any boards from this brand.
