title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
What I'm about to tell you will potentially save you from future catastrophic failures including loss of data. Nothing beats having multiple good backup copies.; however, the following information will instruct you on how to test your new drive to make sure it's free from defects.

Imagine, you have a spinning disk rotating thousands of times per minute separated by its recording/reading head by less thickness of a human hair. Just one wrong thing and .. "click..click..click".

You don't want that.

Generally speaking a bad hard drive will make itself known sooner vs later when it's tested fully. Not always. What YOU can do is put the hard drive through its paces to really give it a good solid work out and make sure every space designated by the drive as available/writeable space, is in fact GOOD. Its magnetic/electrical properties strong.

This test is a LONG test. What it does is write all 01010101s,10101010s,11111111s,and 00000000s, binary, to the disk.--filling it. It does this in 4 passes (i.e. writes the disk fully) 4 times. After each write it will read what was just written beginning to end to ensure all bits were written exactly right.

If they wern't, the drive's detection mechanism for errors (SMART) will notice (i.e. a bit was not written to a sector correctly) and flag the SMART COUNTER. For example, uncorrectable or reallocated sector count would show a non-0 value.

During operation, if the drive encounters a fault with a sector it will swap that sector with another known good sector the drive has in reserve and will log it via SMART.

A PERFECTLY WORKING HARD DRIVE WILL SHOW '0' for 'Reallocated Sector Count','Reported Uncorrectable Errors','Current Pending Sector Count','Uncorrectable Sector Count'.IF ANY OF THESE VALUES SHOWS ANYTHING OTHER THAN A 0 (zero), THEN YOU HAVE A FAILING HDD AND SHOULD REPLACE IT ASAP. DO NOT TRUST YOUR DATA ON IT.

This command will erase everything on the disk if there is data already on there when you run this test. For this 2TB it would have taken about 30 hours, but I stopped it at the start of the final pass since I was confident--4 passes are better but do at least 2. But I am confident the data will be safe because it worked out the drive hard and pictures above show good numbers.

Boot up your computer using a linux distribution boot usb/cd. Debian Ubuntu, any one will do--it doesn't matter.

In a terminal type: sudo fdisk -l
*Identiy which /dev is your HDD you wish to test. Also note if it says 512 or 4096 where it says "Sector size (logical/physical)". For example, if it's /dev/sde and says 4096 Sector Size (such as this 2tb drive) then type the following command:

sudo badblocks -wsv -b 4096 -c 131072 /dev/sde

This will 0101,1010,1111,and 0000 write and read/verify the drive back-to-back in 4 passes. On my slow computer this took around 24-30 hours to complete or 2tb.

The ' -b ' option is the Block Size. This should match the drive. 512 or 4096. The '-c' option tells badblocks how many blocks to test at time. Changing this number will alter the speed and will either make the process go along faster or slower (dependant on Drive Interface, Ram/Cpu speed, etc.). Instead of '-c 131072' ,try '-c 65536 if it seems the test is taking too long to increment the %'s.

In fact try it with '-c 65536' option. Let it run or 30 sec then CTRL-C to cancel it. Then run the command again but with '-c 131072' instead. Run it for 30 sec then CTRL-C to cancel. Compare the 2 and whichever command that had the higher % when you CTRL-C'd would be the number you would choose since that one ran a little bit faster. Google or man page 'badblocks' for more information.

Whenever you buy a new hard drive get into the mindset/habit that you will NOT use them for awhile because you have to test them out first. Trust me on this and it's totally worth it. I'd like to think I avoid catastrophic failures because I did this test and it would have presented itself (or at least more likelihood) then vs months/years down the road. That's not a given--any drive can fail anytime or any reason but this is just an additional layer. Like a "shakedown cruise' if you will.

Regarding this drive: Western Digital 2TB WD Blue PC Internal Hard Drive HDD - 5400 RPM, SATA 6 Gb/s, 256 MB Cache,, I can say that I am pleased it tested clean and I look forward to using this drive.And I'm confident it will keep my data intact.

You are welcome!

I installed this into my Lenovo Thinkpad workstation class laptop, installed Ubuntu Budgie Linux with encrypted ZFS and started to put data on it. The laptop hung 1-2 times and I rebooted, but hoped that it was not a sign... I should have listened to my gut.
2 days after installation, the laptop hung and I rebooted again. It came up to GRUB and hung, waiting for the drive to appear. It gave a detection error on another boot that I cannot remember (POST message from BIOS).
Because I had a virtual machine file on it that was temporarily ONLY on this drive, I tried it in my other M.2 slot and it did the same thing. It detected in the BIOS originally as "Dogfish 2TB" if I recall correctly. Now, it detected as "SM2259AB-10-00811000". I put this same stick into my desktop PC with an mSATA adapter and it detected the same way, but this gave more detail - it was a 1.0 GB disk now!
I requested a replacement from Amazon and received one yesterday, installed Linux on to it - or at least TRIED to... at about 95% into the installation, it hung. As I expanded the installation window to see the terminal output, I saw "Error sending ATA command..." on device sda. Thinking that this might be my USB stick (ok, hopeful thinking) I re-created a boot stick with the same ISO on it... I got to the point of starting to partition, and it told me there was not enough space to install Ubuntu!
So, I checked... and this drive is now detecting as "SM2259AB-10-00811000" as well!! Another 2TB drive magically converted to a 1GB drive. All of this happened while the laptop was fully assembled with the back cover on and sitting securely on a table for installation. I cannot think of any possible way that I damaged these units.
I will not be buying another Dogfish.

text:
I have a veritable rainbow of WD drives (red, green, blue) between my PC, Drobo and newly built NAS and they are all real workhorses. I have yet to have any of them fail or misbehave even after 8 years. I know certain colors are best suited for certain applications, but I find the blue drives to be the best bang for the buck and most versatile. I bought this most recent 4TB blue to install in an old PC that I turned into a Plex media server/home made NAS. I've been wanting to have a dedicated media server for some time and finally had the chance to do it but needed more storage space. The PC I had has a 1TB hard drive that I wanted to remain dedicated to running software and store all of my movies, tv shows, documentaries, and kiddie crap (haha) on its own drive. I installed this the other day and loaded all my visual media on it (I keep pictures and music on yet another drive) and I still have room to spare. I immediately connected the new server to Plex through my Roku 4 and watched a movie (1080p) on the TV while streaming another to my phone and had no trouble whatsoever! I know a lot of the buffering problems stem from inadequate CPU and mine is good, but just in case you're wondering, these blue drives have no trouble streaming content from when you've got adequate transcoding power in your machine. A lot of people would tell you you need red drives but old blue does just fine in my experience and is so much cheaper!

For those of you who are new to installing new hard drives, it's a piece of cake but just be aware that this drive does not come with any cables or mounting hardware, so you'll need to be sure you have your own SATA cable and an available power source cable as well as screws or whatever you need to mount it in your case. Also for the newbies, you can't just plug and use, you'll need to go in to your drive manager and name/format it before you can use it. This is also very very easy to do and only takes a few minutes and then you're ready to go!

I don't use these WD drives to boot and run software anymore (it's all about SSD's for that now - buy one, it will change your life) but I use these drives to hold and back up all of my data for me and I love them! You really can't get more storage and a more reliable drive for a better price than this. And don't be freaked out because the picture shows the inside of the hard disk, this is a fully enclosed drive (see pics). Hope this helps! Happy computing! I did NOT receive this for free or at a discount.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
Good:
* small footprint
* small cubic volume means fans can move the heat more easily
* decent components out of the box, excellent gamedev workstation, very capable gaming rig
* plenty of ports (4x display out, 8x USB-A and 2x USB-C) with a few of them conveniently at the top near the power button
* liquid cooled CPU
* solid PSU and subtle case
* GPU is mounted parallel to the motherboard (using a 90-degree adapter) so the heft of the graphics card isn't dragging down the PCIe slot and there's no need for a support stand to hold the graphics card up.
* glass panel does look nice, if you favor looks over air-flow (I'm going with air-flow)

Upgradable:
* RAM can be maxed out at 96GB
* Four SSD inputs (two NVME and two SATA)
* GPU can be upgraded to the next generation as the PSU has some headroom at 850W
- you could probably upgrade the CPU if you're comfortable disassembling the liquid cooler for it, but you may want to lock in your choice of CPU (7000 or 9000 series, and clock speed) at purchase.

Frustrations:
these are mostly around the case design
* the second NVME allows for RAID but this case design + motherboard cooling makes it a headache to reach
this would be less of a frustration but they actually punch a hole in the case at the right position, it's just that the heat sink on the motherboard is in the way, and (as far as I can tell) you still end up having to remove the entire motherboard just to access the second M.2 slot. The first one can be reached under its own heat sink also, and you need to remove the graphics card, but it's significantly easier to access than the one on the back
* there is only room to mount one SATA SSD drive but there are two SATA connections on the board, so again I'm stuck with one, or leave the second one floating about.

If you don't mind the limited drive upgrades and that every choice has only 16GB on the video card, this is a good choice. It has been stable for me under Windows and Linux OSes and will probably be a home server until I can find a graphics card with enough VRAM to consider upgrading it again.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
So, let me start with a warning. If you are planning on upgrading an older laptop running windows 10, with an Intel CPU, and an older style AMD "GPU", such as the HD series, then there are some serious compatibility issues... but non of them are the fault of this memory. In my case, I upgraded an HP Envy 14 Beats 2020NR.

After the upgrade, system became super unstable, which I'm guessing was somehow related to the 2nd RAM slot being used for the first time ever, but who knows. Regardless, the system had become virtually unusable, even with only the old Samsung RAM installed. To make a long story short, I reset everything on this system every way possible, and read every article, post, or thread on the internet that had anything to do with the problem. Best I could do, a stable system with 2 minute start-up and shutdown times. But just recently I struck gold, so just in case there's someone who could use this, I thought I should share...

First, reset everything. Start with fresh install of Windows, newly formatted drive (if possible), I even did a factory reset on my BIOS. Then install only 1 of the new TimeTec RAM, boot off your Windows install drive of choice, and wait for Windows to do it's thing. After system install, as long as everything is running stable, add the 2nd stick of RAM. Check stability again, then update windows and your drivers to current. And that is where the super long boot and shutdown times will appear. I actually wasted tons of time trying to optimize my drivers manually, then recently discovered driver management software. I highly recommend this approach, as it optimized all my drivers based on my system, even rolled a few back. While it immediately improved my computer's performance in a number of ways, it also highlighted the culprit. The software for my AMD Radeon HD 6630M, which it had completely removed due to the issues. Knowing the problem specifics, I was able to finally do a proper search, and discover that it essentially Windows asking the AMD driver a question it didn't know how to answer, so it basically didn't and caused a long delay. One little change to the registry, and Voila! If you don't know what you're doing here (like me), just find detailed instructions and follow them.

During all this, I initially thought the TimeTec RAM was at fault, so their customer support immediately sent me a replacement so I could rule out their product. Super nice people with just over a week turnaround on the whole exchange. Thanks TimeTec!

I usually buy all the components individually but I needed a Linux server that was small and didn't make any noise so decided to buy something prepackaged. Then I deleted Windows and installed Ubuntu, which went easily. The Kingdel PC has been very fast under Linux, with 4 cores and 8 threads (i.e. 8 virtual cores). And what's also impressive is that it stays cool. I was replacing an older machine that was similarly in a microcase with no moving parts, but I always had to keep the top of the case off because it would overheat. The new Kingdel has stayed quite cool; according to the lmsensors Ubuntu package, the CPU core temp doesn't go over 35c even when I have all the cores busy compiling software.

I don't usually leave reviews, but decided to review this Kingdel because I was so nervous buying it since it didn't have any reviews and it seemed too good to be true - 8th gen CPU, 16GB RAM, 256GB flash and a genuine licensed copy of Win 10 Pro all for $650??! Overall, this is a great little machine. If/when vendor fixes Windows/security issues I'll reconsider, but for the moment I had to return this back through Amazon.

text:
I am a long-time flight, space, and mech sim fan - been playing since the DOS days. Over the years I have had dozens of joysticks and I made sure I gave myself some time to play with this one before writing a review.

The Sol-R 1 is the standalone joystick in the Sol-R # line. If you get a Sol-R 2 (two joysticks, 1 left and one right) or a Sol-R 4 (joystick plus throttle), it is still the Sol-R 1 joystick.

First off, the construction is really good at this price point. Joysticks have gotten crazy expensive over the years - they seemed to sky-rocket price-wise around COVID and have never gone back down. The Sol-R 1 is heavy given its plastic exterior - there must be a fair bit of metal on the inside. It stays put when playing games, feels sturdy, and the plastic is hard enough that I don't think it will get sticky over the years. When I compare it to the other sticks I have had over the years it is clearly the most well-built.

The joystick works well and feels good. The buttons are responsive and have a nice click, the joystick movement is smooth, the throttle works well, and there is no squeaking. The joystick sensors are Hall effect, which means they should not drift or wear out. There are 2 options for a pinky button - a standard button and a more flat button. I opted for the latter since I plan on using the pinky button as a shift (they call it a layer) so that I can double the function of each button. I am impressed with the look and feel - my last new joystick was a Saitek X52 and this is built orders of magnitude better.

On the bottom of the base of the joystick is a left/right switch, so it is simply to change the handedness. They even give you extra hand mounts to make it fit both left and right hands. The manual is just okay - it is sometimes written for a specific joystick, has screenshots that only apply to certain joysticks, the writing is sometimes unclear, etc. For example, the manual says that LEDs are adjusted in T.A.R.G.E.T., but this is not true for the Sol-R 1. You have to go to Windows "Set up USB game controllers," click the LED tab, and them there.

The Thrustmaster T.A.R.G.E.T. software is... not horrible. It works well, don't get me wrong, but it is clunky and looks like something written in the 1990's. And even that is an insult to 1990's software - the Saitek software for the X52 was easier to use and just as functional (okay, it was written in 00's, but you get the idea). T.A.R.G.E.T. is also 32bit, which is not an issue per se, but is an indicator of its legacy background.

The manual is included ("C:\Program Files (x86)\Thrustmaster\TARGET\Resources\TARGET_User_Manual.pdf" but no link gets created, so you have to search for it. The manual is also available online. I found that loading the manual into NotebookLM and asking questions worked REALLY well. Similarly, there is enough info about T.A.R.G.E.T. on the internet that Gemini is able to answer pretty much all questions accurately.

T.A.R.G.E.T. is weird - it is not a TSR or service. The Sol-R 1 is recognized by Windows (I installed the drivers and updated the firmware) accurately. If your game allows robust remapping, you won't need T.A.R.G.E.T. When you use T.A.R.G.E.T., it creates a virtual joystick and the Sol-R 1 disappears from your system. You use the virtual joystick for your game. The process is:
1. Launch T.A.R.G.E.T.
2. Run your T.A.R.G.E.T. profile.
3. Launch your game.
4. Exit your game.
5. Exit T.A.R.G.E.T.

Since T.A.R.G.E.T. is not a TSR or service, it does NOT automatically recognize when you are playing a game for which you have profile and automatically configure itself. See above - you have to run T.A.R.G.E.T. when you need it. There is a FLY NOW function in T.A.R.G.E.T. where you can set up a game profile and have T.A.R.G.E.T. launch the profile and then launch the game, but I found this did not work for some games. Chorus (on Steam) does not like to be launched outside of Steam, so I could not use FLY NOW. No biggie - I just wrote a script to launch T.A.R.G.E.T. and then Chorus.

When using T.A.R.G.E.T. you can program pretty much anything - I liked how it allows me to map up to DirectX button 120. When using the pinky button as a shift (layer 1 and layer 2) switch, I found it easiest to have layer 1 be the normal button assignment (e.g., DX35) and then doubling it when using layer 2 (e.g., DX70). This logic only works for higher number buttons, but you get the idea. I could just add 44 to each button number for layer 2, for example. But you can program buttons to be mouse functions, keystrokes, macros, etc.

T.A.R.G.E.T. allows you to adjust the sensitivity of the joystick, which is great. Chorus is a bit twitchy, so I was able to tune the Sol-R 1 to make it smooth an manageable. You can also adjust deadzone, change the response curve, etc. T.A.R.G.E.T. is a powerful tool.

T.A.R.G.E.T. does not understand the concept of a base profile, which is annoying. I would love to have a base profile that gets used when I create a new game profile. This base profile could have the shift button programmed, the layer 1 and 2 DX buttons programmed, etc. In theory I can create a profile and define all this and call it default, create a new profile for a game (e.g., Chorus), exit T.A.R.G.E.T., copy the default file over the Chorus file, and it should work fine. Gemini says to be careful doing this...

I would love to see T.A.R.G.E.T. updated to be 64bit and run as a service so that it can recognize games on launch and then automatically launch the correct profile. My mouse does this, for example, as does my keyboard. I would like to see T.A.R.G.E.T. officially support a custom default profile. And it would be nice if the GUI were updated and made more user friendly. And for the LED controls to be included. But again, it works fine, using it is not too difficult, the manual is just so-so, and Gemini can answer almost all questions correctly.

It reminds me of playing flight/space/mech sims in the 1990's and 00's when I would launch a game and constantly be alt-tabbing to the joystick software to tweak controls. I am back to doing this - this is not a complaint, just a nostalgic flashback to days gone by.

A final note on the overall layout of the buttons and base. Overall I like them - I am still getting used to them, but I like most of them. I question if I will ever use the rotary dial on the bottom left of the base - I would have prefered more buttons. The 4-way switch on the bottom right of the base seems like a create option to program even more layers. However, the software only supports 3 more layers (Upper, Middle, Lower) so if I program it for those layers, the 4th selector location will not make much sense to use for anything.

I am happy with the purchase and consider the Sol-R 1 to be worth the money. I considered other joysticks before deciding on this one - the Logitech X56 (the modern X52), the VKB Gladiator NXT EVO, the Turtle Beach VelocityOne Flightdeck, etc. I wanted a mid-tier joystick that was sturdy, had a pinky/shift button, and was programmable. The Sol-R 1 checks all those boxes. It is also very upgradable - I can add the throttle and/or rudder pedals in the future. Are there better joysticks? Definitely, but I think the Sol-R 1 is where the point of diminishing returns kicks in unless you are really committed to flight sims and have money to burn.

The initial quality impression is very high. They are heavy bases with sturdy plastic grips and a metal connection. The spring tension feels great and very linear. I use twist for forward/aft thrust and roll and have no issues maintaining precise control.

The buttons on the grips are spaced out quite a bit - maybe even too far if you have smaller hands - but I find everything reachable without changing grip position.

The buttons and encoders on the bases are where the SOL-R system really separates itself. They are DJ quality button pads and so satisfying to use. Not mushy, no mishits on corners or double presses. The encoders can be set to behave as buttons or as an axis in the software, which helps adapt to different games or needs.

The bases are sturdy and I do not find the included extenders necessary to keep them stable on my desk. The individually addressable RGBs on the buttons are also nice to have although I'm only using them decoratively for now.

I'll report back if I have any durability issues, but so far so good.

text:
Remote work and online meetings have become so normal, it’s wild to think we ever tolerated grainy camera feeds. Enter Acer’s 4K Webcam, loaded with a Sony 1/2" sensor, PDAF autofocus, dual noise reduction mics, and a few thoughtful design touches that punch way above its price.

Why a High-Quality Webcam Matters When You Work from Home

Working remotely, your webcam becomes the way you show up in the world. In a meeting or virtual interview, you're often just a face and a voice on someone’s screen. If your image is fuzzy or your audio keeps cutting out, it’s harder to connect, be taken seriously, or just communicate quickly and clearly. With a crisp 4K feed, colleagues see every detail, a reassuring smile, a quick reaction, and real eye contact. You look professional, engaged, and present. Great audio is just as vital. When background noise fades and your voice comes through clearly, it cuts down on the “Sorry, what was that?” interruptions and helps you drive the conversation. With so much of your work life happening through a lens and mic these days, investing in a webcam that gets both right is one of the simplest upgrades you can make for your career.

Let’s talk first impressions. The brushed aluminum body feels solid, definitely not that flimsy plastic you get with cheaper cams. It stays remarkably cool, even through hours-long calls or a marathon gaming session. The lightweight build doesn’t tip your laptop screen, and the privacy cover slides cleanly into place, which is more comforting than you think when you realize how many things are streaming from your device.

Where Acer’s cam sets itself apart is the video quality. The 4K resolution, combined with Sony’s 1/2" sensor, is instantly noticeable. Your face actually looks like your face, even with bad lighting, and PDAF autofocus means you can move around without landing in a blurry mess. For streamers and those who flail their hands during meetings (you know who you are), it’s a huge upgrade.

Audio usually gets ignored on webcams, but Acer didn’t phone it in. The two noise reduction mics pick up your voice cleanly and cut background chatter to a dull hum. No more apologizing for barking dogs or the neighbour’s leaf blower.

Little extras round out the package: plug-and-play on both PC and Mac, a long USB cord, and build quality that feels premium without being bulky. Setup is genuinely simple, with no weird driver glitches.

Now, it’s not perfect. At this price, Acer could’ve tossed in a tripod mount, and if you’re obsessed with ultra-wide angles, you might want something with a little more field of view. But those are small nits for a camera that seriously outclasses your laptop’s built-in cam or most of what you find at the big box stores.

Bottom line: If you’re done settling for potato-quality video (or audio that sounds like it’s underwater), Acer’s 4K Webcam is worth every penny. Whether you’re presenting to a client, running a Twitch stream, or just want to look sharp for the weekly Zoom family roast, this is the upgrade you’ve been waiting for.

text:
For those of you who purchased the Polymega retro gaming console, you know that it is a fun device that allows you to upload your favorite classic games (NES, SNES, Genesis, N64, Playstation, etc.) and play them via emulation using your original game discs/cartridges.

With that said, I have always felt that the universal controller that was offered for the Polymega has issues with input lag (especially with using the 2.4ghz dongle instead of wired). As a gamer, this can be extremely frustrating when the buttons pressed do not respond as they should when compared with the respective original hardware controllers. To top it off, the Polymega is limited on which 3rd party controllers are compatible with the device (it requires X-Input). I have tried various 3rd party controllers which did not work for me. The only one that seemed to work okay was the 8bitdo Pro 2 controller. However, I personally do not care for the Playstation-style design and prefer the modern Xbox controller.

Fortunately, I tried this controller and was pleasantly surprised to find that it works perfectly with the Polymega console. I first used the provided 2.4ghz dongle for wireless play and I noticed that the input lag was much improved over the universal Polymega controller (even the newer WC02 model). To be fair, I tried using the EasySMX X05 Pro Wireless Controller in wired mode and noticed that there was no input lag to speak of (or least none that I could tell). When you plug in the controller to your Polymega (via the 2.4ghz dongle or wired) it will be recognized as a universal Polymega controller (make sure to have the switch on the back of the controller set to 2.4ghz).

As for the controller itself, it is very well constructed (for the price) and feels natural to hold. The buttons all respond well and I was happy with the D-Pad operation (in which the D-Pad is used heavily in most of the emulated game consoles that Polymega offers at this point in time).

I also played around with the controller briefly on my Windows 11 PC. I used the dongle and there were no issues and it worked well.

I highly recommend this controller, not just for the Polymega, but for gaming in general, especially if you are looking for a less expensive solution than an official Xbox controller.

text:
Held back on using this until the Switch 2 arrived, as I was desperately hoping this would be compatible. Thankfully, it is - and it was way easier to pair than I imagined it would be.

The pad comes with a dongle, but it isn't needed on the Switch 2. Simply connect the pad to the to the Switch 2 with the charge cable, then disconnect. Job done. It is now recognised by the Switch 2 as a pro controller.

From there, it has just been an incredibly enjoyable experience. I've only had the chance to use it on Mario Kart World and Zelda: TOTK but it already feels miles better than the original Switch Pro Controller. The sticks are responsive and feel great (I've added some caps just to give them an extra few mm of height and a little more texture), the ABXY buttons are basic looking but work well (no unregistered button presses so far), and the trigger/shoulder buttons work fine, if feeling a little bit lifeless.

There is an offer on the X05 (search Amazon - its not on this listing anymore) where the grey version can be obtained at the time of review (07/06/2025) for £19.97 with a further 22% off, making it £15.57. I don't believe you will get a controller this good for cheaper.

The price is so good, I'm going to get 3 so that everyone can play MKW at the same time. Outstanding value for an outstanding controller.

text:
La casa EasySMX produce diverse tipologie di controller e praticamente tutti riprendono la forma la forma di altri competitor in questo settore, nella fattispecie riprendono per lo più le forme dei più famosi pad di Microsoft. Questo è il modello X05, quello più basilare, che si trova generalmente nel raggio di una ventina di euro. Ed a questo prezzo risulta essere veramente un buon affare per tutto quello che offre.

La confezione è molto simile a quelli di tanti altri controller, all'interno troviamo tutto il necessario per iniziare subito a divertirsi. Oltre al controller e l'indispensabile chiavetta wireless da 2.4 Ghz troviamo il cavetto USB-C che serve per la ricarica ( o se preferite giocare con il cavo). E' abbastanza classico nel design a parte una predominanza di un rosa abbastanza shock veramente bello a vedersi e due cerchi led luminosi sotto entrambi gli stick.

Passiamo però alla parte sicuramente più croccante di questo controller a partire dal collegamento. Molto ma molto buono con il cavo grazie a dei valori di latenza particolarmente bassi che lo rendono ideale anche per un poco di competitivo online. Considerando il prezzo intorno ai 20 euro sono dei risultati veramente da primato in questa fascia di prezzo. Il Bluetooth va come su tanti altri modelli, a latenza abbastanza alta ed ideale per giocare senza particolari aspettative, in maniera abbastanza casual ed in particolar modo in single player. Per quanto riguarda la soluzione con chiavetta, su questo marchio è sempre un pochino più latente ma essendo questo un modello più economico posso anche accettarlo. Parliamoci chiaro, va comunque meglio del Bluetooth ma altri modelli più costosi fanno di meglio.

Molto buoni gli stick, hanno un bel ritorno ed un bel range di movimento che li rende veramente piacevoli da utilizzare. La "zona morta" non è sempre precisamente sullo zero ma in generale ha sicuramente un ottimo range. I pulsanti hanno un bel click meccanico che restituisce delle belle sensazioni durante l'utilizzo, si premono molto bene e ritornano ancora meglio.

Essendo un modello più economico non troviamo particolari funzioni come la Macro ma è presenta all'appello un'interessantissima modalità turbo che consente di fare fuoco molto più velocemente del normale, anche a ripetizione. Comoda per tutti i giochi tipo sparatutto ed è un in più che generalmente manca sui pad "ufficiali".

Se devo essere onesto il controller non mi è proprio dispiaciuto, sarà anche la fascia probabilmente più bassa di questo produttore ma proprio per questo sono riusciti ad unire un prezzo competitivo ad una funzionalità veramente di buon livello che lo rendono secondo me un controller interessante da avere per chi vuole spendere poco e non ha pretese da top di gamma. Spendete per una fascia bassa e portate a casa, secondo me, una buona fascia media.

Il sistema di vibrazione non è nulla per cui gridare al miracolo, per esempio, impostabile su cinque diversi livelli di potenza ma senza particolari guizzi ma è comunque presente. Poi funziona sia su PC, e viene prontamente riconosciuto da Windows e Steam, che su Nintendo Switch, Android e iOS quindi davvero c'è poco da chiedere di più. Se il prezzo si mantiene nell'intorno dei 20 euro risulta essere perfino un buon affare. E proprio in ottica di questo prezzo si merita, secondo me, le cinque stelline.

text:
J’utilise la manette EasySMX X10 comme manette principale sur mon PC depuis un an.

La prise en main est bonne, les joysticks sont précis grâce à la technologie Hall Effect, et les boutons mécaniques répondent bien.

Je la recommande si vous cherchez une manette polyvalente et performante sans trop dépenser.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
For those of you who purchased the Polymega retro gaming console, you know that it is a fun device that allows you to upload your favorite classic games (NES, SNES, Genesis, N64, Playstation, etc.) and play them via emulation using your original game discs/cartridges.

With that said, I have always felt that the universal controller that was offered for the Polymega has issues with input lag (especially with using the 2.4ghz dongle instead of wired). As a gamer, this can be extremely frustrating when the buttons pressed do not respond as they should when compared with the respective original hardware controllers. To top it off, the Polymega is limited on which 3rd party controllers are compatible with the device (it requires X-Input). I have tried various 3rd party controllers which did not work for me. The only one that seemed to work okay was the 8bitdo Pro 2 controller. However, I personally do not care for the Playstation-style design and prefer the modern Xbox controller.

Fortunately, I tried this controller and was pleasantly surprised to find that it works perfectly with the Polymega console. I first used the provided 2.4ghz dongle for wireless play and I noticed that the input lag was much improved over the universal Polymega controller (even the newer WC02 model). To be fair, I tried using the EasySMX X05 Pro Wireless Controller in wired mode and noticed that there was no input lag to speak of (or least none that I could tell). When you plug in the controller to your Polymega (via the 2.4ghz dongle or wired) it will be recognized as a universal Polymega controller (make sure to have the switch on the back of the controller set to 2.4ghz).

As for the controller itself, it is very well constructed (for the price) and feels natural to hold. The buttons all respond well and I was happy with the D-Pad operation (in which the D-Pad is used heavily in most of the emulated game consoles that Polymega offers at this point in time).

I also played around with the controller briefly on my Windows 11 PC. I used the dongle and there were no issues and it worked well.

I highly recommend this controller, not just for the Polymega, but for gaming in general, especially if you are looking for a less expensive solution than an official Xbox controller.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
I’m not going to go over every feature, because that would take too long, so here are the main points.

Size: Perfect, in my opinion. Most Xbox-style controllers are on the larger side, which can make fast gameplay and certain grip styles harder to use. This one is slightly smaller and feels ideal in the hands.

Hall Effect Joysticks: The Hall effect sticks feel extremely precise, and the option to use zero deadzone completely removes any sense of input delay. Everything feels instant and accurate.

Extra Buttons: The additional “M” buttons next to the bumpers are perfectly placed. They’re easy to reach and feel natural to use without accidental presses.

I bought two name-brand $150 controllers to compare against this one, and to my surprise, I returned both. This controller simply feels better overall and punches well above its price.

With the Covid-19 pandemic my job pivoted on a dime and mandated telework for at least two months. The second day of working on my laptop I decided I needed a new monitor so I bought an ultra wide screen one. With such a nice monitor I figured I would buy a new non-laptop computer so the laptop could be used by my kids for their school work. I did my research and having not owned a gaming PC in almost two decades I wound up pick this machine up from IBuyPower which looks to be a family run company and not a huge worldwide company.

Setting up the system was a breeze, I will give you that using Windows for the first time in decades it felt really Mac like in the configuration walk through. The instructions that come with the system are one page and can be summed up as: make sure nothing came loose inside, attach the Wi-Fi antenna, plug in power, keyboard, mouse and monitor, turn on. Easy enough although the antenna cable could be a little bit longer.

Performance is top of the charts in every category. Maxed out setting in every game and plays smooth as butter. Bought a Vive VR setup and ran the performance test and maxed out in every category and boy is VR a lot of fun. I run my work environment in a window with the ultra wide monitor and the system just purrs.

This was my first exposure to a SSD and man-oh-man what a speed difference. With the system powered down, pushing the power button results in a delay of seconds until the Windows sign in screen is shown. Man, I remember the days of watching the BIOS screen scrolling by and now it is so quick. Waking up the computer from sleep mode is nearly instantaneous.

What else... the system is super quiet. The keyboard and mouse that come with the system are cool and work fine. I was getting 139MB/sec download speeds via the wi-fi antenna (I have the computer in the basement) but I ran a Cat-6 cable directly to the router and now am over 500mg/sec download which is nuts.

Downsides: Came shipped in the IBuyPower packaging which would make it a steal target if you are not home. There you have it. I have not had the chance to use tech support so I cannot comment. I am thrilled with the computer and would recommend it in a heartbeat to anyone who asked, I looks great, plays everything and handles everything I throw at it without breaking a sweat. text:
Very nice PC for the money! Fast processor and excellent Nvidia graphics card. Very quiet fan operation. Plenty of fast USB3 ports, front and back. Cool looks.

Mine came with Windows 10 pre-installed and fully functional, but no Windows 10 "activation code". So at first it seems that Windows 10 cannot be activated properly on this machine. I noticed that there is no Windows 10 documentation anywhere in the paperwork that came with my PC. When you go to the Microsoft web site to register it, it says the PC's serial number is not registered for Windows 10, and they send you to a site to pay $120 for a Windows 10 Home license. Also, a watermark is seen on the lower right corner of your screen telling you your Windows 10 is not activated. Lack of Windows activation has given me problems in getting Office 365 to work, since the machine is currently unlicensed according to Microsoft. The Amazon description claims it comes with Windows 10 Home - which is only partially true due to the above situation. In fact, it may be an un-licensed copy. Might have to buy that license at some point.

EDIT : Found the Windows 10 Product key !! by opening PowerShell and typing this command :
wmic path SoftwareLicensingService get OA3xOriginalProductKey
and then pasting the long product key (make sure you write it down for future reference) into the PC Settings > Update>Activation window. All is good now !!

EDIT 2 : I am looking for a memory upgrade, right now it comes with 8+8=16GB of DDR4 2666MHz 288pin ram. I plan to use two sticks of 32GB ram, for a total of 64GB. The memory I am looking at is : Crucial Ballistix 3200 MHz DDR4 DRAM Desktop Gaming Memory Kit (288pin) 64GB (32GBx2) CL16 BL2K32G32C16U4R (RED), or https://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B083TRRT1N/ref=ox_sc_act_title_1?smid=ATVPDKIKX0DER&psc=1

Hopefully that should work straight out of the box !

text: This Pc shipped quickly and arrived as expected. Upon opening the box the pc was packaged wonderfully and securely. Once out of the box I inspected the pc for loose wires and screws as it said in the included quick start guide. I did have a few loose screws and one loose wire however this is expected with shipping. Once I resecured them, I started up the PC, and it turned right on. I noticed the fan in the middle on the bottom would make about a quarter turn then stop, however the RGB was working properly. I turned the computer back off after it finished its installs of window and other basic programs and rechecked the wires to see if it just was not fully seated, but all wires where fully plugged in. Upon further investigation I found one of the black silicone spacers was on the bottom of the case under the fan. Once I removed it the fan started and runs as expected now. I have no idea where this spacer came from as every screw that has needs one has one and there are none missing so I am left to assume that it is an extra that got left when the PC was put together by the system integrator. Since then I have spent about 20 hours gaming and more hours than I care to think about using this computer for school and work and it has been such an impressive machine. I cannot say enough good things about it. I am sure somewhere a part was selected to save money, but I could not have built a better PC for the price!!!

title: 4.0 out of 5 stars
text:
TLDR: would definitely recommend just know what you will be getting some parts will be on the cheaper end.

Had this for 6 months now. Got it on prime day sales. It was my first gaming pc. Been researching for awhile planning to build but with the prices these days pre builts really aren’t a bad way to go if you know what to look for and what you’re getting.

I ended up buying this for less than I could have built it for. I don’t have a microcenter anywhere close so ordering online it is.

The pros:
Better parts than expected
Pny 5070ti
Montech fans unlike what the Amazon post shows
Lexar 2tb gen 4 ssd
Team group t force delta 6000 cl36 memory
Ran great out of the box and no issues so far.
Nicely packaged and delivered without damage
Comes with m&k
Was impressed with great cable management

The cons: (I’m gonna be picky on some of these)
The keyboard is awful…started not working first day.
Mouse is cheap like the keyboard but hey at least they included both right?
It’s a gigabyte b650m mobo(cheaper end) so not as many usb ports as I’d like and 1gbps Ethernet port. (Personal problems imo)
No issues with it but cheaper no name non modular power supply.
Found a couple loose screws on the fans when I first opened it. Probably from shipping.

Overall thoughts:
It was priced right, setup was simple, arrived with no damage, nicely packaged, and gaming is great on it.

IMO if you come into a prebuilt knowing where things might be lower end to save the company some money and know what you’re gonna be in for/getting it’s not a bad route. If you order this pc before plugging any power to it make sure everything is plugged in in fully and maybe double check the screws are not loose anywhere. Shippers don’t like to be gentle so who knows how much movement it goes through before arriving to you.

I’m giving it 4 stars since I had a couple small things that I found. If I could have I would have gave it 4.5 stars honestly.

The screen and gpu support bracket I added after those don’t come with the pc.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
I've been very pleased with this gaming rig so far. Some detailed thoughts:
Pros:
1) The unit was well packaged and I didn't have any issues with parts not being connected or components coming loose during shipping. However, there was no foam insert in the unit I received.
2) Instructions were simple and easy to follow with all of the support options, etc. clearly laid out in the documentation.
3) I love the access to the back of the motherboard and the cables. Easy to get to and the cable ties were solid and well done. Made upgrading easy. Also, the ASUS motherboard is very good and has extremely intuitive and easy to use onboard controls for tweaking settings, etc.
4) Most of the components seem to be of good quality. The motherboard and GPU in particular were top notch.
5) The case is not only attractive but of very, very good quality. One of the best looking gaming PCs I've seen.
Upgrades:
1) Even though the 1660 GPU was of a good quality, I had a GeForce 2070 Super in my old rig so I did swap that out. I sold the 1660 included with this rig for some very good money, lowering the cost of this PC buy a good amount.
2) Because I swapped out the GPU I did have to replace the Power Supply as well. I wasn't very impressed with the 500Watt PSU included (low quality) but that swap was easy and didn't cost me anything as I had a 750W in my old build. I would recommend a 750Watt PSU as a bare minimum if you're going to upgrade anything on this PC.
3) I threw two sticks of RAM in to beef this unit up to 32GB. Easy and cheap (less than $60). Also, I love the fact that this motherboard is upgradable to 64GB of RAM, providing insurance for future upgrading.
4) There are plenty of options to add more peripherals in addition to the already abundant amount of ports, etc. I always appreciate having room to expand a PC so the life of the build can be extended. IBuypower has done a nice job here. It would have been even better to have had one or two more USB ports in the front of the unit, but that's a minor issue.
Cons:
1) As I stated the PSU was not the greatest. But that's an easy swap. I will say the way the PSU is installed (in the bottom of the rig with a molding over it) makes for a tight squeeze and not the easiest of removals.
2) The unit runs very hot in it's original configuration. The CPU cooler, although a step up from a stock unit, is not sufficient to run graphic intensive games at temps I'm used to. Again, this was not a tough fix as I had an upgraded cooler I simply dropped in from my old build. I also installed a fan above the CPU to get some better exhaust. It is good that the top of this PC is vented.
3) Fortunately I use an ethernet connection since I have a 1Gb internet connection. This is a plus since the wifi card (and antennas) provided are basically worthless. I ran the wifi just for fun and couldn't get my connection to more than 15mps. Even my 5 year old laptops wifi card gets me about 600mps on my home network. So I was surprised they would even bother to stock what is a really nice mid range gaming PC with a pierce of junk like this.
Final thoughts:
I know some reading this may criticize my positive review since I made so many modifications to this unit upon receipt. However, my former rig was 8 years old. Yes, I had made some upgrades which helped extend the life of that unit but this iBuypower build has a powerful 17-10700 CPU with a great motherboard, a very attractive case and the latest ports, etc. After selling the included GPU and upgrading some components (most of which I already owned), the net cost for me to upgrade to this PC was about $300 less than the purchase price.
And now I have a pretty impressive gaming PC which rated at the top of the ranks on the UserBenchmark site. Not inly a UFO rating, but numbers that were 120% of that and in the upper 20% of the rigs tested.
So with a few modifications I have a Gaming PC that should last for a very long time.
Overall, I'm very, very pleased with this unit. Well worth the money IMHO.
EDIT: I completely forgot to mention the two fantastic NVME slots on the motherboard. I purchased a 1TB Samsung EVO 750 SSD as well as a corresponding 500GB EVO, keeping the included 256GB SSD as a backup OS in case I ever have a crash (I probably won't use the 1TB HHD at all). The NVME drives are incredibly fast and run smooth as can be! The one slot near the CPU is a little tight so if you're changing out the CPU cooler like I did, be sure to install the NVME drive during that process (with the cooler removed) as it will free up some room on the board. Oh and adding some inexpensive RGB lighting helps as well. A great looking rig that is the fastest best performing PC I've ever owned. Very happy with this!

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
This review is based on owning the computer for a few days. First, I am very technically inclined to use computers, so trivial issues to me may be major issues to others.

I bought the computer for my daughter, that’s into mid-level gaming (Minecraft, Roblocks, etc...) and digital art designing. Overall, this is an excellent machine for the price I got ($879 on Black Friday).

The computer powered on with no issues. After reading some of the reviews, I was worried I could end up with a dud, but luckily I didn’t have to do anything extra. The computer noise level is very quiet when powered on, so that was a very welcoming feature. Cool LED lights as well.

Windows 10 runs really well with the specs, and the operating system wasn’t filled with useless preinstalled software. The setup was really straight forward.

I’m not a fan of the keyboard. It’s too loud when typing, and the keys take a little more effort to press than necessary. That’s an easy replacement and not worth a negative rating, IMO.

The onboard HDMI port is useless as it’s not functional due to the video card having one HDMI port and three display ports. I went to the BIOS to enable the onboard HDMI port, but I didn’t see an option. If you plan to have dual or more monitors, you’ll need to buy additional cables. I needed an HDMI to display port cable to operate the second monitor, a 22E Artist Pro drawing monitor.

One for the wireless ability for the tower, one for the mouse and one for the keyboard. I found the wireless adapter for the mouse inside the battery compartment.

The next issue I ran into is the keyboard was defective. It took some time for me to figure that problem out. My monitor screen, on whatever website I was on, kept flickering with a yellow cursor box everywhere. It acted like a virus was in the computer. Yet, thanks to Gemini, he helped me diagnose the issue. A defective keyboard really didn't matter to me, I had all the parts I needed to hook up two towers to one keyboard, one mouse and one monitor.

The photo on Amazon's description of the rear of the tower is not accurate. I have attached a photo so you can see the rear. Just know that the output for a monitor is a display port. So, I had to order an adapter that converted display port to HDMI. This is a very inexpensive part that works great.

My current desktop is Windows 7. I have had this tower since Windows 7 was released. So changing to a Windows 11 tower was frighting to me. Well, let me tell you this. Windows 11 is awesome. Very intuitive and takes some time to get to where want to go. Mainly because it looks nothing like Windows 7. I found the best thing for me was to PIN the most used features along the bottom of the toolbar. The setup was super easy. Although when it wants you to choose a PIN number for Microsoft, that number is the lock code number you enter every time to open your desktop . DON'T FORGET THIS NUMBER!

Last thing, this is a full size tower. Not a compact. Full size!

It works great, and it is super fast. I hope this information helps. Enjoy, this computer is worth every penny, I absolutely recommend it 👌.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
The Short Version: (Please skip this as it has spoilers if you prefer to read ‘The Long Version’.)
16 GB RAM, 1 TB M.2 SSD. I noticed a vibration from the CPU fan and contacted TekRefurbs and they are shipping me a new fan. Their response time was quick and they were eager to make sure I was a satisfied customer. I added 16 GB more RAM, a 2.5 inch SSD, a low-profile graphics card (supports up to 3 monitors), and a dual M.2 card along with 2 more M.2 SSDs. With the 2 DP ports and HDMI port on the motherboard, I ACTUALLY RAN 6 MONITORS (all at once) while streaming 6 different videos on YouTube. I picked this up to replace my DELL Optiplex 9020 which is too old for Windows 11. (As of now, Microsoft has stated that they will be ending their support for Win 10 by the end of 2024.) Running Crystal Disk Mark I got transfer rates of 1.7 GBps (read) and 1.1 GBps (write) on the SSD that came with the computer and 2 GBps (read) and 1.6 GBps (write) on the HP M.2 SSD I added. **UPDATE: I replaced one of my M.2 SSDs with a fanxiang S660 4TB PCIe 4.0 NVMe M.2 SSD and now get the following speeds (read) 3.5 GBps and (write) 3.1 GBps. They actually make faster M.2s but they far exceed the capability of the motherboard.

I’m thrilled with both the computer and customer service couldn’t be happier with this purchase.

The Long Version:
I have purchased over 1,000 items from Amazon over the past decade and I only give reviews on the best (or the worst) items I have ordered. The renewed DELL Optiplex 7060 SFF I got from TekRefurbs is amazing and so is their customer support. (I had a little vibration with the CPU fan and I sent them a message about it, they replied the next business day and offered to send a replacement.) Awesome service!

With Microsoft stating that they will be ending their support for Windows 10 towards the end of 2024, I decided to replace my Optiplex 9020 SFF (not Win 11 compatible) now, rather than wait for a possible shortage of affordable/renewed Win 11 computers in the future. (As of now, the vast majority of people are still running Win 10.)

The model that I got was the 16 GB/ 1 TB version (other variants may be sold by different vendors). When I opened the box (and even the case) it looked like it was brand new, I couldn’t find even the smallest amount of dust anywhere. Included with the desktop was a free wireless mouse & keyboard and a few BT & WiFi dongles in addition to the built-in features from the motherboard itself. (Even without the dongles, I still have BT & WiFi connectivity.) **Models sold by TekRefurbs come with the built-in M.2 WiFi card which supports both 5 & 2.4 Ghz but for the fun of it I replaced it with the AX210 WiFi 6E Card M.2 NGFF and connected it to the 2 internal antennas.

Display Support: While some desktops (from other sellers) only have 2 Display Ports (DP) and either a VGA port (or missing the 3rd port), mine came with 2 DPs and an HDMI port. (Nice touch!) While being able to connect to 3 monitors (off of the motherboard) is nice, I added an inexpensive VisionTek Products Radeon 6350 SFF 1GB DDR3 3M DMS59 with 2X DVI-I to VGA Adapter Graphics Card that adds support for an additional 3 monitors AND I RAN A TOTAL OF 6 MONITORS AT ONCE while streaming different videos on each monitor. Granted, I’m not a gamer so I’m not concerned with Frames Per Second (FPS) but it did actually work (I normally just run 3 monitors stacked vertically – one on top of each other).

Storage Capacity (hard drives): This model, like most of the DELL SFF cases have 3 SATA ports and the newer models have a space for an M.2 SSD. The model I purchased came with a 1 GB M.2 SSD and the DVD drive and the cables were provided to connect a second hard drive as well. There is room for a 3.5 inch hard drive or you can get an adapter to mount the smaller 2.5 inch drive if you wish (there are adapters that can hold up to three 2.5 inch drives in a single 3.5 inch slot). But why settle for just one additional hard drive when you can have a total of FOUR HARD DRIVES? Thanks to the Dual M.2 PCIE Adapter for SATA or PCIE NVMe SSD with Advanced Heat Sink Solution,M.2 SSD NVME (m Key) and SATA (b Key) 22110 2280 2260 2242 2230 to PCI-e x 4 Host Controller Expansion Card, you can have up to 3 M.2 SSDs plus one 2.5 inch SSD. ***You can also get the M.2 NVME to PCIe 3.0 x4 Adapter with Aluminum Heatsink Solution (single M.2 slot) and add up to two additional 2.5 inch SSDs. I actually recommend getting this card instead of the one I purchased because the second M.2 slot has to connect to one of the SATA ports from the motherboard so the transfer speed is the same as if you connected a 2.5 inch SSD (which are cheaper). Running Crystal Disk Mark I got transfer rates of 1.7 GBps (read) and 1.1 GBps (write) on the M.2 SSD that came with the computer and 2 GBps (read) and 1.6 GBps (write) on the HP M.2 SSD I added.

RAM: The model I purchased came with 16 GB RAM (two 8 GB chips) which was nice because I added an additional 16 GB RAM for a small price. (32 GB is more than enough RAM for most applications.)

Free Extras: The extra dongles, mouse and keyboard are nice touches and pretty good quality as well. I admit that I haven’t tested them because I used a lighted keyboard (wired) and Logitech Trackball.

Summary: Whether you are using the computer ‘as is’ or you want to upgrade it, this is an excellent choice for an affordable and (still) powerful system that will carry you through the Windows 11 lifespan (and probably beyond). Despite this being the Small Form Factor (SFF) model, there is room to add a (low profile) graphics card, USB-C 3.2 card, M.2 card or whatever you wish. (Just be mindful of the power requirements of the graphics cards - this comes with a 200 watt power supply.)

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
So this is the second SkyTech PC I have bought and once again it was generally due to the fact that pricing parts to build my own was a bit difficult (COVID-19 has made GPU's scarce and pricey). My first PC is over 2 years old at this point and I was looking to actually just upgrade it's GPU but everything I was looking for was out of stock or outrageously priced (at the time a 1660 Super was running near $400). So settled on this machine, it had many of the parts I was looking to get myself: AMD 5 3600, 16GB RAM, GTX 1660 Super, B450 Motherboard (though I had looked at B550).
I am not disappointed. The machine is wonderful and came delivered without single flaw. It booted on the first try and immediately went into Windows all the RGB elements performed perfectly. I ran a series of tests after it finished setting up windows and was pleased to see that the SSD was not a total disgrace as some had stated before, getting about 530 MB/s sequential read times at 1Gib and 514 MB/s Write. That's not blazing fast, but it was better than I expected after reading reviews. I received an ADATA SU720 500GB model drive in my build and these Read/Write times are right on par with the stated performance for that drive, so I have no complaints. I dropped a NVMe drive in right away as well as a smaller 256GB solid state drive for games and other files. Storage was my only real concern with the build, but adding storage is not an issue (though it is a bit hard to get power cables up from the power supply, the cords are all quite well bundled and I had to cut a zip tie to get a free power cable for my SSD). Unlike the pictured model my build came with a B450M/AC so it had the Wi-Fi built in to the motherboard, rather than in a PCI slot. This was a pleasant surprise and also meant the motherboard had 4DIMM slots instead of 2 (like I saw some people received in their builds). The RAM I got was OLOY Brand, which is actually Chun Well Technologies and it was just standard RAM, no heat spreaders or anything fancy, but it was strong memory, running 16-18-18-36 at 1.3v with a clock speed of 100Mhz at a 15x multiplier, giving you 1500Mhz DDR, so in total it matches the 3000Mhz advertised. I am unsure what brand GPU I got, but I suspect by the I/O panel (DVI, HDMI, DisplayPort) it is an MSI Brand. Its a single fan, compact unit and I am quite happy with it, though I would have preferred a model without DVI and instead a second DisplayPort or HDMI port. In all I am very pleased with this machine, the quality, the build, the parts, and performance are all above what I anticipated and as a Cyber Monday deal for $200 off list it was pretty much a bargain.
Edit: so Cyberpunk 2077 has dropped and despite the poor reception I had it running at a smooth 60fps @1080p on this machine. I am not a crazy hardcore gamer looking for 4k and Ray Tracing, I was quite happy that my new PC ran the game with no hardware related problems and a strong graphical performance.

text:
This is a fantastic upper midrange PC Tower. Great products used, well built and exactly what your average gamer would need. We chose the i7-14700F with RTX 5070, and paid $1699 on sale while RAM prices are averaging $400 for the 32gb of DDR5 6000mhz RAM that this came with.

One of the things I really appreciate about this computer is that Thermaltake used their own products in as many places as they could. Cooling fans, CPU cooler, RAM, and case are all Thermaltake giving a really cohesive build aesthetically.

A complaint that I have with the PC is that it doesn't come with exhaust fans on top. I feel these are arguably the most important for heat dispersion. Thankfully, I was able to get the 2x 140mm fans needed to fill those top slots and Thermaltake makes them identically to the 120mm fans installed in the side and back. Installation was pretty straight forward, but wiring wasn't as easy as daisy chaining with the other fans. Not sure why they wouldn't power up but thankfully there were open spots on the motherboard. Might consider an ARGB fan hub if we run into any other issues.

Lastly, I want to cover why I removed 1 star. When we first received the PC, I wanted to verify the size and model of the fans it came with and what size fans would fit in the top of the case. So, I messaged their customer support asking these questions. It took them two days to respond and they only told me the size and model of the fans it came with. Neither their website, nor this Amazon page tells you anything about the fans or what sizes fit in each spot. Other case manufacturers have great breakdowns for this making it easy to figure out what fans fit in the case and how many you will need, if it doesn't come with them. Thankfully, I decided to go with the 140mm based on the mounting layout and the size of vent. I ordered these later in the day after waiting for a response from support. I really don't understand why they don't have this information easily accessible on their website and on this Amazon page.

For those wondering, the included fans are 120mm and max at 1500rpm. Amazon carries a 2x Pack of the 140mm Thermaltake Fans that match them for $40 USD. Overall, despite the slow and only semi-helpful support, I think this is a great computer and I'd recommend others seriously consider it. The build is really well put together, it was shipped well with the GPU installed and then cushioned all around it with a specially shaped packaging foam. My wife had this tower up and running by just pulling it out and plugging in the 4 wires in the back.

A decent little PC with plenty of opportunities for upgrading. I should note - I am running Linux Mint on this machine, not Windows 10 or 11. I feel like I get better performance with a Linux distro than I do Windows. I dropped in 32 GB of DDR4 memory into the machine after purchasing it. I also swapped drive out for an SSD 1TB drive. There are two expansion slots on the motherboard. I purchased a form factor GPU, the AMD Radeon RX 550 4GB, to give me some gaming options. Its not perfect - obviously not going to run the newest games at the highest quality, but I was pleasantly surprised at the large variety of games I can run under proton on Steam. BG3 did open and run at 30 FPS at low to medium settings. Not perfect, but anything older than that should run great. Skyrim, Fallout, City Skylines, Palworld, etc. all run smoothly with no issues. For the last expansion slot, I purchased an NVME to PCI card to attach an extra SSD 1TB Drive, giving me some extra storage.

The issues I did have... there is a dead USB port on the back of the machine. Its the one right next to the Ethernet Port. Not a huge deal if that was the only thing broken, just a little frustrating. Was dead under Windows 10 and Linux Mint after I replaced the OS, so I don't think it was a driver issue. There are not many SATA ports on the main board. I think there is only one (I might need to go back and look), so if you want to expand, you will need to get a Sata expansion card or a NVME to PCI card like I did.

All and all, I've been using this as a daily driver now for about half a year. Wanted to put it through its paces before leaving a review. If you are on a budget and don't mind doing a little bit of upgrading, this is a nice little PC. It runs extremely well under Linux and I can see this thing lasting a while with enough care.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
Really happy with my purchase, the M8 is a little workhorse. I can confirm it comes with an activated Win 11 Pro. Even though GMK has never seen an issue, I have a ritual - I boot from USB and image the NVME fresh (after getting the Windows key from a command line just in case), then wipe the mini pc's NVME (deleting all partitions) and install Windows 11 fresh. Windows picked up the BIOS key automatically on install and launched right into a fresh Windows 11 Pro. Network and sounds drivers were missing, but I grabbed them from the Europe site (Google it) and ran the .bat file. Without a reboot, everything picked up and no yellow exclamation marks in Device Manager. Windows Update took about 20 mins, as I fresh installed the newest Win 11 version (25H2 as of this writing).

So the PC itself is rock solid, no blue screens, streams OBS 4k just fine, and have no random crashes or reboots. It's a great Docker server or workstation PC if needed, runs Office just fine. I notice no loud fan noise. Can’t comment on Oculink, I don’t use it.

If you're looking for an all-in-one on the Ryzen platform, this one is a good bang for the buck.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
I bought the GMKtec Mini PC G10 (3500U) because I wanted a full-featured PC that would not take up a lot of desk space. After using the Mini PC for a couple of weeks now, I am very happy with my purchase. First of all, it not only replaced my old desktop PC , but it is also much faster. For those interested in the GMKtec G10, here are some specifics…

Performance: Very good. All my apps open fast without any issues. All the typical Windows, Google desktop and my other well-used programs operated smoothly. Also, for a small unit, it is very quiet.

Video: Very good. I hooked mine using the HDMI port (it also comes with a HDMI cable) to my large screen TV. No problem.

Set-up: Very easy. My GMKtec Mini PC G10 package came with a power cord, power adapter, and HDMI cable. The Mini PC connected easily to my home wi-fi. It also has a hard-wired LAN port for a wired connection. I simply disconnected my old pc system and plugged in the G10, and it was ready to go

Size: Very small cube size. Looks like about 4 inches on each side

Overall: I would highly recommend the GMKtec Mini PC G10. It is a good value and has very good performance.

It has all the normal features a Windows PC should have; it connects to the internet easily; it has lots of ports for peripheral devices. with lots of USB ports. If you are like me and don’t want a huge computer taking up a lot of desk space, and want one at a good price, the Mini PC G10 will be a good choice.

text: I would have given it 5 stars, if it had not became inoperable within a week. The problem was most likely due to a Windows update that removed necessary hardware definition files. I added a second NVMe drive then installed the operating system that I trust for daily, efficient, flawless, and spy-free operation... Debian 13. Installing a drive on this computer is so easy...just pop off the top and insert it. This computer is as strong and functional as a Intel i5 series 8. For those who prefer an uncluttered desk, install this powerful, little box to the back of the monitor. Processing speed, graphics and storage are more than enough, even for power users. I am very happy with my purchase and I would buy it again.

text:
I've been looking for a smaller PC with low power demands to use as a little server. The G10 with a AMD Ryzen 53500U sips power at the default setting and has the 4 cores/8 threads to perform office tasks, minor gaming, and the server tasks (Network Attached Storage in my case) that I was looking for. This would also be a great second PC for your house, especially if you have limited space.

It was easy to set up - open the box, remove the sticker off the back, and plug it into your existing keyboard/mouse/monitor or TV. The Windows 11 set up took a little time but that happens on all PCs. Windows 11 Pro is included. I let the Windows update run and download all the updates and then wanted to run a quick test. I used Blackmagic Design's RAW Speed Test and was surprised to see that it could handle editing 2160p30 for both the CPU and GPU with BRAW 3:1 - I can take this as a basic portable video editor.

Pros:
Includes HDMI cable
Low out-of-the-box power consumption (you can adjust the TDP in the BIOS if you want it faster).
Extremely quiet
65W USB power adapter included so no proprietary power adapter to worry about.
Clean install of Windows 11 (no garbageware)
Upgradable (open NVMe slot (up to 16TB total), swappable Dual Channel DDR4 SODIMM RAM (up to 64GB))
Includes VESA Mount for flexible mounting
Can drive 3x 4k monitors.
Lots of connectivity: Wifi 5, Bluetooth, 2.5Gbps Ethernet, lots of USB ports, HDMI and DisplayPort.

Cons:
Power adapter is on the short side.
Plastic construction (although it's well constructed and light

Pictures:
1. Test from the Blackmagic Design RAW Speed Test
2. You can see in the pictures that it's a little larger than my GMKtec NucBox G5.
3. It has a nice fan on the bottom to keep it cool
4. Yippee - a USB-C power adapter.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
WOW!

My new GMK Core i9-13900HK (NucBox_K10) has put a smile on my face. It's replacing an outdated Win 7 machine for our everyday use: research, email, entertainment, surfing, and some gaming. It came preloaded with Windows 11 Pro, which includes New Outlook. For sure, I was immediately very impressed with the K10's performance.

Specifics:
Device name NucBox_K10
Processor 13th Gen Intel(R) Core(TM) i9-13900HK 2.60 GHz
Installed RAM 32.0 GB (31.8 GB usable)
System type 64-bit operating system, x64-based processor
Pen and touch No pen or touch input is available for this display
Edition Windows 11 Pro Version 24H2
Installed on ‎5/‎1/‎2025
OS build 26100.4202
Experience Windows Feature Experience Pack 1000.26100.107.0

First, I updated the OS using Windows Update. The update took perhaps 2 hrs (typical given other users' comments re: Win11 updates). Next order of business was to install my security software and run a full scan: pleasantly, no issues.
Bios access was simple using the esc key, though I had no reason to change anything.
The machine runs extremely quiet and was very fast at all the tasks I performed. I'm currently using WiFi and the GMK K10 is equally distant from my router and an Access Point in the lower level. I tested performance on 4 local networks I had defined: Router(2.4 and 5.0) and AP(2.4 and 5.0). No matter the network, the GMK K10 was impressively snappy.
The wi-fi antennas are clearly a plus. Web pages appear in a flash, and every task I perform delivers at turbo-speed.
I ran multiple applications simultaneously with numerous tabs open and everything ran flawlessly.
I plan to add a second SSD and the easy access panel on the underside should make things easier.
Additionally, the Kensington Lock capability provides for a layer of physical security if that's an issue.

On the flip side, the power button could use better illumination. Depending on ambient lighting, it can be difficult to tell if the machine is on or off (a tribute to how quiet it is). When I ran the OS update the screen went blank multiple times and, judging from the power button, I didn't know if the K10 was asleep, in the middle of a reboot, shutdown, or even if the update was complete.

In sum, the GMK K10 is a great machine. Big shout out to GMKTec, I'm impressed.
If you're looking for a low cost, up-to-date upgrade to replace your present pc, you should consider the new GMK NucBox_K10.

text:
EVO-T1 Ultra 9 285H 64 GB RAM, 1 TB NVME SSD

This is one very nice mini PC. I originally bought this to use as my main server in my homelab. The first couple of weeks I kept Windows 11 on the system to use and test out the components. The is one great mini PC. I could easily be used a a small workstation for most people. The weakest link is the iGPU, but even this is not a deal breaker; it is very capable, and you can always use the oculink for and eGPU. It easily handled everything I tested on it and was very quite in comparison to my workstation with an NVidia GPU.

Since then I've removed Windows and installed Proxmox. It has been working great running many VMs and LXCs. It has been on 24/7 running everything from Frigate (with detector inference speeds of 6-8 ms with YOLOv9), to Windows 11, and everything in-between that a homelab runs.

The mini PC comes is a very nice box with and HDMI cable and external power brick. There is very little documentation, and it would be nice if there was info on the fan button and how to open the mini PC to add additional drives or upgrade the RAM. If you want this info you have to Google it, as their own GMKtec's website has no info on it.

I gave the product 4/5 stars, only because I could not do 4.5/5. It loses 0.5 because of the lack of proper documentation or the lack of being able to find it on GMKtec's website.

My new GMK Core i9-13900HK (NucBox_K10) has put a smile on my face. It's replacing an outdated Win 7 machine for our everyday use: research, email, entertainment, surfing, and some gaming. It came preloaded with Windows 11 Pro, which includes New Outlook. For sure, I was immediately very impressed with the K10's performance.

Specifics:
Device name NucBox_K10
Processor 13th Gen Intel(R) Core(TM) i9-13900HK 2.60 GHz
Installed RAM 32.0 GB (31.8 GB usable)
System type 64-bit operating system, x64-based processor
Pen and touch No pen or touch input is available for this display
Edition Windows 11 Pro Version 24H2
Installed on ‎5/‎1/‎2025
OS build 26100.4202
Experience Windows Feature Experience Pack 1000.26100.107.0

First, I updated the OS using Windows Update. The update took perhaps 2 hrs (typical given other users' comments re: Win11 updates). Next order of business was to install my security software and run a full scan: pleasantly, no issues.
Bios access was simple using the esc key, though I had no reason to change anything.
The machine runs extremely quiet and was very fast at all the tasks I performed. I'm currently using WiFi and the GMK K10 is equally distant from my router and an Access Point in the lower level. I tested performance on 4 local networks I had defined: Router(2.4 and 5.0) and AP(2.4 and 5.0). No matter the network, the GMK K10 was impressively snappy.
The wi-fi antennas are clearly a plus. Web pages appear in a flash, and every task I perform delivers at turbo-speed.
I ran multiple applications simultaneously with numerous tabs open and everything ran flawlessly.
I plan to add a second SSD and the easy access panel on the underside should make things easier.
Additionally, the Kensington Lock capability provides for a layer of physical security if that's an issue.

On the flip side, the power button could use better illumination. Depending on ambient lighting, it can be difficult to tell if the machine is on or off (a tribute to how quiet it is). When I ran the OS update the screen went blank multiple times and, judging from the power button, I didn't know if the K10 was asleep, in the middle of a reboot, shutdown, or even if the update was complete.

In sum, the GMK K10 is a great machine. Big shout out to GMKTec, I'm impressed.
If you're looking for a low cost, up-to-date upgrade to replace your present pc, you should consider the new GMK NucBox_K10.

I am using a 1080p TV that I have this pc connected to and as such have no interest in higher resolution gaming. This pc has three USB ports that support power delivery but one of them, which uses a USB A connector does not seem to work for charging, but it could be that I need a proper USB A to C charging cable. So, in the end, while this computer can play the latest games at 1080p on medium graphics setting, I would not consider this to be a gaming pc for the reason that it runs very hot when gaming as well as there being some slowdown and that is my biggest concern with this pc as I will be using it to play games. I highly recommend this PC for anyone who is looking for something small and powerful.
