title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
Upfront, I am impressed with the GMKtec G2.

I have purchased a number of mini/micro PCs recently for various projects (both personal and commercial) so I feel I have some good points of reference for this unit. From a "brand" standpoint, I've tried a few different ones but I find myself coming back to GMKtec. I like their designs, the products are solid and well engineered, and they have a fully open/unlocked BIOS, which allows for some case-specific tweaking on my end.

I have a total of 3 comparable units: this GMKtec G2 (Intel N100, 12G DDR5-4800 RAM, 512GB mSATA), the GMKtec KB5 (Intel N5105, 8G DDR4-2933 RAM, 128GB mSATA), Kamrui AK1Plus (Intel N95, 8G DDR4-2933 RAM, 256GB mSATA).

Out of the box, the G2 scored 8.7% better than the AK1Plus and 42% better than the KB5 on Passmark PerformanceTest 9 (older version sure, but it's what I have). The N5105 is an older generation CPU, so this difference is understandable, but still bigger than I expected. The KB5 was something I purchased for a remote monitoring PC and a digital signage project, it's extremely capable for those tasks as well as light office type tasks. This G2 with the boost CPU and RAM push it into the range of honest general usage. You're not really going to play any modern games on it, but any web browsing, video streaming, day to day basic usage is easily handled. It would also make a great emulation rig for a home arcade machine project or classic gaming station.

The N95 vs N100 is fairly close in overall specs, with the N95 being slightly higher TDP/power and slightly faster graphics (but less execution engines: 16 vs N100's 24), so the main difference maker here is the memory. DDR5 4800 MT/s over the DDR4 2933 MT/s provides a solid boost in both CPU, Memory, and 2D graphics benchmarks and real world performance.

2D graphics benchmarks clock in at 628 for G2, 565 for AK1Plus, 458 for KB5; and 3D benchmarks are within 1% across all 3 chips/models (the scores are low, these aren't made for 3D graphics).

The CPU benchmarks show the biggest difference with the N100 here coming in at 7881, the N95 in the AK1Plus model scored 7062, and the N5105 in the KB5 model scored 3660.

Now there is a tweak I did in the BIOS to boost performance and benchmark scores here to a consistent 8300, which is a 5% boost. I changed the fan settings, adjusted the power limits, and tweaked the core boost values. This does not overclock this CPU at all, but what it does do is allows the CPU to run at full strength. Raising the fan setting here is the most important to help offset heat and thermal throttling. Normal usage doesn't cause it to throttle very often and by default the fan is quite quiet, but if you do anything that pushes all the cores for any length of time, it does heat up and then throttle.

I've taken mine apart to see how it fits together and the design is clever and impressive. Taking the bottom panel off shows the CPU cooler (all copper) and is where the LED ring on the bottom plugs into the motherboard. Nothing really accessible there. RAM is soldered on in chiplets, so non-replaceable, but at 12G running DDR5 you likely wouldn't need to anyway. The top panel, which is replaceable with the included red 3D-printed option, reveals the mSATA SSD, and underneath is the WiFi/BT card. If you disconnect either WiFi antenna connection, they are a bit difficult to reconnect but must be done otherwise you'll have terrible WiFi reception. The plastic insert sitting under the WiFi card can only be removed by disconnecting the WiFi antennas and really doesn't reveal anything replaceable or upgradable underneath.

The form factor of the unit is nice and small, somewhat impressively so at 3.5"x3.5"x1.6". They make the most use of the size available too, with power button on front, USB on right side, display on left side, and networking & power on the rear. This design works great for being mounted to the back of a monitor or underside of a desk/cabinet. If you're looking for a minimalist and clean cable arrangement, you might find this layout annoying.

With dual 1G LAN ports, this box could also be repurposed as a small firewall device if you chose to install PFSense or OPNSense. You could also install Hyper-V on the included Win11 Pro install and have a dedicated port for a VM. I tested each port and got close to line speed on both simultaneously (~800-900mbps). WiFi performance was acceptable too, with an avg of 300-400 mbps on a WiFi5 connection and 600-800 mbps on a WiFi6 connection.

I was unable to test the bandwidth of the 3 USB 3.2 ports, but anything I threw at it worked just fine, included an external SSD.

Triple display support with 2 HDMI and 1 DP is nice. The DP is v1.4 but doesn't support 8k as a limitation of the CPU itself, but triple 4k displays isn't too shabby!

The unit pulled about 8-9W of power at idle and ramped up to about 36W at absolute max, averaging closer to 16W during normal usage. Hooking this up to even a small UPS should allow plenty of runtime in power outages if you want/need to keep this up 24/7.

The CPU cooler is well sized and designed for the CPU used. A more powerful CPU (or the ability to overclock this chip) would require a more powerful cooler.

My only slight issues with the unit are: it would have been nice to have a USB Type-C on the front near the power button, and the Realtek LAN choice over an Intel (possibly even a 2.5G) option is a bit limiting but an understandable cost measure.

As a lightweight office-use PC or Kiosk type machine, it is absolutely sufficient. As a low power, low cost, task specific project PC this is a fantastic choice with enough CPU and RAM power to take more complex tasks. Small on-premise web server or digital signage, custom Arcade emulator or classic console game emulator, running monitoring or automation software, or even lightweight Hypervisor are all fantastic choices for this unit.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
I am incredibly impressed with the sheer multitasking power packed into this compact chassis. The AMD Ryzen V2748 processor is a total workhorse, featuring 8 cores and 16 threads that handle heavy workloads, massive Excel spreadsheets, and 4K video streaming simultaneously without any stuttering. Unlike many other mini PCs that struggle with heat, the thermal management here is top-notch; even under a heavy load, the fan remains a low, unobtrusive hum, and the unit stays remarkably cool to the touch. It comes pre-installed with a clean version of Windows 11 Pro and the 16GB of DDR4 RAM provides a very snappy user experience right out of the box, making it a perfect primary desktop replacement for anyone looking to reclaim their desk space.

The connectivity and upgrade potential are where this machine truly shines as a long-term investment. Having the ability to run a triple 4K monitor setup via the HDMI, DisplayPort, and full-featured Type-C ports is a game changer for productivity and creative work. I also appreciate that the internal layout is accessible, allowing for future RAM upgrades up to 64GB or swapping in a larger SSD if the 512GB NVMe drive eventually fills up. The build quality feels premium with a sleek, textured finish that doesn’t attract fingerprints, and the inclusion of a VESA mount allowed me to hide the entire PC behind my monitor for a completely wire-free look. For the price point, the performance-to-value ratio is simply unbeatable for a home office or a high-end media center.

Edit- After some tinkering, I came to the conclusion that the stock Sata SSD is too slow. I added an 500GB NVME for extra storage. This definitely helped the write speeds. I also ditched the Realtek RTL8852BE wifi card, and replaced it with an Intel Ax210. My wifi speeds DOUBLED, I went from 231mbps to 461mbps. My Bluetooth went from 5.3 to 5.4, a nice bonus. I added another 16gb of DDR4, to 32GB total. This is now a proper speed demon, capable of heavy multitasking. Don't get me wrong It was pretty good out of the box, BUT NOW IT'S GREAT!!!

title: 4.0 out of 5 stars
text:
In these modern times, when the multiplicity of devices clamors for attention and connection, the UGREEN USB 3.0 Hub, with its four ports, presents itself as a most commendable instrument of order. Its construction is modest yet firm, the ports accommodating a variety of implements with ease and without fuss. I have employed it with several devices—external drives, keyboards, and a host of other technological appendages—and found it to perform with admirable constancy, maintaining swift transmission of data as if it were an obedient steward attending to the whims of its master.

The hub, though competent, does not escape entirely the occasional flicker of instability under duress, and the length of its cable may, for some, impose slight inconvenience. Nevertheless, these trifles are easily outweighed by the convenience it affords, bringing order to the chaos of multiple connections. Four stars, for the device demonstrates both utility and steadfastness, a faithful companion for those who navigate the ever-growing labyrinth of modern electronics.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
Like it or not, USB "A" is going to be around for a long time - especially if you have a bunch of legacy devices. That leaves most of us needing to expand the number of USB ports from our laptop or other devices. Please do note that this hub is not intended for high power consumption devices or charging. It may trickle a small charge to your phone or tablet, but expect it to take a very long time.

I use this for numerous devices that are primarily moving data and it handles them all efficiently. Webcam, printer, sound bar, mouse, keyboard, thumb drives, and the list goes on. I even have one with the longer cable attached to my desktop computer that has a plethora of USB ports, but many are on the back of the tower out of reach. After all, USB is about quick and easy access.

So why this one? I've owned a number of USB hubs and this is the best one I've found so far. One of the biggest problems with lesser USB hubs is a poor fiit of the USB A ports that can result in sketchy connections. Not good when you're transferring critical data. This is particularly important with a laptop where the hub may be dangling or input cables may move around. Additionally it feels sturdy, its compact size helps keep my desk tidy, and I have not yet found a use case where it doesn't work although as they say, YMMV.

I just bought three of these units and have them all connected to multiple screen displays. The build quality is excellent, especially for the price. You get a compact form factor, it runs very quietly, and the Intel chip delivers plenty of performance.

I am a happy repeat customer, and I would definitely recommend GMKtec products to other computer users. Overall, it’s a great product and fantastic value.

title: 1.0 out of 5 stars
text:
Late 2023 probably: Super fast, compared to my other PCs. I had a problem connecting an external BD reader (via a SATA-to-USB3 connector), so I cannot use that with this PC. Otherwise everything is working as advertised, including USB3 for external HDDs. HDMI and DP also worked fine, as did wireless (USB2 dongle) keyboard and mouse. My gigabit LAN works just fine. Windows 11 Pro is successfully activated. I have not tested USB-C. I was able to expand the RAM to the maximum 64 GB, but due to unclear documentation, I was not able to add an SSD expansion (which I had bought and then returned). In fact, I found the documentation so lacking that I tried "Contact Us" with the manufacturer, and did not get a reply. I finally gave up, and did not add more internal SSD. Because this PC uses SSD storage, I do NOT use it for a lot of writes and rewrites: that is all done with real, networked HDDs. (In my experience, SSDs have a limited shelf life if you constantly write and rewrite them.) This was well worth the money.

UPDATE March 2025: I am changing my review from 5 stars to 1 star. This Mini-PC was working great until a Microsoft (MS) update killed it. After I log in, the screen goes black. I can then Ctrl+Alt+Del and THAT window shows up (rest of screen) still black. I finally muddled through restoring an earlier version of the PC (before the Windows Update). By the next day the PC had died again because Microsoft insisted on reinstalling the "bad" update. It took me forever to figure out how to stop MS from reinstalling the update. (You stop downloads via the Registry. It still thinks I should install the update, but it seems thwarted -- for now.) Trying to contact MS proved impossible. Their automation is such that it doesn't consider that an update is bad. There is no way to tell them that, that I could find. I tried looking on the Intel site for a video-driver update, but that accomplished nothing. Some INTEL GRAPHICS UTILITY (or some such) comes up from time to time and says something is wrong, but it doesn't tell me what. I go to the MS shop and it says that app is installed and up-to-date. TWICE I HAVE TRIED TO CONTACT GMKtec support and TWICE it has ignored my entreaties. I hold open the possibility that my firewall or Ad Blocker or Privacy Badger is blocking something (since I run an email server), but there is no indication ANYWHERE of what I have to let through. If GMKtec is trying to get through, they are blocked, and the AMAZON page gives no hint on what IPs, etc. need to get through. In my experience, it is not my PC blocking the connection: it is there is no active GMKtec support, despite what the AMAZON web page says. So I am STUCK with no longer being able to install MS updates. And to underline how arrogant MS is, it doesn't give you the ability to block just one update. In older versions of Windows, you could block a specific update, but not in the newer versions. If I went back to allowing downloads, it would install the bad update. The PC is running Windows 11 Pro. I can still use the Mini-PC; I can just no longer update it with MS updates. And if you're wondering, I did connect a second monitor and try to get things to work that way, but MS Windows completely freaked out and forgot how to do the desktop. (I've done it before with other WIndows, and I can navigate mulitple displays just fine with them. It's something about the video on this PC and Windows 11, is my guess.) So for now, I can use the Mini-PC but cannot get MS updates for, for example, so-called critical vulnerabilities. MS is absolutely no help -- their interface has no "update is bad" report function. And GMKtec, as far as I can tell, does not actively support their product, despite what the implication is on the AMAZON web site. The Mini-PC worked for for more than a year...until the "bad" MS update. Oh, yeah, I searched for and downloaded drivers from the GKMtec web site and presumably installed them (that process was clear as mud), so who knows -- maybe I didn't install them. I wasn't born knowing how hardware works...or software for that matter...

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
This thing is perfect for my needs - I shopped around on here for a solid ~60 days comparing different mini-PC brands and models, and their individual price points vs. features/compatibility. My needs were as follows:

- < $200 in cost
- minimum of N150 CPU
- shipped with or can be upgraded to 32 GB RAM
- M.2 NVMe Gen 3 minimum, with 2x M.2 slots, shipping with a minimum of 500 GB on at least one slot
- must run Linux (Debian based distros) without causing any complications w/ the hardware
- WiFi 6, BT 5.2
- minimum of 4x USB 3.2 ports
- ideally at least 1x USB-C port (this is the only attribute that this machine is lacking!)

Immediately upon arrival, I installed a second M.2 NVMe @ 1 TB, and a few days later I upgraded the RAM, replacing the single stick of 16 GB DDR4 it shipped with, and installed a single 32 GB DDR4 - I believe this is more than the manufacturers max specs, but I did research this before doing so, just as I have with my other machines that have hardware upgrades beyond max specs.

I left Windows 11 Pro that it shipped with on the 500 GB M.2, and then installed MX Linux 23.6 onto the secondary M.2 1 TB that I installed, and assigned the secondary M.2 running MX Linux to be the primary boot device..

Everything works perfectly, without any problems whatsoever. Before the upgrade of the RAM from 16 to 32 GB, Windows 11 Pro felt snappy and responsive for most basic tasks, but heavy multitasking began to make things feel sluggish.

However, when booting into MX Linux, this thing shreds.. Everything is extremely smooth, and super responsive, even when heavy multitasking, and this was before the upgrade of the RAM to 32 GB.. Basically, if you prefer to use Linux as your primary OS on bare metal, this thing feels much better in Linux vs. Windows, but that is to be expected.

Video quality is good, no screen tearing or anything like that in Linux, but I have not tried installing any distro with a KDE Plasma desktop environment yet, which is where I would expect to experience anything suboptimal relating to the video.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
This is my 2nd BMAX mini-PC purchase after 5 years, and I am absolutely a fan of mini-PCs in general. BMAX stands out from the rest of the mini-PC offerings in that they incorporate recent chipsets (AMD or Intel), dual NVMe support, and all the connections (USB-C, DisplayPort, HDMI, etc) you would expect on an up to date PC today. In short, this is not system comprised of a hodgepodge of generations old surplus components. Although maybe the 'surplus' description is still applicable.

My first basic and very affordable mini PC still works today, but due to my extremely positive experience, I decided to upgrade to one of their most powerful offerings today. The BMAX B8A Pro runs a current AMD Ryzen 7 8745HS released July 2024. When it comes to mini-PCs using generations old chipsets, this is pretty much as good as it gets.

The B8A Pro touts itself as a gaming mini-PC but here's the reality. Call of Duty Warzone runs at the lowest settings, and struggles with 30fps at 1080p. The bottleneck is not so much with the internal Radeon 780M graphics but with the memory. The single 16GB DDR5 4400Mhz memory module is great for home office, streaming and browsing, but not for gaming. For gaming, 2 memory modules are recommended. 4400Mhz DDR5 is also on the slower end when there options up to 6400Mhz today. This gaming bottleneck applies to other BMAX offerings also as the 24GB or 8GB are also single memory modules.

So in short, this is not a FPS capable mini-PC out of the box (unless you want to run it at super low resolution and frame rates). You would be better served purchasing a PS5 or Xbox instead. If you keep these expectations in mind, then the BMAX mini-PC then becomes an incredible system that delivers great value and is blazing fast for everything else.

Lastly, one thing that is obvious but not mentioned often in reviews is that laptops are just not great at being a static home PC. Biggest issue with long term reliability is cooling and wearing out the USB-C connector. So if you are primarily using your PC at home, this is where the compact form, power saving, and most of all....value of a mini-PC shines.

title: 4.0 out of 5 stars
text:
This is a great little PC in a small package, but takes a bit of tweaking to get it running properly.

PROs:
Great small form factor PC, nice build quality and small footprint. Once configured correctly, it runs like a dream with my 3 screens - 2 x 32" Samsungs and 1 x 24" LG in portrait mode. I have not used it for gaming, but for streaming and dev work it runs amazingly well - no lag or difference from my old i7-13900k gaming machine. The file transfer speeds are insanely fast, and I have several USB hubs with many peripherals running without any issues. All in all, it's mindblowing how much computing power is in such a small box.

CONs:
There is a decent amount of configuration required to get it running seamlessly.

First of all, the included HDMI cable would not connect to some of my displays, and the HDMI ports are fickle depending on the cables you are using. I ended up buying JSAUX and oldboytech cables from Amazon and I can confirm that both of those brands work, but several others I tried did not.

Secondly, the default fan noise is really loud, even when it isn't under load. I had to go to the Geekom website and download a BIOS unlocker so that I could enter the BIOS and turn the thermal profile to quiet.

Lastly, the out-of-the-box drivers are out of date and need updating in order to get things working properly. I use three screens and could not get them all to connect at the right resolution until I downloaded the latest Intel Arc drivers from Intel. Similarly with the wireless and bluetooth, they were finicky until I downloaded and installed the latest drivers.

Conclusion:
Don't get me wrong, this is a great little box, but it is not plug-and-play if you have specific setup requirements. That said, I would happily buy it again knowing what I know now, but it is the reason why it doesn't get a 5 star from me. I spent a good few hours of trial and error to get it running how I like it, but now I am very happy with it.

text:
this GEEKOM A5 2025 Edition Mini-PC definitely presents Quality: First, the box it came looks like it might last over 50 years. You might say “So what?”, but it was designed to give the purchaser a sense of quality before they even open the box. Inside the box, the GEEKOM A5 2025 Edition Mini PC speaks stylish quality with its gleaming metallic appearance; chrome edge along the top, and crisp airflow cutouts. Ports for just about any application (even USB Charging) are available on nearly every side; including a card reader slot. Plus has a Kensington security slot (If you gotta ask, you probably don’t use it). Inside the GEEKOM A5 (no tools needed) is space for extra M.2 SSD storage; both SATA-3 and NVMe. I effortlessly added a 1T NVMe.
Also included is a sturdy VESA mount (Convenient for mounting on the back of a monitor or someplace else with a VESA standard).
The preinstalled Windows 11 Pro was a bit of a challenge however. More challenging than other mini-PC with Windows “preinstalled”, which took only 10s of minutes. This install was an hour or so, with many trips to the Windows Update Server and slow reboots. I may mention that to GEEKOM when I review on their site.
But now it’s fast, smooth and quiet, and more importantly it’s cool – just a couple of degrees F over ambient. Time will tell if I need the 90-day return or 3-Year Warranty Coverage.
This GEEKOM A5/2025 mini-PC is a great value for the money; I highly recommend it to anyone who’s looking for a mini-PC.

Nachdem mein alter Stand-Pc zu langsam geworden ist, habe ich mich nach einem neuen Pc für Office arbeiten umgesehen. Da bin ich auf dieses kompakte Kraftpaket gestoßen. Ich war erst skeptisch ob der Prozessor genug Leistung bringt, aber nach einigen Tests bin ich äusserst positiv überrascht.
Der kleine Celeron aus der 11. Generation kommt mit 4 Kernen daher und hat einen Basistakt von 2 GHz. In der Realität kommt er aber dank Intel Turbo Boost 2.0 auf 2,6 GHz in kurzen Phasen sogar auf 2,9 GHz.
Ich hatte keinerlei Probleme was die Leistung angeht. Mein Gerät ist ausserdem mit 8GB RAM und 256 GB SSD Speicher ausgestattet. Das wirkt vielleicht auf den ersten Blick etwas klein, aber für das was ich damit anstelle reicht es mehr als aus.
Als Betriebssystem kommt Windows 11 vorinstalliert. Es gibt keine unnötigen vorinstallierten Programme, nur Windows.
Die Einrichtung war ziemlich einfach. Nach ca. 15 Minuten war alles fertig und der Pc einsatzbereit.
Ich habe auch ein paar kleine Benchmarks laufen lassen. Leistungstechnisch bewegt sich der Prozessor ca. bei halber Lestung eines i7 der 11. Generation. Das klingt erst mal mager, aber wie gesagt, für Büroarbeiten mehr als ausreichend.
Was die Grafikleistung angeht kommt hier eine Intel UHD Grafikeinheit zum Einsatz. Damit lassen sich bis theoretisch bis zu 3 4k@60Hz Monitore ansteuern. Allerdings gibt es nur 2 dedizierte Video Ausgänge.
Nach etwas rumprobieren kann ich sagen, dass Videowiedergabe von 4k Inhalten möglich ist, alles was über 4k hinaus geht ist dann aber doch zu viel. Aber als solide Media Station kann ich das kleine Ding auf jeden Fall auch empfehlen.

I/O ist für so ein kleines Gerät auch beachtlich:
Wir haben insgesamt 3 normale USB Typ-A und 2 USB Typ-C Schnittstellen. Die beiden USB-A Ports auf der Rückseite sind USB 3.1 Anschlüsse mit 5 Gbps, der auf der Front ist ein USB 3.2 mit 10 Gbps.
Bei den Typ-C Ports ist es anders herum. Auf der Vorderseite haben wir 5 Gbps und auf der Rückseite sind es 10 Gbps.
Ausserdem befindet sich auf der Rückseite noch ein Gigabit Ethernet Port, ein HDMI 1.4 und ein Mini DisplayPort (ein Adapter von Mini auf Voll sit dabei) und der Stromanschluss.
Auf der Vorderseite befindet sich neben den beiden USB Ports noch ein Kombo Kopfhörer-Mikrofon 3,5mm Klinke Anschluss und der Anschalter.
Auf der linken Seite befindet sich ein SD-Karten Leser und rechts haben wir ein Kenisington Lock. Wer seine Gräte gerne anschließt, kann das also auch tun ;)
Dazu gibt es dann noch Bluetooth und Wlan mit dabei, sodass man kein Lan-Kabel Quer durchs Hauslegen muss. Bislang gab es auch noch keine negativen Verbindungsabbrüche.

Was die Benutzung angeht bin ich echt beeindruckt. Selbst unter Vollast hört man nicht mehr als ein flüster-leises säuseln des Lüfters. Mein alter Stand Pc war deutlich lauter im Vergleich. Ein nettes Feature ist die VESA Halterung die mitgeliefert wird. Damit lässt sich der kleine Kasten sehr einfach auf die Rückseite von Monitoren, and die Wand oder unter den Schreibtisch hängen und ist somit einfach zu verstecken.
Mit einem Bluetooth Tastatur/Maus Set lässt sich so ein komplett kabelloser Schreibtisch einrichten - sehr schick, allerdings für mich nicht so wichtig.

Für alle die ihren Stromverbrauch senken wollen habe ich gute Neuigkeiten: Das kleine Teil braucht zwischen 8 und 20 Watt, je nach Auslastung natürlich.

Alles in allem bin ich wirklich zufrieden. Der Rechner ist klein, leise und für die Leistung echt günstig. Office Programme laufen ohne Probleme, Videos schauen (streamen oder von Platte) geht ohne Probleme. Wer keinen NASA Rechner braucht oder einen Gaming Pc sucht, der wird hiermit mehr als zufrieden sein.

text:
Este mini-PC es una pasada.

El producto, además del ordenador en sí, trae una funda, por si quieres llevarte el ordenador en una mochila, para que no se ralle. Trae también un cable HDMI, y una plaquita cuadrada con tornillos, para ponerla detrás de tu monitor (si tiene soporte VESA) y tener así un all-in-one (aunque claro, para meter y sacar pendrives podría quedar un poco a desmano).

En un tamaño súper compacto que te podrías meter en el bolsillo de un abrigo tienes un ordenador personal completo. La presentación es inmejorable, viene en una cajita compacta muy bien protegida. El diseño es muy bonito, la superficie es de color negro y brillante, puede dejar marcas de dedos pero no se ve especialmente "sucio" y además se limpia fácil. La calidad de materiales se hace patente en cuanto lo sacas de la caja. Tiene 3 USB normales, 2 USB-C, salida de auriculares, toma de red RJ45, mini Displayport y HDMI. También tiene una ranura de lector de tarjetas SD. El botón de Power se pone en naranja parpadeante cuando el equipo está en suspensión, es apretarlo y se enciende la pantalla de bloqueo de windows de forma instantánea.

El equipo en sí no es muy potente. Pero es que me ha costado poco más de 200€ cuando los modelos superiores i3, i5 o i7 están entre 300 y 600 euros. Obviamente para juegos o para meterle caña con temas gráficos seguramente no sea la mejor opción. Sin embargo sí que es más que suficiente para un uso diario normal, como para temas de ofimática, usar el Chrome para ver vídeos en youtube, navegar por redes como Facebook, instalar aplicaciones sencillas como Spotify, tener algún gestor de fotos, programitas no muy pesados, etc. El procesador muy raramente llega al 100%, y esto es algo que sorprende, pues los céleron antes iban muy limitados. Al parecer las nuevas versiones de los céleron van bastante más holgadas que antes.

De momento estoy impresionado y muy contento. Tengo conectado un monitor QHD de 1440 líneas y se ve súper nítido. Viene con el nuevo Windows 11, que se configura nada más encenderlo, en 5 minutos, y que me está resultando bastante atractivo.

Très satisfait.

text:
Mein Laptop ist nach zehn bis elf Jahre in sein Alter gekommen, um sich so langsam in Rente zu verabschieden. Daher habe ich schon seit längerer Zeit nach einem Ersatz gesucht und bin dabei auf die MiniPCs gestoßen. Da ich Tastatur und Monitore zur Erweiterung des Laptops schon habe und diese nicht wegwerfen will, habe ich mich mit dem Thema MiniPC befasst. Durch Zufall bin ich auf die Firma Geekom aufmerksam geworden und schwankte noch zwischen IT8 und IT11. Letzten Endes habe ich mich nun für den IT11 mit 16 GB RAM und 512 GB SSD entschieden. Ich bereue es kein bisschen und freue, dass ich nun auch endlich Windows 11 habe, da mein alter Laptop nicht Win11-fähig ist. Zudem kommt noch hinzu, dass ich durch den MiniPC wieder mehr Platz auf dem Schreibtisch habe.

Der MiniPC ist sehr handlich und kompakt gebaut, passt in meine Hand und ist leicht. Klar, Plastik bzw. Kunststoff ist dabei, doch sieht er hochwertig aus und die Verarbeitung, soweit es sich mir erschließt, ist auch sehr gelungen.

Anschlüsse sind mehr als genug vorhanden. An der linken Seite ist ein SD-Kartenslot vorhanden, an der rechten Seite ein Kensington Security Lock, was sicherlich auch bei dem ein oder anderen Verwendung finden wird. An der Vorderseite sind USB-C, USB-A, Klinkenanschluss und der Powerbutton. Hinten gibt es dem Stromanschluss, einen Mini DisplayPort, LAN-Anschluss, zwei USB-A, HMDI und USB-C. Alles in den neuesten Generationen und Variationen. Es sind genug Schnittstellen vorhanden, um allerlei Geräte anzuschließen. Ich gehe davon aus, dass man über HDMI und DisplayPort 4K rausbekommt und so ein sehr gutes Sehvergnügen hat. Offiziell sollen es bis zu vier 4K-Monitoren sein, da bin ich sehr gespannt, wenn ich mal dazu komme, meinen Schreibtisch soweit auszubauen und aufzurüsten.

Im Inneren ist es ein Intel-Chip i7 der 11. Generation verbaut, der meiner Meinung nach fast alle Wünsche für normaler (Office-)Anwendungen, außerhalb des Gamings, erfüllt. Die Testung als Media Server folgt, wenn ich alle Daten und Einstellungen vom Laptop auf dem MiniPC übertragen habe. Soweit ich gelesen habe, sind WiFi 6 und Bluetooth 5.2 mit an Bord. Mein Mobiltelefon (Samsung Galaxy) konnte ich problemlos über Bluetooth verbinden und das sogar einfacher und sehr viel schneller als mit meinem Laptop. Der Lüfter ist leise und vollbringt seine Arbeit.

Die Office Programme laufen flüssig und smooth und das Surfen im Netz ist bisher problemlos möglich, sogar mit vielen geöffneten Tabs. Windows 11 Pro ist schon vorinstalliert und das Starten und erstmalige Einrichten ging in unter sieben Minuten von statten, was mich überraschte und die Augen aufreißen ließ in Bezug auf Windows 11. Ich besitze den MiniPC erst seit etwa einer Woche, doch bin ich jetzt schon mehr als begeistert und zufrieden.

Die Möglichkeiten des Upgrades sind immens und ich werde nach und nach mit Sicherheit die Komponenten erweitern. Als erstes mit Sicherheit den Arbeitsspeicher, auch wenn der mit 16 GB erst einmal vollkommen ausreichend bemessen sein sollte. Allerdings fahre ich mittlerweile die Strategie, gleich hochzuzüchten, um hinterher meine Ruhe zu haben. Der Arbeitsspeicher (DDR4) ist laut Angabe bis auf 64 GB erweiterbar, was ich mir für die kommende Tage vorgenommen habe. Die SSD mit 512 GB mit dem Formfaktor 2280 ist bis auf 2 TB erweiterbar und zudem kann man noch in einem 2,5-Zoll-Schacht eine weitere SSD oder HDD mit SATA- oder PCI-Anschluss hinzufügen. Ausgelobt sind hierbei ebenfalls bis zu 2 TB. Dadurch hätte man 4 TB Speicher und dies sollte mehr als ausreichend sein und wenn einem doch noch etwas fehlt, einfach über einen der USB-Anschlüsse externe Speicher hinzufügen. An der Unterseite lässt dich der MiniPC jedenfalls aufschrauben und dadurch die Erweiterungen einbauen.

Der Lieferumfang ist ebenfalls zu benennen, da ein kleines Täschchen mitgeliefert wird. Dazu ein HDMI-Kabel, das Stromgerät, eine Befestigungsplatte, wenn man den MiniPC irgendwo anbringen möchte und Schrauben. Ich habe den MiniPC während einer Aktion gekauft und so bekam ich die graumelierte originale Geekom-Tasche dazu, die auch etwas her macht und den Transport noch sicherer gestalten lässt.

Zusammenfassend kann ich sagen, dass ich ein richtiger Fan von dem MiniPC und von Geekom geworden bin und ich die Firma definitiv weiter im Auge behalten werden. Der MiniPC hat sich schon jetzt gelohnt und bereitet mir sehr viel Freude. Er verbindet in meinen Augen hohe Leistungsperformance mit geringer Größe und das ist etwas, bei dem ich dachte, dass man lange danach suchen müsste. Die vorab verbauten Speicher (RAM und SSD) sind Markenprodukte, was mich positiv überrascht und ein Zeichen davon sind, dass jemand bei der Entwicklung und Ausstattung mitgedacht hatte. Die (leichte) Erweiterbarkeit finde ich gut und werde ich nach und nach angehen und freue mich schon darauf, aus dem Ding sowohl meinen Arbeits- und Alltagsrechner als auch mein Media Server zu machen und somit mehrere Dinge in einem vereint haben zu können. Das vorinstallierte Windows 11 Pro ist ebenfalls eine Überraschung, da man sonst nur die Home Edition bekommt. Somit kann ich diesen MiniPC weiterempfehlen und hoffe, dass Geekom weiter daran arbeitet dieses Niveau zu halten und sogar auszubauen. Ich bin auf die zukünftigen Produktentwicklungen in diesem Bereich gespannt.

text:
GEEKOM A5 Mini PC with AMD Ryzen 5 7430U

WOW!! What an upgrade from my old PC running Win7. I have been stubborn and refused to upgrade until it had gotten to the point where most Websites wouldn't load due to outdated browsers. Couldn't update the Browsers due to my version of Windows. Grrrr!

Didn't want to update to Windows because, well..... Let's just say I don't trust them to protect my privacy and that company seems to think that THEY own my computer and not me.

Thankfully, this GeekOM is fully compatible with Linux. What a game changer compared to the Windows environment. Should have done it years ago.

Great processing Speed. plenty of ports (never enough though) and it just runs. This PC is Quite and produces no noise. I really like that it is so compact. Also, It pulls a whole lot less power than my old Desktop unit did. I think GeekOM could sell this for just a few dollars less if they didn't pre-install Windows. However, this is a good value for the upgrade I got.

It was very easy to setup Linux, in fact, I tried a couple of versions of the operating system before I chose what I did. If I later change my mind, it is a simple install process again.

I highly recommend this GeekOM over others due to the features that it has for the money.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
this GEEKOM A5 2025 Edition Mini-PC definitely presents Quality: First, the box it came looks like it might last over 50 years. You might say “So what?”, but it was designed to give the purchaser a sense of quality before they even open the box. Inside the box, the GEEKOM A5 2025 Edition Mini PC speaks stylish quality with its gleaming metallic appearance; chrome edge along the top, and crisp airflow cutouts. Ports for just about any application (even USB Charging) are available on nearly every side; including a card reader slot. Plus has a Kensington security slot (If you gotta ask, you probably don’t use it). Inside the GEEKOM A5 (no tools needed) is space for extra M.2 SSD storage; both SATA-3 and NVMe. I effortlessly added a 1T NVMe.
Also included is a sturdy VESA mount (Convenient for mounting on the back of a monitor or someplace else with a VESA standard).
The preinstalled Windows 11 Pro was a bit of a challenge however. More challenging than other mini-PC with Windows “preinstalled”, which took only 10s of minutes. This install was an hour or so, with many trips to the Windows Update Server and slow reboots. I may mention that to GEEKOM when I review on their site.
But now it’s fast, smooth and quiet, and more importantly it’s cool – just a couple of degrees F over ambient. Time will tell if I need the 90-day return or 3-Year Warranty Coverage.
This GEEKOM A5/2025 mini-PC is a great value for the money; I highly recommend it to anyone who’s looking for a mini-PC.

This is the second mini PC I’ve purchased to run lasers in my shop. I didn’t know for sure what I was buying when I purchased the first one but I knew with this one. I can’t tell the difference between it and a new laptop that I have other than it boots up much faster. It’s been compatible with all the software I use for laser work, it has more than enough connection ports, it works perfectly with my WiFi and Bluetooth devices and attaches to the back of the monitor.
It’s also quiet. The first one was a little loud as it worked but this one is much quieter.
In addition to the machines it controls, I also use it for internet and mail without any problems.
Don’t let the small size of these minicomputers fool you. They are very capable machines and all that will be on your desk is a monitor, mouse and keyboard. With Bluetooth, the only wire connects to the monitor.

text:
Mein Laptop ist nach zehn bis elf Jahre in sein Alter gekommen, um sich so langsam in Rente zu verabschieden. Daher habe ich schon seit längerer Zeit nach einem Ersatz gesucht und bin dabei auf die MiniPCs gestoßen. Da ich Tastatur und Monitore zur Erweiterung des Laptops schon habe und diese nicht wegwerfen will, habe ich mich mit dem Thema MiniPC befasst. Durch Zufall bin ich auf die Firma Geekom aufmerksam geworden und schwankte noch zwischen IT8 und IT11. Letzten Endes habe ich mich nun für den IT11 mit 16 GB RAM und 512 GB SSD entschieden. Ich bereue es kein bisschen und freue, dass ich nun auch endlich Windows 11 habe, da mein alter Laptop nicht Win11-fähig ist. Zudem kommt noch hinzu, dass ich durch den MiniPC wieder mehr Platz auf dem Schreibtisch habe.

Der MiniPC ist sehr handlich und kompakt gebaut, passt in meine Hand und ist leicht. Klar, Plastik bzw. Kunststoff ist dabei, doch sieht er hochwertig aus und die Verarbeitung, soweit es sich mir erschließt, ist auch sehr gelungen.

Anschlüsse sind mehr als genug vorhanden. An der linken Seite ist ein SD-Kartenslot vorhanden, an der rechten Seite ein Kensington Security Lock, was sicherlich auch bei dem ein oder anderen Verwendung finden wird. An der Vorderseite sind USB-C, USB-A, Klinkenanschluss und der Powerbutton. Hinten gibt es dem Stromanschluss, einen Mini DisplayPort, LAN-Anschluss, zwei USB-A, HMDI und USB-C. Alles in den neuesten Generationen und Variationen. Es sind genug Schnittstellen vorhanden, um allerlei Geräte anzuschließen. Ich gehe davon aus, dass man über HDMI und DisplayPort 4K rausbekommt und so ein sehr gutes Sehvergnügen hat. Offiziell sollen es bis zu vier 4K-Monitoren sein, da bin ich sehr gespannt, wenn ich mal dazu komme, meinen Schreibtisch soweit auszubauen und aufzurüsten.

Im Inneren ist es ein Intel-Chip i7 der 11. Generation verbaut, der meiner Meinung nach fast alle Wünsche für normaler (Office-)Anwendungen, außerhalb des Gamings, erfüllt. Die Testung als Media Server folgt, wenn ich alle Daten und Einstellungen vom Laptop auf dem MiniPC übertragen habe. Soweit ich gelesen habe, sind WiFi 6 und Bluetooth 5.2 mit an Bord. Mein Mobiltelefon (Samsung Galaxy) konnte ich problemlos über Bluetooth verbinden und das sogar einfacher und sehr viel schneller als mit meinem Laptop. Der Lüfter ist leise und vollbringt seine Arbeit.

Die Office Programme laufen flüssig und smooth und das Surfen im Netz ist bisher problemlos möglich, sogar mit vielen geöffneten Tabs. Windows 11 Pro ist schon vorinstalliert und das Starten und erstmalige Einrichten ging in unter sieben Minuten von statten, was mich überraschte und die Augen aufreißen ließ in Bezug auf Windows 11. Ich besitze den MiniPC erst seit etwa einer Woche, doch bin ich jetzt schon mehr als begeistert und zufrieden.

Die Möglichkeiten des Upgrades sind immens und ich werde nach und nach mit Sicherheit die Komponenten erweitern. Als erstes mit Sicherheit den Arbeitsspeicher, auch wenn der mit 16 GB erst einmal vollkommen ausreichend bemessen sein sollte. Allerdings fahre ich mittlerweile die Strategie, gleich hochzuzüchten, um hinterher meine Ruhe zu haben. Der Arbeitsspeicher (DDR4) ist laut Angabe bis auf 64 GB erweiterbar, was ich mir für die kommende Tage vorgenommen habe. Die SSD mit 512 GB mit dem Formfaktor 2280 ist bis auf 2 TB erweiterbar und zudem kann man noch in einem 2,5-Zoll-Schacht eine weitere SSD oder HDD mit SATA- oder PCI-Anschluss hinzufügen. Ausgelobt sind hierbei ebenfalls bis zu 2 TB. Dadurch hätte man 4 TB Speicher und dies sollte mehr als ausreichend sein und wenn einem doch noch etwas fehlt, einfach über einen der USB-Anschlüsse externe Speicher hinzufügen. An der Unterseite lässt dich der MiniPC jedenfalls aufschrauben und dadurch die Erweiterungen einbauen.

Der Lieferumfang ist ebenfalls zu benennen, da ein kleines Täschchen mitgeliefert wird. Dazu ein HDMI-Kabel, das Stromgerät, eine Befestigungsplatte, wenn man den MiniPC irgendwo anbringen möchte und Schrauben. Ich habe den MiniPC während einer Aktion gekauft und so bekam ich die graumelierte originale Geekom-Tasche dazu, die auch etwas her macht und den Transport noch sicherer gestalten lässt.

Zusammenfassend kann ich sagen, dass ich ein richtiger Fan von dem MiniPC und von Geekom geworden bin und ich die Firma definitiv weiter im Auge behalten werden. Der MiniPC hat sich schon jetzt gelohnt und bereitet mir sehr viel Freude. Er verbindet in meinen Augen hohe Leistungsperformance mit geringer Größe und das ist etwas, bei dem ich dachte, dass man lange danach suchen müsste. Die vorab verbauten Speicher (RAM und SSD) sind Markenprodukte, was mich positiv überrascht und ein Zeichen davon sind, dass jemand bei der Entwicklung und Ausstattung mitgedacht hatte. Die (leichte) Erweiterbarkeit finde ich gut und werde ich nach und nach angehen und freue mich schon darauf, aus dem Ding sowohl meinen Arbeits- und Alltagsrechner als auch mein Media Server zu machen und somit mehrere Dinge in einem vereint haben zu können. Das vorinstallierte Windows 11 Pro ist ebenfalls eine Überraschung, da man sonst nur die Home Edition bekommt. Somit kann ich diesen MiniPC weiterempfehlen und hoffe, dass Geekom weiter daran arbeitet dieses Niveau zu halten und sogar auszubauen. Ich bin auf die zukünftigen Produktentwicklungen in diesem Bereich gespannt.

text:
The volume is very good and these speakers produce a "rich" or "full" sound. Especially considering the low price. I was surprised that each speaker has substantial weight which seems to contribute to a quality product (at least to me).

UPDATE 15 January 2026: I opened each speaker and this is what I found:
1. The Amazon web page for this item states "Woofer 3.9 Inches" and "Tweeter 1 Inches [sic]" under the "Product information" > "Additional details" category. That information is completely false.

The actual (correct) speaker information is a single 1.5 inch (I measured it) speaker, one for the left and one for the right enclosure. A tweeter speaker does not exist in this item. However, a downward-facing passive oval radiator is in each speaker enclosure and measures 2-1/2 x 1-5/16 inches.

Stamped on the rear of each speaker is "250822 FD43-3BEHR, 4Ω 3W" for whatever it's worth.

2. The only reason each speaker has substantial weight is because of the bottom metal (appears to be pot metal) plate. This is the plate with the foam attached to it and is actually worthwhile to help keep the speakers from moving.

3. I disabled the two blue LEDs that illuminates the bottom base of each speaker when powered on. That was done by de-soldering the two wires that are connected to the mini-PCB that holds the two blue LEDs.

Even thought this item has incorrect product information, I still maintain the speakers have very good sound quality considering the very low price. The passive radiator most likely contributes to that.

text:
The "AOOSTAR MACO AMD R7 6850H Mini PC" is a pretty good little PC. The processor is plenty fast for day to day usage and much faster than the N150 from my last mini PC. 24GB of ram is nice to see and should be enough for most use cases. Do note that the RAM is soldered so you will not be able to add more.
This has 3 M.2 SSD slots that ONLY fit 2280 sized SSDs. This is the size most people would want to use anyways but it should be pointed out that it only has a mount for that one size.
The power brick that came with the PC has a 19V 120W output. This should be enough power for this PC.
I do not have any of of testing the OCuLink port, but this should make for a pretty good gaming PC with an eGPU dock. The port does have a rubber cover built in that is nice for when the port is not in use. It is a little tricky to take the rubber cover out though, but that could be a skill issue on my part.
The bottom cover comes off with only 4 Phillips screws. These screws are fully accessible and not hidden under the rubber feet,m which is a big plus.
This PC came with a 1TB SSD with a heat-sink already applied. The box came with 2 more heat-sinks for the other 2 slots.
Under load, you can hear the fan on this PC, but it it not very loud.
I did a quick look through the Windows 11 install and did not see any random programs installed. The only thing I found that AOOSTAR added was a shortcut on the desktop to bring you to their support page. The Windows installation this PC came with seems to be fully in English. I have seen before on some mini PC where the install is in English but some of the core Windows functions were only in Chinese. This PC does not have that issue.
After checking the Windows install, I immediately installed Linux and have had no issues.
I would recommend this PC to anyone who is looking for a good mini PC. If you have an eGPU dock, this would make for a good gaming machine. Even without an eGPU, this would still work for 1080p gaming for many games.

- Great options for cable management inside the case with preinstalled loop straps for cable bundling. Existing cables inside the case (e.g. for front panel) are very well managed also.
- Included fans are very efficient and high quality, getting 6 of them included makes this case not only great quality but also a great value. They come pre-installed and hooked up to a small daughter board near the front/top panel with nicely routed cabling.
- Excellent and quiet air cooling performance. Using AMD 9800X3D and NH-D15 cooler, Sapphire AMD 7900XT GPU with default curves on the case fans, baseline 40% on the NH-D15 up to about 60C and an aggressive curve ramping quickly to 100% by 80C. The resulting system is totally silent for basic use and nearly all gaming loads; fans only become audible under very CPU heavy loads like code or shader compilation. Most of the time the GPU fan (and some GPU coil whine...) are the loudest thing in the system. I rarely ever see the CPU above about 65C, and even maxing out all cores I simply can't get it much above 76C with instant peak of 81-82C before fans catch up. Of course the 9800 and Noctua also get credit for this, but it's truly impressive how quiet it is.
- The HDD rack in the lower bay is easy to completely remove if you aren't using it, for slightly better airflow from the two lower fans pulling up through the bottom of the case.
- Power supply is easy to install with plenty of room for dealing with cables thanks to the large mostly empty lower bay.
- The mesh front panel and small holes on the bottom panel do a good job of minimizing dust in the case. Not perfect, but very good given the outstanding airflow of the case. The spacious interior also makes it easy to clean.
- The USB ports and power button on the top/front panel are solid and firmly mounted.
- The CPU/GPU temperature display works well (with required software installed) and is kind of cool.
- I didn't really care about the wood accent when I purchased, but it looks quite good and is a nice "premium" touch.
- No quality issues with my unit of any kind.

A small nit, but depending on the arrangement of your motherboard, the cables from the front panel may be very slightly on the short side. Not really a problem, but for one of the cables from the front panel I had to basically force a shortest path diagonally across the back of the motherboard (ignoring most cable management) to be able to reach the far left side of the bottom edge of the mobo.

text:
I bought this Techkey Bluetooth adapter because I have a custom built PC with no bluetooth, and I wanted to use my ear buds rather than a set of headphones. It comes with an instruction manual that gives you step by step instructions.

On my PC, installation was just a tad different than the manual. I plugged it into a front USB port, and attached the booster, then I went to Settings-->Devices-->Bluetooth and other devices, and I turned Bluetooth on. There was no Bluetooth option prior to my plugging in the device.

Now to pair with my ear buds. It was simple. Staying on the "Settings" screen, I took my ear buds out of the case, they auto go to pairing mode. I chose them from a list of audio devices and they paired easily. I now see my ear buds under Bluetooth, with an added plus of battery life left.

As far as range goes, I walked around the house, and this is probably dependent upon the structure you're in, walls, etc, etc...but I would say it was clear without a break for about 50 feet, and that was through multiple rooms. The reception got a bit spotty after that, but again, I think it's dependent upon what type of building you're in. This at least gives you a ballpark range plus/minus.

I would recommend for quality and ease of installation.

Great price, performance and functionality.

text:
This PC is a great choice for office or home use but not ideal for gaming due to its limited power supply.

At first, I misunderstood its capabilities and assumed I could play a game like God of War which was my fault. Technically, it can run the game, but it struggles to maintain a stable frame rate, often dipping well below 30 FPS. The BIOS is surprisingly open for a system like this, allowing for plenty of customization—both good and bad. While it’s designed to be power-efficient, tuning it for higher performance quickly runs into stability issues due to the small power supply, which sometimes prevents it from booting.

That said, this PC excels in its intended role as a reliable, efficient machine for everyday tasks. If you're looking for a simple, energy-efficient system for office work, web browsing, or media consumption, you'll likely be very satisfied. However, if you're hoping to tweak the BIOS for maximum performance, you may be disappointed.

Side note: I purchased a returned unit from Amazon Warehouse Deals, and unfortunately, I believe mine was a dud. It had random issues from the start, and the Bluetooth failed entirely. I don’t think this reflects the quality of the PC itself—just bad luck with a returned unit that likely wasn’t properly tested.

Ultimately, I returned it and went with the Beelink SER6, which has the same hardware but performed much better for my needs. With that, I can get a stable 40 FPS on God of War at medium settings (probably more with further tweaking).

text:
This seems to be a well constructed machine. Very quiet and smooth.

Opening the case is easy and quick, especially for a small PC, and it compares favorably to models I've owned or worked with from other makers (like HP Elite Mini series, some NUC-style machines, etc.) in both accessibility and easy of cleaning. (Obviously it does require unscrewing things, but that's a minimal issue.) You can replace all the major things like RAM, SSD, and wifi card w/o any trouble. Port choices are also very reasonable and well positioned.

Currently running perfectly on Manjaro (Arch Linux derivative) with one minor issue - I had to set Bluetooth control panel to "receive from trusted devices" to send a file from my phone to the machine. Getting 150/380 Mbps Internet speed over wifi (no idea what router is supposed to be capable of, happy enough with that). 150% scaling factor on a TV display works well, no issues.

Did not work as well w/ OpenSUSE tumbleweed, which had constant wifi issues - it seems to not have a good kernel or driver for the Intel AX200 for whatever reason. (I think it's known that Intel's driver's for AX200 are kind of finicky.) Was able to swap M.2 wifi card with no issues while evaluating tumbleweed, wouldn't recommend, just go w/ Arch or Manjaro.

Any case, highly recommend the machine, it's without a doubt the best mini PC I've owned, though probably the most comparable machine is a Mac Mini, which I can't totally speak to in comparison.

title: 4.0 out of 5 stars
text:
I recently purchased a Beelink SER8 / 8745HS Mini PC on Amazon. While I have a MOSTLY favorable impression of this mini PC system, there are also some negatives, which I will list below. I received the PC in good condition, and started installing Windows 11 Pro updates, and some of my basic user software. The good stuff first :-) This mini PC is REALLY FAST, and extremely quiet, with very low fan noise! Also the fan ventilation is very effective, keeping the CPU temperatures low, even under moderate CPU loads. Since I do some audio editing on my PC, low fan noise is very important to me, and this mini PC meets this requirement. The AMD Ryzen 7 processor is speedy, and the AMD Radeon display adapter plays videos smoothly, with high frame rates. It handles my older Windows 10 apps, without any noticeable difficulties. It has an audio output jack on both the front and rear panels, which is a handy feature, not found on most mini PCs. The build quality of this mini PC feels quite solid, and the brushed metal top cover looks great.

There are also a few negative aspects to this Beelink mini PC. First off, I immediately noticed the poor download speed performance of the internal Intel AX200 WiFi controller. Using my home 5G WiFi connection and the built-in Intel WiFi adapter, I was only able to reach a download speed of 34 Mbps, which is really dismal.

THE SOLUTION : I disabled the internal WiFi adapter in "Device Manager", and connected a TP Link AC600 external USB WiFi adapter/antenna, and was able to achieve a download speed of 174 Mbps - which is about 5 times faster! Since the $15 USB WiFi adapter performs so much better, I have left the internal Intel WiFi adapter disabled, and am using the external USB WiFi adapter all the time now. While this is a cheap fix for the WiFi download speed problem, it is also a bit of a disappointment. ( NOTE :The download performance is probably degraded because of the placement of the built-in WiFi antenna, inside the metal case. )

Other issues that I have yet to resolve, are problems with "sleep mode". One problem is that even if I set the "Power Options" setting to "Put the computer to sleep : 45 minutes", this PC does not actually go to sleep after 45 minutes! I have dug around in the other device software settings, but have been unable to fix this problem so far. The other problem with "sleep mode" is that it occasionally wakes up from manually initiated sleep mode, for no apparent reason. No clue as to why this happens, although it may have something to do with the fact that this PC is never fully asleep. This is because the SER8 system's BIOS only supports "S0 Modern Sleep" mode, which means that while it is "sleeping", Windows 11 is still running in the background, USB power is still on, and network internet activity is also happening! Apparently there is no way to disable this "feature" in the Windows 11 software, nor in the BIOS settings. While this is a very common "feature" (LOL) of most modern PC's, including Apple PCs, it is a potential network security issue, and it's also a waste of electric power.

To sum up - this is overall a solid mini PC, despite the issues I have mentioned here.

text:
Impressed with the performance and value of this SER8 mini PC. AMD’s 8745HS is a great option compared to 8845HS for most of us that don’t care about AI processing, or those who do and use an eGPU. The 780M built-in graphics are capable of running any game, albeit on low settings and/or with upscaling tech like FSR/FidelityFX.

The upgradability is welcome; two RAM slots and two nvme SSD slots is fantastic. Adding a 2TB SSD (secondary) and replacing the RAM with 2x 32gb Crucial modules was easy. The 40gbps USB4 works great with my Razer Core X eGPU and RTX 4070S GPU. It almost feels like a regular desktop in terms of customization.

The Mac Mini inspired metal design is attractive, though like other Beelink units, it negatively affects the wireless radio. You can mitigate this by putting the unit upside down. This model includes an Intel AX200 wireless card, which is a good card, but the antennas get such poor reception that the wireless signal tops out at 200mbps on a network where I usually get >600mbps.

I've pushed this thing a fair bit and haven't seen the CPU go beyond 80 degrees Celsius. The cooling is quite good, and quiet too! The build quality is sturdy and I've got a good feeling it will last a good long time.

text:
I’m a novel writer, not a coder or gamer. I don’t do rendering or streaming, so I don’t need extreme performance. What matters to me is reliability, quiet operation, and smooth everyday use, and this notebook delivers on those points.

I’ve researched nearly every notebook and laptop that uses a Snapdragon chip, and I ultimately chose the Surface Laptop. I’ve tested devices with the Snapdragon X Plus, Snapdragon X, and Snapdragon X Elite, and in everyday use they all feel very similar in speed and responsiveness.

During my research IT experts warned me about app compatibility, but I mainly use Microsoft Edge and Microsoft Office. If your workflow is similar, this laptop will work perfectly fine. For my needs—Microsoft Office, ChatGPT, and Grok—the laptop that uses Snapdragon X chip is more than fast enough, especially if you’re on a budget.

Many reviewers say Snapdragon laptops run quietly and stay cool, and I found that to be true. The system is nearly silent, and even the SSD is quieter than others I’ve used. However, despite the hype around battery life, I didn’t find it to last significantly longer than comparable Intel or AMD Ryzen laptops.

Some people describe this device as Microsoft’s answer to the MacBook, and I can see why. The Surface Laptop feels premium, reliable, and durable. Its thin and lightweight design makes it feel more like a high‑end notebook than a traditional laptop.

There are cheaper laptops out there, but many of them feel poorly built, too big, too heavy, and won’t hold up over years of use. The Surface Laptop, by contrast, feels like it’s made to last. It is not the cheapest notebook, but you get what you pay for: quality, speed, and reliability.

I also appreciate that it supports Wi‑Fi 7 instead of Wi‑Fi 6. This notebook is extremely thin, very light to carry and store, and genuinely looks great in person.

Overall, I’m giving it 4 out of 5 stars because of the limited port selection (only two USB‑C ports), the proprietary charging connector, and the average battery life.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
Why did you pick this product vs others?:
I bought this laptop as a spec upgrade to my old 2021 HP laptop, and this one is better in every aspect!
I got this laptop for general use and for gaming. Yes, this laptop's processor is so powerful with the Ryzen AI 7 350 chipset. It outperforms the steam deck and Asus ROG Ally X. In fact, I'm selling my steam deck so I can stick to using this laptop instead. I never used my steam deck and I'm on my laptop every day. So, having a two-in-one device is much better. I decided not to get a gaming laptop because I wanted a longer lasting battery while web browsing and this laptop excels at that! It lasts significantly longer than my old laptop and the temps range from 32 - 45 C for general use. Using energy saver at all times also greatly extends the battery life further.

About the other review regarding the screen color quality, it certainly holds true. The colors are terrible on this laptop by default. It's a difference compared to my old HP laptop, looking like it has a yellow tint as if night light mode is enabled. However, this can be fixed using Window's color calibration tool. Go through the calibration program until you get to the part where you adjust the three RGB color balancing. I set blue to about 90%, green to 75%, and red to 65%. With these changes, the screen colors look normal without the yellow tint. The screen was my main worry and now I can enjoy the laptop fully.

The Pros:
- The ips display is perfect, you can view the screen from any angle without glare. This is not an OLED screen though so don't get it mixed up like me.
- The lit-up keyboard can be toggled any time whenever you need it. It auto dims when not typing.
- The touchscreen is useful for times when you're doing tedious tasks like clicking check boxes.
- The camera is nice for signing into the laptop without typing anything. Though sometimes it doesn't work so I use a pin code instead.
- The taller screen helps you see more on webpages and images at once without scrolling down.
- The battery while doing basic web browsing or reading lasts for over 7 hours which is much more than I've ever seen from a Windows laptop! Just be sure to enable energy saver. I barely have to charge it up and the temps stay low.
- The incredible processor having such high speeds and the RAM being at 7500 MT/s makes for a snappy experience. Just buy a laptop stand to help with cooling and you'll be golden.
- The AI key can be remapped to chatGPT instead.
- The chassis is made out of aluminum and feels cold to touch, good for thermals. It is also very thin.
- It has a built-in battery optimizer enabled by default that can learn your usage patterns and prevent you from always charging to 100%, which helps the battery last more years down the line. Though this confused me because the battery still shows 100% even though it doesn't reflect the lower amount that it really is.
- Running a medium ended 3D game got 54 C in temp, starting the TDP at 25 watts and went down to 15 watts automatically. This is very reasonable temps so far for playing a game.
- The max TDP is 28 watts which is useful for pushing higher end games. It automatically fluctuates between 2 watts to 28 watts as it needs for the tasks. It hovers around 2 - 4 watts TDP when web browsing.

The cons:
- You can only charge the laptop on the right side.
- The so-called fast charge is not that fast. I gain 35% in 30 minutes instead of 50% like the advertisement. But it's still reasonably fast while the battery lasts long between charges.
- The screen aspect ratio is 16:10, so 16:9 videos won't fill the screen and shows a black bar on top and bottom.
- There's no SD card slot for extra storage, but you can use a small-sized USB SD card adapter instead.
- The power button is next to the delete key. But at least it's harder to press in and it has to be pressed down for a bit to work.
- There are AI services that start up with the system and use up a chunk of memory. You cannot permanently disable them and have to remember to close them upon each reboot.
- The rubber grip on the back causes the laptop to slide around on certain surfaces.
- The USB ports are stiff to insert into, but this also helps keep peripherals plugged in sturdier.

Overall, I'm happy with this laptop and it surpasses my old HP laptop and my steam deck in so many ways and combines both of their uses into one device. I would recommend this laptop to pc enthusiasts and to anyone who wants an actual GOOD computer without paying $1000. These specs do not disappoint. This is a future laptop to use over the years until its end of life. No need to ever upgrade from here.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
I love Android, and I love ChromeOS. I have an Acer chromebook, an Amazon Fire, an Apple iPad, and a Samsung Galaxy, and so far, and oddly enough, this chromebit is my favourite piece of technology.

First things first. This is NOT a fast machine. It is slower than the chromebook I bought three years ago, yet not that slow: I've watched Rio 2016 on streaming and there is just the barest hint of lag, and I think it is my ISP's fault rather than the chromebit. It's completely portable. Just this morning I did a presentation by plugging it into an HD monitor instead of looking for an overhead projector. It does everything a chromebook or a chromebox can, except that this thing, sadly, does not have USB 3.0 capabilities. I also miss having a microphone, but at least it paired nice and easy with my bluetooth hearphones and keyboard. Wifi reception may be a little bit compromised behind the monitor or TV, but at least you can use an expander cable (I got one that was a meter long and got a coupler, and it works like a charm). Using google drive eases the lack of internal capacity: it has barely 16 GB on board, but I've tested it with USB drives up to 128 GB and external SSD drives up to 256 GB; however, cheap drives tend to use more oower and some of them can be read but not write. Mechanical drives, using too much power, are simply not up to the task. Or to the power supply available, to tell you the truth; you need a wall outlet to power up the chromebit, because there isn't enough juice available from the USB ports of any standard TV. So if you want to connect several drives or accessories, you need a hub that supports an external power supply.

My only complaints are that the only USB port available is 2.0 instead of 3.0, and that it lacks a microsd expansion slot. Except for that, it's a perfect little machine for under a hundred bucks.

text:
ウィンドウズ3台、アンドロイド1台ときて、5台目のスティックPCです。
安いしコンパクトだし、この際一通りのOSを体験してみようじゃないかということで買いました。
本機の使い心地は、最初にテスト使用した程度では問題なしだったという感じで、ここではクロームOSというものについて。
本機の性能じたいは★4なり5でいいと思いますが、クロームOSによって3です。

今までPCを使ったことがない人に使わせるものとして、クロームOSというのは最もとっつきやすそうと思います。
理由としては、各種アップデートやセキュリティ対策で、ユーザー側の負担がかなり小さく、ほぼゼロに近いことです。
そのあたりはグーグルでも全面に出していて売りにしていますが、一方では、ハードウェアごとにサポート期間が決まっているという、個人的にはかなり大きいと感じる欠点があります。
私の勉強不足ではあるにしろ、このサポート期間の件はだいぶ後になってから知り、何となくですがグーグルに限らずネットではクロームOSの良い面ばかりが喧伝され、この短所はあまり知られていないのでは？と感じます。
まあいったんそれを知ってしまって検索してみると情報はわんさか出て来はしますが、ただクロームOSのことを調べている限りでは、「まあすべてブラウザ内で作業して、データもクラウドに置いとく、あまり広いことはできないにしろ初心者やライトユーザーには手軽で安全なものなのね」といった評価に収斂していくのではないかと。

個人的にはPCは5年かそれ以上、ハード的に故障するとかOSの進化についていけなくなって動作が遅くてどうにもならんといった感じになるまで使いたいほうなので、セキュリティやらOSのアップで一律線引きされて「これ以下はサポート打ち切りです」というやり方のものはできれば使いたくないと思っています。
普段メインで使っているMacについてはそれなりにサポート長いので使ってはいますが、やはりOSのバージョンが上がるごとに対応ハードの条件も上がって古いのは打ち切られていくのは、中には納得し難いものもあったりします。
そういう意味ではウィンドウズが一番緩そうで好感が持てますね。

まあグーグルに関してはそれ言ったらアンドロイドスマホなんてOSのメジャーアップは1回でも有れば良い方で、特にエントリークラスなどはほとんど非対応に見受けられ、それを求めるならピクセルなりアンドロイド・ワンなりとなりますが、それにしたってサポートは2年だか3年だかでやはりiOSに比べたら短いようですし。
まあなんやかんや、アンドロイドの場合は古いバージョンでも使い続けてしまったりしていてそこまでサポートがどうのと気にはしていないので、クロームOSもあまりお金絡みのことには使わないとか一定の注意をしながら、サポートが切れたハードウェアも使い続けるつもりではいます。
実際、本機もこの投稿の2020年12月時点ではサポート切れ直後だったかと思いますので、そのあたり把握済みでその前提での使い方をするつもりならありかなと思います。

text:
Ho da poco acquistato uno splendido Surface Pro 9 in color graphite, da dover utilizzare per forza durante sopralluoghi presso cantieri edili, o comunque dove purtroppo corro un rischio particolarmente alto di rovinare il dispositivo. Sono al contempo una persona che apprezza “le cose belle e ben fatte”, e che cerca, in qualunque ambito, di mantenere al meglio le proprie cose. Quindi, dopo aver cercato una cover che unisca un bel design (non necessariamente rugged), una bella costruzione e che soprattutto protegga il mio dispositivo, sono capitato su questa cover della UAG, che a prima vista sembrava perfetta per i miei utilizzi.
In realtà anche dopo diverse settimane di utilizzo, non posso che confermare che si tratti di un prodotto estremamente solido, ben realizzato, e che riesce a proteggere al meglio il mio dispositivo.
La fattura è davvero ottima, tutti i materiali sono ben realizzati, la plastica è rigida ma non estremamente, tranne per la componente trasparente sul retro che è a tutti gli effetti una plastica molto molto rigida. L’unico elemento che avrebbero potuto curare un po’ meglio è il piedistallo posteriore, sia per la fattura (è l’unico elemento che risulta, almeno al tatto, non del tutto solidissimo), sia per funzionalità (da una cover da 100€ quasi potevano elaborare un meccanismo che consentisse di fermarsi in più posizioni, invece di una soltanto).
La cosa estremamente comoda è il portapenna integrato, che attenzione è realizzato per la penna SLIM, sono sicuro che può contenere anche penne più spesse, ma non troppo grosse.
In cantiere o comunque quando occorre utilizzare il Surface stando in piedi risulta estremamente comodo l’appiglio posteriore, cui infilare dentro la mano. E’ estremamente solido (al contrario di moooooolti altri prodotti), regolabile, e soprattutto può ruotare di 360 gradi, trovando sempre la posizione più comoda per l’utilizzo del tablet pc.
È chiaramente pienamente compatibile con la tastiera, che non viene intralciata in nessun modo, e la cover presenta anche un piccolo laccetto nella parte alta che consente di “fissare” la tastiera quando chiusa, in modo da evitare aperture accidentali.
E’ presente anche la staffa da appoggio, già menzionata essendo il componente “più debole” della cover, che però risulta estremamente ben studiata sull’angolo di inclinazione. Ne abbiamo a disposizione soltanto 1, ma è davvero perfetto. Tuttavia essendo la staffa del surface studiata per qualunque angolo possibile, avrebbero potuto fare uno sforzo e progettare un meccanismo simile. E’ l’unica lamentela che posso fare per questo prodotto, altrimenti perfetto.
Se non bastasse, abbiamo a corredo anche una comodissima tracolla, da fissare al retro della cover, che consente di portare a spalla (oppure come sicurezza da tenere al collo) il nostro pc durante magari gli spostamenti o quando non si ha la sicurezza di avere entrambe le mani salde al pc.
Insomma, in conclusione, sono estremamente soddisfatto della mia cover. Prima di questa ne ho provate 2 simili dal prezzo decisamente inferiore, tuttavia ne sono rimasto molto deluso soprattutto per la qualità costruttiva. Avere in mano un pc favoloso da 2000€, e poi inserirlo in una cover orribile da 25/30 euro lo trovo non proprio il massimo. Con questa, seppur davvero cara, il colpo d’occhio è assicurato, e soprattutto l’utilizzo in cantiere o in zone rischiose diventa decisamente più sicuro.

I own most of the Razer controllers that they've released (pictured are just some that aren't in storage) so I'm what you may call an expert and also bad with money.

Razer controllers prior have all had some issues to put it lightly, or in the case of the Raiju's so much so that the lineup is now effectively dead in favor of the Wolverine. The Wolverine v3 Pro feels like a true culmination of all the past controller issues and questionable design decisions being ironed out.

I will list my own personal highlights compared to previous offerings as I do not see any of the "tech reviewers" mentioning them.

+ Tension on thumb sticks and full pull on triggers nearly identical to stock Xbox, stick tension slightly tighter from what I can tell and it feels amazing compared to how loose the tension on every Razer controllers has been prior

+ Thumbstick material and texture provides actual grip, previous controllers were slip city

+ ACTUALLY GOOD AND ERGONOMIC BACK BUTTONS OH MY GOD HOW I'VE LONGED FOR THIS

+ Face buttons have been changed for the better, sound and feel is still clicky like Razer is known for but much more muted, and in general they've felt less fatiguing to use

+ M1 and M2 switches changed to be same as bumper, previously they were not and had slightly different feeling actuation force needed so if you tested your fingers on the extra buttons you may have accidentally triggered them due to the lesser force needed

+ Actually good trigger stops bravo 👏

+ Wireless that works without issue!!! On a Razer controller no less wow!

+ Good polling rates??? 250hz 2.4 wireless polling rate on Xbox is double than the standard and elite controller offerings from Xbox, finally a pro controller from Razer that actually lives up to the pro name. With up to 1000hz wired on PC Razer has finally caught up to current year and as a result this is their most responsive feeling controller ever.

+ Razer actually priced it fairly for a wireless pro controller, remembered to include a carrying case this time, and included a 10ft cable for wired. Immaculate W

+ Hall effect sticks in a big name pro controller, to see Razer adopt this before Microsoft and Sony absolutely blows my mind, they actually did it. Bravo.

If you play on Xbox and PC it's a no brainer. While they could certainly do more in offering a wider variety of stick options, let alone the means of easily obtaining more which historically they've never done outside of ordering a "replacement set" at absurd prices from their parts store, I'm just in awe that Razer actually knocked it out of the park for once.

Honestly I'm just in shock they actually priced it at $200, I feel like I actually got what I paid for so the finance team must be on vacation or something.

title: 1.0 out of 5 stars
text:
Ok, Out of the box I immediately set deadzones to zero. Upon checking found there is an inherent centering issue that causes heavy drift reading with no way to recalibrate.

Pros:
Feel of buttons are great, tactile, responsive, good placement. The “feel” of the controller is one of the bests. The trigger locks to enable a mouse click tactile pull is satisfying to say the least. All these features are great enough for me to over look other features not given at this price range ie - tension adjustment, full button mapping, lackluster app interface, polling rate to name a few.
Major con:
However, having out of box centering issues this high is just kind of a hard one to look over. All HE sticks do have centering performance concerns. I just wish this would center closer to 0,0 (I know it’s impossible to get true 0,0 reading). But no matter what I do, direction I flick it, it re-centers back to these values. I’d have to widen the dead zones, sacrificing a substantial amount responsiveness which defeats the purpose of buying a performance controller. Maybe I’ll try to exchange and hope I get something better, but if it’s worse, it’s a full refund. Will update review if I do. But not to hopeful as more research, this is a more common than a one off situation.

UPDATE: GOT A NEW REPLACEMENT (3.5-3.9 Stars max)

Firmware updater released on PC. But now can be updated on Xbox App however the app sucks. I already lost confidence in the software(& probably the Razer brand too) and updated through PC anyway. Major gripe about the PC updater: it doesn’t confirm if you already have the latest firmware. Pros: quality weight and feel, rgb(if you even care for this?), tactile mouse click triggers, a really decent clicky gated d-pad (better than most), a lot of extra decently placed buttons that feel good, adjustable haptic, multiple profile config saves, easy quick instant button mapping. Carrying case.

Cons: app, firmware update required, updated app didn’t include a calibration option, Outdated 2020 Hall Effect tech used in 2024 when newer VRS is more economical, durable, accurate, and energy efficient. No adjustable tension for a $200 price tag. Only two extra plastic thumb sticks, why not just throw in two identical pairs? They’re plastic anyways. You still need a dongle. Face buttons could feel “mushy” to some, And I could be wrong, but I don’t think it’s Bluetooth as they advertise. Size, if only it was a couple centimeters larger it would probably rest perfectly in most hands. It’s not switch pro small but with back paddle placement it can be noticeable.

Biggest con. Razer as a company is incompetent. Do not buy if you do not have a windows pc. Razer is company who creates an Xbox controller with an Xbox app, but does not push firmware updates through the Xbox. You have to download a separate software on a PC then update firmware through there cuz if you don’t, it won’t allow you to use the Xbox app! This is after a year of use, and while hardware is ok, I’ve grown more tired with this company as it’s a controller with inconveniences that start to pile up which is no excuse at this price range. Save your money.

UPDATE 2025-11-29: Swapped the HDMI cables for Thunderbolt-to-DisplayPort cables on both screens and for almost a month now have no longer had the screen "static" issue on startup. Faulty HDMI subsystem on the NUC. Dropping from 2 stars to 1 as final review.

Not made like they used to (before ASUS took them over). This is my third NUC. I've owned a NUC8 and a NUC11 that are still in use today with zero issues. But this ASUS NUC13....

• Average IDLE temps running side-by-side to the NUC11 in a 71°F room are 14(!) degrees HOTTER... at idle!!!
• Simply starting Chrome and watching a YouTube video hits 94-98°C on almost every P-core. Thermal throttles constantly.
• HDMI interface is faulty. Using a single screen and cable on either HDMI1 or HDMI2 on the back of the NUC will frequently (like 2-3 times a week on daily startups) cause the screen to show static and generate "popping" artifacts through the HDMI audio of the screen. It also does it when it's setup as a multi-monitor using both HDMI ports as well. Swapping screens, cables, ports, resetting BIOS, updating BIOS, changing HDMI settings per ASUS's own knowledge base did nothing. Will have to get and try a Thunderbolt-to-DisplayPort cable to see if that works any better. Currently the only way to fix it is disconnect the HDMI cable, wait a minute or two, and plug it back in.
• Haphazard driver and software support between it and Intel's own DSA, which still partially works and offers newer and more frequent NUC drivers than ASUS does yet. MyASUS is an overweight, functionally-reduced replacement to what Intel's NUC Software Studio, which stopped supporting NUC's past 11th or 12th gen I think.

Gone are the days of the quality Intel-built and supported NUCs. I wish now I would have bought another 11th or 12th gen NUC when they were still available if I had known what this 13th gen would be like.
