text:
One of the best PC cases in my opinion. Good for all sizes of motherboards from mini-ATX to EATX.

You get 4 fans included, three of them are 120s with RGB in the front and one 140 on the rear side. You get magnetic filters for the front, top, and the bottom (below the PSU). These will protect the insides from dust. You can add 3 more 120 fans on the top.

You get enough accessories for your HDDs and SSDs. Two sliding trays for 3.5” or 2.5” drives and 2 slots on the back side and two on the front side which equals to four more 2.5” drives. So the total this case can accommodate is 6 drives which is plenty.

There is enough space for a large PSU. Lots of holes for cables management. The texture on the case is beautiful with a tempered glass side panel. You get a large power button on the panel, 2 HD audio ports, and 2 usb 3.0 ports. There is no Reset Button though.

You won’t regret getting this. But keep one thing in mind, this case is huge, so check if you can accommodate this beast of a cabinet.

I got the cabinet in perfect condition. Thanks Amazon for this.

text:
I've used over 10 different cases, mostly popular corsair ones, but also other manufactures. Some I liked more than others, and only one of them I considered bad design.

This Asus Tuf GT 501 is simply by far the best I've ever owned. I'll never look back, it's what I've always wanted in a case. That's few screws, quick easy removal and replace of panels, filters, SSD and HDD trays, internal easy customization for space, (PSU cover for example) great cable management possibilities. All sturdy and logically fitting into position by lightly pushing pulling a panel or filter no screws mostly, but due to clever use of angled tooless parts very firm and solid when in place.
Comes with 2 120mm front intake fans and one 140mm exhaust fan, many places to attach your own fans. Plus abiltiy to take AIO (water cooling for CPU) in all popular sizes from 120mm right up to 360mm with all between too.
It's easy to forget how much engineering logic has gone into this because the case seems to help make installation easy and just get on with it.
All other cases I've owned, even ones which I considered very good have always had one annoying thing like a difficult to reach screw, panels which must be lined up carefully, or having to remove several parts in order to get to the part you want to reach. None of that is relevant here, things fit together quickly and easily, but firmly with no wiggle or vibration. It's simple and hugely functional, but just so well thought out for ease of use. First time system builders will even find few if any problems, and for people like me who have made many desktops it's just brilliant.
The last two cases I purchased were Corsair 780T full tower. A highly regarded case, which I also thought were very good too. They still are of course, but nothing comes close to the simple but sturdy, fit of the parts.
The side panels for example have two screws which are designed to be used by hand, just undo them, angle down and lift, plus no lost screws as they are made to stay attatched. The front panel and filters don't have any screws at all. Completely tool less, yet again, good solid confident fit when put back on.

I could go on but all I will say is the best, highly recommended, fairly priced mid tower/tower case that I had given up on finding. Well finally I found this case. The GT501 is outstanding in all regards.

text:
I've been waiting for the right time to land this case because I'm all about the TUF line of products made by ASUS.
I'll make this review shorter than my normal lengthy reviews with a simple PROS/CONS list:
PROS:
Cost - At $129.99 (on sale) I felt this was a reasonable price to pay for a style of case that catches my eye.
Ample space - This case has lots of space for airflow, components, and LEDs. I'm not used to working with LEDs but there are also connectors for the built in case LEDs (front fans). The headspace for a radiator and a full water cooling systems is generous as well. With this case, you won't have to worry about cramping things into a tightly confined space.
Screens/Filters - The case comes with some very nice screen and filter features to keep dust to a minimum. My house accumulates dust with people and dogs (and a ball python!) so I'm a stickler for having space for filters.
Fans - Plenty of provided fans that are quiet, move air handily, and the front fan LEDs are a nice touch.
Enclosed PSU channel - This is a nice touch. This IS a PRO, but I'm a little disappointed that there's no rubber passthrough grommets. They're located to the right of the motherboard mounting space but I think the PSU channel's opening should have them as well. Keep the PSU isolated as much as possible is my thought.
CONS:
Cable Management - It's a defacto standard in most all cases now, and while this is addressed, the right-side panel seems short on zip-tie anchor points. I would like to see more of a lattice of anchor points, even if they're affixed to the base instead of being punched through. Asus included a good number of zip-ties however. So a small CON and not too glaringly annoying. It's a personal wish so I'm not deducting any stars.
Width - While there's lots of space in this case, a little narrower of a design would be good. I know cases are handling larger and larger GPUs and water cooling, but I think ASUS designed this one overly generous. It encroaches on too much of my desk space and I didn't realize this prior to buying it. Should I have measured? Yes. Did I? No. My fault. But it's still pretty wide.

All in all, I'm happy with the case. It's a nice change from my black case without any RGB. I don't need a lot of RGB but his provides just enough to keep things happy and not too distracting. I would recommend this case to any PC builder that wants a very cool looking case, likes the ASUS brand, and wants to customize a PC that fits an individuals varying tastes in components, cooling, and lighting.

I really like this design. Although similar to a Lian Li 011 (and others) in layout, this is a far superior product. Every aspect was thought of and well planned. From the release of the side panels, the top cover's magnetic retention, to the way the radiator rack on the top pivots out, EVERYTHING was designed and made by someone who, like me, build PC's on a regular basis. I've Been building PC's since 1990 and have seen a lot of good and bad over the decades. This is by far the best case I have ever used. I had to track a wire with a bad connection and within seconds I was able to remove a few panels and move a radiator to find the offending connection. All that without cutting up my hands or popping a zip-tie. The GPU vertical mount kit works better than any other I've used and the included anti-sag was a really nice, effective bonus.
I initially thought the straps on top were cheap gimmick until I started using them. Today, most high-end components are full of heatsinks, heat pipes, radiators and chunks of metal just to look cool. A motherboard and radiator can be 20 pounds, before you add in the heft of a video card. Instead of putting that weight into the meat of your hands while grabbing onto metal and glass corners, lifting by the straps is so much easier and less likely to do damage (to you or the case). This has changed how I do a lot of things, and all for the better. My hat's off to Asus on this one I don't know how they will top it, but for now this will be the only tower I recommend.

text:
I picked up the GT302 to replace my NZXT H510 Flow, and I couldn't be happier with the swap.
The H510 Flow served me well and had solid airflow, but during intensive gaming sessions the exhaust ran warmer than I was comfortable with. The GT302 was a welcome change in every sense — starting with its noticeably larger footprint. I originally appreciated the compact size of the H510, but the extra space the GT302 provides makes navigating the build so much easier and more enjoyable.

The included fans are incredible and the airflow improvement is immediately apparent. The detachable top cover is a slick touch that proved genuinely useful when installing my Nautilus 240 RS ARGB AIO. One thing worth noting for prospective buyers — if your motherboard isn't a BTF/zero connector design like my MAG Z690 Tomahawk WiFi DDR4, the PSU cable routing may limit you to a 240mm AIO rather than a 360mm. Not a dealbreaker at all, just something to be aware of going in.

Build quality is top notch throughout. The panels feel solid, the dust filters do their job, and the subtle ARGB lighting hits just the right balance — present without being overdone. I manage everything through MSI Mystic Light and it integrates beautifully.

For everything it includes and delivers, the GT302 hits the sweet spot. Highly recommended.

I've gone through quite a few cases the last few years and I've found reason to replace all of them. The white ASUS TUF Gaming GT302 ARGB feels like a keeper.

Some of the benefits I can think of compared to the other ATX cases I've had lately:
- It comes with useable nice standard ARGB-fans that you can connect straight to the motherboard (unlike e.g. Corsair that have their own non-standard stuff)
- The case panel/ports are easily accessible in the front and not awkwardly positioned on the top or side.
- Great size. Not too small, it still fits EATX motherboards and is easy to work with, but it's not too big so it feels clumsy and/or extremely heavy.
- The white color is actual white and not dirty white like some other so called 'white' cases. It's not as snow-white as some Fractal Design cases, but still what I'd call true white.
- The front fans cover the full front area all the way to the bottom, so you can put U.2/U.3 SSD drives close to the bottom fan, as such drives desperately needs cooling.

Is it perfect? No, but I say it's 90% there, and I can't think of a better case available today, so I definitely rate it five stars.
Just to mention something negative, which like everything here, is just personal opinions, is that I'm not too fond of the fully covering PSU 'shroud', and I definitely miss 5.25" external bays (which I find just sad that almost no cases has today).

text:
TP-Link Nano 2-in-1 USB Bluetooth WiFi Adapter
I’ve been using the Archer T2UB Nano for a while now, and it’s one of those small tech accessories that punches way above its weight.

Setup and Compatibility
Installation was simple: plug it in, disable any conflicting built-in WiFi/Bluetooth, and Windows picked it up quickly. It supports Windows 7 through 11 for both WiFi and Bluetooth, but it’s strictly PC-only (no Mac/Linux/TV support). That’s worth keeping in mind if you’re hoping to use it cross-platform.

Performance – WiFi
The dual-band AC600 speeds are solid for such a tiny device. On 5 GHz I saw stable connections near the rated 433 Mbps, which handled HD streaming and video calls without issues. On 2.4 GHz, speeds are naturally lower (\~200 Mbps peak), but still reliable for browsing and lighter tasks. WPA3 support is a nice bonus for security, especially on public networks.

Performance – Bluetooth
Bluetooth 4.2 worked flawlessly for connecting my headphones, mouse, and even a PS4 controller on PC. Latency was low enough that gaming felt smooth, and range was decent given the size. Just note you’ll need to disable any internal Bluetooth to avoid conflicts.

Design
The nano form factor is excellent – it barely sticks out from the USB port, so I can leave it in permanently even when moving my laptop around. Build feels sturdy despite its tiny size.

Bottom line: For under \$20, this adapter is an easy 5/5. It’s compact, reliable, and effectively turns an older desktop or laptop into a dual-band WiFi and Bluetooth-capable machine. Great value if you need a simple, no-hassle upgrade.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
Due to a botched repair (My fault...again...) I had to convert the WLAN card slot in an older Yoga laptop to use an compact SSD card instead. This meant that the laptop no longer had onboard WiFi or Bluetooth. I am a retired Wi-Fi field engineer and I know a bit about client performance.

First priority here was preventing damage to the USB port, which meant it had to project less than a half inch from the body. It also had to provide Bluetooth. My expectations for performance were minimal and I expected all kinds of grief from power management turning the adapter off during sleep, doze, etc. This adapter more than meets this size requirement.

-And surprise surprise, it works much better than I'd hoped. It easily saturates my cable modem link (150 down, 15 up) and more importantly, the link is consistent during Teams meetings and voice calls. The AP I'm using is 10' away on the other side of a kitchen wall. My PHY rate is 250mbps as I write this (5Ghz, 80mhz channel, 1SS, Wi-Fi5/AC link) and the external mouse is BT connected. Too much attention is paid to signal strength and even data rate. What really matters is link consistency and this thing hits the mark.

I've been using it for weeks and don't remember having any link drops or issues waking up from power save. There was one occurrence where the laptop went to sleep during a Google Voice call, and the stream was interrupted. It came right back after wiggling the mouse. (BT has been flawless).

It's a little expense in my opinion, but as far as I know this is the smallest USB WLAN adapter out there so maybe it's worth the premium. It does allow me to keep this old (But expensive) laptop on the road for another year or two. It dropped right in to Windows 11 without any manual driver installation. My network is WPA-2 so I can't speak to WPA-3 support.

I also messed with the super-cheap adapters you can by on the direct-from-china sites. Don't bother. While the size is right, they are consistently awful, even at $5. If you need a tiny Wi-Fi adapter, get this one.

title: 1.0 out of 5 stars
text:
The goodish: At first I really liked this computer, I got it for some at home work and gaming (Minecraft & Valorant). It was great for work. Minecraft lagged badly in Java but once I switched to the windows/bedrock version it played smoother. Valorant seemed to play good but I don’t have great internet so it’s hard to tell & the PC would occasionally crash mid game leading to afk offenses. One thing to note is that the monitor it came with was a wall monitor, I knew there was variations to what monitor you could get but there was no info about it possibly being a wall monitor. It was actually kind of nice for me but if you live in a place that can’t have a wall monitor keep in mind it’s possible for it to come with one that only works on the wall.
The very bad:
As mentioned before it would occasionally crash completely powering down but it would always boot back up and work fine after. About 6 months after I got it the pc crashed mid use, I went to turn it back on and it popped up with a screen saying the PC needed to be recovered with a special disk. I looked up the error code and saw that sometimes that is caused by a usb or power cord not being properly connected and to unplug all cords and check their connection. I did this and In doing this found that the power cord (sent with the computer originally) had melted. For background I only use the computer 4-6 hours at max in a day and had only had the computer on for about an hour when this happened so if I was using this full time for work instead of just occasional projects I don’t know how this pc would have held up. I reached out to the pc seller and after about a week of trying to get in contact (calling and them never picking up or calling me back, them insisting on calling me and then not) they told me to simply pick up a new standard 3 prong power cord. I was obviously worried that there was a bigger issue that would lead to the pc melting a cord but did what they said. They didn’t tell me any other details like what voltage requirements it needed so I looked around and got one that matched the voltage that most on the market are, that didn’t work. I looked at the original cord and it had a different requirement and after scouring the web found one that matched it and tried it however that didn’t work either with the computer only having a flashing orange power light/nothing on screen/and the fan running loud. I then reached out to the seller again and told them this and they said to take it to a local computer repair person because my warranty had ended. Luckily I had gotten the extra asurion protection plan. I called their tech support and they told me that this usually means that the power supply unit has failed and I would need to file a claim to get a refund. I’m glad I got the protection plan but this means packing up a pc, monitor, keyboard, and mouse and shipping it to asurion in order to get an Amazon gift card refund.
Bottom line I’m in shock that in only 6 months of owning this pc the power supply unit failed and on top of that the customer support was incredibly lacking once I did experience issues.

text:
I ordered up 14 of these units (a couple different orders) and started installing them in client locations. Within a week, we started getting calls about the units trying to boot from PXE or saying "Operating System not found." Thought it was a fluke at first but eventually determined that this company has their own white-labeled M.2/PCIe SSDs and this series of Optiplex 7010s do NOT like them. In the end, we ended up having to replace the half dozen or so units we couldn't really swap out with new, brand-name SSDs to resolve the problem.

We did manage to return 7 of them, but I had to go buy big boxes as we'd already tossed the ones they were delivered in. Then we had to hound Amazon for several days to get the seller to actually refund the money (several days in, two of them had been refunded, but Amazon's site just kept saying "Refund in process" and they'd refund the money once they all were received). After a few pokes at Amazon, we did get our money back, but man did this cost me a lot of man hours having to rebuild failed/incompatible SSDs on the fly.

I don't know what's wrong with their white-labeled SSDs, but they must be incredibly cheap (and modern Optiplex units only really like NVMe models that can run in native RAID mode).

For the record, I did go to their web site and it looks like it was done in Microsoft Word. I managed to get a request out explaining my situation but only got a "please create a ticket" response.

I'd used OEMGENUINE in the past with good results, but wow was this a disaster. Do NOT buy these units unless you intend to put a quality SSD in it!!

title: 4.0 out of 5 stars
text:
But, be ready for what you're getting. You'll receive an OLDER, ahead-of-its-time system that was probably built and sold to schools or colleges and used very little by the time it rotated back out and was replaced. Those older systems then go to a refurbisher who cleans them up, checks them out, and resells them.

That means they're in reliably-good shape when you get them, but be careful to read VERY CAREFULLY. Many of the systems you see being advertised for pennies-on-the-dollar are cheap because they aren't capable of running Windows 11 and future OS that requires TPM 2.0 (or higher). They'll be fine until about 2025, but after that, it's up to the manufacturer as to whether they will support Windows 10 or another OS on the unit.

But enough. My Optiplex 5060 arrived in a plain box that was well-suited for shipping. But, honestly, the Optiplex was the ONLY THING IN THE BOX. No power cord, no keyboard, no mouse, no driver CDs, NOTHING. So, these little units may not be for everyone.

That being said, within 3 hours of receiving the Optiplex, I had connected it up to existing keyboard, mouse, and power and was in the process of transferring all the files and apps from my old Windows 10 computer (thank you Lap-Link Mover Pro!).

After getting the Windows 11 up and running, I added a second 1 TB SDD (you'll need a SATA power splitter and an additional SATA data cable to connect to the vacant second channel SATA adapter connector on the main board to add a second SATA drive.) The main board also supports the micro-format and large-format M.2 SDD drives if you crave yet another TB or so of storage.

Don't expect much of the WiFi either. You may want to reserve the limited PCIe slots to add a Wifi-Bluetooth combo card, because the USB-based WiFi dongle I got with my system was an 802.11n which cut my WiFi speeds by 66% over my retired system running 802.11ac.

Overall, I'd give this little diamond 5 stars if it weren't for the corners cut on things like power cords and WiFi. But, as it sits, this little system was worth every penny paid and more.

I was a bit dubious about ordering this machine as the price seemed to good to be true and it was not available with Prime. I chose the free shipping option and it arrived much faster than predicted - no HST or duties payable on receipt. It was sent form the USA.

It was packed very well and the machine was very clean, the only defect that I could see was that there was a tiny ding in the case otherwise it was in perfect condition.

I ordered the Win11 version with 32GB of memory and a 512GB NVMe drive. In retrospect, I discovered that if I had chosen the Win10 version then I could have ordered it with 64GB of memory and a 1TB NVMe drive. I would have done that if I had realised that at the time, but I can add more memory later if I wish so matter.

My machine did come with on-board wifi and Bluetooth and it also came with a DVD-RW which I was not expecting. There was also the inevitable wired keyboard and mouse.

I like Dell business computers like this, they are solid and workmanlike, are not stuffed with crap software and, most importantly, Dell publishes very detailed online manuals on how to service and upgrade their hardware.

I will be using this computer mostly for software development and running a Linux VM so having lots of memory will be good.

I have been using the machine for a few weeks now with no problems and it is much faster then the Dell Optiplex 5050 that it replaces.

All in all, I am very happy with my purchase and will check out ReUse computers next time I am looking for an upgrade.

BTW. As stated, this version of the 7090 has a 10th generation Intel processor in it, a slighty later version of the 7090 has an 11th generation processor which would allow you to use somewhat faster NVMe drives (4 lanes versus 3). Otherwise I don't think that it makes a significant difference.

text:
I ordered 3 of these. On paper, they are great. The first one I received had a 256GB SSD instead of the advertised 512. It also only had 8GB memory instead of the 16GB advertised. I contacted amazon support and they wanted me to contact the seller. I contacted the seller and they said "We are sorry for the inconvenience. Please reach out to Amazon customer support for a return/replacement as this was fulfilled by Amazon." According to Amazon "Sorry, this order is not eligible for a refund under the A-to-z Guarantee because you have not yet submitted a return request with the seller. Please request a return via the Online Returns Center and allow the seller two days to get back to you."

I had already remotely deployed the unit in a customer's environment, installed AV, Office, & joined to their domain and setup user profiles, so I just gave up.

The other two, came as advertised, but the 2nd unit I setup is so slow it took about 2 hours to get through the out of box experience. Once in windows, it was not possible to open an explorer window or browser. the cursor just spun for hours. I tried about 10 times after rebooting, etc. I gave up on that one as well ready to return it. (haven't tried starting that process again)

I was able to setup the 3rd unit in place of the 2nd one okay, but later I noticed it wasn't as quick as it should be for a computer with a 6 core i5, 16GB of ram and SSD. Task manager showed it running at .79GHz. So I changed the performance profile to High Performance and rebooted. That changed nothing. I created my own custom high performance profile, selected that and rebooted. Again only .79GHz. I checked the advanced power settings and min and max CPU were set to 100%. I then reset the bios to factory defaults and low and behold on boot I got a message that the type of power supply could not be determined. When this happens to a DELL, it throttles the CPU at the slowest possible speed. The seller is providing a PSU that on paper would have more than enough power for this micro pc, but the barrel jack is too long so the center pin doesn't make contact. That is required for the system to determine the wattage of the PSU.

THE SELLER INTENTIONALLY TURNED OFF THE POST ADAPTER WARNING about the PSU not being identified. I verified this to be the case on ALL 3 UNITS! Unfortunately, I don't have time to wait for returns and refunds, so I ordered myself 2 new PSU's that are advertised as being for this specific model. I will be returning the 2nd unit because despite the PSU .79GHz issue, there has got to be something else going on with the hardware as the other two units were still somewhat usable at .79GHz. If you don't believe me look at the images.

Update 1/2/2022:
After ordering 7 of these, I can say that I've received only 1 unit with the advertised Wireless KB & Mouse. Sadly only the mouse worked...

I bought this I purchased this Dell Inspiron laptop in June 2024, and by October 2025 the hinge completely failed during normal, careful use.
The hinge did not loosen gradually. The plastic casing around the hinge cracked and separated, exposing internal components. This is not wear and tear or accidental damage. It is a structural design issue where the hinge is mounted into thin plastic instead of reinforced metal.
I am a careful user. The laptop was opened and closed normally and was never dropped or abused. Once the hinge failed, the laptop became unsafe to open and close without risking screen or cable damage.
After researching, I discovered this is a common problem with this model, and replacement requires disassembling the laptop and replacing major parts. This should not happen to a laptop that is barely over a year old.
For the price point, I expected basic durability. I would not recommend this model unless you are prepared for potential hinge repairs

text:
CAREFUL!
I bought this Dell laptop on Amazon on February 24, 2025, and received it just a few days later. So far, I’m impressed with the performance—the computer runs fast, the touchscreen is responsive, and the overall build feels sturdy. The sound is decent too, especially after a full round of updates (which took almost a full day to complete when I first set it up).

However, I’m writing this review to share something important that buyers should know. When I checked the warranty on March 4, I found that there were less than six months remaining—even though I had just bought the device. After contacting Dell, I learned that the warranty started when the third-party seller originally purchased the laptop, not when I did. So, even though this was a new, unopened product, the warranty had already been ticking down for months.

This detail wasn’t clearly mentioned on the Amazon product page. I had no idea buying from a third-party seller on Amazon could mean getting a product with an almost expired warranty. In my opinion, this should be more transparent. It’s something I definitely wish I had known ahead of time.

Other notes: the battery life is on the shorter side, and the fans are constantly running—so it’s not the quietest laptop out there. But in terms of speed and features, it’s a solid machine. The touchscreen is smooth and responsive, and everything else feels like good quality. text:
Not what I wanted. I made the mistake. I ordered this computer under the new Dell's renaming plan. I wanted the renamed Latitude, not the renamed Inspiron which this computer is, and the seller CLEARLY titled it as such. The Latitude has more ports than the Inspiron. Again, MY BAD. Why... Why me. After looking and looking and then making this mistake...GRRRR. Anyways, what a fantastic computer!! I purchased my previous computer around ~2008, so yes, I am impressed with the newest and latest. I chose the upgraded components such as the Ultra 9, 32GB the high-end LPDDR5X (I'm talking about a max of 8,533Mbps, OMG), 2TB SSD... Logi M650L mouse. This combo is so fast, I mean so fast, I can't even keep up. Just a blink of an eye and my photography program(s) run, and the task is finished.
The backlit keyboard keeps turning off and turns back on with a touch of any key. I'll have to find the way to disable this in that I want to see the keyboard when I initially place my fingers. After that, it can turn off as I know where the symbols are.
Very easy and actually very quick setup. I chose to use a thumb drive to bring my programs and data over. Recognized my printer very quickly. My home webpage already saved my 'favorites', so no problems there.
Speaker is sufficient in that I do not have to turn it up to 100, just to barely hear it. Usually, 50-55 suffices with this computer. I can actually hear the stereo separation. Even with the audio/video players equalizer, it still plays music flat. Absolutely no bass. Yes, I know this isn't a home 5,000w speaker system, but this is 2025. I would expect a laptop to sound like a mini stereo system with, I don't know, BASS... or at least better than the cheapest cellphone. Come-on.
USB ports... As stated before, I wanted the Latitude with more ports. This one has only one USB. My mouse takes that one. That's it. No more ports. Hmm, 2025 says at least 2 ports standard?? It has 2 USB-C ports. One is occupied for power, although I believe it can be used if running off of battery.
This computer gets slightly; I mean very, very, VERY slightly warm on the bottom of the left side. Hardly even noticeable unless you are actually looking for it. The fan is also very quiet. I do not notice it unless I'm looking for the noise, slightly turning my head or it speeds up Still very quiet. Other than that, I can't hear it with the awesome, no bass music playing.
Screen is crystal clear and is advertised as "Low Blue Light (Hardware Solution)". Yeah, don't ask me. It seems to work.
I love this computer...BUT, as stated previously, I wanted the Latitude. Meh, I'll have to use my USB adapter.
Only one con I see. When turning on the computer, everything loads up fast to include connecting to the internet. However, the computer is slow to allow the home webpage to connect to the internet. I don't know why. I click the internet icon and shows it, in of itself, will not connect for a good minute, although the computer itself indicates it is connected to the Wi-Fi network. Could be my non-McAfee internet security checking things out first or could be this newest and latest Wi-Fi7 but who knows. Just a minor inconvenience.
Lesson learned. Take your time and know which model you are purchasing.

text:
This is a semi-budget laptop with quite a few premium features. I bought it Feb 2026 for $718 making it even more of a value then the current price which I see is over $900. I've been using it for a week so I don't know how it will hold up over time but so far I'm very impressed.

PROS

- PROCESSOR: The Intel Core Ultra 7 256V seems really fast and responsive.

- NPU: It has an integrated NPU (Neural Processing Unit) rated around 47 TOPS to accelerate AI tasks. This seems great for this price-range laptop. I didn't even expect it to come with any NPU at all.

- DISPLAY: 2.5K resolution looks really nice and seems to be 100% sRGB which shows the full color gamut. It's also anti-glare which is really nice given how many amazing OLED and glossy laptops have unfortunate amounts of glare.

- GRAPHICS: Intel Arc Graphics which are better for gaming & content creation than Intel Integrated Graphics

- STORAGE: 1 TB storage is pretty good in this price range.

- SPEAKERS: Waves MaxxAudio Output + Dolby Atmos Cores and Stereo Speakers. The sound seems fantastic for a laptop but I was coming from an Acer Aspire which had pretty awful audio.

- LID OPENING: Can open and close the lid with one hand

CONS

- PORTS: Only 1 USB-A port. I really hate this. 2 USB-A ports seem to be the standard lately. I'm going to need to start carrying around a USB hub just because of this.

- KEYBOARD PLACEMENT: The keyboard is paused back further than I'm used to. I think it's because this model prioritizes a bigger trackpad over keyboard ergonomics. title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
Having upgraded from a cheaper 1080p webcam, these are my comparisons:

Pros:
- Auto-focus works amazing. No more fighting with manual adjustments. You really couldn't do better in the settings yourself. Trust me, I tried.
- Low light image quality is a definite improvement.
- HDR mode works great to balance highlights and shadows.
- AI tracking is a neat feature though I don't intend to use it.
- Zoom feature in DELL software is nice (though its not really an optical zoom, it's just a blown up image).
- 65 degree vs 78 degree viewing angle options are also nice. (though again, it just looks like 65 degrees seems to be a more zoomed in version of 78 with no improvement in sharpness or image quality).
- Build quality is solid.
- Camera feed has never randomly dropped out. I always had to unplug and re-plug my old webcam.

Cons (kinda):
- Coming from a 1080p camera I expected the image detail on a 2K camera to be twice as sharp?
Well, not really.
The output resolution is definitely 2560x1440p and there are bit more details in the image, but I guess I had forgotten to do the actual math. The difference in horizontal and vertical resolution is about 33% (from 1920x1080), so remember, 2K doesn't necessarily mean twice as much. There is also a definite improvement in image quality as well. I was going to give this 4 stars because I expected something near a 2x improvement, but after doing a side by side comparison I've changed my mind. It was a poor assumption to begin with and probably a ridiculous expectation as well.

Conclusion:
While I haven't had other 1080p cameras to compare to, I'm pretty sure there are others out there that might probably do what this does, for cheaper, with comparable image quality, albeit at a slightly lower resolution. So if you really don't *need* that extra resolution (to show the real texture of your skin during those Zoom meetings), I wouldn't bother with getting a 2K webcam. That being said, everything that this webcam does, it does do pretty well, so, if you specifically want to get a 2K camera, this is the one I'd get.

This Philips monitor strikes a smart balance of price, image quality, and performance. If you need a secondary display or value smooth visuals and eye care features, it’s a solid pick. Just be prepared to add accessories if you want adjustability or audio built in.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
This HP 24mh monitor has a clear, crisp display and is the perfect size for desktop use (not too big, not too small). It accepts both HDMI and DisplayPort inputs (and even VGA for old school PCs). While Windows will select 60Hz refresh rate by default, you can go into Windows' display settings and select 75Hz refresh rate for this monitor. The 75Hz refresh rate really does help smooth out motion. You should also go into the monitor's "Image" menu setting and set Response Time to Level 3 which provides the best VSYNC performance. One of the best features that places this monitor above and beyond its price range is the 90-degree rotating screen, height adjustment, and swiveling base. The stand is rock-solid without any wobble. The speakers are just fine once you discover the menu control I explain below:

HOW TO FIX LOW VOLUME SOUND: The built-in speakers are better than some reviewers indicate. I believe most people don't discover that the monitor menu has its own volume control that's set to 50% volume by factory default. If you just connect this monitor to the PC you'll automatically get sound through the HP speakers via HDMI or DisplayPort (you only have to use the separate audio cable when using the VGA input). But no matter how high you turn up your PC volume control, you'll only get 50% volume from the monitor's speakers which is why people complain about low volume. To fix this, all you need to do is go to the "Management" tab of the monitor menu, select "Audio", and then turn up the volume control from 50 (default) to 100 and you'll find the monitor speakers are plenty loud. After that, you'll only have to use your PC volume control as normal.

This is a great quality monitor with features beyond its price range. Fantastic value, HP!

ADDITIONAL NOTE: HP sells an identical monitor to the HP 24mh under the model P24h. The only difference is that the P24h has a black plastic logo strip along the bottom instead of silver like the 24mh. Everything else is identical (specs, speakers, height adjustable stand, etc.) plus the P24h comes with both an HDMI cable and a DisplayPort cable.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
I bought the MSI PRO MP273W E14A for pretty much one specific reason: Xbox Series X + Black Ops 7 at 120Hz. I wanted the smoother tracking and reduced motion blur you get from such a high refresh without turning my desk into a “RGB spaceship.” This monitor nailed that balance alongside superior portability. Clean.

On console, the win isn’t 144Hz (since Xbox won’t use that), it’s that the panel has enough refresh headroom to run a clean, stable 120Hz pipeline when the game supports it. In BO7, the feel difference is immediate:

Smoother camera pans (less judder)
Cleaner target tracking (less perceived blur)
More responsive aim (lower perceived input delay bc frames update twice as often vs 60Hz)

So if you’ve been playing at 60Hz, 120Hz doesn’t just look better — it plays better, especially in fast FPS fights where micro-adjustments matter.

Office + daily use: underrated strengths:

Text looks clean and stable for long coding / spreadsheet sessions
Viewing angles don’t shift if you lean back or sit off-center
Anti-glare + IPS is a great combo for daytime work setups

A quick technical note: 27" at 1080p is about ~82 PPI, so for office work it’s best at a normal desk distance. If you sit very close, you’ll notice pixels more than you would on a 1440p panel — but for mixed gaming + productivity, it’s still very usable (and the high refresh makes even scrolling feel “premium”).

What i Like most:

True high-refresh feel (especially noticeable in FPS)
IPS clarity for work
Clean look that fits an office desk
144Hz headroom helps keep 120Hz operation comfortable and stable

tldr: I came for BO7 at 120Hz on Series X, and I ended up with a monitor that’s legitimately enjoyable for work too. Smooth where it counts, clean where it matters.

Setup tip: On Xbox, go to Settings → General → TV & display options and set:

Refresh rate: 120Hz
Resolution: 1080p
Enable VRR (if your unit exposes it / your HDMI path supports it)
Turn hdmi settings off for peak performance and less tearing

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
I’m particular about design. It took me 5 tries to find a monitor that met my needs. Thought I’d write up a review in case it’s helpful to someone else.

No one has paid me for this review. Keep in mind I am using a monitor to extend the display of my MacBook Pro.

My needs: I am a writer and wanted to be able to have multiple pages documents open at the same time. I also do some graphic design and wanted to have true colors represented on the screen. I live in a small cabin so this monitor would also need to serve as my TV—high streaming quality and beautiful resolution is a must. They pretty much only make 4K monitors in the 27” size and those are too large for me to use as a work screen and also too large for my space. That left me trying to figure out what smaller monitor would have a high resolution--it took multiple tries. I also am sensitive to light and wanted something that wouldn’t hurt my eyes after being in front of it for long hours.

Dell 24 Plus Monitor - S2425HSM

CONS
There is no option to hook up a USB-C or thunderbolt cable on this monitor. Thus you can not charge your laptop by plugging it into the monitor.
This monitor is designed so that you plug an HDMI cable into your laptop and then into the monitor. HDMI cables are bulky and don’t bend as easily as a USB-C or Thunderbolt cable. HDMI cables do not charge your laptop. USB-C or Thunderbolt cables are more bendy and charge your laptop directly from your monitor.
You cannot have your MacBook in clamshell mode (laptop closed) without having your laptop charging cable plugged in. Thus instead of one USB-C or Thunderbolt cable you have the bulky HDMI and your laptops power cord. When I had all the cables hooked up it felt messy and it was all sort of awkwardly mashed into the desk riser I built.
The text resolution of this monitor was pretty pixilated. Downloading Better Display and creating a virtual screen helped a bit.

PROS
144Hz refresh rate
The streaming quality wasn’t as good as some of the monitors I’d try later on but it was pretty darn good! Speakers are great.
Pretty much no eye strain!
It’s so odd but I completely fell in love with this monitor despite the fact that it really didn’t meet any of my core needs. I loved the color, the sleek design and the ease of the mini joystick on the monitor itself. The menu on this monitor via the joystick was really enjoyable and adjusting the settings produced effective results (more so than the U2424HE which I’ll review next). I actually liked the menu options on this (adjusting the color, brightness, gamma, screen mode etc) better than any other monitor.
I loved the 16:9 ratio which I would return to when all was said and done.
I barely was able to return this monitor because I was weirdly attached to it. I’d say this is perfect for a high school or college student. As far as budget monitors go, this is a really great option. If it had a USB C option I doubt I would have returned it or bought a thousand other monitors trying to find the right one.

Dell UltraSharp 24" Hub Monitor - (U2424HE)
CONS
This monitor supposedly has better resolution than the Dell S2425HSM. I put them side by side and played the same show. No matter how I adjusted the settings, the U2424HE looked overly red. And the resolution wasn’t that much better, if at all. Text did appear to be slightly sharper but it wasn’t a significant difference.
Contains a USB C Port but would not allow me to put laptop into clamshell mode without having laptop power cord plugged in.
Only 60Hz refresh rate

PROS
None. I can’t recommend this for anyone.

ASUS ProArt 24” (24.1” viewable) 16:10 HDR Professional Monitor (PA248CRV)

CONS
Text still wasn’t as sharp as I’d like.
I didn’t like the screen ratio. But I didn’t know how much I would miss the 16:9 of that first Dell until I tried this one. This is more of a personal preference than a mark against the brand. It does have more vertical space if that is important to you.

PROS
It features a USB-C port (one step down from a Thunderbolt cable) that handles video, data, and charging simultaneously.
Streaming quality was decent. Better than both Dells, not as good as BenQ or Asus PA24ACRV.
Daisy chaining and comprehensive USB hub with 4 ports.
No noticeable eye strain after adjusting settings a bit.
I got very close to keeping this one but I couldn’t get over the ratio. It is a decent monitor though so I ended up giving it to a friend.

BenQ MA270U 27” 4K 3840x2160
CONS
At this point I was about at my wits end and thought that I’d have to get a 27” to get the resolution that I was after. I tried to use this as my work monitor and it was overwhelming. I know a lot of people use a 27” monitor but that was too much for me.
4K panels often require much stronger backlights to push light through those tiny pixels, which can be brutal for light-sensitive eyes in a small space. No matter what I did with the settings it was too bright. This monitor supposedly has blue light blocking technology built in. Look—if eye stain is an issue for you, what I realized is that less is more. Some of these high resolution monitors achieve true colors by using a lot of light, and no amount of filters, screen shade, night shift, blue light glasses etc, is going to help with that much light coming at you. Even when I took the opacity waaaaay down and had all the filters on I still felt like I was being radiated.
This monitor is very large and heavy. Not great for a small desk set up in a small cabin. It about crushed my desk riser.

PROS
Really beautiful colors and crisp text.
Super cool software download (from BenQ website) that allows you to adjust settings. No need for clunky buttons.
Compatibility with Apple.
I ended up giving this monitor to my partner to use as his new TV in the living room. Sitting back from it a few more feet, it’s easier to appreciate.

ASUS ProArt Display 24” (23.8 inch viewable) 1440P Professional Monitor (PA24ACRV)
This is the one I ultimately kept for myself.

CONS
My main complaint is that the physical design of the monitor feels a bit outdated. Sort of 90’s. Dell did a really great job condensing their buttons on their monitor to the one mini joystick. On the Asus monitors it’s a bunch of buttons across the bottom right side of the monitor. Feels clunky. These should be accessed through the joystick or hidden.
Speakers are pretty awful.

PROS
16:9 ratio
It has very sharp text.
The silver color of the monitor base is the same as my MacBook Pro.
USB-C Power Delivery (A step down from Thunderbolt—working great for me). I only have ONE cable plugged in to the monitor and no need for the powercord for my laptop.
Daisy Chain capability with multiple USB ports for mouse, external hard drive etc. and other types as well.
Pixel Density (123 PPI). Standard 24" monitors are usually 1080p (~93 PPI), which macOS struggles to scale, leading to "gray/blurry" text.
Much higher resolution than the Asus PA248CRV that I had tried. Text is crisp. Even crisper after implementing Better Display. Seriously try Better Display. Ask Ai how to set it up. Spending $21 for the pro version of this software can make a monitor like this feel like a much more expensive monitor because macOS assumes most of these monitors are a low-resolution screen. It doesn't use its high-quality "Retina" scaling. Using this software helps these monitors reach their potential.
This monitor has a deeper black than the Dell monitors I tried where the text appeared to be a gray. Colors are vibrant and photos are incredibly vivid.
Resolution quality is great in Adobe/Design work and during streaming. I noticed that when I’m streaming from Safari as opposed to Chrome, the quality is significantly better.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
This review is for the S2725HS 27in model.

This is a very nice, high value, well featured monitor. Very well thought out and designed, and certainly a complete package sort of item in its budget friendly segment.

Aside from its clear and vibrant picture with good color accuracy and contrast ratio, its the extras here not found on many other monitors in this segment that set it apart. It features a fully adjustable stand that can be easily set for height, tilt, angle (swivel), and also rotate 180 degrees. It's base is anti-slip, which adds even more stability to an already sturdy set up. Two HDMI ports mean you can seamlessly connect two devices to the monitor, which is very nice for the casual gamer such as myself. And its built in speakers are very good for what they are. The unit lacks USB ports, a headphone jack, and has no audio in/out features otherwise. But given the quality of the audio, the less demanding user won't miss separate speaker options. The audio output quality is on par with popular, basic 2.0 computer speakers on the market today, if not quite as crisp. They're simply a convenient alternative to have, whether you want a less cluttered set up, an alternative to your current external speakers, or need an additional audio source for a connected device. As for myself, it was the former and latter. I have a very small space to work with and added a game console to it. I wanted to upgrade my aging and average monitor to go with, and this monitor made it all plug and play, no additional hardware or wiring needed. Two HDMI ports for laptop and game console, acceptable built in speakers for said game console, and it was a wrap. Simple, space efficient, and easy. I like that.

Nothing feels cheap or flimsy about this monitor, and its attractive and a bit stylish. It has nice cable management touches, and a fair enough range of adjustability concerning its set up and physical footprint. Considering its a standard FHD monitor with a 27in display, it also doesn't lack clarity or sharpness concerning its 81ppi count. It is a good, colorful, and even vibrant panel in its segment with nice clarity and good viewing angles. If you are obsessed about perfectly sharp text and inspect it with the macro lens on your cellphone to verify it meets personal standards, don't get this. title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
I never review my Amazon purchases, but I'm so impressed with this one I had to say something. I had an old Dell monitor that I loved for its color accuracy, but after 12 years the backlight died on me and I had to find a replacement quick and on a tight budget. I caught this one on a limited-time sale for $100, but IMO it would still be an excellent deal at full price.

1. The included stand is the most adjustable I've ever seen out of the box. Notably, it can rotate into portrait mode in _either direction_ (clockwise or counter-clockwise), which doesn't sound super impressive, but it makes things like cable management and getting a good look at the inputs much easier, even if you don't intend to leave it that way.

2. The picture quality (and adjustability via the menu) is way above and beyond my expectations. Straight out of the box it had excellent brightness and contrast but the image was way too cool (par for the course, since default configurations are usually optimized for in-store displays where they're going to be overwhelmed by bright, cool fluorescent store lights). I was able to eyeball-calibrate it to match my primary display in less than 5 minutes using just the built-in menu options. I still need to dig my Spyder out of storage and give it a proper deep-dive software calibration, but already it's good enough that I'd be comfortable doing most of my design work on this display.

3. The included I/O options are excellent. Most of the displays you'll find in this price range only have 1 HDMI and 1 VGA (?!) input, which doesn't meet the bare minimum requirements for my home-office setup, where I need to plug my personal desktop in via DisplayPort and my work laptop in (through a DisplayLink dock) via HDMI or DisplayPort. This has 2x HDMI and 1x DisplayPort input for video, plus a headphone-out (for sending audio through the HDMI or DP inputs), and it can also act as a USB hub. While I would have loved some Mini-DP inputs and DP daisy-chaining support like my old Dell had, this is plenty sufficient for my setup, and, again, really atypical for the price range.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
This is a really nice monitor. It was very easy to set up. It weighs a lot less than the antiquated Samsung 4:3 monitor it replaced. The bezel is very thin, and color rendering seems excellent. There were no dead pixels. I also was pleasantly surprised to see a built in power supply instead of the ubiquitous "line lump."

The user manual is for multiple models and I wasted some time looking for the menu access buttons to change sources, adjust screen settings, etc. It turns out that with this model everything is accessed via a joystick-style arrangement on the power button. No wonder I couldn't find any discrete buttons! Samsung should really put an addendum in their instructions concerning this.

It should be noted that though the height shown is 19.59", this is with the stand fully raised. When it's fully collapsed, the actual height is much closer to 18". This might be important for someone whose available space is height constrained.

The built in headphone output was recognized immediately as another audio device, with no driver installation required. Output level is more than sufficient for earbuds and even works well with full sized headphones. I listened to some uncompressed wave files and quality seems quite good..

There are only a couple of negatives that I've found so far. One is the placement of the USB and headphone ports; it is virtually impossible to connect to these without physically tilting the monitor up, and even then it's a hassle. Second, installation would look a bit cleaner if Samsung had supplied rear exit right angles on the monitor end of both the HDMI and Display Port cables. The power cable has a right angle connector on both ends, which is great for the monitor side but may or may not be an issue when you connect it to your AC outlet (I seem to find that these always want to interfere with other plugs, or point in the opposite direction to what you need).

Overall I'm very satisfied with my purchase, and recommend this monitor.

I saw a video about this monitor being available for $70 on black Friday pricing. By the time I got around to buying it, it was $85. I bought two of them, and I'm very happy, but there's some caveats I think you should know.

This monitor does exactly what it says on the tin... and no more. It has one HDMI and one VGA input (why?) and that's it. It takes in audio via HDMI and has a headphone out jack, and even has volume control on the control nub, but no speakers. It takes 19v power from a barrel jack, but you can swap that for a 20v supply from a USB-C brick with the right adapter (you want the 6.0x4.4mm barrel).

The HDR is rubbish, the VRR works fine. The picture quality is plenty good but not remarkable. The settings are pretty minimal and sane out of the box, you'll tweak one or two of them and then never touch them again.

The stand is a joke. Of the two of these I bought, one of them was missing the 2 required screws to mount the display to the stand. Fortunately, it has a 100x100mm vesa mount on the back, though it doesn't come with screws for that either. I put mine on monitor arms, and threw out the stands.

Basically, if you need a 24" 1080p 120Hz display, and nothing else, of good quality, for as cheap as possible, this is it. For everything else, you'll have to pay more.

⭐ Rating: 4.5/5

The LG 24U411A-B 24-inch Full HD IPS Monitor is a solid, budget-friendly option that delivers smooth performance, vibrant visuals, and eye-friendly features—making it a great pick for everyday use, light gaming, and productivity.

The 120Hz refresh rate is a big upgrade from standard 60Hz monitors. Everything feels noticeably smoother—whether you're scrolling, gaming, or editing photos/videos.

🔹 IPS Panel = Great Colors & Viewing Angles

⚠️ Things to Consider

Students & teachers (like your setup 👀)

I purchased this keyboard for both gaming and everyday computer use.

As an everyday keyboard, this product is perfect. It isn't obnoxiously loud and I have had no issues with keys being faulty in any way, which you would expect from a company as established as Dell. If you find the keyboard is too flat, it has flaps underneath, offering a more comfortable angle to type for long periods. The keyboard uses a USB connection to the PC with a 1m cable which is plentiful but you may want to use cable management if there is too much.

If you want to use this as a gaming keyboard, by all means, you will still enjoy gaming as much as you always have. For less than £20, don't expect reasonable responsiveness from the keys that other gaming keyboards - in higher price bands - might offer. In my opinion, being good at a game mostly comes down to the player, hence "a builder doesn't blame his tools." That said, I'm sure others are insistent that a more expensive keyboard is required to enable optimal performance, which may be the case for them.

Overall, the keyboard is an ordinary keyboard that fulfils its role as a reliable piece of hardware, The packaging didn't seem too special, but delivery has no complaints. I just love this keyboard! Its well made, the keys feel great and it looks good (high gloss black body, matte black keys). Comes with a mouse too, which I though I just throw out, but I tried it out and to be honest after using an Apple trackpad for a few years, its a joy to use a mouse again :). The mouse is nice too, matte black, very light weight, simple.

It's a Windows keyboard, so you'll have to re-map the command key and options keys, just use an app like Karabiner, 5 min fix.

The only minor gripe I have with the keyboard is there's no Windows/alt/control key mirror to the right of the keyboard, instead there's a alt, right-click glyph tagged button, function key and control key (in that order). That strange right-click key is not recognized by Mac, so it can't be remapped with the app I'm using. text:
I bought three of these. I use one for regular computer use and use all three together when running stock trading charts. The displays look great and work really well independently as well as together, mostly because of the "borderless" frames. I'm so happy with them.

The 2560x1440 size is basically a 2K monitor which is, unfortunately, becoming harder to find.
I loved the 2K resolution on my old Apple Thunderbolt monitors and I wanted to replicate them, but 4K seemed to be the thing at the time. However, when I tried a 4K monitor, I found that it caused more eye strain so 2K ended up being the sweet spot for me.
I'm very happy with the deep blacks, great resolution and good light control.
I do a lot of design work on a Mac, but would be happy to use these monitors for that as well if I did not need a PC for charts.
The price of these is actually pretty amazing as well.

A couple of things to know:
-- these use either HDMI (2x) or DP-IN cables, so make sure you have inputs for those types in your computer.
-- the stands are not all the same height, so if you are using several monitors, they may not line up. It's close, but I personally would like it better if they were the same height since I extend my screen to span all three monitors as a virtual single screen.
-- obviously make sure your graphics cards can handle 2K, especially if using multiple monitors.

I'm very happy with these monitors. They were recommended by a friend who uses them for the same reason and he steered me well!

title: 4.0 out of 5 stars
text:
If you are on a budget but still want a decent quality 1440p monitor, this won't do you wrong. However, don't expect to be blown away by it. Previously I was daily driving a 1080p Asus. I bought two of these LGs for a dual screen setup. After switching to these, I was a little disappointed with colors. The Asus had better contrast, brightness, saturation, & black levels. I also noticed the lack of local dimming zones. However, it's still acceptable for everyday casual use. I primarily work from my computer but occasionally game too. It's perfectly fine for me, but if you do professional color grading work or want a gaming experience with really vibrant colors or a good HDR experience, look elsewhere. If you're looking for a good 1440p experience at a currently (2021) quite enticing price, this monitor is tough to beat. Despite it's shortcomings, I'm very happy with my decision to buy 2 of these.

Things I love:
- Not necessarily specific to this monitor, but 27" is a great size for 1440p. (108 ppi)
- Menus & navigation. It was really easy to customize all settings to my liking
- Ultra slim bezels!
- No dead pixels. I have 2 of these monitors.
- Black level adjust. No more eye strain in games with dark scenes
- Matte black screen handles reflections well.
- PRICE! At least at the time of purchase, nothing else competes, or even exists at this price point.

Cons
- Viewing angles. Has a perfect viewing spot. Outside of that, blacks are inconsistent across the screen.
- Backlight bleed. Problematic with screen brightness above 65-70%.
- Black levels. Does not have deep blacks. Black is still black, but other monitors have much deeper blacks.
- HDR experience. Wouldn't recommend bothering with it.
- Power cable. Short cable, w/ barrel plug into monitor and an adapter to take up lots of space on your power strip.
- Color/Contrast/Saturation. It's no OLED. It's even easily beaten by other IPS monitors. Still acceptable, but don't expect any similarities here with the LG TVs you may see in the store.

Conclusion: None of the cons were a deal breaker for me and I'm happy. 1440p monitors are expensive, but a dual monitor setup was reasonable with these. If you have the money to spend on a higher quality 1440p monitor, do it. But if you are like me and want decent quality 1440p on as small of a budget as possible, this monitor is absolutely the way to go.

I didn't rate this for gaming because I don't have a video card to drive a 4K monitor at a good speed yet, but for everything else, it looks brilliant for the money.

I'm a working stiff these days, so I don't have the free time I'd like to have to play around and get everything set up just so, and I found that there are little hurdles and speed bumps along the way with these newer displays if you want to actually USE all of the fancy marketing buzzwords like HDR or Freesync or G-Sync or high frame rates or FALD (full array local dimming). I haven't gotten those all figured out just yet and the documentation and user interface aren't quite intuitive if you've never had to set those up and get them actually enabled and working correctly in real life before. They're not just "plug it in and bask in the full glory" easy yet-- you have to make sure you have the right combinations of hardware, cables, drivers, and settings between all the devices and peripherals to take full advantage of those newer features. But 4K crystal clear beautiful brilliance does pretty much work right out of the box, and at this price, even just that is worth having. It takes very little adjusting to get very realistic colors compared to my old calibrated Dell setup. I didn't even have to delve into the color calibration tool in Windows to get it fairly close to what I prefer in my lighting environment and get my pictures to look almost exactly like they looked in real life when I originally took the pictures. I don't even feel bad quite yet about not pulling out a hardware calibration tool.

So while I haven't put together all of those pieces in a way that lets me enjoy all the features and functionality of this monitor yet, I am already satisfied with my purchase even if I never take the time to make it all work at peak performance. This is a pretty darn good buy.

I've even considered picking up another one or two to replace my old 1080P monitor and at least one of my work monitors at the office because of the price to performance ratio. The only reason I haven't is because I may get my work to buy one or two for me for that, and at home I'm planning to buy one of the top of the line 4K G-Sync quantum dot monitors as my main/gaming monitor once I've upgraded my rig to push 4K really well, and it seems silly to me to buy a perfectly good monitor to only use for a few months. title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
Been using the standard (no USB-C ports) monitor for a couple days now, and I'm super impressed.

Let's get the negatives out the way up front: The standard, cheaper version has no USB connectivity. I wish the silver stand and white cables were black instead. I wish it had even a basic set of built-in stereo speakers. Response times and refresh rates are decidedly unimpressive, but if you're not a gamer, you really won't notice or care.

For me, these aren't deal breakers for a display that otherwise gives you so much at such a good price point.

OK, let's move on to the long list of positives: Super easy to assemble, comes with HDMI and display port cables, very easy to connect on the back vs. bottom. The raise/lower and tilt stand is fantastic for dialing in a great viewing angle. The matte screen handles overhead light and ambient light superbly - annoying glare and reflections are exceptionally well managed. Straight out the box, brightness and contrast are fairly high and good if you like things punchy; color temp is a tad warm to be easier on the eyes. It's super easily adjusted if you prefer a bit cooler and even more accurate and there are many other profiles you can try to match what works best for you - the nice joystick based control on the bottom front lip of the monitor is great and IMO preferable to the buttons you have to reach around back or bottom edges for on other displays. I've done a fair bit of photo editing (not as a pro colorist, just an experienced hobbyist) and the reach the monitor has into shadows and highlights is very good. Gamut coverage is superb at this price point. No dead pixels. What more could you ask for, really?

Conclusion: If you're not a gamer, don't require built-in speakers or USB-C, and want to get a great display at a great price, put it in your cart and buy it now. You won't regret it.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
As an I.T. professional for decades... I've opened a LOT of monitors. Yes, this does what you'd expect from a product perspective. I've ordered and installed a couple dozen of these so far. Great screens, no dead pixels, 27" with 2K resolution, comes with HDMI cable, built in power supply so no dumb wall wart or AC adapter. All good things... But let me tell you what the biggest perk is of this thing if you are buying a lot of monitors... THE PACKAGING.

Yes folks, you heard it here first. I appreciate SO MUCH the choices here. Dell nailed it:
- No styrofoam blocks that inevitably break in transit and then leave dozens of single pellets of static electricity annoyance that cling to everything like a toddler to a mom's leg when all she wants is to use the bathroom in peace
- No sliding a block of goods out of a too-tight box that won't move because the "handle" punch-ins were used and now they block any possible extraction of the contents of said box
- No stickers on the bezel that advertise stats about the monitor that you already purchased and don't need to have as selling points, but inevitably leave some sticky residue when removed
- No fingerprint magnet piano black covered in cellophane peels that you will either miss removing or you will remove and then will stick to you despite you flicking your wrist towards the trash can 8 times only to find it on your shoe later in the day
- No plastic sheet covering the screen taped on with industrial strength shipping adhesive tape with fiber reinforcements that surely will not pull off cleanly and will instead peel like a banana when you try to remove it
- No tape sealing every possible ingress point of the box that requires you to cut every seam wondering where the heck the open end is

They NAILED it. The box is opened by laying it on its side, cutting a single piece of tape, opening the lid, pulling out the power and HDMI cables, stand parts (assembled tool-less), and then lifting off a single cardboard insert to reveal a foam bag which is pre-torn at the middle-bottom and you can tear further to expose the VESA mount and snap the stand into the monitor, lift it up and out... plug in cables, snap on a cover, and done.

You are left with only cardboard save for a few sheets of paper, a foam bag, and a plastic bag from the power cable (not sure why a bag is needed) and a plastic wrap (that easily slides off) from the HDMI cable.

If you need quick turnaround and/or appreciate relatively friendly environmentally conscious packaging, this is the winner. Best I've ever seen in terms of packaging.

Plus it looks nice as a white monitor. Well worth the price if you can find it sub $200. Even at full price it's worth it if you are buying in bulk as it will save you time and hassle in deployment. Well done Dell! I bought one... then dozens more. It's now my "go-to" monitor for office use.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
I do not game, I do not care about refresh rate, I care about reasonably accurate colors, view angle, and 2D performance for office productivity. For that purpose - it's great.

It comes very well packed, the assembly is super easy as it can only go together one way, and the screws are captive with folding handles, so it's dead simple to setup and get going. The base is solid, it doesn't rock around at max height.

Inputs are limited, it's doesn't have connections coming out its ears, but for the standard office needs it is completely and totally adequate.

Color is good. View angle is good. Not a ton of gradient or hot spots with backlighting.

QHD is the way to go - 4K irritates most people on shared screen meetings, and most of the time people set them to 150% or 200% zoom. 2K is a sweet spot between legibility and size. Connected directly to a laptop at native resolution, it's sharp, and perfect. I did not see any obvious dead pixels.

There are only two things I don't like: One is the little joystick button on the back. It's not terrible, but it's just one more little thing that can break off if you grab it wrong or move it a lot. title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
I was hesitant to buy this speaker for my Dell U2415 monitor based on so many reviews that said it didn't work as advertised (i.e. that it needed both a USB connection for power as well as an aux cable for the sound signal "THAT ISN'T EVEN INCLUDED!!!). Some folks even said that it didn't work with both a USB and aux cable connected.
But I wanted a speaker that wouldn't take up any space on my desk and I don't need disco club volume nor thumping base, so I went for it. I figured worst case I'd need to use an aux cable (or worst worst-case it wouldn't work for me at all and I have to return it, but hey, returning stuff is one of Amazon's strengths, right?)
So anyway it delivered next day after ordering (the joys of living in a metropolitan area!), I pulled it out of the box and connected the speaker's USB cable into one of the monitor's USB hub outlets and voila, sound was coming out of the speaker even before Skype and all of the other annoying Microsoft bloat-ware had finished starting up after I powered my computer on. Absolutely no setup of any sort required from me on the computer side of things. See the attached picture to this review for how the computer shows the speaker in the audio output section after all is said and done. So easy and I'm running Windows 8 on this machine, for Pete's Sake!

Which leads me to wonder; do people not realize that if you plug this speaker's USB plug into one of the monitor's USB ports that the monitor itself has to ALSO be connected to the computer independently via its own USB cord?
Even if you don't have your monitor hub connected (or don't have a monitor hub at all), the attached USB plug on the speaker has quite a long cord so hypothetically it would easily plug directly into the computer itself. I haven't tried that, but am absolutely confident it would work just fine. Even better, theoretically, since plugging the speaker into the monitor USB port instead of the computer's means the audio has the extra complexity of going through the USB hub in the monitor. Not that I've noticed any problems at all with that but I suppose if you were doing high data-rate transfers through the hub the sound could take a hit because of it.

Sound is perfectly fine, even great, for the size and price of this thing. Again, I don't need disco club volume nor thumping base nor battlefield realistic sound for my application so you may feel differently.
Actually I had to lower the speaker, computer, and music app volumes all down to the lower ends of their respective sliders while playing some test tracks since my kid's bedroom is right next to my "office" and the sound output was pretty significant when I first plugged it in.

My U2415 has two slots in the bottom of it that were covered up with some glorified tape pieces. Once I pulled the tape off with a mini-screwdriver the two tabs on top of the speaker slotted right into the monitor slots and it looks just like one of the photos Amazon has posted for this item.

If you go to Dell's page for this speaker, click on the "Tech Specs" tab, and scroll down to "Compatibility" you'll see a long list of Dell monitors this speaker is designed to work with. I'd guesstimate 2 out of 3 or maybe even 4 out of 5 in that list don't need the included monitor stand mount (the list differentiates which do or don't). Mine was one of those that don't so I can't speak to people's issues with the monitor stand mount, but I'm wondering if their monitor is even on that list at all.

I got this for a desktop computer I was building and added it under my Dell monitor. I use it for conference calls, not for music. It plays music just fine and plenty loud but it is a soundbar. Simple USB cable was plug and play with Windows 10. Zoom, MS Teams, etc... all recognize it. It is small and discreet but the buttons are big enough for you to find and press with ease. Sounds: Voices are loud and clear for calls. The soundbar has volume adjust buttons which increase or decrease the Windows volume control. The sound is a bit deeper and richer than you get from typical "tinny" sounding PC speakers. I have not run into any issues with audio.

Mic: This unit has an integrated far-field microphone. I typically sit 2-4 feet from the microphone and it picks my voice up well. Feedback has been that I sound clear on calls. There is a mute button on the soundbar, in addition to buttons for answer and hang-up, which could be handy in certain circumstances. The microphone on this soundbar is far better than the integrated mic on my USB camera. However, I would say it's generally of average sound capture quality. I have had no issues with it and it is sufficient for hours of daily conference calls.

I have attached pictures of the front view under monitor and the rear view of the mounting adapter.

I purchased this because it had an integrated microphone. I believe that is the key feature to choose this soundbar over all other alternatives available. The second feature would be mounting compatibility with Dell monitors. The third feature would be the inclusion of front mounted buttons for volume, mute, and call handling if someone were looking for a setup without easy access to a keyboard or mouse (i.e. distributed setup or TV display as a conferencing interface).

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
I have an HP EliteDesk 800 G5 SFF running on Windows 11 and noticed my 3 DELL 32" LCDs sometimes flicker and reset (black screen). I also noticed maxed GPU utilization on the task manager. There are 3 built-in Motherboard display ports for this SFF PC; 2x DP and 1x HDMI. I have to use passive/active HDMI adapters as my Dell LCD's only connection is via HDMI and VGA (no longer using VGA, all HD). So I determined that the best course of action to remedy this issue is to purchase a PCIeX GPU and I decided to try this Glorto Universal Graphics Card (Glorto GeForce GT 730 4Gb, 2x HDMI, 1x DP, and 1x VGA). The reason I picked this product is I needed a GPU card that would work on SFF and at the same time does not require a power supply wattage upgrade (current power supply cannot exceed 250 watts).

Install:

To properly install this graphics adapter on my PC, I had to remove the existing faceplate and the VGA port to fit in the SFF chassis. The product came with a faceplate bracket for the HDMI and DP ports. I installed the card in the PCIeXP X16 (black) slot to maximize efficiency since high-performance devices tend to rely on PCIe x26 almost exclusively. I had to use a combination of different HD cables as the DELL HDMI cables won't fit in the slots as they have wider heads.

Once all install tasks were completed, I powered on the PC and it only detected 1 display monitor so I logged in and proceeded to the next steps.

Setup/Config of new GPU card:

Having only 1 display active, I checked the display adapter under the device manager and it showed "Standard Windows Display". Right-click on it and update the driver using Windows Update. The WU automatically detected the chip and installed the appropriate driver (NVIDIA). Right after the update, the 2 remaining displays turned ON and all my desktop icon settings were back to NORMAL!

Device Manager shows "NVIDIA Display Adapter" and Task Manager shows GPU information and utilization.

Summary:

I don't play a lot of OL games purely work-related and multi-tasking kinds of stuff. I am hoping this GPU card will prove itself worthy of its reputation and last longer.

Overall, I am satisfied with my purchase of this Glorto GPU card. It has met my requirements and solved my built-in graphics card issue.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
I have an HP EliteDesk 800 G5 SFF running on Windows 11 and noticed my 3 DELL 32" LCDs sometimes flicker and reset (black screen). I also noticed maxed GPU utilization on the task manager. There are 3 built-in Motherboard display ports for this SFF PC; 2x DP and 1x HDMI. I have to use passive/active HDMI adapters as my Dell LCD's only connection is via HDMI and VGA (no longer using VGA, all HD). So I determined that the best course of action to remedy this issue is to purchase a PCIeX GPU and I decided to try this Glorto Universal Graphics Card (Glorto GeForce GT 730 4Gb, 2x HDMI, 1x DP, and 1x VGA). The reason I picked this product is I needed a GPU card that would work on SFF and at the same time does not require a power supply wattage upgrade (current power supply cannot exceed 250 watts).

Install:

To properly install this graphics adapter on my PC, I had to remove the existing faceplate and the VGA port to fit in the SFF chassis. The product came with a faceplate bracket for the HDMI and DP ports. I installed the card in the PCIeXP X16 (black) slot to maximize efficiency since high-performance devices tend to rely on PCIe x26 almost exclusively. I had to use a combination of different HD cables as the DELL HDMI cables won't fit in the slots as they have wider heads.

Once all install tasks were completed, I powered on the PC and it only detected 1 display monitor so I logged in and proceeded to the next steps.

Setup/Config of new GPU card:

Having only 1 display active, I checked the display adapter under the device manager and it showed "Standard Windows Display". Right-click on it and update the driver using Windows Update. The WU automatically detected the chip and installed the appropriate driver (NVIDIA). Right after the update, the 2 remaining displays turned ON and all my desktop icon settings were back to NORMAL!

Device Manager shows "NVIDIA Display Adapter" and Task Manager shows GPU information and utilization.

Summary:

I don't play a lot of OL games purely work-related and multi-tasking kinds of stuff. I am hoping this GPU card will prove itself worthy of its reputation and last longer.

Overall, I am satisfied with my purchase of this Glorto GPU card. It has met my requirements and solved my built-in graphics card issue.
