title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
Everything about it feels like an upgrade. The button, stick and trigger response feels right. The programmable macro switches on the back and underside are placed perfectly so I didn't have to be a contortionist to use them. And since we're on the subject, every single button and switch is programmable. You can send every function to wherever you want it to be.
Another cool touch is that the wireless dongle is tucked away in the docking station. You have the choice to remove it and plug directly into your PC. But it's better to use the dock. Because everything is automatic. Place the controller in the dock and you're instantly charging. Remove it and it instantly connects wirelessly at 2.8ghz. It with the flick of a switch via Bluetooth. And of course you can plug it directly and use it wired.
Another unique feature are the LED lights. You can change the colors but also how they behave. Evenb option to have every action show as a location on your stick ring colors. You have to see it to get it.
As I said, best controller I've ever used. Well worth the price. About $90 in 2026.

title: 5.0 out of 5 stars
text:
They fixed the connection issue from version 1. Now it never drops connection. The version 1 drops connect like 4-5 times a day. This never does. I should give it 4 stars but on these scales, a 4 star would make people not buy it when compared to other controllers it's probably better. I wish they would let you configure all the buttons on a keyboard because as it is right now, all their extra buttons are useless when it can only map to a game controller's buttons. Also I really dislike the R buttons placement, it's way too high up making me extend my index finger sideways. The joysticks padding is way too thin. It should've been fat and rounded. I really like how fast it connects after taking it off of the charger, this is way better than xbox one controller on pc.

I never used the led lights. It's super distracting to have a bright light right under your eye. As for construction quality, it has a solid premium feel. I mean I'm using it for a reason. This is a decent controller and probably better than most of them. Although button placement on an xbox one controller was perfection. Also having an actual charge stand is so much nicer than a little charger that sticks to it. It's so nitpicky to say this but it feel so much nicer to just put it on a charger and take it off with one hand. Very convenient feeling and that makes all the difference.

text:
Simplesmente controle incrível. O 8BitDo Ultimate 2 superou minhas expectativas em tudo. A construção é premium, passa muita qualidade na mão, nada de plástico vagabundo. Os botões são macios, precisos e silenciosos, dá pra jogar por horas sem cansar.

Os analógicos são extremamente precisos, sem zona morta estranha, ótimos tanto pra jogos competitivos quanto pra single player. O D-pad é excelente, um dos melhores que já usei, perfeito pra jogos retrô e luta.

A conexão é estável, sem lag perceptível, e a bateria dura muito bem. A base de carregamento é outro ponto positivo: prática, bonita e facilita demais o dia a dia. Pegou, jogou, colocou na base, pronto.

Além disso, a personalização pelo software é completa e fácil de usar, dá pra ajustar do jeito que você gosta. É aquele controle que você percebe que foi pensado pra quem realmente joga.

Resumo: confortável, preciso, bonito e confiável. Hoje, pra mim, é facilmente um dos melhores controles custo-benefício que já usei. Recomendo sem pensar duas vezes.

text:
J'ai changé de manette suite à une extinction complète après des années de dure labeur d'une nacon ultimate (200€) et je suis extrêmement content de cette 8bitdo (60€).
Manette très réactive, parfaitement compatible avec mon pc qui l'a détecte aussitôt enlevé du socle de charge.
Très qualitatives, ergonomique, impression de robustesse ...
Sur le plan technique, c'est une des meilleures manette du marché avec un prix explosant toute concurrence (joystick tmr, gâchette hall effect/ lineaire...).
Taille de manette unique plus petite qu'une manette élite ou PS5, peut être déplaisant pour certain, elle me convient parfaitement malgré de grandes mains.

Les seuls points "négatif" (subjectifs) que je lui ai trouvé sont:
- le software qui ne propose pas de personnalisation des paramètres joystick ( courbe d'accélération)
-Le software qui ne propose pas de couleur constante, seuls des mods de couleurs variables sont personnalisables

Si vous êtes un joueur plus occasionnel sa petite sœur ultimate 2c fait parfaitement l'affaire ,étant pour moi le meilleur rapport qualité-prix existant (il n'y a bien sûr pas les même caractéristiques).

title: 3.0 out of 5 stars
text:
Function:

It just works. Plugs in, works. The dpi setting button is superfluous though. Not needed because once a mouse is plugged in and adjusted in speed at the OS, theres little to no sense futzing with the dpi button when it screws up the speed when you do. So, useless feature they didn't need to bother adding (its not a gaming mouse).

Mouse Feel:

I'm a "Claw Mouser", so it can be a bit of a hassle to find a thin/small enough mouse to suit my needs (that isnt TOO thin or small). This mouse fits very well in the finger tips, and does not suffer from 'palm touch' like many other mice do. At the most, it lightly bumps the thumb pad (the bottom of the thumb that meets the hand). So, as a mouse for "claw grip users", this works out very well.

Silence? Well....

It is silent with its mouse button presses. Thats for sure. They are a nice 'thump' feel and sound, no clack, no click, no kachunks. It also has very slick feet which glide very well on pads, and is virtually impossible to hear.

Unfortunately the mouse "Wheel" is not silent at all. In fact it is louder than almost all mice I have and have tried (which is a lot of them, as I'm a picky snit). What makes it so loud? Well, it 'rattles'. Thats right. RATTLE. Its a loud rattle that even happens when you just grab the mouse quickly. Or shift the mouse side to side on the pad quickly. You bump it with a finger, and it rattles in response. And when finally trying to scroll with the wheel, it thunks clacks and rattles as it goes over its notched wheel response.

So whats the deal?

Apparently the shaft of the mouse is just loose in its cradle. It was a poorly engineered piece to an overall lovely and quiet mouse design. It wouldn't have killed them to add two thin grommets to the side of the wheel on the shaft to prevent it from shifting about so loudly. Being a cheap mouse, 1 penny wouldn't have made a difference. In fact, I can 'fix' this noise by opening up the mouse and adding some thin teflon washers there.

However since not many people want to go through the hassle of taking apart a mouse that doesn't want to be taken apart, and finding the right thin teflon washers, and do the operation... I can only conclude this mouse is not a good buy. It is not silent when a klicketyklacketyrattleklank mouse wheel overshadows every other aspect of the mouse.

If MacAlly can remedy this, then this mouse would truly be a 5 star masterpiece.

title: 3.0 out of 5 stars
text:
Function:

It just works. Plugs in, works. The dpi setting button is superfluous though. Not needed because once a mouse is plugged in and adjusted in speed at the OS, theres little to no sense futzing with the dpi button when it screws up the speed when you do. So, useless feature they didn't need to bother adding (its not a gaming mouse).

Mouse Feel:

I'm a "Claw Mouser", so it can be a bit of a hassle to find a thin/small enough mouse to suit my needs (that isnt TOO thin or small). This mouse fits very well in the finger tips, and does not suffer from 'palm touch' like many other mice do. At the most, it lightly bumps the thumb pad (the bottom of the thumb that meets the hand). So, as a mouse for "claw grip users", this works out very well.

Silence? Well....

It is silent with its mouse button presses. Thats for sure. They are a nice 'thump' feel and sound, no clack, no click, no kachunks. It also has very slick feet which glide very well on pads, and is virtually impossible to hear.

Unfortunately the mouse "Wheel" is not silent at all. In fact it is louder than almost all mice I have and have tried (which is a lot of them, as I'm a picky snit). What makes it so loud? Well, it 'rattles'. Thats right. RATTLE. Its a loud rattle that even happens when you just grab the mouse quickly. Or shift the mouse side to side on the pad quickly. You bump it with a finger, and it rattles in response. And when finally trying to scroll with the wheel, it thunks clacks and rattles as it goes over its notched wheel response.

So whats the deal?

Apparently the shaft of the mouse is just loose in its cradle. It was a poorly engineered piece to an overall lovely and quiet mouse design. It wouldn't have killed them to add two thin grommets to the side of the wheel on the shaft to prevent it from shifting about so loudly. Being a cheap mouse, 1 penny wouldn't have made a difference. In fact, I can 'fix' this noise by opening up the mouse and adding some thin teflon washers there.

However since not many people want to go through the hassle of taking apart a mouse that doesn't want to be taken apart, and finding the right thin teflon washers, and do the operation... I can only conclude this mouse is not a good buy. It is not silent when a klicketyklacketyrattleklank mouse wheel overshadows every other aspect of the mouse.

If MacAlly can remedy this, then this mouse would truly be a 5 star masterpiece.

I usually dont write reviews, but I felt compelled to do this...

Seagate's manual doesn't include Mac setup instructions, which is probably why some people think this hard drive isn't compatible, but it absolutely is.

After doing extensive research, I found that you don't need to download anything. The only thing required is a quick setup on your Mac:

1. Plug the Seagate external hard drive into your Mac
2. Open Disk Utility
3. Select the external hard drive from the list
4. Click Erase (top right)
5. Rename it to whatever you want
6. For the format, make sure you choose EXFAT (this is very important)!!!!

After that, it works perfectly.

For the other key points:

- Functionality / Computer recognition: Works perfectly once formatted correctly and is recognized without issues
- Portable / Compact size: Small, lightweight, and easy to carry around
- Scalability: Great for general storage needs like files, backups, and everyday use
- Power source: If you have a newer Mac with USB-C ports, the included cable uses USB-A, so you'll need a simple adapter or a compatible USB-C cable

So if you're seeing reviews saying it's not compatible, that's incorrect. It just needs to be formatted properly first.

title: 4.0 out of 5 stars
text:
The external hard drive enclosure is slightly bigger than the actual hard drive itself. In my experience it has an okay speed. Not the fastest drive that I've used. The USB port is a normal usb-a 3.0 port so no usb-c. The power source has multiple adapters for people who would use it for their travels so no matter what kind of power outlet it present you should be okay. The design of the external case has openings to vent the heat coming from the actual hard drive inside. In terms of security, the drive is held in my rubber pads within the external enclosure that are surrounded by plastic tabs that hold it in.

The external hard drive is a good choice to use for a NAS build if you are comfortable shucking the external case. The price is competitive when compared to a normal NAS internal drive. If you choose to go that route bear in mind that shucking the drive comes at the risk of voiding the warranty. Overall it's decent and has been running well on my NAS.

The okay speed on the drive is the limiting factor which is why it's 4 out of 5 stars.

Lastly the actual enclosure itself will still run other old drives if the ribbon cable and board aren't damaged during the shucking process. Any old 3.5 internal drives would work perfectly to recycle and not throw out the remaining hardware.

Like with other barrettes of this design, these apple barrettes work better on hair that's already styled to act as accent pieces, or to help keep hair back out of my face. Since they have a smooth clip surface and nothing to grip hair with, they will not be doing any heavy lifting when it comes to keeping up lots of hair or securing fancy styles. As accent barrettes, these are great.

I have no complaints really. These are a cute set and came just as described! I am really happy with them so far.
